text: The Dynasties of International Bankers
text_raw: The  Dynasties  of  International  Bankers

text: The merchant bankers of London had already at hand in 1810-1850 the Stock Exchange, the Bank of England, and the London money market when the needs of advancing industrialism called all of these into the industrial world which they had hitherto ignored.
text_raw:
The  merchant  bankers  of  London  had  already  at  hand  in  1810-1850  the  Stock
Exchange,  the  Bank  of  England,  and  the  London  money  market  when  the  needs  of
advancing  industrialism  called  all  of  these  into  the  industrial  world  which  they  had
hitherto  ignored.

text: In time they brought into their financial network the provincial banking centers, organized as commercial banks and savings banks, as well as insurance companies, to form all of these into a single financial system on an international scale which manipulated the quantity and flow of money so that they were able to influence, if not control, governments on one side and industries on the other.
text_raw:
In  time  they  brought  into  their  financial  network  the  provincial  banking
centers,  organized  as  commercial  banks  and  savings  banks,  as  well  as  insurance
companies,  to  form  all  of  these  into  a  single  financial  system  on  an  international  scale
which  manipulated  the  quantity  and  flow  of  money  so  that  they  were  able  to  influence,  if
not  control,  governments  on  one  side  and  industries  on  the  other.

text: The men who did this, looking backward toward the period of dynastic monarchy in which they had their own roots, aspired to establish dynasties of international bankers and were at least as successful at this as were many of the dynastic political rulers.
text_raw:
The  men  who  did  this,
looking  backward  toward  the  period  of  dynastic  monarchy  in  which  they  had  their  own
roots,  aspired  to  establish  dynasties  of  international  bankers  and  were  at  least  as
successful  at  this  as  were  many  of  the  dynastic  political  rulers.

text: The greatest of these dynasties, of course, were the descendants of Meyer Amschel Rothschild (1743-1812) of Frankfort, whose male descendants, for at least two generations, generally married first cousins or even nieces.
text_raw:
The  greatest  of  these
dynasties,  of  course,  were  the  descendants  of  Meyer  Amschel  Rothschild  (1743-1812)  of
Frankfort,  whose  male  descendants,  for  at  least  two  generations,  generally  married  first
cousins  or  even  nieces.

text: Rothschild's five sons, established at branches in Vienna, London, Naples, and Paris, as well as Frankfort, cooperated together in ways which other international banking dynasties copied but rarely excelled.
text_raw:
Rothschild's  five  sons,  established  at  branches  in  Vienna,  London,
Naples,  and  Paris,  as  well  as  Frankfort,  cooperated  together  in  ways  which  other

text: In each country the supply of money took the form of an inverted pyramid or cone balanced on its point.
text_raw:
In  each  country  the  supply  of  money  took  the  form  of  an  inverted  pyramid  or  cone
balanced  on  its  point.

text: In the point was a supply of gold and its equivalent certificates; on the intermediate levels was a much larger supply of notes; and at the top, with an open and expandable upper surface, was an even greater supply of deposits.
text_raw:
In  the  point  was  a  supply  of  gold  and  its  equivalent  certificates;  on
the  intermediate  levels  was  a  much  larger  supply  of  notes;  and  at  the  top,  with  an  open
and  expandable  upper  surface,  was  an  even  greater  supply  of  deposits.

text: Each level used the levels below it as its reserves, and, since these lower levels had smaller quantities of money, they were "sounder." A holder of claims on the middle or upper level could increase his confidence in his claims on wealth by reducing them to a lower level, although, of course, if everyone, or any considerable number of persons, tried to do this at the same time the volume of reserves would be totally inadequate.

Thus,  the  various  parts  of  the  pyramid  of  money

fact  that  the  controls  were  compulsive  in  a  deflationary  direction  and  were  only
permissive  in  an  inflationary  direction.

text: This last point can be seen in the fact that the supply of gold could be decreased but could hardly be increased.
text_raw:
This  last  point  can  be  seen  in  the  fact  that  the  supply  of  gold  could  be  decreased  but
could  hardly  be  increased.

If  such  an  ounce  of

text_raw: The  Money  Power  Persuaded  Governments  to  Establish  a

text: Deflationary Monetary Unit
text_raw: Deflationary  Monetary  Unit

text: Throughout modern history the influence of the gold standard has been deflationary, because the natural output of gold each year, except in extraordinary times, has not kept pace with the increase in output of goods.
text_raw:
Throughout  modern  history  the  influence  of  the  gold  standard  has  been  deflationary,
because  the  natural  output  of  gold  each  year,  except  in  extraordinary  times,  has  not  kept
pace  with  the  increase  in  output  of  goods.

text: Only new supplies of gold, or the suspension of the gold standard in wartime, or the development of new kinds of money (like notes and checks) which economize the use of gold, have saved our civilization from steady price deflation over the last couple of centuries.
text_raw:
Only  new  supplies  of  gold,  or  the  suspension  of
the  gold  standard  in  wartime,  or  the  development  of  new  kinds  of  money  (like  notes  and
checks)  which  economize  the  use  of  gold,  have  saved  our  civilization  from  steady  price
deflation  over  the  last  couple  of  centuries.

text: As it was, we had two long periods of such deflation from 1818 to 1850 and from 1872 to about 1897.
text_raw:
As  it  was,  we  had  two  long  periods  of  such
deflation  from  1818  to  1850  and  from  1872  to  about  1897.

text: The three surrounding periods of inflation (1790-1817, 1850-1872, 1897-1921) were caused by (1) the wars of the French Revolution and Napoleon when most countries were not on gold;

(2) the new gold strikes of California and Alaska in 1849-1850, followed by a series of wars, which included the Crimean War of 1854-1856, the Austrian-French War of 1859, the American Civil War of 1861-1865, the Austro-Prussian and Franco-Prussian wars of 1866 and 1870, and even the Russo-Turkish War of 1877; and (3) the Klondike and Transvaal gold strikes of the late 1890's, supplemented by the new cyanide method of refining gold (about 1897) and the series of wars from the Spanish- American War of 1898-1899, the Boer War of 1899-1902, and the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-1905, to the almost uninterrupted series of wars in the decade 1911-1921.
text_raw:
(2)  the  new  gold
strikes  of  California  and  Alaska  in  1849-1850,  followed  by  a  series  of  wars,  which
included  the  Crimean  War  of  1854-1856,  the  Austrian-French  War  of  1859,  the  American
Civil  War  of  1861-1865,  the  Austro-Prussian  and  Franco-Prussian  wars  of  1866  and
1870,  and  even  the  Russo-Turkish  War  of  1877;  and  (3)  the  Klondike  and  Transvaal  gold
strikes  of  the  late  1890's,  supplemented  by  the  new  cyanide  method  of  refining  gold
(about  1897)  and  the  series  of  wars  from  the  Spanish- American  War  of  1898-1899,  the
Boer  War  of  1899-1902,  and  the  Russo-Japanese  War  of  1904-1905,  to  the  almost
uninterrupted  series  of  wars  in  the  decade  1911-1921.

text: In each case, the three great periods of war ended with an extreme deflationary crisis (1819, 1873, 1921) as the influential Money Power persuaded governments to reestablish a deflationary monetary unit with a high gold content.
text_raw:
In  each  case,  the  three  great
periods  of  war  ended  with  an  extreme  deflationary  crisis  (1819,  1873,  1921)  as  the
influential  Money  Power  persuaded  governments  to  reestablish  a  deflationary  monetary
unit  with  a  high  gold  content.

text: Money Power Is More Concerned With Money Than Goods
text_raw: Money  Power  Is  More  Concerned  With  Money  Than  Goods

text: The obsession of the Money Power with deflation was partly a result of their concern with money rather than with goods, but was also founded on other factors, one of which was paradoxical.
text_raw:
The  obsession  of  the  Money  Power  with  deflation  was  partly  a  result  of  their  concern
with  money  rather  than  with  goods,  but  was  also  founded  on  other  factors,  one  of  which
was  paradoxical.

text: The paradox arose from the fact that the basic economic conditions of the nineteenth century were deflationary, with a money system based on gold and an industrial system pouring out increasing supplies of goods, but in spite of falling prices (with its increasing value of money) the interest rate tended to fall rather than to rise.
text_raw:
The  paradox  arose  from  the  fact  that  the  basic  economic  conditions  of
the  nineteenth  century  were  deflationary,  with  a  money  system  based  on  gold  and  an
industrial  system  pouring  out  increasing  supplies  of  goods,  but  in  spite  of  falling  prices
(with  its  increasing  value  of  money)  the  interest  rate  tended  to  fall  rather  than  to  rise.

text: This occurred because the relative limiting of the supply of money in business was not reflected in the world of finance where excess profits of finance made excess funds available for lending.
text_raw:
This
occurred  because  the  relative  limiting  of  the  supply  of  money  in  business  was  not
reflected  in  the  world  of  finance  where  excess  profits  of  finance  made  excess  funds
available  for  lending.

text: Moreover, the old traditions of merchant banking continued to prevail in financial capitalism even to its end in 1931.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  old  traditions  of  merchant  banking  continued  to
prevail  in  financial  capitalism  even  to  its  end  in  1931.

text: It continued to emphasize bonds rather than equity securities (stocks), to favor government issues rather than private offerings, and to look to foreign rather than to domestic investments.
text_raw:
It  continued  to  emphasize  bonds
rather  than  equity  securities  (stocks),  to  favor  government  issues  rather  than  private
offerings,  and  to  look  to  foreign  rather  than  to  domestic  investments.

text: Until 1825, government bonds made up almost the whole of securities on the London Stock Exchange.
text_raw:
Until  1825,
government  bonds  made  up  almost  the  whole  of  securities  on  the  London  Stock
Exchange.

text: In 1843, such bonds, usually foreign, were 80 percent of the securities registered, and in 1875 they were still 68 percent.
text_raw:
In  1843,  such  bonds,  usually  foreign,  were  80  percent  of  the  securities
registered,  and  in  1875  they  were  still  68  percent.

text: The funds available for such loans were so great that there were, in the nineteenth century, sometimes riots by subscribers seeking opportunities to buy security flotations; and offerings from many remote places and obscure activities commanded a ready sale.
text_raw:
The  funds  available  for  such  loans  were
so  great  that  there  were,  in  the  nineteenth  century,  sometimes  riots  by  subscribers  seeking
opportunities  to  buy  security  flotations;  and  offerings  from  many  remote  places  and
obscure  activities  commanded  a  ready  sale.

text: The excess of savings led to a fall in the price necessary to hire money, so that the interest rate on British government bonds fell from 4.42 percent in 1820 to 3.11 in 1850 to 2.76 in 1900.
text_raw:
The  excess  of  savings  led  to  a  fall  in  the  price
necessary  to  hire  money,  so  that  the  interest  rate  on  British  government  bonds  fell  from
4.42  percent  in  1820  to  3.11  in  1850  to  2.76  in  1900.

text: This tended to drive savings into foreign fields where, on the whole, they continued to seek government issues and fixed
text_raw:
This  tended  to  drive  savings  into
foreign  fields  where,  on  the  whole,  they  continued  to  seek  government  issues  and  fixed

text: interest securities.
text_raw: interest  securities.

text: All this served to strengthen the merchant bankers' obsession both with government influence and with deflation (which would increase value of money and interest rates).
text_raw:
All  this  served  to  strengthen  the  merchant  bankers'  obsession  both  with
government  influence  and  with  deflation  (which  would  increase  value  of  money  and
interest  rates).

text: Banker Policies Lead to Inflation and Deflation
text_raw: Banker  Policies  Lead  to  Inflation  and  Deflation

text: Another paradox of banking practice arose from the fact that bankers, who loved deflation, often acted in an inflationary fashion from their eagerness to lend money at interest.
text_raw:
Another  paradox  of  banking  practice  arose  from  the  fact  that  bankers,  who  loved
deflation,  often  acted  in  an  inflationary  fashion  from  their  eagerness  to  lend  money  at
interest.

text: Since they make money out of loans, they are eager to increase the amounts of bank credit on loan.
text_raw:
Since  they  make  money  out  of  loans,  they  are  eager  to  increase  the  amounts  of
bank  credit  on  loan.

text: But this is inflationary.
text_raw: But  this  is  inflationary.

text: The conflict between the deflationary ideas and inflationary practices of bankers had profound repercussions on business.
text_raw:
The  conflict  between  the  deflationary  ideas
and  inflationary  practices  of  bankers  had  profound  repercussions  on  business.

text: The bankers made loans to business so that the volume of money increased faster than the increase in goods.
text_raw:
The
bankers  made  loans  to  business  so  that  the  volume  of  money  increased  faster  than  the
increase  in  goods.

text: The result was inflation.
text_raw: The  result  was  inflation.

text: When this became clearly noticeable, the bankers would flee to notes or specie by curtailing credit and raising discount rates.
text_raw:
When  this  became  clearly  noticeable,  the
bankers  would  flee  to  notes  or  specie  by  curtailing  credit  and  raising  discount  rates.

text: This was beneficial to bankers in the short run (since it allowed them to foreclose on collateral held for loans), but it could be disastrous to them in the long run (by forcing the value of the collateral below the amount of the loans it secured).
text_raw:
This
was  beneficial  to  bankers  in  the  short  run  (since  it  allowed  them  to  foreclose  on  collateral
held  for  loans),  but  it  could  be  disastrous  to  them  in  the  long  run  (by  forcing  the  value  of
the  collateral  below  the  amount  of  the  loans  it  secured).

text: But such bankers' deflation was destructive to business and industry in the short run as well as the long run.
text_raw:
But  such  bankers'  deflation  was
destructive  to  business  and  industry  in  the  short  run  as  well  as  the  long  run.

text: Changing the Quality of Money
text_raw: Changing  the  Quality  of  Money

text: The resulting fluctuation in the supply of money, chiefly deposits, was a prominent aspect of the "business cycle." The quantity of money could be changed by changing reserve requirements or discount (interest) rates.
text_raw:
The  resulting  fluctuation  in  the  supply  of  money,  chiefly  deposits,  was  a  prominent
aspect  of  the  "business  cycle."  The  quantity  of  money  could  be  changed  by  changing
reserve  requirements  or  discount  (interest)  rates.

text: In the United States, for example, an upper limit has been set on deposits by requiring Federal Reserve member banks to keep a certain percentage of their deposits as reserves with the local Federal Reserve Bank.
text_raw:
In  the  United  States,  for  example,  an
upper  limit  has  been  set  on  deposits  by  requiring  Federal  Reserve  member  banks  to  keep
a  certain  percentage  of  their  deposits  as  reserves  with  the  local  Federal  Reserve  Bank.

text: The percentage (usually from 7 to 26 percent) varies with the locality and the decisions of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.
text_raw:
The  percentage  (usually  from  7  to  26  percent)  varies  with  the  locality  and  the  decisions  of
the  Board  of  Governors  of  the  Federal  Reserve  System.

text: Central Banks Vary Money in Circulation
text_raw: Central  Banks  Vary  Money  in  Circulation

text: Central banks can usually vary the amount of money in circulation by "open market operations" or by influencing the discount rates of lesser banks.
text_raw:
Central  banks  can  usually  vary  the  amount  of  money  in  circulation  by  "open  market
operations"  or  by  influencing  the  discount  rates  of  lesser  banks.

text: In open market operations, a central bank buys or sells government bonds in the open market.
text_raw:
In  open  market
operations,  a  central  bank  buys  or  sells  government  bonds  in  the  open  market.

text: If it buys, it releases money into the economic system; if it sells it reduces the amount of money in the community.
text_raw:
If  it  buys,
it  releases  money  into  the  economic  system;  if  it  sells  it  reduces  the  amount  of  money  in
the  community.

text: The change is greater than the price paid for the securities.
text_raw: The  change  is  greater  than  the  price  paid  for  the  securities.

text: For example, if the Federal Reserve Bank buys government securities in the open market, it pays for these by check which is soon deposited in a bank.
text_raw:
For  example,
if  the  Federal  Reserve  Bank  buys  government  securities  in  the  open  market,  it  pays  for
these  by  check  which  is  soon  deposited  in  a  bank.

text: It thus increases this bank's reserves with the Federal Reserve Bank.
text_raw:
It  thus  increases  this  bank's  reserves
with  the  Federal  Reserve  Bank.

text: Since banks are permitted to issue loans for several times the value of their reserves with the Federal Reserve Bank, such a transaction permits them to issue loans for a much larger sum.
text_raw:
Since  banks  are  permitted  to  issue  loans  for  several  times
the  value  of  their  reserves  with  the  Federal  Reserve  Bank,  such  a  transaction  permits
them  to  issue  loans  for  a  much  larger  sum.

text: Central Banks Raise and Lower Interest Rates
text_raw: Central  Banks  Raise  and  Lower  Interest  Rates

text: Central banks can also change the quantity of money by influencing the credit policies of other banks.
text_raw:
Central  banks  can  also  change  the  quantity  of  money  by  influencing  the  credit  policies
of  other  banks.

text: This can be done by various methods, such as changing the re-discount
text_raw: This  can  be  done  by  various  methods,  such  as  changing  the  re-discount

text: rate or changing reserve requirements.
text_raw: rate  or  changing  reserve  requirements.

text: By changing the re-discount rate we mean the interest rate which central banks charge lesser banks for loans backed by commercial paper or other security which these lesser banks have taken in return for loans.
text_raw:
By  changing  the  re-discount  rate  we  mean  the
interest  rate  which  central  banks  charge  lesser  banks  for  loans  backed  by  commercial
paper  or  other  security  which  these  lesser  banks  have  taken  in  return  for  loans.

text: By raising the re-discount rate the central bank forces the lesser bank to raise its discount rate in order to operate at a profit; such a raise in interest rates tends to reduce the demand for credit and thus the amount of deposits (money).
text_raw:
By  raising
the  re-discount  rate  the  central  bank  forces  the  lesser  bank  to  raise  its  discount  rate  in
order  to  operate  at  a  profit;  such  a  raise  in  interest  rates  tends  to  reduce  the  demand  for
credit  and  thus  the  amount  of  deposits  (money).

text: Lowering the re-discount rate permits an opposite result.
text_raw:
Lowering  the  re-discount  rate  permits  an
opposite  result.

text: Central Banks Force Local Banks to Decrease Credit
text_raw: Central  Banks  Force  Local  Banks  to  Decrease  Credit

text: Changing the reserve requirements as a method by which central banks can influence the credit policies of other banks is possible only in those places (like the United States) where there is a statutory limit on reserves.
text_raw:
Changing  the  reserve  requirements  as  a  method  by  which  central  banks  can  influence
the  credit  policies  of  other  banks  is  possible  only  in  those  places  (like  the  United  States)
where  there  is  a  statutory  limit  on  reserves.

text: Increasing reserve requirements curtails the ability of lesser banks to grant credit, while decreasing it expands that ability.
text_raw:
Increasing  reserve  requirements  curtails  the
ability  of  lesser  banks  to  grant  credit,  while  decreasing  it  expands  that  ability.

text: It is to be noted that the control of the central bank over the credit policies of local banks are permissive in one direction and compulsive in the other.
text_raw:
It  is  to  be  noted  that  the  control  of  the  central  bank  over  the  credit  policies  of  local
banks  are  permissive  in  one  direction  and  compulsive  in  the  other.

text: They can compel these local banks to curtail credit and can only permit them to increase credit.
text_raw:
They  can  compel  these
local  banks  to  curtail  credit  and  can  only  permit  them  to  increase  credit.

text: This means that they have control powers against inflation and not deflation â€” a reflection of the old banking idea that inflation was bad and deflation was good.
text_raw:
This  means  that
they  have  control  powers  against  inflation  and  not  deflation â€” a  reflection  of  the  old
banking  idea  that  inflation  was  bad  and  deflation  was  good.

text: The Powers of Government Over Money
text_raw: The  Powers  of  Government  Over  Money

text: The powers of governments over the quantity of money are of various kinds, and include (a) control over a central bank, (b) control over public taxation, and (c) control over public spending.
text_raw:
The  powers  of  governments  over  the  quantity  of  money  are  of  various  kinds,  and
include  (a)  control  over  a  central  bank,  (b)  control  over  public  taxation,  and  (c)  control
over  public  spending.

text: The control of governments over central banks varies greatly from one country to another, but on the whole has been increasing.
text_raw:
The  control  of  governments  over  central  banks  varies  greatly  from
one  country  to  another,  but  on  the  whole  has  been  increasing.

text: Since most central banks have been (technically) private institutions, this control is frequently based on custom rather than on law.
text_raw:
Since  most  central  banks
have  been  (technically)  private  institutions,  this  control  is  frequently  based  on  custom
rather  than  on  law.

text: In any case, the control over the supply of money which governments have through centra! banks is exercised by the regular banking procedures we have discussed.
text_raw:
In  any  case,  the  control  over  the  supply  of  money  which  governments
have  through  centra!  banks  is  exercised  by  the  regular  banking  procedures  we  have
discussed.

text: The powers of the government over the quantity of money in the community exercised through taxation and public spending are largely independent of banking control.
text_raw:
The  powers  of  the  government  over  the  quantity  of  money  in  the  community
exercised  through  taxation  and  public  spending  are  largely  independent  of  banking
control.

text: Taxation tends to reduce the amount of money in a community and is usually a deflationary force; government spending tends to increase the amount of money in a community and is usually an inflationary force.
text_raw:
Taxation  tends  to  reduce  the  amount  of  money  in  a  community  and  is  usually  a
deflationary  force;  government  spending  tends  to  increase  the  amount  of  money  in  a
community  and  is  usually  an  inflationary  force.

text: The total effects of a government's policy will depend on which item is greater.
text_raw:
The  total  effects  of  a  government's  policy
will  depend  on  which  item  is  greater.

text: An unbalanced budget will be inflationary; a budget with a surplus will be deflationary.
text_raw:
An  unbalanced  budget  will  be  inflationary;  a  budget
with  a  surplus  will  be  deflationary.

text: A government can also change the amount of money in a community by other, more drastic, methods.
text_raw:
A  government  can  also  change  the  amount  of  money  in  a  community  by  other,  more
drastic,  methods.

text: By changing the gold content of the monetary unit they can change the amount of money in the community by a much greater amount.
text_raw:
By  changing  the  gold  content  of  the  monetary  unit  they  can  change  the
amount  of  money  in  the  community  by  a  much  greater  amount.

text: If, for example, the gold content of the dollar is cut in half, the amount of gold certificates will be able to be doubled, and the amount of notes and deposits reared on this basis will be increased many fold, depending on the customs of the community in respect to reserve requirements.
text_raw:
If,  for  example,  the  gold
content  of  the  dollar  is  cut  in  half,  the  amount  of  gold  certificates  will  be  able  to  be
doubled,  and  the  amount  of  notes  and  deposits  reared  on  this  basis  will  be  increased  many
fold,  depending  on  the  customs  of  the  community  in  respect  to  reserve  requirements.

text: Moreover, if a government goes off the gold standard completely â€” that is, refuses to exchange certificates and notes for specie â€” the amount of notes and deposits can be
text_raw:
Moreover,  if  a  government  goes  off  the  gold  standard  completely â€” that  is,  refuses  to
exchange  certificates  and  notes  for  specie â€” the  amount  of  notes  and  deposits  can  be

text: increased indefinitely because these are no longer limited by limited amounts of gold reserves.

increased  indefinitely  because  these  are  no  longer  limited  by  limited  amounts  of  gold
reserves.

text: Dominates Business and Government
text_raw: Dominates  Business  and  Government

text: In the various actions which increase or decrease the supply of money, governments, bankers, and industrialists have not always seen eye to eye.
text_raw:
In  the  various  actions  which  increase  or  decrease  the  supply  of  money,  governments,
bankers,  and  industrialists  have  not  always  seen  eye  to  eye.

text: On the whole, in the period up to 1931, bankers, especially the Money Power controlled by the international investment bankers, were able to dominate both business and government.
text_raw:
On  the  whole,  in  the  period
up  to  1931,  bankers,  especially  the  Money  Power  controlled  by  the  international
investment  bankers,  were  able  to  dominate  both  business  and  government.

text: They could dominate business, especially in activities and in areas where industry could not finance its own needs for capital, because investment bankers had the ability to supply or refuse to supply such capital.
text_raw:
They  could
dominate  business,  especially  in  activities  and  in  areas  where  industry  could  not  finance
its  own  needs  for  capital,  because  investment  bankers  had  the  ability  to  supply  or  refuse
to  supply  such  capital.

text: Thus, Rothschild interests came to dominate many of the railroads of Europe, while Morgan dominated at least 26,000 miles of American railroads.
text_raw:
Thus,  Rothschild  interests  came  to  dominate  many  of  the  railroads
of  Europe,  while  Morgan  dominated  at  least  26,000  miles  of  American  railroads.

text: Such bankers went further than this.
text_raw:
Such
bankers  went  further  than  this.

text: In return for flotations of securities of industry, they took seats on the boards of directors of industrial firms, as they had already done on commercial banks, savings banks, insurance firms, and finance companies.
text_raw:
In  return  for  flotations  of  securities  of  industry,  they  took
seats  on  the  boards  of  directors  of  industrial  firms,  as  they  had  already  done  on
commercial  banks,  savings  banks,  insurance  firms,  and  finance  companies.

text: From these lesser institutions they funneled capital to enterprises which yielded control and away from those who resisted.
text_raw:
From  these
lesser  institutions  they  funneled  capital  to  enterprises  which  yielded  control  and  away
from  those  who  resisted.

text: These firms were controlled through interlocking directorships, holding companies, and lesser banks.
text_raw:

text: International Financial Practices
text_raw: International  Financial  Practices

text: The financial principals which apply to the relationships between different countries are an expansion of those which apply within a single country.
text_raw:

text: When goods are exchanged between countries, they must be paid for by commodities or gold.

When  goods  are
exchanged  between  countries,  they  must  be  paid  for  by  commodities  or  gold.

text: They cannot be paid for by the notes, certificates, and checks of the purchaser's country, since these are of value only in the country of issue.
text_raw:
They
cannot  be  paid  for  by  the  notes,  certificates,  and  checks  of  the  purchaser's  country,  since
these  are  of  value  only  in  the  country  of  issue.

text: To avoid shipment of gold with every purchase, bills of exchange are used.
text_raw:
To  avoid  shipment  of  gold  with  every
purchase,  bills  of  exchange  are  used.

text: These are claims against a person in another country which are sold to a person in the same country.
text_raw:
These  are  claims  against  a  person  in  another  country
which  are  sold  to  a  person  in  the  same  country.

text: The latter will buy such a claim if he wants to satisfy a claim against himself held by a person in the other country.

wants  to  satisfy  a  claim  against  himself  held  by  a  person  in  the  other  country.

text: He can satisfy such a claim by sending to his creditor in the other country the claim which he has bought against another person in that other country, and let his creditor use that claim to satisfy his own claim.
text_raw:
He  can
satisfy  such  a  claim  by  sending  to  his  creditor  in  the  other  country  the  claim  which  he  has
bought  against  another  person  in  that  other  country,  and  let  his  creditor  use  that  claim  to
satisfy  his  own  claim.

text: Thus, instead of importers in one country sending money to exporters in another country, importers in one country pay their debts to exporters in their own country, and their creditors in the other country receive payment for the goods they have exported from importers in their own country.
text_raw:
Thus,  instead  of  importers  in  one  country  sending  money  to
exporters  in  another  country,  importers  in  one  country  pay  their  debts  to  exporters  in  their
own  country,  and  their  creditors  in  the  other  country  receive  payment  for  the  goods  they
have  exported  from  importers  in  their  own  country.

text: Thus, payment for goods in an international trade is made by merging single transactions involving two persons into double transactions involving four persons.

text: Since the bills available in any market were drawn in the monetary units of many different foreign countries, there arose exchange relationships between the amounts of money available in the country's own units (put there by importers) and the variety of bills drawn in foreign moneys and put into the market by exporters.

text: Elimination of the Gold Standard
text_raw: Elimination  of  the  Gold  Standard

text: The flow of gold from country to country resulting from unbalanced trade tends to create a situation which counteracts the flow.
text_raw:
The  flow  of  gold  from  country  to  country  resulting  from  unbalanced  trade  tends  to
create  a  situation  which  counteracts  the  flow.

text: If a country exports more than it imports so that gold flows in to cover the difference, this gold will become the basis for an increased quantity of money, and this will cause a rise of prices within the country sufficient to reduce exports and increase imports.
text_raw:
If  a  country  exports  more  than  it  imports  so
that  gold  flows  in  to  cover  the  difference,  this  gold  will  become  the  basis  for  an  increased
quantity  of  money,  and  this  will  cause  a  rise  of  prices  within  the  country  sufficient  to
reduce  exports  and  increase  imports.

text: At the same time, the gold by flowing out of some other country will reduce the quantity of money there and will cause a fall in prices within that country.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  the  gold  by  flowing  out  of  some
other  country  will  reduce  the  quantity  of  money  there  and  will  cause  a  fall  in  prices
within  that  country.

text: These shifts in prices will cause shifts in the flow of goods because of the obvious fact that goods tend to flow to higher-priced areas and cease to flow to lower-priced areas.
text_raw:
These  shifts  in  prices  will  cause  shifts  in  the  flow  of  goods  because
of  the  obvious  fact  that  goods  tend  to  flow  to  higher-priced  areas  and  cease  to  flow  to
lower-priced  areas.

text: These shifts in the flow of goods will counteract the original unbalance in trade which caused the flow of gold.
text_raw:
These  shifts  in  the  flow  of  goods  will  counteract  the  original
unbalance  in  trade  which  caused  the  flow  of  gold.

text: As a result, the flow of gold will cease, and a balanced international trade at slightly different price levels will result.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  the  flow  of  gold  will  cease,
and  a  balanced  international  trade  at  slightly  different  price  levels  will  result.

text: The whole process illustrates the subordination of internal price stability to stability of exchanges.
text_raw:
The  whole
process  illustrates  the  subordination  of  internal  price  stability  to  stability  of  exchanges.

text: It was this subordination which was rejected by most countries after 1931.
text_raw:
It
was  this  subordination  which  was  rejected  by  most  countries  after  1931.

text: This rejection was signified by (a) abandonment of the gold standard at least in part, (b) efforts at control of domestic prices, and (c) efforts at exchange control.

This  rejection
was  signified  by  (a)  abandonment  of  the  gold  standard  at  least  in  part,  (b)  efforts  at
control  of  domestic  prices,  and  (c)  efforts  at  exchange  control.

because  of  a  desire  to  free  the  economic  system  from  the  restricting  influence  of  a  gold-

text: Major Countries Forced to Abandon Gold Standard
text_raw: Major  Countries  Forced  to  Abandon  Gold  Standard

text: This wonderful, automatic mechanism of international payments represents one of the greatest social instruments ever devised by man.
text_raw:
This  wonderful,  automatic  mechanism  of  international  payments  represents  one  of  the
greatest  social  instruments  ever  devised  by  man.

text: It requires, however, a very special group of conditions for its effective functioning and, as we shall show, these conditions were disappearing by 1900 and were largely wiped away as a result of the economic changes brought about by the First World War.

It  requires,  however,  a  very  special
group  of  conditions  for  its  effective  functioning  and,  as  we  shall  show,  these  conditions
were  disappearing  by  1900  and  were  largely  wiped  away  as  a  result  of  the  economic
changes  brought  about  by  the  First  World  War.

text_raw:
Because  of  these  changes  it  became
impossible  to  restore  the  financial  system  which  had  existed  before  1914.

text: Efforts to restore it were made with great determination, but by 1933 they had obviously failed, and all major countries had been forced to abandon the gold standard and automatic exchanges.

Efforts  to
restore  it  were  made  with  great  determination,  but  by  1933  they  had  obviously  failed,  and
all  major  countries  had  been  forced  to  abandon  the  gold  standard  and  automatic
exchanges.

text: When the gold standard is abandoned, gold flows between countries like any other commodity, and the value of foreign exchanges (no longer tied to gold) can fluctuate much more widely.
text_raw:
When  the  gold  standard  is  abandoned,  gold  flows  between  countries  like  any  other
commodity,  and  the  value  of  foreign  exchanges  (no  longer  tied  to  gold)  can  fluctuate
much  more  widely.

text: In theory an unbalance of international payments can be rectified either through a shift in exchange rates or through a shift in internal price levels.
text_raw:
In  theory  an  unbalance  of  international  payments  can  be  rectified
either  through  a  shift  in  exchange  rates  or  through  a  shift  in  internal  price  levels.

text: On the gold standard this rectification is made by shifts in exchange rates only between the gold points.
text_raw:
On  the
gold  standard  this  rectification  is  made  by  shifts  in  exchange  rates  only  between  the  gold
points.

text: When the unbalance is so great that exchanges would be forced beyond the gold points, the rectification is made by means of changing internal prices caused by the fact that gold flows at the gold points, instead of the exchanges passing beyond the gold points.
text_raw:
When  the  unbalance  is  so  great  that  exchanges  would  be  forced  beyond  the  gold
points,  the  rectification  is  made  by  means  of  changing  internal  prices  caused  by  the  fact
that  gold  flows  at  the  gold  points,  instead  of  the  exchanges  passing  beyond  the  gold
points.

text: On the other hand, when a currency is off the gold standard, fluctuation of exchanges is not confined between any two points but can go indefinitely in either direction.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  when  a  currency  is  off  the  gold  standard,  fluctuation  of
exchanges  is  not  confined  between  any  two  points  but  can  go  indefinitely  in  either
direction.

text: In such a case, the unbalance of international payments is worked out largely by a shift in exchange rates and only remotely by shifts in internal prices.
text_raw:
In  such  a  case,  the  unbalance  of  international  payments  is  worked  out  largely
by  a  shift  in  exchange  rates  and  only  remotely  by  shifts  in  internal  prices.

text: In the period of 1929-1936, the countries of the world went off gold because they preferred to bring their international balances toward equilibrium by means of fluctuating exchanges rather than by means of fluctuating price levels.

In  the  period  of
1929-1936,  the  countries  of  the  world  went  off  gold  because  they  preferred  to  bring  their

by  means  of  fluctuating  price  levels.

text: They feared these last because changing (especially falling) prices led to declines in business activity and shifts in the utilization of economic resources (such as labor, land, and capital) from one activity to another.

text: Major Changes in Government Occur in 1830
text_raw: Major  Changes  in  Government  Occur  in  1830

text: The Founding Fathers had assumed that the political control of the country would be conducted by men of property and leisure who would generally know each other personally and, facing no need for urgent decisions, would move government to action when they agreed and be able to prevent it from acting, without serious damage, when they could not agree.

conducted  by  men  of  property  and  leisure  who  would  generally  know  each  other
personally  and,  facing  no  need  for  urgent  decisions,  would  move  government  to  action
when  they  agreed  and  be  able  to  prevent  it  from  acting,  without  serious  damage,  when
they  could  not  agree.

text: The American Constitution, with its provisions for division of powers and selection of the chief executive by an electoral college, reflected this point of view.

text: The arrival of a mass democracy after 1830 changed this situation, establishing the use of party conventions for nominations and the use of entrenched political party machines, supported on the patronage of public office, to mobilize sufficient votes to elect their candidates.

text: As a result of this situation, the elected official from 1840 to 1880 found himself under pressure from three directions: from the popular electorate which provided him with the votes necessary for election, from the party machine which provided him with the nomination to run for office as well as the patronage appointments by which he could reward his followers, and from the wealthy economic interests which gave him the money for campaign expenses with, perhaps, a certain surplus for his own pocket.

text: Naturally, they were not so foolish as to do this, although Morgan came very close to it in precipitating the "panic of 1907," but they did not hesitate to wreck individual corporations, at the expense of the holders of common stocks, by driving them to bankruptcy.

The  religious  and  linguistic  divisions  of  the  Ottoman  Empire  were  complicated  by

provided  such  contrasts  as  the  relatively  advanced  commercial  and  mercantile  activities

text_raw: Such  diversity  made  any

text: Indeed, it was almost impossible to draw any political lines which would coincide with geographic and linguistic or religious lines, because linguistic and religious distinctions frequently indicated class distinctions.
text_raw:
Indeed,  it  was  almost  impossible  to  draw  any  political  lines  which  would  coincide  with
geographic  and  linguistic  or  religious  lines,  because  linguistic  and  religious  distinctions

text: Thus the upper and lower classes or the commercial and the agricultural groups even in the same district often had different languages or different religions.
text_raw:
Thus  the  upper  and  lower  classes  or  the
commercial  and  the  agricultural  groups  even  in  the  same  district  often  had  different
languages  or  different  religions.

text: Such a pattern of diversity could be held together most easily by a simple display of military force.
text_raw:
Such  a  pattern  of  diversity  could  be  held  together  most
easily  by  a  simple  display  of  military  force.

text: This was what the Turks provided.
text_raw: This  was  what  the  Turks  provided.

text: Militarism and fiscalism were the two keynotes of Turkish rule, and were quite sufficient to hold the empire together as long as both remained effective and the empire was free from outside interference.
text_raw:
Militarism
and  fiscalism  were  the  two  keynotes  of  Turkish  rule,  and  were  quite  sufficient  to  hold  the
empire  together  as  long  as  both  remained  effective  and  the  empire  was  free  from  outside
interference.

text: But in the course of the eighteenth century Turkish administration became ineffective and outside interference became important.
text_raw:
But  in  the  course  of  the  eighteenth  century  Turkish  administration  became
ineffective  and  outside  interference  became  important.

text: The sultan, who was a completely absolute ruler, became very quickly a completely arbitrary ruler.
text_raw:
The  sultan,  who  was  a  completely  absolute  ruler,  became  very  quickly  a  completely
arbitrary  ruler.

text: This characteristic extended to all his activities.
text_raw: This  characteristic  extended  to  all  his  activities.

text: He filled his harem with any women who pleased his fancy, without any formal ceremony.
text_raw:
He  filled  his  harem  with
any  women  who  pleased  his  fancy,  without  any  formal  ceremony.

text: Such numerous and temporary liaisons produced numerous children, of whom many were neglected or even forgotten.
text_raw:
Such  numerous  and
temporary  liaisons  produced  numerous  children,  of  whom  many  were  neglected  or  even
forgotten.

text: Accordingly, the succession to the throne never became established and was never based on primogeniture.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  the  succession  to  the  throne  never  became  established  and  was
never  based  on  primogeniture.

text: As a consequence, the sultan came to fear murder from almost any direction.
text_raw:
As  a  consequence,  the  sultan  came  to  fear  murder  from
almost  any  direction.

text: To avoid this, he tended to surround himself with persons who could have no possible chance of succeeding him: women, children, Negroes, eunuchs, and Christians.
text_raw:
To  avoid  this,  he  tended  to  surround  himself  with  persons  who
could  have  no  possible  chance  of  succeeding  him:  women,  children,  Negroes,  eunuchs,
and  Christians.

text: All the sultans from 1451 onward were born of slave mothers and only one sultan after this date even bothered to contract a formal marriage.
text_raw:
All  the  sultans  from  1451  onward  were  born  of  slave  mothers  and  only
one  sultan  after  this  date  even  bothered  to  contract  a  formal  marriage.

text: Such a way of life isolated the sultan from his subjects completely.
text_raw:
Such  a  way  of  life
isolated  the  sultan  from  his  subjects  completely.

text: This isolation applied to the process of government as well as to the ruler's personal life.
text_raw:
This  isolation  applied  to  the  process  of  government  as  well  as  to  the  ruler's  personal
life.

text: Most of the sultans paid little heed to government, leaving this to their grand viziers and the local pashas.
text_raw:
Most  of  the  sultans  paid  little  heed  to  government,  leaving  this  to  their  grand  viziers
and  the  local  pashas.

text: The former had no tenure, being appointed or removed in accordance with the whims of harem intrigue.
text_raw:
The  former  had  no  tenure,  being  appointed  or  removed  in
accordance  with  the  whims  of  harem  intrigue.

text: The pashas tended to become increasingly independent, since they collected local taxes and raised local military forces.
text_raw:
The  pashas  tended  to  become  increasingly
independent,  since  they  collected  local  taxes  and  raised  local  military  forces.

text: The fact that the sultan was also caliph (and thus religious successor to Muhammad), and the religious belief that the government was under divine guidance and should be obeyed, however unjust and tyrannical, made all religious thinking on political or social questions take the form of justification of the status quo, and made any kind of reform almost impossible.
text_raw:
The  fact  that
the  sultan  was  also  caliph  (and  thus  religious  successor  to  Muhammad),  and  the  religious
belief  that  the  government  was  under  divine  guidance  and  should  be  obeyed,  however
unjust  and  tyrannical,  made  all  religious  thinking  on  political  or  social  questions  take  the
form  of  justification  of  the  status  quo,  and  made  any  kind  of  reform  almost  impossible.

text: Reform could come only from the Sultan, but his ignorance and isolation from society made reform unlikely.
text_raw:
Reform  could  come  only  from  the  Sultan,  but  his  ignorance  and  isolation  from  society
made  reform  unlikely.

text: In consequence the whole system became increasingly weak and corrupt.
text_raw:
In  consequence  the  whole  system  became  increasingly  weak  and
corrupt.

text: The administration was chaotic, inefficient, and arbitrary.
text_raw: The  administration  was  chaotic,  inefficient,  and  arbitrary.

text: Almost nothing could be done without gifts and bribes to officials, and it was not always possible to know what official or series of officials were the correct ones to reward.
text_raw:
Almost  nothing  could
be  done  without  gifts  and  bribes  to  officials,  and  it  was  not  always  possible  to  know  what
official  or  series  of  officials  were  the  correct  ones  to  reward.

text: The chaos and weakness which we have described were in full blossom by the seventeenth century, and grew worse during the next two hundred years.
text_raw:
The  chaos  and  weakness  which  we  have  described  were  in  full  blossom  by  the
seventeenth  century,  and  grew  worse  during  the  next  two  hundred  years.

text: As early as 1699 the sultan lost Hungary, Transylvania, Croatia, and Slavonia to the Habsburgs, parts of the western Balkans to Venice, and districts in the north to Poland.
text_raw:
As  early  as  1699
the  sultan  lost  Hungary,  Transylvania,  Croatia,  and  Slavonia  to  the  Habsburgs,  parts  of
the  western  Balkans  to  Venice,  and  districts  in  the  north  to  Poland.

text: In the course of the eighteenth century, Russia acquired areas north of the Black Sea, notably the Crimea.
text_raw:
In  the  course  of  the
eighteenth  century,  Russia  acquired  areas  north  of  the  Black  Sea,  notably  the  Crimea.

text: During the nineteenth century, the Near East question became increasingly acute.
text_raw: During  the  nineteenth  century,  the  Near  East  question  became  increasingly  acute.

text: Russia emerged from the Napoleonic Wars as a Great Power, able to increase its pressure on Turkey.
text_raw:
Russia  emerged  from  the  Napoleonic  Wars  as  a  Great  Power,  able  to  increase  its  pressure
on  Turkey.

text: This pressure resulted from three motivations.
text_raw: This  pressure  resulted  from  three  motivations.

text: Russian imperialism sought to win an outlet to open waters in the south by dominating the Black Sea and by winning access to the Aegean through the acquisition of the Straits and Constantinople.
text_raw:
Russian  imperialism  sought  to
win  an  outlet  to  open  waters  in  the  south  by  dominating  the  Black  Sea  and  by  winning
access  to  the  Aegean  through  the  acquisition  of  the  Straits  and  Constantinople.

text: Later this effort was supplemented by economic and diplomatic pressure on Persia in order to reach the Persian Gulf.
text_raw:
Later  this
effort  was  supplemented  by  economic  and  diplomatic  pressure  on  Persia  in  order  to  reach
the  Persian  Gulf.

text: At the same time, Russia regarded itself as the protector of the Orthodox Christians in the Ottoman Empire, and as early as 1774 had obtained the sultan's consent to this protective role.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  Russia  regarded  itself  as  the  protector  of  the
Orthodox  Christians  in  the  Ottoman  Empire,  and  as  early  as  1774  had  obtained  the
sultan's  consent  to  this  protective  role.

text: Moreover, as the most powerful Slav state, Russia had ambitions to be regarded as the protector of the Slavs in the sultan's domains.
text_raw:
Moreover,  as  the  most  powerful  Slav  state,  Russia
had  ambitions  to  be  regarded  as  the  protector  of  the  Slavs  in  the  sultan's  domains.

text: These Russian ambitions could never have been thwarted by the sultan alone, but he did not need to stand alone.
text_raw:
These  Russian  ambitions  could  never  have  been  thwarted  by  the  sultan  alone,  but  he
did  not  need  to  stand  alone.

text: He generally found support from Britain and increasingly from France.
text_raw:
He  generally  found  support  from  Britain  and  increasingly
from  France.

text: Britain was obsessed with the need to defend India, which was a manpower pool and military staging area vital to the defense of the whole empire.
text_raw:
Britain  was  obsessed  with  the  need  to  defend  India,  which  was  a  manpower
pool  and  military  staging  area  vital  to  the  defense  of  the  whole  empire.

text: From 1840 to 1907, it faced the nightmare possibility that Russia might attempt to cross Afghanistan to northwest India, or cross Persia to the Persian Gulf, or penetrate through the Dardanelles and the Aegean onto the British "lifeline to India" by way of the Mediterranean.
text_raw:
From  1840  to
1907,  it  faced  the  nightmare  possibility  that  Russia  might  attempt  to  cross  Afghanistan  to
northwest  India,  or  cross  Persia  to  the  Persian  Gulf,  or  penetrate  through  the  Dardanelles
and  the  Aegean  onto  the  British  "lifeline  to  India"  by  way  of  the  Mediterranean.

text: The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 increased the importance of this Mediterranean route to the east in British eyes.
text_raw:
The
opening  of  the  Suez  Canal  in  1869  increased  the  importance  of  this  Mediterranean  route
to  the  east  in  British  eyes.

text: It was protected by British forces in Gibraltar, Malta (acquired 1800), Cyprus (1878), and Egypt (1882).
text_raw:
It  was  protected  by  British  forces  in  Gibraltar,  Malta  (acquired
1800),  Cyprus  (1878),  and  Egypt  (1882).

text: In general, in spite of English humanitarian sympathy for the peoples subject to the tyranny of the Turk, and in spite of England's regard for the merits of good government, British imperial policy considered that its interests would be safer with a weak, if corrupt, Turkey in the Near East than they would be with any Great Power in that area or with the area broken up into small independent states which might fall under the influence of the Great Powers.
text_raw:
In  general,  in  spite  of  English  humanitarian
sympathy  for  the  peoples  subject  to  the  tyranny  of  the  Turk,  and  in  spite  of  England's
regard  for  the  merits  of  good  government,  British  imperial  policy  considered  that  its
interests  would  be  safer  with  a  weak,  if  corrupt,  Turkey  in  the  Near  East  than  they  would
be  with  any  Great  Power  in  that  area  or  with  the  area  broken  up  into  small  independent
states  which  might  fall  under  the  influence  of  the  Great  Powers.

text: The French concern with the Near East was parallel to, but weaker than, that of Britain.
text_raw:
The  French  concern  with  the  Near  East  was  parallel  to,  but  weaker  than,  that  of
Britain.

text: They had cultural and trade relations with the Levant going back, in some cases, to the Crusades.
text_raw:
They  had  cultural  and  trade  relations  with  the  Levant  going  back,  in  some  cases,
to  the  Crusades.

text: In addition the French had ancient claims, revived in 1854, to he considered the protectors of Roman Catholics in the Ottoman Empire and of the "holy places" in Jerusalem.
text_raw:
In  addition  the  French  had  ancient  claims,  revived  in  1854,  to  he
considered  the  protectors  of  Roman  Catholics  in  the  Ottoman  Empire  and  of  the  "holy
places"  in  Jerusalem.

text: Three other influences which became increasingly strong in the Near East were the growth of nationalism and the growing interests of Austria (after 1866) and of Germany (after 1889).
text_raw:
Three  other  influences  which  became  increasingly  strong  in  the  Near  East  were  the
growth  of  nationalism  and  the  growing  interests  of  Austria  (after  1866)  and  of  Germany

text: The first stirrings of Balkan nationalism can be seen in the revolt of the Serbs in 1804-1812.
text_raw:
The  first  stirrings  of  Balkan  nationalism  can  be  seen  in  the  revolt  of  the
Serbs  in  1804-1812.

text: By seizing Bessarabia from Turkey in 1812, Russia won the right for local self-government for the Serbs.
text_raw:
By  seizing  Bessarabia  from  Turkey  in  1812,  Russia  won  the  right  for
local  self-government  for  the  Serbs.

text: Unfortunately, these latter began almost immediately to fight one another, the chief split being between a Russophile group led by Milan Obrenovich and a Serb nationalist group led by George Petroviae (better known as Karageorge).
text_raw:
Unfortunately,  these  latter  began  almost  immediately
to  fight  one  another,  the  chief  split  being  between  a  Russophile  group  led  by  Milan
Obrenovich  and  a  Serb  nationalist  group  led  by  George  Petroviae  (better  known  as

text: The Serb state, formally established in 1830, was bounded by the rivers Dvina, Save, Danube, and Timok.
text_raw:
The  Serb  state,  formally  established  in  1830,  was  bounded  by  the  rivers
Dvina,  Save,  Danube,  and  Timok.

text: With local autonomy under Turkish suzerainty, it continued to pay tribute to the sultan and to support garrisons of Turkish troops.
text_raw:
With  local  autonomy  under  Turkish  suzerainty,  it
continued  to  pay  tribute  to  the  sultan  and  to  support  garrisons  of  Turkish  troops.

text: The vicious feud between Obrenovich and Karageorgevic continued after Serbia obtained complete independence in 1878.
text_raw:
The
vicious  feud  between  Obrenovich  and  Karageorgevic  continued  after  Serbia  obtained
complete  independence  in  1878.

text: The Obrenovich dynasty ruled in 1817-1842 and 1858- 1903, while the Karageorgevic group ruled in 1842-1858 and 1903-1945.
text_raw:
The  Obrenovich  dynasty  ruled  in  1817-1842  and  1858-
1903,  while  the  Karageorgevic  group  ruled  in  1842-1858  and  1903-1945.

text_raw: The  intrigues  of

text: these two against each other broadened into a constitutional conflict in which the Obrenovich group supported the somewhat less liberal constitution of 1869, while the Karageorgevic group supported the somewhat more liberal constitution of 1889.

these  two  against  each  other  broadened  into  a  constitutional  conflict  in  which  the
Obrenovich  group  supported  the  somewhat  less  liberal  constitution  of  1869,  while  the

The
former  constitution  was  in  effect  in  1869  1889  and  again  in  1894-1903,  while  the  latter

text: In order to win popular support by an appeal to nationalist sentiments, both groups plotted against Turkey and later against Austria-Hungary.
text_raw:
In  order  to  win  popular  support  by  an
appeal  to  nationalist  sentiments,  both  groups  plotted  against  Turkey  and  later  against
Austria-Hungary.

text: A second example of Balkan nationalism appeared in the Greek struggle for independence from the sultan (1821-1830).
text_raw:
A  second  example  of  Balkan  nationalism  appeared  in  the  Greek  struggle  for
independence  from  the  sultan  (1821-1830).

text: After Greeks and Muslims had massacred each other by the thousands, Greek independence was established with a constitutional monarchy under the guarantee of the three Great Powers.
text_raw:
After  Greeks  and  Muslims  had  massacred
each  other  by  the  thousands,  Greek  independence  was  established  with  a  constitutional
monarchy  under  the  guarantee  of  the  three  Great  Powers.

text: A Bavarian prince was placed on the throne and began to establish a centralized, bureaucratic, constitutional state which was quite unsuited for a country with such unconstitutional traditions, poor transportation and communications, a low level of literacy, and a high level of partisan localism.
text_raw:
A  Bavarian  prince  was  placed
on  the  throne  and  began  to  establish  a  centralized,  bureaucratic,  constitutional  state  which
was  quite  unsuited  for  a  country  with  such  unconstitutional  traditions,  poor  transportation
and  communications,  a  low  level  of  literacy,  and  a  high  level  of  partisan  localism.

text: After thirty turbulent years (1832-1862), Otto of Bavaria was deposed and replaced by a Danish prince and a completely democratic unicameral government which functioned only slightly better.
text_raw:
After
thirty  turbulent  years  (1832-1862),  Otto  of  Bavaria  was  deposed  and  replaced  by  a
Danish  prince  and  a  completely  democratic  unicameral  government  which  functioned
only  slightly  better.

text: The Danish dynasty continues to rule, although supplanted by a republic in 1924-1935 and by military dictatorships on sundry occasions, notably that of Joannes Metaxas (1936-1941).
text_raw:
The  Danish  dynasty  continues  to  rule,  although  supplanted  by  a
republic  in  1924-1935  and  by  military  dictatorships  on  sundry  occasions,  notably  that  of
Joannes  Metaxas  (1936-1941).

text: The first beginnings of Balkan nationalism must not be overemphasized.
text_raw: The  first  beginnings  of  Balkan  nationalism  must  not  be  overemphasized.

text: While the inhabitants of the area have always been unfriendly to outsiders and resentful of burdensome governments, these sentiments deserve to be regarded as provincialism or localism rather than nationalism.
text_raw:
While  the
inhabitants  of  the  area  have  always  been  unfriendly  to  outsiders  and  resentful  of
burdensome  governments,  these  sentiments  deserve  to  be  regarded  as  provincialism  or
localism  rather  than  nationalism.

text: Such feelings are prevalent among all primitive peoples and must not be regarded as nationalism unless they are so wide as to embrace loyalty to all peoples of the same language and culture and are organized in such fashion that this loyalty is directed toward the state as the core of nationalist strivings.
text_raw:
Such  feelings  are  prevalent  among  all  primitive  peoples
and  must  not  be  regarded  as  nationalism  unless  they  are  so  wide  as  to  embrace  loyalty  to
all  peoples  of  the  same  language  and  culture  and  are  organized  in  such  fashion  that  this
loyalty  is  directed  toward  the  state  as  the  core  of  nationalist  strivings.

text: Understood in this way, nationalism became a very potent factor in the disruption of the Ottoman Empire only after 1878.
text_raw:
Understood  in  this
way,  nationalism  became  a  very  potent  factor  in  the  disruption  of  the  Ottoman  Empire
only  after  1878.

text: Closely related to the beginnings of Balkan nationalism were the beginnings of Pan- Slavism and the various "pan-movements" in reaction to this, such as Pan-Islamism.
text_raw:
Closely  related  to  the  beginnings  of  Balkan  nationalism  were  the  beginnings  of  Pan-
Slavism  and  the  various  "pan-movements"  in  reaction  to  this,  such  as  Pan-Islamism.

text: These rose to a significant level only at the very end of the nineteenth century.
text_raw: These  rose  to  a  significant  level  only  at  the  very  end  of  the  nineteenth  century.

text: Simply defined, Pan-Slavism was a movement for cultural unity, and, perhaps in the long run, political unity among the Slavs. In practice it came to mean the right of Russia to assume the role of protector of the Slav peoples outside Russia itself.
text_raw:
Simply
defined,  Pan-Slavism  was  a  movement  for  cultural  unity,  and,  perhaps  in  the  long  run,
political  unity  among  the  Slavs.  In  practice  it  came  to  mean  the  right  of  Russia  to  assume
the  role  of  protector  of  the  Slav  peoples  outside  Russia  itself.

text: At times it was difficult for some peoples, especially Russia's enemies, to distinguish between Pan-Slavism and Russian imperialism.
text_raw:
At  times  it  was  difficult  for
some  peoples,  especially  Russia's  enemies,  to  distinguish  between  Pan-Slavism  and
Russian  imperialism.

text: Equally simply defined, Pan-Islamism was a movement for unity or at least cooperation among all the Muslim peoples in order to resist the encroachments of the European Powers on Muslim territories.
text_raw:
Equally  simply  defined,  Pan-Islamism  was  a  movement  for  unity  or
at  least  cooperation  among  all  the  Muslim  peoples  in  order  to  resist  the  encroachments  of
the  European  Powers  on  Muslim  territories.

text: In concrete terms it sought to give the caliph a religious leadership, and perhaps in time a political leadership such as he had really never previously possessed.
text_raw:
In  concrete  terms  it  sought  to  give  the  caliph
a  religious  leadership,  and  perhaps  in  time  a  political  leadership  such  as  he  had  really
never  previously  possessed.

text: Both of these pan-movements are of no importance until the end of the nineteenth century, while Balkan nationalism was only slightly earlier than they in its rise to importance.
text_raw:
Both  of  these  pan-movements  are  of  no  importance  until  the
end  of  the  nineteenth  century,  while  Balkan  nationalism  was  only  slightly  earlier  than
they  in  its  rise  to  importance.

text: These Balkan nationalists had romantic dreams about uniting peoples of the same language, and generally looked back, with a distorted historical perspective, to some period when their co-linguists had played a more important political role.
text_raw:
These  Balkan  nationalists  had  romantic  dreams  about  uniting  peoples  of  the  same
language,  and  generally  looked  back,  with  a  distorted  historical  perspective,  to  some
period  when  their  co-linguists  had  played  a  more  important  political  role.

text: The Greeks dreamed of a revived Byzantine state or even of a Periclean Athenian Empire.
text_raw:
The  Greeks
dreamed  of  a  revived  Byzantine  state  or  even  of  a  Periclean  Athenian  Empire.

text: The Serbs dreamed of the days of Stephen Dushan, while the Bulgars went further back to the days of the Bulgarian Empire of Symeon in the early tenth century.
text_raw:
The  Serbs
dreamed  of  the  days  of  Stephen  Dushan,  while  the  Bulgars  went  further  back  to  the  days

The  first  intervention  led  to  the  Crimean  War  (1854-1856)  and  the  Congress  of

text: In 1853 the czar, as protector of the Orthodox Christians of the Ottoman Empire, occupied the principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia north of the Danube and east of the Carpathians.

In  1853  the  czar,  as  protector  of  the  Orthodox  Christians  of  the  Ottoman  Empire,

text: Under British pressure the sultan declared war on Russia, and was supported by Britain, France, and Sardinia in the ensuing "Crimean War." Under threat of joining the anti-Russian forces, Austria forced the czar to evacuate the principalities and occupied them herself, thus exposing an Austro-Russian rivalry in the Balkans which continued for two generations and ultimately precipitated the World War of 1914-1918.
text_raw:
Under  British  pressure  the  sultan  declared  war  on  Russia,  and  was

text: The Congress of Paris of 1856 sought to remove all possibility of any future Russian intervention in Turkish affairs.
text_raw:
The  Congress  of  Paris  of  1856  sought  to  remove  all  possibility  of  any  future  Russian
intervention  in  Turkish  affairs.

text: The integrity of Turkey was guaranteed, Russia gave up its claim as protector of the sultan's Christian subjects, the Black Sea was "neutralized" by prohibiting all naval vessels and naval arsenals on its waters and shores, an International Commission was set up to assure free navigation of the Danube, and in 1862, after several years of indecision, the two principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia, along with Bessarabia, were allowed to form the state of Romania.
text_raw:
The  integrity  of  Turkey  was  guaranteed,  Russia  gave  up
its  claim  as  protector  of  the  sultan's  Christian  subjects,  the  Black  Sea  was  "neutralized"
by  prohibiting  all  naval  vessels  and  naval  arsenals  on  its  waters  and  shores,  an
International  Commission  was  set  up  to  assure  free  navigation  of  the  Danube,  and  in
1862,  after  several  years  of  indecision,  the  two  principalities  of  Moldavia  and  Wallachia,
along  with  Bessarabia,  were  allowed  to  form  the  state  of  Romania.

text: The new state remained technically under Turkish suzerainty until 1878.
text_raw:
The  new  state
remained  technically  under  Turkish  suzerainty  until  1878.

text: It was the most progressive of the successor states of the Ottoman Empire, with advanced educational and judicial systems based on those of Napoleonic France, and a thorough-going agrarian reform.
text_raw:
It  was  the  most  progressive  of
the  successor  states  of  the  Ottoman  Empire,  with  advanced  educational  and  judicial
systems  based  on  those  of  Napoleonic  France,  and  a  thorough-going  agrarian  reform.

text: This last, which was executed in two stages (1863-1866 and 1918-1921), divided up the great estates of the Church and the nobility, and wiped away all vestiges of manorial dues or serfdom.

This  last,  which  was  executed  in  two  stages  (1863-1866  and  1918-1921),  divided  up  the
great  estates  of  the  Church  and  the  nobility,  and  wiped  away  all  vestiges  of  manorial  dues
or  serfdom.

text: Under a liberal, but not democratic, constitution, a German prince, Charles of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen (1866-1914), established a new dynasty which was ended only in 1948.

Under  a  liberal,  but  not  democratic,  constitution,  a  German  prince,  Charles  of
Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen  (1866-1914),  established  a  new  dynasty  which  was  ended
only  in  1948.

text: During this whole period the cultural and educational systems of the country continued to be orientated toward France in sharp contrast to the inclinations of the ruling dynasty, which had German sympathies.

During  this  whole  period  the  cultural  and  educational  systems  of  the
country  continued  to  be  orientated  toward  France  in  sharp  contrast  to  the  inclinations  of
the  ruling  dynasty,  which  had  German  sympathies.

Bessarabia  and  their  general  pride  in  their  Latin  heritage,  as  reflected  in  the  name  of  the

text: The political and military weakness of the Ottoman Empire in the face of Russian pressure and Balkan nationalisms made it obvious that it must westernize and it must reform, if it was going to survive.
text_raw:
The  political  and  military  weakness  of  the  Ottoman  Empire  in  the  face  of  Russian
pressure  and  Balkan  nationalisms  made  it  obvious  that  it  must  westernize  and  it  must
reform,  if  it  was  going  to  survive.

text: Broad verbal promises in this direction were made by the sultan in the period 1839-1877, and there were even certain efforts to execute these promises.
text_raw:
Broad  verbal  promises  in  this  direction  were  made  by
the  sultan  in  the  period  1839-1877,  and  there  were  even  certain  efforts  to  execute  these
promises.

text: The army was reorganized on a European basis with the assistance of Prussia.
text_raw: The  army  was  reorganized  on  a  European  basis  with  the  assistance  of  Prussia.

text: Local government was reorganized and centralized, and the fiscal system greatly improved, chiefly by curtailing the use of tax farmers; government officials were shifted from a fee-paid basis to a salaried basis; the slave market was abolished, although this meant a large reduction in the sultan's income; the religious monopoly in education was curtailed and a considerable impetus given to secular technical education.
text_raw:
Local  government  was  reorganized  and  centralized,  and  the  fiscal  system  greatly
improved,  chiefly  by  curtailing  the  use  of  tax  farmers;  government  officials  were  shifted
from  a  fee-paid  basis  to  a  salaried  basis;  the  slave  market  was  abolished,  although  this
meant  a  large  reduction  in  the  sultan's  income;  the  religious  monopoly  in  education  was
curtailed  and  a  considerable  impetus  given  to  secular  technical  education.

text: Finally, in 1856, in an edict forced on the sultan by the Great Powers, an effort was made to establish a secular state in Turkey by abolishing all inequalities based on creed in respect to personal freedom, law, property, taxation, and eligibility for office or military service.
text_raw:
Finally,  in
1856,  in  an  edict  forced  on  the  sultan  by  the  Great  Powers,  an  effort  was  made  to
establish  a  secular  state  in  Turkey  by  abolishing  all  inequalities  based  on  creed  in  respect
to  personal  freedom,  law,  property,  taxation,  and  eligibility  for  office  or  military  service.

text: In practice, none of these paper reforms was very effective.
text_raw: In  practice,  none  of  these  paper  reforms  was  very  effective.

text: It was not possible to change the customs of the Turkish people by paper enactments.
text_raw:
It  was  not  possible  to
change  the  customs  of  the  Turkish  people  by  paper  enactments.

text: Indeed, any attempt to do so aroused the anger of many Muslims to the point where their personal conduct toward non-Muslims became worse.
text_raw:
Indeed,  any  attempt  to  do
so  aroused  the  anger  of  many  Muslims  to  the  point  where  their  personal  conduct  toward
non-Muslims  became  worse.

text: At the same time, these promises led the non-Muslims to expect better treatment, so that relations between the various groups were exacerbated.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  these  promises  led  the  non-Muslims  to
expect  better  treatment,  so  that  relations  between  the  various  groups  were  exacerbated.

text: Even if the sultan had had every intention of carrying out his stated reforms, he would have had extraordinary difficulties in doing so because of the structure of Turkish society and the complete lack of trained administrators or even of literate people.
text_raw:
Even  if  the  sultan  had  had  every  intention  of  carrying  out  his  stated  reforms,  he  would
have  had  extraordinary  difficulties  in  doing  so  because  of  the  structure  of  Turkish  society
and  the  complete  lack  of  trained  administrators  or  even  of  literate  people.

text: The Turkish state was a theocratic state, and Turkish society was a patriarchal or even a tribal society.
text_raw:
The  Turkish
state  was  a  theocratic  state,  and  Turkish  society  was  a  patriarchal  or  even  a  tribal  society.

text: Any movement toward secularization or toward social equality could easily result, not in reform, but in complete destruction of the society by dissolving the religious and authoritarian relationships which held both the state and society together.
text_raw:
Any  movement  toward  secularization  or  toward  social  equality  could  easily  result,  not  in
reform,  but  in  complete  destruction  of  the  society  by  dissolving  the  religious  and
authoritarian  relationships  which  held  both  the  state  and  society  together.

text: But the movement toward reform lacked the wholehearted support of the sultan; it aroused the opposition of the more conservative, and in some ways more loyal, groups of Muslims; it aroused the opposition of many liberal Turks because it was derived from Western pressure on Turkey; it aroused opposition from many Christian or non-Turkish groups who feared that a successful reform might weaken their chances of breaking up the Ottoman Empire completely; and the efforts at reform, being aimed at the theocratic character of the Turkish state, counteracted the sultan's efforts to make himself the leader of Pan-Islamism and to use his title of caliph to mobilize non-Ottoman Muslims in India, Russia, and the East to support him in his struggles with the European Great Powers.
text_raw:

movement  toward  reform  lacked  the  wholehearted  support  of  the  sultan;  it  aroused  the

pressure  on  Turkey;  it  aroused  opposition  from  many  Christian  or  non-Turkish  groups

text: On the other hand, it was equally clear that Turkey could not meet any European state on a basis of military equality until it was westernized.

On  the  other  hand,  it  was  equally  clear  that  Turkey  could  not  meet  any  European  state
on  a  basis  of  military  equality  until  it  was  westernized.

text: At the same time, the cheap machinery-made industrial products of the Western Powers began to pour into Turkey and to destroy the ability of the handicraft artisans of Turkey to make a living.

At  the  same  time,  the  cheap
machinery-made  industrial  products  of  the  Western  Powers  began  to  pour  into  Turkey
and  to  destroy  the  ability  of  the  handicraft  artisans  of  Turkey  to  make  a  living.

text: This could not be prevented by tariff protection because the sultan was bound by international agreements to keep his customs duties at a low level.

This  could
not  be  prevented  by  tariff  protection  because  the  sultan  was  bound  by  international

text: These began to agitate for industrialism or for railroad construction, for wider opportunities in education, especially technical education, for reforms in the Turkish language, and for new, less formal, kinds of Turkish literature, for honest and impersonal methods of administration in justice and public finance, and for all those things which, by making the Western Powers strong, made them a danger to Turkey.

text: The sultan made feeble efforts to reform in the period 1838-1875, but by the latter date he was completely disillusioned with these efforts, and shifted over to a policy of ruthless censorship and repression; this repression led, at last, to the so-called "Young Turk" rebellion of 1908.
text_raw:
The  sultan  made  feeble  efforts  to  reform  in  the  period  1838-1875,  but  by  the  latter
date  he  was  completely  disillusioned  with  these  efforts,  and  shifted  over  to  a  policy  of
ruthless  censorship  and  repression;  this  repression  led,  at  last,  to  the  so-called  "Young
