text: The shift from feeble reform to merciless repression coincided with a renewal of the Russian attacks on Turkey.
text_raw:
The  shift  from  feeble  reform  to  merciless  repression  coincided  with  a  renewal  of  the
Russian  attacks  on  Turkey.

text: These attacks were incited by Turkish butchery of Bulgarian agitators in Macedonia and a successful Turkish war on Serbia.
text_raw:
These  attacks  were  incited  by  Turkish  butchery  of  Bulgarian
agitators  in  Macedonia  and  a  successful  Turkish  war  on  Serbia.

text: Appealing to the doctrine of Pan-Slavism, Russia came to the rescue of the Bulgars and Serbs, and quickly defeated the Turks, forcing them to accept the Treaty of San Stefano before any of the Western Powers could intervene (1877).
text_raw:
Appealing  to  the  doctrine
of  Pan-Slavism,  Russia  came  to  the  rescue  of  the  Bulgars  and  Serbs,  and  quickly  defeated
the  Turks,  forcing  them  to  accept  the  Treaty  of  San  Stefano  before  any  of  the  Western
Powers  could  intervene  (1877).

text: Among other provisions, this treaty set up a large state of Bulgaria, including much of Macedonia, independent of Turkey and under Russian military occupation.
text_raw:
Among  other  provisions,  this  treaty  set  up  a  large  state  of
Bulgaria,  including  much  of  Macedonia,  independent  of  Turkey  and  under  Russian
military  occupation.

text: This Treaty of San Stefano, especially the provision for a large Bulgarian state, which, it was feared, would be nothing more than a Russian tool, was completely unacceptable to England and Austria.
text_raw:
This  Treaty  of  San  Stefano,  especially  the  provision  for  a  large  Bulgarian  state,  which,
it  was  feared,  would  be  nothing  more  than  a  Russian  tool,  was  completely  unacceptable
to  England  and  Austria.

text: Joining with France, Germany, and Italy, they forced Russia to come to a conference at Berlin where the treaty was completely rewritten (1878).
text_raw:
Joining  with  France,  Germany,  and  Italy,  they  forced  Russia  to
come  to  a  conference  at  Berlin  where  the  treaty  was  completely  rewritten  (1878).

independence  of  Serbia,  Montenegro,  and  Romania  was  accepted,  as  were  the  Russian

Only  Germany  asked  for  nothing,  and  received  the  sultan's  thanks  and

text: The Treaty of Berlin of 1878 was a disaster from almost every point of view because it left every state, except Austria, with its appetite whetted and its hunger unsatisfied.

text: This declaration was revolutionary because, for the first time, it specifically enunciated British hopes for India's future and because it used, for the first time, the words "responsible government." The British had spoken vaguely for over a century about "self-government" for India; they had spoken increasingly about "representative government"; but they had consistently avoided the expression "responsible government." Pershing insisted on the necessity to keep large numbers of horses behind the lines, waiting for the "breakthrough" which was to be obtained by bayonet charge.

Although  transport  across  the  Atlantic  was  critically  short  throughout  the

text: Time for training recruits was also a critical bottleneck, but most armies spent more time on bayonet practice than on anything else.

Time  for  training  recruits  was

hardly  appear  in  the  statistics  dealing  with  the  subject.

text: The belief of military men that an assault made with high morale could roll through wire, machine guns, and trenches was made even more unrealistic by their insistence that such an offensive unit maintain a straight front.

The  belief  of  military  men  that  an  assault  made  with  high  morale  could  roll  through
wire,  machine  guns,  and  trenches  was  made  even  more  unrealistic  by  their  insistence  that
such  an  offensive  unit  maintain  a  straight  front.

text: This meant that it was not to be permitted to move further in a soft spot, but was to hold back where advance was easy in order to break down the defensive strong points so that the whole front could precede at approximately the same rate.

This  meant  that  it  was  not  to  be  permitted
to  move  further  in  a  soft  spot,  but  was  to  hold  back  where  advance  was  easy  in  order  to
break  down  the  defensive  strong  points  so  that  the  whole  front  could  precede  at

This  was  done,  they  explained,  in  order  to  avoid  exposed
flanks  and  enemy  cross  fire  on  advanced  salients.

There  was  some  opposition  to  these  unrealistic  theories,  especially  in  the  German

text: At the outbreak of war in August 1914, both sides began to put into effect their complicated strategic plans made much earlier.
text_raw:
At  the  outbreak  of  war  in  August  1914,  both  sides  began  to  put  into  effect  their
complicated  strategic  plans  made  much  earlier.

text: On the German side this plan, known as the Schlieffen Plan, was drawn up in 1905 and modified by the younger Helmuth von Moltke (nephew of the Moltke of 1870) after 1906.
text_raw:
On  the  German  side  this  plan,  known  as
the  Schlieffen  Plan,  was  drawn  up  in  1905  and  modified  by  the  younger  Helmuth  von
Moltke  (nephew  of  the  Moltke  of  1870)  after  1906.

text: On the French side the plan was known as Plan XVII, and was drawn up by Joffre in 1912.
text_raw:
On  the  French  side  the  plan  was
known  as  Plan  XVII,  and  was  drawn  up  by  Joffre  in  1912.

text: The original Schlieffen Plan proposed to hold the Russians, as best as could be done, with ten divisions, and to face France with a stationary left wing of eight divisions and a great wheeling right and center of fifty-three divisions going through Holland and Belgium and coming down on the flank and rear of the French armies by passing west of Paris.
text_raw:
The  original  Schlieffen  Plan  proposed  to  hold  the  Russians,  as  best  as  could  be  done,
with  ten  divisions,  and  to  face  France  with  a  stationary  left  wing  of  eight  divisions  and  a
great  wheeling  right  and  center  of  fifty-three  divisions  going  through  Holland  and
Belgium  and  coming  down  on  the  flank  and  rear  of  the  French  armies  by  passing  west  of
Paris.

text: Moltke modified this by adding two divisions to the right wing (one from the Russian front and one new) and eight new divisions to the left.
text_raw:
Moltke  modified  this  by  adding  two  divisions  to  the  right  wing  (one  from  the
Russian  front  and  one  new)  and  eight  new  divisions  to  the  left.

text: He also cut out the passage through Holland, making it necessary for his right wing to pass through the Liege gap, between the Maastricht appendix of Holland and the forested terrain of the Ardennes.
text_raw:
He  also  cut  out  the
passage  through  Holland,  making  it  necessary  for  his  right  wing  to  pass  through  the  Liege
gap,  between  the  Maastricht  appendix  of  Holland  and  the  forested  terrain  of  the
Ardennes.

text: The French Plan XVII proposed to stop an anticipated German attack into eastern France from Lorraine by an assault of two enlarged French armies on its center, thus driving victoriously into southern Germany whose Catholic and separatist peoples were not expected to rally with much enthusiasm to the Protestant, centralist cause of a Prussianized German Empire.
text_raw:
The  French  Plan  XVII  proposed  to  stop  an  anticipated  German  attack  into  eastern
France  from  Lorraine  by  an  assault  of  two  enlarged  French  armies  on  its  center,  thus
driving  victoriously  into  southern  Germany  whose  Catholic  and  separatist  peoples  were
not  expected  to  rally  with  much  enthusiasm  to  the  Protestant,  centralist  cause  of  a
Prussianized  German  Empire.

text: While this was taking place, a force of 800,000 Russians was to invade East Prussia, and 150,000 British were to bolster the French left wing near Belgium.
text_raw:
While  this  was  taking  place,  a  force  of  800,000  Russians
was  to  invade  East  Prussia,  and  150,000  British  were  to  bolster  the  French  left  wing  near
Belgium.

text: The execution of these plans did not completely fulfill the expectations of their supporters.
text_raw:
The  execution  of  these  plans  did  not  completely  fulfill  the  expectations  of  their
supporters.

text: The French moved 3,781,000 men in 7,000 trains in 16 days (August 2-18), opening their attack on Lorraine on 29 August 14th.
text_raw:
The  French  moved  3,781,000  men  in  7,000  trains  in  16  days  (August  2-18),
opening  their  attack  on  Lorraine  on  29  August  14th.

text: By August 20th they were shattered, and by August 25th, after eleven days of combat, had suffered 300,000 casualties.
text_raw:
By  August  20th  they  were  shattered,
and  by  August  25th,  after  eleven  days  of  combat,  had  suffered  300,000  casualties.

text: This was almost 25 percent of the number of men engaged, and represented the most rapid wastage of the war.
text_raw:
This
was  almost  25  percent  of  the  number  of  men  engaged,  and  represented  the  most  rapid
wastage  of  the  war.

text: In the meantime the Germans in 7 days (August 6-12) transported 1,500,000 men across the Rhine at the rate of 550 trains a day.
text_raw:
In  the  meantime  the  Germans  in  7  days  (August  6-12)  transported  1,500,000  men
across  the  Rhine  at  the  rate  of  550  trains  a  day.

text: These men formed 70 divisions divided into 7 armies and forming a vast arc from northwest to southeast.
text_raw:
These  men  formed  70  divisions  divided
into  7  armies  and  forming  a  vast  arc  from  northwest  to  southeast.

text: When the German plan became clear on August 18th, Joffre formed a new Sixth Army, largely from garrison troops, under Michel-Ioseph Maunoury but really commanded by loseph Gallieni, Minitary Governor of Paris.
text_raw:
When  the  German  plan  became  clear  on  August  18th,  Joffre  formed  a
new  Sixth  Army,  largely  from  garrison  troops,  under  Michel-Ioseph  Maunoury  but  really

text: By August 22nd the whole French line west of Verdun was in retreat.
text_raw:
By  August  22nd  the  whole
French  line  west  of  Verdun  was  in  retreat.

text: Three days later, Moltke, believing victory secure, sent two army corps to Russia from the Second and Third armies.
text_raw:
Three  days  later,  Moltke,  believing  victory
secure,  sent  two  army  corps  to  Russia  from  the  Second  and  Third  armies.

text: These arrived on the Eastern Front only after the Russian advance into Prussia had been smashed at Tannenberg and around the Masurian Lakes (August 26th-September Isth).
text_raw:
These  arrived
on  the  Eastern  Front  only  after  the  Russian  advance  into  Prussia  had  been  smashed  at
Tannenberg  and  around  the  Masurian  Lakes  (August  26th-September  Isth).

text: In the meantime in the west, Schlieffen's project swept onward toward fiasco.
text_raw:
In  the
meantime  in  the  west,  Schlieffen's  project  swept  onward  toward  fiasco.

text: When Lanrezac slowed up Billow's advance on August 28th, Kluck, who was already a day's march ahead of Biilow, tried to close the gap between the two by turning southeastward.
text_raw:
When  Lanrezac
slowed  up  Billow's  advance  on  August  28th,  Kluck,  who  was  already  a  day's  march  ahead
of  Biilow,  tried  to  close  the  gap  between  the  two  by  turning  southeastward.

text: This brought his line of advance east of Paris rather than est of that city as originally planned.
text_raw:
This  brought
his  line  of  advance  east  of  Paris  rather  than  est  of  that  city  as  originally  planned.

text: Gallieni, bringing the Sixth Army from Paris in any vehicles he could commandeer, threw it at Kluck's exposed right flank.
text_raw:
Gallieni,
bringing  the  Sixth  Army  from  Paris  in  any  vehicles  he  could  commandeer,  threw  it  at
Kluck's  exposed  right  flank.

text: Kluck turned again to face Gallieni, moving northwestward
text_raw: Kluck  turned  again  to  face  Gallieni,  moving  northwestward

text: in a brilliant maneuver in order to envelop him within the German arc before resuming his advance southeastward.
text_raw:
in  a  brilliant  maneuver  in  order  to  envelop  him  within  the  German  arc  before  resuming
his  advance  southeastward.

text: This operation was accompanied hy considerable success except that it opened a gap thirty miles wide between Kluck and Biilow.
text_raw:
This  operation  was  accompanied  hy  considerable  success
except  that  it  opened  a  gap  thirty  miles  wide  between  Kluck  and  Biilow.

text: Opposite this gap was the B.E.F., which was withdrawing southward with even greater speed than the French.
text_raw:
Opposite  this
gap  was  the  B.E.F.,  which  was  withdrawing  southward  with  even  greater  speed  than  the
French.

text: On September 5th the French retreat stopped; on the following day they began a general counterattack, ordered by Joffre on the insistence of Gallieni.
text_raw:
On  September  5th  the  French  retreat  stopped;  on  the  following  day  they  began  a
general  counterattack,  ordered  by  Joffre  on  the  insistence  of  Gallieni.

text: Thus began the First Battle of the Marne.
text_raw:
Thus  began  the
First  Battle  of  the  Marne.

text: Kluck was meeting with considerable success over the Sixth French Army, although Biilow was being badly mauled by Lanrezac, when the B.E.F. began to move into the gap between the First and Second German armies (September 8th).
text_raw:
Kluck  was  meeting  with  considerable  success  over  the  Sixth  French  Army,  although
Biilow  was  being  badly  mauled  by  Lanrezac,  when  the  B.E.F.  began  to  move  into  the  gap
between  the  First  and  Second  German  armies  (September  8th).

text: A German staff officer, Lieutenant-Colonel Hentsch, ordered the whole German right to fall back to the Aisne River where a front was formed on September 13th by the arrival of some of the German forces which had been attacking the Belgian forts.
text_raw:
A  German  staff  officer,
Lieutenant-Colonel  Hentsch,  ordered  the  whole  German  right  to  fall  back  to  the  Aisne
River  where  a  front  was  formed  on  September  13th  by  the  arrival  of  some  of  the  German
forces  which  had  been  attacking  the  Belgian  forts.

text: The Germans were willing to fall back to the Aisne because they believed the advance could be resumed when they wished to do so.
text_raw:
The  Germans  were  willing  to  fall  back
to  the  Aisne  because  they  believed  the  advance  could  be  resumed  when  they  wished  to  do
so.

text: In the next few months the Germans tried to resume their advance, and the French tried to dislodge the Germans from their positions.
text_raw:
In  the  next  few  months  the  Germans  tried  to  resume  their  advance,  and  the  French
tried  to  dislodge  the  Germans  from  their  positions.

text: Neither was able to make any headway against the firepower of the other.
text_raw:
Neither  was  able  to  make  any
headway  against  the  firepower  of  the  other.

text: A succession of futile efforts to outflank each other's positions merely succeeded in bringing the ends of the front to the English Channel on one extreme and to Switzerland on the other.
text_raw:
A  succession  of  futile  efforts  to  outflank  each
other's  positions  merely  succeeded  in  bringing  the  ends  of  the  front  to  the  English
Channel  on  one  extreme  and  to  Switzerland  on  the  other.

text: In spite of millions of casualties, this line, from the sea to the mountains across the fair face of France, remained almost unchanged for over three years.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  millions  of
casualties,  this  line,  from  the  sea  to  the  mountains  across  the  fair  face  of  France,  remained
almost  unchanged  for  over  three  years.

text: During these terrible years, the dream of military men was to break through the enemy line by infantry assault, then roll up his flanks and disrupt his rearward communications by pouring cavalry and other reserves through the gap.
text_raw:
During  these  terrible  years,  the  dream  of  military  men  was  to  break  through  the  enemy
line  by  infantry  assault,  then  roll  up  his  flanks  and  disrupt  his  rearward  communications
by  pouring  cavalry  and  other  reserves  through  the  gap.

text: This was never achieved.
text_raw: This  was  never  achieved.

text: The effort to attain it led to one experiment after another.
text_raw:
The
effort  to  attain  it  led  to  one  experiment  after  another.

text: In order these were:
text_raw: In  order  these  were:

text: (1) bayonet assault, (2) preliminary artillery barrage, (3) use of poison gas, (4) use of the tank, (5) use of infiltration.
text_raw:
(1)  bayonet
assault,  (2)  preliminary  artillery  barrage,  (3)  use  of  poison  gas,  (4)  use  of  the  tank,  (5)  use
of  infiltration.

text: The last four of these innovations were devised alternately by the Allies and by the Central Powers.
text_raw:
The  last  four  of  these  innovations  were  devised  alternately  by  the  Allies
and  by  the  Central  Powers.

text: Bayonet assault was a failure by the end of 1914.
text_raw: Bayonet  assault  was  a  failure  by  the  end  of  1914.

text: It merely created mountains of dead and wounded without any real advance, although some officers continued to believe that an assault would be successful if the morale of the attackers could be brought to a sufficiently high pitch to overcome machine-gun fire.
text_raw:
It  merely  created  mountains  of  dead
and  wounded  without  any  real  advance,  although  some  officers  continued  to  believe  that
an  assault  would  be  successful  if  the  morale  of  the  attackers  could  be  brought  to  a
sufficiently  high  pitch  to  overcome  machine-gun  fire.

text: An artillery barrage as a necessary preliminary to infantry assault was used almost from the beginning.
text_raw:
An  artillery  barrage  as  a  necessary  preliminary  to  infantry  assault  was  used  almost
from  the  beginning.

text: It was ineffectual.
text_raw: It  was  ineffectual.

text: At first no army had the necessary quantity of munitions.
text_raw:
At  first  no  army  had  the  necessary  quantity  of
munitions.

text: Some armies insisted on ordering shrapnel rather than high-explosive shells for such barrages.
text_raw:
Some  armies  insisted  on  ordering  shrapnel  rather  than  high-explosive  shells
for  such  barrages.

text: This resulted in a violent controversy between Lloyd George and the generals, the former trying to persuade the latter that shrapnel was not effective against defensive forces in ground trenches.
text_raw:
This  resulted  in  a  violent  controversy  between  Lloyd  George  and  the
generals,  the  former  trying  to  persuade  the  latter  that  shrapnel  was  not  effective  against
defensive  forces  in  ground  trenches.

text: In time it should have become clear that high- explosive barrages were not effective either, although they were used in enormous quantities.
text_raw:
In  time  it  should  have  become  clear  that  high-
explosive  barrages  were  not  effective  either,  although  they  were  used  in  enormous
quantities.

text: They failed because:
text_raw: They  failed  because:

text: (1) earth and concrete fortifications provided sufficient protection to the defensive forces to allow them to use their own firepower against the infantry assault which followed the barrage;
(2) a barrage notified the defense where to
text_raw: (2)  a  barrage  notified  the  defense  where  to

text: expect the following infantry assault, so that reserves could be brought up to strengthen that position; and (3) the doctrine of the continuous front made it impossible to penetrate the enemy positions on a wide-enough front to break through.
text_raw:
expect  the  following  infantry  assault,  so  that  reserves  could  be  brought  up  to  strengthen
that  position;  and  (3)  the  doctrine  of  the  continuous  front  made  it  impossible  to  penetrate
the  enemy  positions  on  a  wide-enough  front  to  break  through.

text: The efforts to do so, however, resulted in enormous casualties.

The  efforts  to  do  so,
however,  resulted  in  enormous  casualties.

At  Verdun  in  1916  the  French  lost  350,000  and
the  Germans  300,000.

On  the  Somme
in  the  same  year  the  British  lost  410,000,  the  French  lost  190,000,  and  the  Germans  lost

text_raw: The  following  year  the  slaughter  continued.

At  Chemin  des  Dames  in  April,  1917,
the  French,  under  a  new  commander,  Robert  Nivelle,  fired  11  million  shells  in  a  10-day

The  attack  failed,  suffering  losses  of  1 18,000  men  in  a  brief
period.

text: Many corps mutinied, and large numbers of combatants were shot to enforce discipline.
text_raw:
Many  corps  mutinied,  and  large  numbers  of  combatants  were  shot  to  enforce
discipline.

text: Twenty-three civilian leaders were also executed.
text_raw: Twenty-three  civilian  leaders  were  also  executed.

text: Nivelle was replaced by Petain.

text: Haig obtained permission for his Passchendaele offensive only because General (later Field Marshal and Baronet) William Robertson, Chief of the Imperial General Staff, covered up Haig's falsifications about German reserves and because First Sea Lord Admiral John Jellicoe told the Cabinet that unless Haig could capture the- submarine bases on the Belgian coast (an utterly impossible objective) he considered it "improbable that we could go on with the war next year for lack of shipping." text: Then it was applied with such ruthless efficiency that almost a million tons of shipping was sunk in the month of April 1917, and Britain was driven within three weeks of exhaustion of her food supply.

Then  it  was  applied  with  such  ruthless
efficiency  that  almost  a  million  tons  of  shipping  was  sunk  in  the  month  of  April  1917,
and  Britain  was  driven  within  three  weeks  of  exhaustion  of  her  food  supply.

text: This danger of a British defeat, dressed in the propaganda clothing of moral outrage at the iniquity of submarine attacks, brought the United States into the war on the side of the Entente in that critical month of April, 1917.
text_raw:
This  danger
of  a  British  defeat,  dressed  in  the  propaganda  clothing  of  moral  outrage  at  the  iniquity  of
submarine  attacks,  brought  the  United  States  into  the  war  on  the  side  of  the  Entente  in
that  critical  month  of  April,  1917.

text: In the meantime the Germany policy of military attrition on the Western Front worked well until 1918.
text_raw:
In  the  meantime  the  Germany  policy  of  military
attrition  on  the  Western  Front  worked  well  until  1918.

text: By January of that year Germany had been losing men at about half her rate of replacement and at about half the rate at which she was inflicting losses on the Entente Powers.
text_raw:
By  January  of  that  year  Germany
had  been  losing  men  at  about  half  her  rate  of  replacement  and  at  about  half  the  rate  at
which  she  was  inflicting  losses  on  the  Entente  Powers.

text: Thus the period 1914-1918 saw a race between the economic attrition of Germany by the blockade and the personal attrition of the Entente by military action.
text_raw:
Thus  the  period  1914-1918  saw  a
race  between  the  economic  attrition  of  Germany  by  the  blockade  and  the  personal
attrition  of  the  Entente  by  military  action.

text: This race was never settled on its merits because three new factors entered the picture in 1917.
text_raw:
This  race  was  never  settled  on  its  merits
because  three  new  factors  entered  the  picture  in  1917.

text: These were the German counter- blockade by submarines on Britain, the increase in German manpower in the West resulting from her victory in the East, and the arrival on the Western Front of new American forces.
text_raw:
These  were  the  German  counter-
blockade  by  submarines  on  Britain,  the  increase  in  German  manpower  in  the  West
resulting  from  her  victory  in  the  East,  and  the  arrival  on  the  Western  Front  of  new
American  forces.

text: The first two of these factors were overbalanced in the period March- September, 1918, by the third.
text_raw:
The  first  two  of  these  factors  were  overbalanced  in  the  period  March-
September,  1918,  by  the  third.

text: By August of 1918 Germany had given her best, and it had not been adequate.
text_raw:
By  August  of  1918  Germany  had  given  her  best,  and  it  had
not  been  adequate.

text: The blockade and the rising tide of American manpower gave the German leaders the choice of surrender or complete economic and social upheaval.
text_raw:
The  blockade  and  the  rising  tide  of  American  manpower  gave  the
German  leaders  the  choice  of  surrender  or  complete  economic  and  social  upheaval.

text: Without exception, led by the Junker military commanders, they chose surrender.
text_raw: Without  exception,  led  by  the  Junker  military  commanders,  they  chose  surrender.

text: The beginnings of military action in August 1914 did not mark the end of diplomatic action, even between the chief opponents.
text_raw:
The  beginnings  of  military  action  in  August  1914  did  not  mark  the  end  of  diplomatic
action,  even  between  the  chief  opponents.

text: Diplomatic activity continued, and was aimed, very largely, at two goals:
text_raw:
Diplomatic  activity  continued,  and  was  aimed,
very  largely,  at  two  goals:

text: (a) to bring new countries into the military activities or, on the contrary, to keep them out, and (b) to attempt to make peace by negotiations.
text_raw:
(a)  to  bring  new  countries  into  the  military  activities  or,  on  the
contrary,  to  keep  them  out,  and  (b)  to  attempt  to  make  peace  by  negotiations.

text: Closely related to the first of these aims were negotiations concerned with the disposition of enemy territories after the fighting ceased.
text_raw:
Closely
related  to  the  first  of  these  aims  were  negotiations  concerned  with  the  disposition  of
enemy  territories  after  the  fighting  ceased.

text: Back of all the diplomatic activities of the period 1914-1918 was a fact which impressed itself on the belligerents relatively slowly.
text_raw:
Back  of  all  the  diplomatic  activities  of  the  period  1914-1918  was  a  fact  which
impressed  itself  on  the  belligerents  relatively  slowly.

text: This was the changed character of modern warfare.
text_raw:
This  was  the  changed  character  of
modern  warfare.

text: With certain exceptions the wars of the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries had been struggles of limited resources for limited objectives.
text_raw:
With  certain  exceptions  the  wars  of  the  eighteenth  and  early  nineteenth
centuries  had  been  struggles  of  limited  resources  for  limited  objectives.

text: The growth of political democracy, the rise of nationalism, and the industrialization of war led to total war with total mobilization and unlimited objectives.
text_raw:
The  growth  of
political  democracy,  the  rise  of  nationalism,  and  the  industrialization  of  war  led  to  total
war  with  total  mobilization  and  unlimited  objectives.

text: In the eighteenth century, when rulers were relatively free from popular influences, they could wage wars for limited objectives and could negotiate peace on a compromise basis when these were objectives were attained or appeared unattainable.
text_raw:
In  the  eighteenth  century,  when
rulers  were  relatively  free  from  popular  influences,  they  could  wage  wars  for  limited
objectives  and  could  negotiate  peace  on  a  compromise  basis  when  these  were  objectives
were  attained  or  appeared  unattainable.

text: Using a mercenary army which fought for pay, they could put that army into war or out of war, as seemed necessary, without vitally affecting its morale or its fighting qualities.
text_raw:
Using  a  mercenary  army  which  fought  for  pay,
they  could  put  that  army  into  war  or  out  of  war,  as  seemed  necessary,  without  vitally
affecting  its  morale  or  its  fighting  qualities.

text: The arrival of democracy and of the mass army required that the great body of the citizens give wholehearted support for any war effort, and made it impossible to wage wars for limited objectives.
text_raw:
The  arrival  of  democracy  and  of  the  mass
army  required  that  the  great  body  of  the  citizens  give  wholehearted  support  for  any  war
effort,  and  made  it  impossible  to  wage  wars  for  limited  objectives.

text: Such popular support could be won only in behalf of great moral goals or universal philosophic values or, at the very least, for survival.
text_raw:
Such  popular  support
could  be  won  only  in  behalf  of  great  moral  goals  or  universal  philosophic  values  or,  at  the
very  least,  for  survival.

text: At the same time the growing industrialization and economic integration of modern society made it impossible to mobilize for war except on a very extensive basis which approached total mobilization.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time  the  growing  industrialization  and  economic
integration  of  modern  society  made  it  impossible  to  mobilize  for  war  except  on  a  very
extensive  basis  which  approached  total  mobilization.

text: This mobilization could not be directed toward limited objectives.
text_raw:
This  mobilization  could  not  be
directed  toward  limited  objectives.

text: From these factors came total war with total mobilization and unlimited objectives, including the total destruction or unconditional surrender of the enemy.
text_raw:
From  these  factors  came  total  war  with  total
mobilization  and  unlimited  objectives,  including  the  total  destruction  or  unconditional
surrender  of  the  enemy.

text: Having adopted such grandiose goals and such gigantic plans, it became almost impossible to allow the continued existence of noncombatants within the belligerent countries or neutrals outside them.
text_raw:
Having  adopted  such  grandiose  goals  and  such  gigantic  plans,  it
became  almost  impossible  to  allow  the  continued  existence  of  noncombatants  within  the
belligerent  countries  or  neutrals  outside  them.

text: It became almost axiomatic that "who is not with me is against me." At the same time, it became almost impossible to compromise sufficiently to obtain the much more limited goals which would permit a negotiated peace.
text_raw:
It  became  almost  axiomatic  that  "who  is
not  with  me  is  against  me."  At  the  same  time,  it  became  almost  impossible  to
compromise  sufficiently  to  obtain  the  much  more  limited  goals  which  would  permit  a
negotiated  peace.

text: As Charles Seymour put it:
text_raw: As  Charles  Seymour  put  it:

text: "Each side had promised itself a peace of victory.
text_raw:
"Each  side  had  promised  itself  a  peace  of
victory.

text: The very phrase 'negotiated peace' became synonymous with treachery." Moreover, the popular basis of modern war required a high morale which might easily be lowered if the news leaked out that the government was negotiating peace in the middle of the fighting.
text_raw:
The  very  phrase  'negotiated  peace'  became  synonymous  with  treachery."
Moreover,  the  popular  basis  of  modern  war  required  a  high  morale  which  might  easily  be
lowered  if  the  news  leaked  out  that  the  government  was  negotiating  peace  in  the  middle
of  the  fighting.

text: As a consequence of these conditions, efforts to negotiate peace during the First World War were generally very secret and very unsuccessful.
text_raw:
As  a  consequence  of  these  conditions,  efforts  to  negotiate  peace  during
the  First  World  War  were  generally  very  secret  and  very  unsuccessful.

text: The change from limited wars with limited objectives fought with mercenary troops to unlimited wars of economic attrition with unlimited objectives fought with national armies had far-reaching consequences.
text_raw:
The  change  from  limited  wars  with  limited  objectives  fought  with  mercenary  troops  to
unlimited  wars  of  economic  attrition  with  unlimited  objectives  fought  with  national
armies  had  far-reaching  consequences.

text: The distinction between combatants and noncombatants and between belligerents and neutrals became blurred and ultimately undistinguishable.
text_raw:
The  distinction  between  combatants  and
noncombatants  and  between  belligerents  and  neutrals  became  blurred  and  ultimately
undistinguishable.

text: International law, which had grown up in the period of limited dynastic wars, made a great deal of these distinctions.
text_raw:
International  law,  which  had  grown  up  in  the  period  of  limited
dynastic  wars,  made  a  great  deal  of  these  distinctions.

text: Noncombatants had extensive rights which sought to protect their ways of life as much as possible during periods of
text_raw:
Noncombatants  had  extensive
rights  which  sought  to  protect  their  ways  of  life  as  much  as  possible  during  periods  of

text: warfare; neutrals had similar rights.
text_raw: warfare;  neutrals  had  similar  rights.

text: In return, strict duties to remain both noncombatant and neutral rested on these "outsiders." All these distinctions broke down in 1914-1915, with the result that both sides indulged in wholesale violations of existing international law.
text_raw:
In  return,  strict  duties  to  remain  both  noncombatant
and  neutral  rested  on  these  "outsiders."  All  these  distinctions  broke  down  in  1914-1915,
with  the  result  that  both  sides  indulged  in  wholesale  violations  of  existing  international
law.

text: Probably on the whole these violations were more extensive (although less widely publicized) on the part of the Entente than on the part of the Central Powers.
text_raw:
Probably  on  the  whole  these  violations  were  more  extensive  (although  less  widely
publicized)  on  the  part  of  the  Entente  than  on  the  part  of  the  Central  Powers.

text: The reasons for this were that the Germans still maintained the older traditions of a professional army, and their position, both as an invader and as a "Central Power" with limited manpower and economic resources, made it to their advantage to maintain the distinctions between combatant and noncombatant and between belligerent and neutral.
text_raw:
The  reasons
for  this  were  that  the  Germans  still  maintained  the  older  traditions  of  a  professional  army,
and  their  position,  both  as  an  invader  and  as  a  "Central  Power"  with  limited  manpower
and  economic  resources,  made  it  to  their  advantage  to  maintain  the  distinctions  between
combatant  and  noncombatant  and  between  belligerent  and  neutral.

text: If they could have maintained the former distinction, they would have had to fight the enemy army and not the enemy civilian population, and, once the former was defeated, would have had little to fear from the latter, which could have been controlled by a minimum of troops.
text_raw:
If  they  could  have
maintained  the  former  distinction,  they  would  have  had  to  fight  the  enemy  army  and  not
the  enemy  civilian  population,  and,  once  the  former  was  defeated,  would  have  had  little
to  fear  from  the  latter,  which  could  have  been  controlled  by  a  minimum  of  troops.

text: If they could have maintained the distinction between belligerent and neutral, it would have been impossible to blockade Germany, since basic supplies could have been imported through neutral countries.
text_raw:
If  they
could  have  maintained  the  distinction  between  belligerent  and  neutral,  it  would  have  been
impossible  to  blockade  Germany,  since  basic  supplies  could  have  been  imported  through
neutral  countries.

text: It was for this reason that Schlieffen's original plans for an attack on France through Holland and Belgium were changed by Moltke to an attack through Belgium alone.
text_raw:
It  was  for  this  reason  that  Schlieffen's  original  plans  for  an  attack  on
France  through  Holland  and  Belgium  were  changed  by  Moltke  to  an  attack  through
Belgium  alone.

text: Neutral Holland was to remain as a channel of supply for civilian goods.
text_raw: Neutral  Holland  was  to  remain  as  a  channel  of  supply  for  civilian  goods.

text: This was possible because international law made a distinction between war goods, which could be declared contraband, and civilian goods (including food), which could not be so declared.
text_raw:
This  was  possible  because  international  law  made  a  distinction  between  war  goods,
which  could  be  declared  contraband,  and  civilian  goods  (including  food),  which  could  not
be  so  declared.

text: Moreover, the German plans, as we have indicated, called for a short, decisive war against the enemy armed forces, and they neither expected nor desired a total economic mobilization or even a total military mobilization, since these might disrupt the existing social and political structure in Germany.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  German  plans,  as  we  have  indicated,  called  for  a  short,
decisive  war  against  the  enemy  armed  forces,  and  they  neither  expected  nor  desired  a
total  economic  mobilization  or  even  a  total  military  mobilization,  since  these  might
disrupt  the  existing  social  and  political  structure  in  Germany.

text: For these reasons, Germany made no plans for industrial or economic mobilization, for a long war, or for withstanding a blockade, and hoped to mobilize a smaller proportion of its manpower than its immediate enemies.
text_raw:
For  these  reasons,  Germany
made  no  plans  for  industrial  or  economic  mobilization,  for  a  long  war,  or  for
withstanding  a  blockade,  and  hoped  to  mobilize  a  smaller  proportion  of  its  manpower
than  its  immediate  enemies.

text: The failure of the Schlieffen plan showed the error of these ideas.
text_raw: The  failure  of  the  Schlieffen  plan  showed  the  error  of  these  ideas.

text: Not only did the prospect of a long war make economic mobilization necessary, but the occupation of Belgium showed that national feeling was tending to make the distinction between combatant and noncombatant academic.
text_raw:
Not  only  did  the
prospect  of  a  long  war  make  economic  mobilization  necessary,  but  the  occupation  of
Belgium  showed  that  national  feeling  was  tending  to  make  the  distinction  between
combatant  and  noncombatant  academic.

text: When Belgian civilians shot at German soldiers, the latter took civilian hostages and practiced reprisals on civilians.
text_raw:
When  Belgian  civilians  shot  at  German  soldiers,
the  latter  took  civilian  hostages  and  practiced  reprisals  on  civilians.

text: These German actions were publicized throughout the world by the British propaganda machine as "atrocities" and violations of international law (which they were), while the Belgian civilian snipers were excused as loyal patriots ( although their actions were even more clearly violations of international law and, as such, justified severe German reactions).
text_raw:
These  German
actions  were  publicized  throughout  the  world  by  the  British  propaganda  machine  as
"atrocities"  and  violations  of  international  law  (which  they  were),  while  the  Belgian
civilian  snipers  were  excused  as  loyal  patriots  (  although  their  actions  were  even  more
clearly  violations  of  international  law  and,  as  such,  justified  severe  German  reactions).

text: These "atrocities" were used by the British to justify their own violations of international law.
text_raw:
These  "atrocities"  were  used  by  the  British  to  justify  their  own  violations  of  international
law.

text: As early as August 20, 1914, they were treating food as contraband and interfering with neutral shipments of food to Europe.
text_raw:
As  early  as  August  20,  1914,  they  were  treating  food  as  contraband  and  interfering
with  neutral  shipments  of  food  to  Europe.

text: On November 5, 1914, they declared the whole sea from Scotland to Iceland a "war zone," covered it with fields of explosive floating mines, and ordered all ships going to the Baltic, Scandinavia, or the Low Countries to go by way of the English Channel, where they were stopped, searched, and much of their cargoes seized, even when these cargoes could not be declared contraband under existing international law.
text_raw:
On  November  5,  1914,  they  declared  the  whole
sea  from  Scotland  to  Iceland  a  "war  zone,"  covered  it  with  fields  of  explosive  floating
mines,  and  ordered  all  ships  going  to  the  Baltic,  Scandinavia,  or  the  Low  Countries  to  go
by  way  of  the  English  Channel,  where  they  were  stopped,  searched,  and  much  of  their
cargoes  seized,  even  when  these  cargoes  could  not  be  declared  contraband  under  existing
international  law.

text: In reprisal the Germans on February 18, 1915 declared the English Channel a "war zone," announced that their submarines would sink shipping in that area, and ordered shipping for the Baltic area to use the route north of Scotland.
text_raw:
In  reprisal  the  Germans  on  February  18,  1915  declared  the  English
Channel  a  "war  zone,"  announced  that  their  submarines  would  sink  shipping  in  that  area,
and  ordered  shipping  for  the  Baltic  area  to  use  the  route  north  of  Scotland.

text: The United
text_raw: The  United

text: States, which rejected a Scandinavian invitation to protest against the British war zone closed with mines north of Scotland, protested violently against the German war zone closed with submarines on the Narrow Seas, although, as one American senator put it, the "humanity of the submarine was certainly on a higher level than that of the floating mine, which could exercise neither discretion nor judgment."
text_raw:
States,  which  rejected  a  Scandinavian  invitation  to  protest  against  the  British  war  zone
closed  with  mines  north  of  Scotland,  protested  violently  against  the  German  war  zone
closed  with  submarines  on  the  Narrow  Seas,  although,  as  one  American  senator  put  it,  the
"humanity  of  the  submarine  was  certainly  on  a  higher  level  than  that  of  the  floating  mine,
which  could  exercise  neither  discretion  nor  judgment."

text: The United States accepted the British "war zone," and prevented its ships from using it.
text_raw:
The  United  States  accepted  the  British  "war  zone,"  and  prevented  its  ships  from  using
it.

text: On the other hand, it refused to accept the German war zone, and insisted that American lives and property were under American protection even when traveling on armed belligerent ships in this war zone.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  it  refused  to  accept  the  German  war  zone,  and  insisted  that
American  lives  and  property  were  under  American  protection  even  when  traveling  on
armed  belligerent  ships  in  this  war  zone.

text: Moreover, the United States insisted that German submarines must obey the laws of the sea as drawn for surface vessels.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  United  States  insisted  that
German  submarines  must  obey  the  laws  of  the  sea  as  drawn  for  surface  vessels.

text: These laws provided that merchant ships could be stopped by a war vessel and inspected, and could be sunk, if carrying contraband, after the passengers and the ships' papers were put in a place of safety.
text_raw:
These
laws  provided  that  merchant  ships  could  be  stopped  by  a  war  vessel  and  inspected,  and
could  be  sunk,  if  carrying  contraband,  after  the  passengers  and  the  ships'  papers  were  put
in  a  place  of  safety.

text: A place of safety was not the ships' boats, except in sight of land or of other vessels in a calm sea.
text_raw:
A  place  of  safety  was  not  the  ships'  boats,  except  in  sight  of  land  or
of  other  vessels  in  a  calm  sea.

text: The merchant vessel so stopped obtained these rights only if it made no act of hostility against the enemy war vessel.
text_raw:
The  merchant  vessel  so  stopped  obtained  these  rights  only
if  it  made  no  act  of  hostility  against  the  enemy  war  vessel.

text: It was not only difficult, or even impossible, for German submarines to meet these conditions; it was often dangerous, since British merchant ships received instructions to attack German submarines at sight, by ramming if possible.
text_raw:
It  was  not  only  difficult,  or
even  impossible,  for  German  submarines  to  meet  these  conditions;  it  was  often
dangerous,  since  British  merchant  ships  received  instructions  to  attack  German
submarines  at  sight,  by  ramming  if  possible.

text: It was even dangerous for the German submarines to apply the established law of neutral vessels; for British vessels, with these aggressive orders, frequently flew neutral flags and posed as neutrals as long as possible.
text_raw:
It  was  even  dangerous  for  the  German
submarines  to  apply  the  established  law  of  neutral  vessels;  for  British  vessels,  with  these
aggressive  orders,  frequently  flew  neutral  flags  and  posed  as  neutrals  as  long  as  possible.

text: Nevertheless, the United States continued to insist that the Germans obey the old laws, while condoning British violations of the same laws to the extent that the distinction between war vessels and merchant ships was blurred.
text_raw:
Nevertheless,  the  United  States  continued  to  insist  that  the  Germans  obey  the  old  laws,
while  condoning  British  violations  of  the  same  laws  to  the  extent  that  the  distinction
between  war  vessels  and  merchant  ships  was  blurred.

text: Accordingly, German submarines began to sink British merchant ships with little or no warning.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  German  submarines
began  to  sink  British  merchant  ships  with  little  or  no  warning.

text: Their attempts to justify this failure to distinguish between combatants and noncombatants on the ground that British floating mines, the British food blockade, and the British instructions to merchant ships to attack submarines made no such distinction were no more successful than their efforts to show that their severity against the civilian population of Belgium was justified by civilian attacks on German troops.
text_raw:
Their  attempts  to  justify
this  failure  to  distinguish  between  combatants  and  noncombatants  on  the  ground  that
British  floating  mines,  the  British  food  blockade,  and  the  British  instructions  to  merchant
ships  to  attack  submarines  made  no  such  distinction  were  no  more  successful  than  their
efforts  to  show  that  their  severity  against  the  civilian  population  of  Belgium  was  justified
by  civilian  attacks  on  German  troops.

text: They were trying to carry on legal distinctions remaining from an earlier period when conditions were entirely different, and their ultimate abandonment of these distinctions on the grounds that their enemies had already abandoned them merely made matters worse, because if neutrals became belligerents and noncombatants became combatants, Germany and her allies would suffer much more than Britain and her friends.
text_raw:
They  were  trying  to  carry  on  legal  distinctions
remaining  from  an  earlier  period  when  conditions  were  entirely  different,  and  their
ultimate  abandonment  of  these  distinctions  on  the  grounds  that  their  enemies  had  already
abandoned  them  merely  made  matters  worse,  because  if  neutrals  became  belligerents  and
noncombatants  became  combatants,  Germany  and  her  allies  would  suffer  much  more
than  Britain  and  her  friends.

text: In the final analysis this is why the distinctions were destroyed; but beneath all legal questions was to be found the ominous fact that war, by becoming total, had made both neutrality and negotiated peace almost impossible.
text_raw:
In  the  final  analysis  this  is  why  the  distinctions  were
destroyed;  but  beneath  all  legal  questions  was  to  be  found  the  ominous  fact  that  war,  by
becoming  total,  had  made  both  neutrality  and  negotiated  peace  almost  impossible.

text: We shall now turn our attention to this struggle over neutrality and the struggle over negotiated peace.
text_raw:
We
shall  now  turn  our  attention  to  this  struggle  over  neutrality  and  the  struggle  over
negotiated  peace.

text: So far as legal or diplomatic commitments went, Germany, in July, 1914, had the right to expect that Austria-Hungary, Italy, Romania, and perhaps Turkey would be at her side and that her opponents would consist of Serbia, Montenegro, Russia, and France, with England maintaining neutrality, at the beginning, at least.
text_raw:
So  far  as  legal  or  diplomatic  commitments  went,  Germany,  in  July,  1914,  had  the  right

groups  set  up  governmental  committees  in  Entente  capitals  and  organized  "Legions"  to
fight  on  the  Entente  side.

text: Italy organized a great meeting of these peoples at Rome in April 1918.
text_raw:
Italy  organized  a  great  meeting  of  these  peoples  at  Rome  in
April  1918.

text: They signed the "Pact of Rome," promising to work for self-determination of subject peoples and agreeing to draw the frontier between the Italians and the South Slavs on nationality lines.
text_raw:
They  signed  the  "Pact  of  Rome,"  promising  to  work  for  self-determination  of
subject  peoples  and  agreeing  to  draw  the  frontier  between  the  Italians  and  the  South  Slavs
on  nationality  lines.

text: Russia, like Romania, was forced out of the war in 1917, and forced to sign a separate peace by Germany in 1918.
text_raw:
Russia,  like  Romania,  was  forced  out  of  the  war  in  1917,  and  forced  to  sign  a  separate
peace  by  Germany  in  1918.

text: The Russian attack on Germany in 1914 had been completely shattered at the battles of Tannenberg and the Masurian Lakes in August and September, but their ability to hold their own against Austrian forces in Galicia made it impossible to bring the war in the east to a conclusion.
text_raw:
The  Russian  attack  on  Germany  in  1914  had  been  completely
shattered  at  the  battles  of  Tannenberg  and  the  Masurian  Lakes  in  August  and  September,
but  their  ability  to  hold  their  own  against  Austrian  forces  in  Galicia  made  it  impossible  to
bring  the  war  in  the  east  to  a  conclusion.

text: Russian casualties were very heavy because of inadequate supplies and munitions, while the Austrians lost considerable forces, especially of Slavs, by desertion to the Russians.
text_raw:
Russian  casualties  were  very  heavy  because  of
inadequate  supplies  and  munitions,  while  the  Austrians  lost  considerable  forces,
especially  of  Slavs,  by  desertion  to  the  Russians.

text: This last factor made it possible for Russia to organize a "Czech Legion" of over 100,000 men.
text_raw:
This  last  factor  made  it  possible  for
Russia  to  organize  a  "Czech  Legion"  of  over  100,000  men.

text: German reinforcements to the Austrian front in Galicia in 1915 made possible a great Austro-German offensive which crossed Galicia and by September had taken all of Poland and Lithuania.
text_raw:
German  reinforcements  to  the
Austrian  front  in  Galicia  in  1915  made  possible  a  great  Austro-German  offensive  which
crossed  Galicia  and  by  September  had  taken  all  of  Poland  and  Lithuania.

text: In these operations the Russians lost about a million men.
text_raw:
In  these
operations  the  Russians  lost  about  a  million  men.

text: They lost a million more in the "Brusilov" counterattack in 1916 which reached the Carpathians before it was stopped by the arrival of German reinforcements from France.
text_raw:
They  lost  a  million  more  in  the
"Brusilov"  counterattack  in  1916  which  reached  the  Carpathians  before  it  was  stopped  by
the  arrival  of  German  reinforcements  from  France.

text: By this time the prestige of the czarist government had fallen so low that it was easily replaced by a parliamentary government under Kerensky in March 1917.
text_raw:
By  this  time  the  prestige  of  the  czarist
government  had  fallen  so  low  that  it  was  easily  replaced  by  a  parliamentary  government
under  Kerensky  in  March  1917.

text: The new government tried to carry on the war, but misjudged the temper of the Russian people.
text_raw:
The  new  government  tried  to  carry  on  the  war,  but
misjudged  the  temper  of  the  Russian  people.

text: As a result the extreme Communist group, known as Bolsheviks, were able to seize the government in November 1917, and hold it by promising the weary Russian people both peace and land.
text_raw:
As  a  result  the  extreme  Communist  group,
known  as  Bolsheviks,  were  able  to  seize  the  government  in  November  1917,  and  hold  it
by  promising  the  weary  Russian  people  both  peace  and  land.

text: The German demands, dictated by the German General Staff, were so severe that the Bolsheviks refused to sign a formal peace, but on March 3, 1918, were forced to accept the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk.
text_raw:
The  German  demands,
dictated  by  the  German  General  Staff,  were  so  severe  that  the  Bolsheviks  refused  to  sign
a  formal  peace,  but  on  March  3,  1918,  were  forced  to  accept  the  Treaty  of  Brest-Litovsk.

text: By this treaty Russia lost Finland, Lithuania, the Baltic Provinces, Poland, the Ukraine and Transcaucasia.
text_raw:
By  this  treaty  Russia  lost  Finland,  Lithuania,  the  Baltic  Provinces,  Poland,  the  Ukraine
and  Transcaucasia.

text: German efforts to exploit these areas in an economic sense during the war were not successful.
text_raw:
German  efforts  to  exploit  these  areas  in  an  economic  sense  during  the
war  were  not  successful.

text: The Japanese intervention in the war on August 23, 1914, was determined completely by its ambitions in the Far East and the Pacific area.
text_raw:
The  Japanese  intervention  in  the  war  on  August  23,  1914,  was  determined  completely
by  its  ambitions  in  the  Far  East  and  the  Pacific  area.

text: It intended to use the opportunity arising from the Great Powers' concern with Europe to win concessions from China and Russia and to replace Germany, not only in its colonial possessions in the East but also to take over its commercial position so far as possible.
text_raw:
It  intended  to  use  the  opportunity
arising  from  the  Great  Powers'  concern  with  Europe  to  win  concessions  from  China  and
Russia  and  to  replace  Germany,  not  only  in  its  colonial  possessions  in  the  East  but  also  to
take  over  its  commercial  position  so  far  as  possible.

text: The German island colonies north of the equator were seized at once, and the German concession at Kiaochow was captured after a brief siege.
text_raw:
The  German  island  colonies  north  of
the  equator  were  seized  at  once,  and  the  German  concession  at  Kiaochow  was  captured
after  a  brief  siege.

text: In January 1915, "Twenty-one Demands" were presented to China in the form of an ultimatum, and largely accepted.
text_raw:
In  January  1915,  "Twenty-one  Demands"  were  presented  to  China  in
the  form  of  an  ultimatum,  and  largely  accepted.

text: These demands covered accession to the German position in Shantung, extension of Japanese leases in Manchuria, with complete commercial liberty for the Japanese in that area, extensive rights in certain existing iron and steel enterprises of North China, and the closing of China's coast to any future foreign concessions.
text_raw:
These  demands  covered  accession  to  the
German  position  in  Shantung,  extension  of  Japanese  leases  in  Manchuria,  with  complete
commercial  liberty  for  the  Japanese  in  that  area,  extensive  rights  in  certain  existing  iron
and  steel  enterprises  of  North  China,  and  the  closing  of  China's  coast  to  any  future
foreign  concessions.

text: A demand for the use of Japanese advisers in Chinese political, military, and financial matters was rejected, and withdrawn.
text_raw:
A  demand  for  the  use  of  Japanese  advisers  in  Chinese  political,
military,  and  financial  matters  was  rejected,  and  withdrawn.

text: On July 3, 1916, Japan won Russian recognition of its new position in China in return for her recognition of the
text_raw:
On  July  3,  1916,  Japan  won
Russian  recognition  of  its  new  position  in  China  in  return  for  her  recognition  of  the

text: Russian penetration into Outer Mongolia.
text_raw: Russian  penetration  into  Outer  Mongolia.

text: New concessions were won from China in February 1917, and accepted by the United States in November in the so-called Lansing- Ishii Notes.
text_raw:
New  concessions  were  won  from  China  in
February  1917,  and  accepted  by  the  United  States  in  November  in  the  so-called  Lansing-
Ishii  Notes.

text: In these notes the Japanese gave verbal support to the American insistence on the maintenance of China's territorial integrity, political independence, and the "Open Door" policy in commercial matters.
text_raw:
In  these  notes  the  Japanese  gave  verbal  support  to  the  American  insistence  on
the  maintenance  of  China's  territorial  integrity,  political  independence,  and  the  "Open
Door"  policy  in  commercial  matters.

text: The outbreak of the Bolshevik Revolution in Russia, followed by the German victory over that country, and the beginning of civil war, gave the Japanese an opportunity in the Far East which they did not hesitate to exploit.
text_raw:
The  outbreak  of  the  Bolshevik  Revolution  in  Russia,  followed  by  the  German  victory
over  that  country,  and  the  beginning  of  civil  war,  gave  the  Japanese  an  opportunity  in  the
Far  East  which  they  did  not  hesitate  to  exploit.

text: With the support of Great Britain and the United States, they landed at Vladivostok in April 1918, and began to move westward along the route of the Trans-Siberian Railway.
text_raw:
With  the  support  of  Great  Britain  and  the
United  States,  they  landed  at  Vladivostok  in  April  1918,  and  began  to  move  westward
along  the  route  of  the  Trans-Siberian  Railway.

text: The Czech Legion on the Russian front had already rebelled against Bolshevik rule and was fighting its way eastward along the same railroad.
text_raw:
The  Czech  Legion  on  the  Russian  front
had  already  rebelled  against  Bolshevik  rule  and  was  fighting  its  way  eastward  along  the
same  railroad.

text: The Czechs were eventually evacuated to Europe, while the Japanese continued to hold the eastern end of the railroad, and gave support to the anti-Bolshevik factions in the civil war.
text_raw:
The  Czechs  were  eventually  evacuated  to  Europe,  while  the  Japanese
continued  to  hold  the  eastern  end  of  the  railroad,  and  gave  support  to  the  anti-Bolshevik
factions  in  the  civil  war.

text: After a year or more of confused fighting, it became clear that the anti-Bolshevik factions would be defeated and that the Japanese could expect no further concessions from the Bolsheviks.
text_raw:
After  a  year  or  more  of  confused  fighting,  it  became  clear  that
the  anti-Bolshevik  factions  would  be  defeated  and  that  the  Japanese  could  expect  no
further  concessions  from  the  Bolsheviks.

text: Accordingly, they evacuated Vladivostok in October 1922.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  they  evacuated  Vladivostok  in
October  1922.

text: Undoubtedly, the most numerous diplomatic agreements of the wartime period were concerned with the disposition of the Ottoman Empire.
text_raw:
Undoubtedly,  the  most  numerous  diplomatic  agreements  of  the  wartime  period  were
concerned  with  the  disposition  of  the  Ottoman  Empire.

text: As early as February 1915, Russia and France signed an agreement by which Russia was given a free hand in the East in return for giving France a free hand in the West.
text_raw:
As  early  as  February  1915,  Russia
and  France  signed  an  agreement  by  which  Russia  was  given  a  free  hand  in  the  East  in
return  for  giving  France  a  free  hand  in  the  West.

text: This meant that Russia could annex Constantinople and block the movement for an independent Poland, while France could take Alsace-Lorraine from Germany and set up a new, independent state under French influence in the Rhineland.
text_raw:
This  meant  that  Russia  could  annex
Constantinople  and  block  the  movement  for  an  independent  Poland,  while  France  could
take  Alsace-Lorraine  from  Germany  and  set  up  a  new,  independent  state  under  French
influence  in  the  Rhineland.

text: A month later, in March 1915, Britain and France agreed to allow Russia to annex the Straits and Constantinople.
text_raw:
A  month  later,  in  March  1915,  Britain  and  France  agreed  to
allow  Russia  to  annex  the  Straits  and  Constantinople.

text: The immediate activities of the Entente Powers, however, were devoted to plans to encourage the Arabs to rebel against the sultan's authority or at least abstain from supporting his war efforts.
text_raw:
The  immediate  activities  of  the
Entente  Powers,  however,  were  devoted  to  plans  to  encourage  the  Arabs  to  rebel  against
the  sultan's  authority  or  at  least  abstain  from  supporting  his  war  efforts.

text: The chances of success in these activities were increased hy the fact that the Arabian portions of the Ottoman Empire, while nominally subject to the sultan, were already breaking up into numerous petty spheres of authority, some virtually independent.
text_raw:
The  chances  of
success  in  these  activities  were  increased  hy  the  fact  that  the  Arabian  portions  of  the
Ottoman  Empire,  while  nominally  subject  to  the  sultan,  were  already  breaking  up  into
numerous  petty  spheres  of  authority,  some  virtually  independent.

text: The Arabs, who were a completely separate people from the Turks, speaking a Semitic rather than a Ural-Altaic language and who had remained largely nomadic in their mode of life while the Turks had become almost completely a peasant people, were united to the Ottoman peoples by little more than their common allegiance to the Muslim religion.
text_raw:
The  Arabs,  who  were  a
completely  separate  people  from  the  Turks,  speaking  a  Semitic  rather  than  a  Ural-Altaic
language  and  who  had  remained  largely  nomadic  in  their  mode  of  life  while  the  Turks
had  become  almost  completely  a  peasant  people,  were  united  to  the  Ottoman  peoples  by
little  more  than  their  common  allegiance  to  the  Muslim  religion.

text: This connection had been weakened by the efforts to secularize the Ottoman state and by the growth of Turkish nationalism which called forth a spirit of Arabic nationalism as a reaction to it.
text_raw:
This  connection  had
been  weakened  by  the  efforts  to  secularize  the  Ottoman  state  and  by  the  growth  of
Turkish  nationalism  which  called  forth  a  spirit  of  Arabic  nationalism  as  a  reaction  to  it.

text: In 1915-1916 the British high commissioner in Egypt, Sir Henry McMahon, entered into correspondence with the Sherif Hussein of Mecca.
text_raw:
In  1915-1916  the  British  high  commissioner  in  Egypt,  Sir  Henry  McMahon,  entered
into  correspondence  with  the  Sherif  Hussein  of  Mecca.

text: While no binding agreement was signed, the gist of their discussions was that Britain would recognize the independence of the Arabs if they revolted against Turkey.
text_raw:
While  no  binding  agreement  was
signed,  the  gist  of  their  discussions  was  that  Britain  would  recognize  the  independence  of
the  Arabs  if  they  revolted  against  Turkey.

text: The area covered by the agreement included those parts of the Ottoman Empire south of the 37th degree of latitude except Adana, Alexandretta, and "those portions of Syria lying to the west of the districts of Damascus, Horns, Hama, and Aleppo, [which] cannot be said to be purely Arab." In addition, Aden

The  interpretation  of  these  terms  to  exclude  Palestine  from  Arab
hands  was  subsequently  made  by  McMahon  on  several  occasions  after  1922  and  most

text: While McMahon was negotiating with Hussein, the Government of India, through Percy Cox, was negotiating with Ibn-Saud of Nejd, and, in an agreement of December 26, 1915, recognized his independence in return for a promise of neutrality in the war.
text_raw:
While  McMahon  was  negotiating  with  Hussein,  the  Government  of  India,  through
Percy  Cox,  was  negotiating  with  Ibn-Saud  of  Nejd,  and,  in  an  agreement  of  December  26,
1915,  recognized  his  independence  in  return  for  a  promise  of  neutrality  in  the  war.

text: Shortly afterward, on May 16, 1916, an agreement, known as the Sykes-Picot agreement from the names of the chief negotiators, was signed between Russia, France, and Britain.
text_raw:
Shortly  afterward,  on  May  16,  1916,  an  agreement,  known  as  the  Sykes-Picot  agreement
from  the  names  of  the  chief  negotiators,  was  signed  between  Russia,  France,  and  Britain.

text: Early in 1917 Italy was added to the settlement.
text_raw: Early  in  1917  Italy  was  added  to  the  settlement.

text: It partitioned the Ottoman Empire in such a way that little was left to the Turks except the area within 200 or 250 miles of Ankara.
text_raw:
It  partitioned  the  Ottoman  Empire  in
such  a  way  that  little  was  left  to  the  Turks  except  the  area  within  200  or  250  miles  of
Ankara.

text: Russia was to get Constantinople and the Straits, as well as northeastern Anatolia, including the Black Sea coast;
text_raw:
Russia  was  to  get  Constantinople  and  the  Straits,  as  well  as  northeastern
Anatolia,  including  the  Black  Sea  coast;

text: Italy was to get the southwestern coast of Anatolia from Smyrna to Adalia;
text_raw:
Italy  was  to  get  the  southwestern  coast  of
Anatolia  from  Smyrna  to  Adalia;

text: France was to get most of eastern Anatolia, including Mersin, Adana, and Cilicia, as well as Kurdistan, Alexandretta, Syria, and northern Mesopotamia, including Mosul;

Britain was to get the Levant from Gaza south to the Red Sea, Transjordan, most of the Syrian Desert, all of Mesopotamia south of Kirkuk (including Baghdad and Basra), and most of the Persian Gulf coast of Arabia.

It  was  also
envisaged  that  western  Anatolia  around  Smyrna  would  go  to  Greece.

text: The Holy Land itself was to be internationalized.
text_raw:
The  Holy  Land
itself  was  to  be  internationalized.

text: The next document concerned with the disposition of the Ottoman Empire was the famous "Balfour Declaration" of November 1917.
text_raw:
The  next  document  concerned  with  the  disposition  of  the  Ottoman  Empire  was  the
famous  "Balfour  Declaration"  of  November  1917.

text: Probably no document of the wartime period, except Wilson's Fourteen Points, has given rise to more disputes than this brief statement of less than eleven lines.
text_raw:
Probably  no  document  of  the  wartime
period,  except  Wilson's  Fourteen  Points,  has  given  rise  to  more  disputes  than  this  brief
statement  of  less  than  eleven  lines.

Much  of  the  controversy  arises  from  the  belief  that  it
promised  something  to  somebody  and  that  this  promise  was  in  conflict  with  other
promises,  notably  with  the  "McMahon  Pledge"  to  Sherif  Hussein.

text: The Balfour Declaration took the form of a letter from British Foreign Secretary Arthur James Balfour to Lord Rothschild, one of the leading figures in the British Zionist movement.

Declaration  took  the  form  of  a  letter  from  British  Foreign  Secretary  Arthur  James  Balfour

text: This movement, which was much stronger in Austria and Germany than in Britain, had aspirations for creating in Palestine, or perhaps elsewhere, some territory to which refugees from anti-Semitic persecution or other Jews could go to find "a national home." text: There is a sharp contrast between the imperialist avarice to be found in the secret agreements like Sykes-Picot and the altruistic tone of the publicly issued statements; there is also a sharp contrast between the tenor of the British negotiations with the Jews and those with the Arabs regarding the disposition of Palestine, with the result that Jews and Arabs were each justified in believing that Britain would promote their conflicting political ambitions in that area: these beliefs, whether based on misunderstanding or deliberate deception, subsequently served to reduce the stature of Britain in the eyes of both groups, although both had previously held a higher opinion of British fairness and generosity than of any other Power; lastly, the raising of false Arab hopes and the failure to reach any clear and honest understanding regarding Syria led to a long period of conflict between the Syrians and the French government, which held the area as a mandate of the League of Nations after 1923.

text: The most important diplomatic event of the latter part of the First World War was the intervention of the United States on the side of the Entente Powers in April 1917.
text_raw:
The  most  important  diplomatic  event  of  the  latter  part  of  the  First  World  War  was  the
intervention  of  the  United  States  on  the  side  of  the  Entente  Powers  in  April  1917.

text: The causes of this event have been analyzed at great length.
text_raw:
The
causes  of  this  event  have  been  analyzed  at  great  length.

text: In general there have been four chief reasons given for the intervention from four quite different points of view.
text_raw:
In  general  there  have  been  four
chief  reasons  given  for  the  intervention  from  four  quite  different  points  of  view.

text: These might be summarized as follows:
text_raw:
These
might  be  summarized  as  follows:

text: (1) The German submarine attacks on neutral shipping made it necessary for the United States to go to war to secure "freedom of the seas";
text_raw:
(1)  The  German  submarine  attacks  on  neutral  shipping
made  it  necessary  for  the  United  States  to  go  to  war  to  secure  "freedom  of  the  seas";

text: (2) the United States was influenced by subtle British propaganda conducted in drawing rooms, universities, and the press of the eastern part of the country where Anglophilism was rampant among the more influential social groups;
text_raw:
(2)
the  United  States  was  influenced  by  subtle  British  propaganda  conducted  in  drawing
rooms,  universities,  and  the  press  of  the  eastern  part  of  the  country  where  Anglophilism
was  rampant  among  the  more  influential  social  groups;

text: (3) the United States was inveigled into the war by a conspiracy of international bankers and munitions manufacturers eager to protect their loans to the Entente Powers or their wartime profits from sales to these Powers; and (4) Balance of Power principles made it impossible for the United States to allow Great Britain to be defeated by Germany.
text_raw:
(3)  the  United  States  was
inveigled  into  the  war  by  a  conspiracy  of  international  bankers  and  munitions
manufacturers  eager  to  protect  their  loans  to  the  Entente  Powers  or  their  wartime  profits
from  sales  to  these  Powers;  and  (4)  Balance  of  Power  principles  made  it  impossible  for
the  United  States  to  allow  Great  Britain  to  be  defeated  by  Germany.

text: Whatever the weight of these four in the final decision, it is quite clear that neither the government nor the people of the United States were prepared to accept a defeat of the Entente at the hands of the Central Powers.
text_raw:
Whatever  the  weight
of  these  four  in  the  final  decision,  it  is  quite  clear  that  neither  the  government  nor  the
people  of  the  United  States  were  prepared  to  accept  a  defeat  of  the  Entente  at  the  hands  of
the  Central  Powers.

text: Indeed, in spite of the government's efforts to act with a certain semblance of neutrality, it was clear in 1914 that this was the view of the chief leaders in the government with the single exception of Secretary of State William Jennings Bryan.
text_raw:
Indeed,  in  spite  of  the  government's  efforts  to  act  with  a  certain
semblance  of  neutrality,  it  was  clear  in  1914  that  this  was  the  view  of  the  chief  leaders  in
the  government  with  the  single  exception  of  Secretary  of  State  William  Jennings  Bryan.

text: Without analyzing the four factors mentioned above, it is quite clear that the United States could not allow Britain to be defeated by any other Power.
text_raw:
Without  analyzing  the  four  factors  mentioned  above,  it  is  quite  clear  that  the  United
States  could  not  allow  Britain  to  be  defeated  by  any  other  Power.

text: Separated from all other Great Powers by the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, the security of America required either that the control of those oceans be in its own hands or in the hands of a friendly Power.
text_raw:
Separated  from  all  other
Great  Powers  by  the  Atlantic  and  Pacific  oceans,  the  security  of  America  required  either
that  the  control  of  those  oceans  be  in  its  own  hands  or  in  the  hands  of  a  friendly  Power.

text: For almost a century before 1917 the United States had been willing to allow British control of the sea to go unchallenged, because it was clear that British control of the sea provided no threat to the United States, but on the contrary, provided security for the United States at a smaller cost in wealth and responsibility than security could have been obtained by any other method.
text_raw:
For  almost  a  century  before  1917  the  United  States  had  been  willing  to  allow  British
control  of  the  sea  to  go  unchallenged,  because  it  was  clear  that  British  control  of  the  sea
provided  no  threat  to  the  United  States,  but  on  the  contrary,  provided  security  for  the
United  States  at  a  smaller  cost  in  wealth  and  responsibility  than  security  could  have  been
obtained  by  any  other  method.

text: The presence of Canada as a British territory adjacent to the United States, and exposed to invasion by land from the United States, constituted a hostage for British naval behavior acceptable to the United States.

its  ruthless  sinking  of  the  merchant  shipping  upon  which  Britain's  existence  depended.

text: Defeat of Britain could not be permitted because the United States was not prepared to take over control of the sea itself and could not permit German control of the sea because it had no assurance regarding the nature of such German control.

Defeat  of  Britain  could  not  be  permitted  because  the  United  States  was  not  prepared  to

text: The unconscious assumption by American leaders that an Entente victory was both necessary and inevitable was at the bottom of their failure to enforce the same rules of neutrality and international law against Britain as against Germany.

text: In 1914-1918, however, in order to win public support for total mobilization, each country's propaganda had been directed toward a total victory for itself and total defeat for the enemy.
text_raw:
In  1914-1918,
however,  in  order  to  win  public  support  for  total  mobilization,  each  country's  propaganda
had  been  directed  toward  a  total  victory  for  itself  and  total  defeat  for  the  enemy.

text: In time, both sides became so enmeshed in their own propaganda that it became impossible to admit publicly one's readiness to accept such lesser aims as any negotiated peace would require.
text_raw:
In  time,
both  sides  became  so  enmeshed  in  their  own  propaganda  that  it  became  impossible  to
admit  publicly  one's  readiness  to  accept  such  lesser  aims  as  any  negotiated  peace  would

text: Moreover, as the tide of battle waxed and waned, giving alternate periods of elation and discouragement to both sides, the side which was temporarily elated became increasingly attached to the fetish of total victory and unwilling to accept the lesser aim of a negotiated peace.
text_raw:
Moreover,  as  the  tide  of  battle  waxed  and  waned,  giving  alternate  periods  of
elation  and  discouragement  to  both  sides,  the  side  which  was  temporarily  elated  became
increasingly  attached  to  the  fetish  of  total  victory  and  unwilling  to  accept  the  lesser  aim
of  a  negotiated  peace.

text: Accordingly, peace became possible only when war weariness had reached the point where one side concluded that even defeat was preferable to continuation of the war.

Accordingly,  peace  became  possible  only  when  war  weariness  had
reached  the  point  where  one  side  concluded  that  even  defeat  was  preferable  to
continuation  of  the  war.

text: This point was reached in Russia in 1917 and in Germany and Austria in 1918.

This  point  was  reached  in  Russia  in  1917  and  in  Germany  and

text: In Germany this point of view was greatly reinforced by the realization that military defeat and political change were preferable to the economic revolution and social upheaval which would accompany any effort to continue the war in pursuit of an increasingly unattainable victory.

In  Germany  this  point  of  view  was  greatly  reinforced  by  the  realization

social  upheaval  which  would  accompany  any  effort  to  continue  the  war  in  pursuit  of  an
increasingly  unattainable  victory.

text: From the various efforts to negotiate peace it is clear that Britain was unwilling to accept any peace which would not include the restoration of Belgium or which would leave Germany supreme on the Continent or in a position to resume the commercial, naval, and colonial rivalry which had existed before 1914;
