text: The Fourteen Points promised the end of secret diplomacy; freedom of the seas; freedom of commerce; disarmament; a fair settlement of colonial claims, with the interests of the native peoples receiving equal weight with the titles of imperialist Powers; the evacuation of Russia; the evacuation and restoration of Belgium; the evacuation of France and the restoration to her of Alsace-Lorraine as in 1870; the readjustment of the Italian frontiers on nationality lines; free and autonomous development for the peoples of the Habsburg Empire; the evacuation, restoration, and guarantee of Romania, Montenegro, and Serbia, with the last-named securing free access to the sea; international guarantees to keep the Straits permanently opened to the ships and commerce of all nations; freedom for the autonomous development of the non- Turkish nationalities of the Ottoman Empire, along with a secure sovereignty for the Turks themselves; an independent Polish state with free access to the sea and with international guarantees; a League of Nations to afford "mutual guarantees of political independence and territorial integrity to great and small states alike"; and no destruction of Germany or even any alteration of her institutions except those necessary to make it clear when her spokesmen spoke for the Reichstag majority and when they "speak for the military party and the men whose creed is imperial domination."
text_raw:
The  Fourteen  Points  promised  the  end  of  secret  diplomacy;
freedom  of  the  seas;  freedom  of  commerce;  disarmament;  a  fair  settlement  of  colonial
claims,  with  the  interests  of  the  native  peoples  receiving  equal  weight  with  the  titles  of
imperialist  Powers;  the  evacuation  of  Russia;  the  evacuation  and  restoration  of  Belgium;
the  evacuation  of  France  and  the  restoration  to  her  of  Alsace-Lorraine  as  in  1870;  the
readjustment  of  the  Italian  frontiers  on  nationality  lines;  free  and  autonomous
development  for  the  peoples  of  the  Habsburg  Empire;  the  evacuation,  restoration,  and
guarantee  of  Romania,  Montenegro,  and  Serbia,  with  the  last-named  securing  free  access
to  the  sea;  international  guarantees  to  keep  the  Straits  permanently  opened  to  the  ships
and  commerce  of  all  nations;  freedom  for  the  autonomous  development  of  the  non-
Turkish  nationalities  of  the  Ottoman  Empire,  along  with  a  secure  sovereignty  for  the
Turks  themselves;  an  independent  Polish  state  with  free  access  to  the  sea  and  with
international  guarantees;  a  League  of  Nations  to  afford  "mutual  guarantees  of  political
independence  and  territorial  integrity  to  great  and  small  states  alike";  and  no  destruction
of  Germany  or  even  any  alteration  of  her  institutions  except  those  necessary  to  make  it
clear  when  her  spokesmen  spoke  for  the  Reichstag  majority  and  when  they  "speak  for  the
military  party  and  the  men  whose  creed  is  imperial  domination."

text: In a series of notes between Germany and the United States, Wilson made it clear that he would grant an armistice only if Germany would withdraw from all occupied territory, make an end to submarine attacks, accept the Fourteen Points, establish a responsible government, and accept terms which would preserve the existing Entente military superiority.

make  an  end  to  submarine  attacks,  accept  the  Fourteen  Points,  establish  a  responsible
government,  and  accept  terms  which  would  preserve  the  existing  Entente  military
superiority.

text: He was most insistent on the responsible government, warning that if he had to deal "with military masters or monarchical autocrats" he would demand "not negotiations but surrender." The German constitution was changed to give all powers to the Reichstag;

text_raw:
In  the  German  attack  of
March  1918,  62  divisions  with  4,500  heavy  guns  and  1,000  planes  were  hurled  on  a  front
only  45  miles  wide.

text: On all fronts in the whole war almost 13,000,000 men in the various armed forces died from wounds and disease.
text_raw:
On  all  fronts  in  the  whole  war  almost  13,000,000  men  in  the  various
armed  forces  died  from  wounds  and  disease.

text: It has been estimated by the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace that the war destroyed over $400,000,000,000 of property at a time when the value of every object in France and Belgium was not worth over $75,000,000,000.
text_raw:
It  has  been  estimated  by  the  Carnegie
Endowment  for  International  Peace  that  the  war  destroyed  over  $400,000,000,000  of
property  at  a  time  when  the  value  of  every  object  in  France  and  Belgium  was  not  worth
over  $75,000,000,000.

text: Obviously, expenditures of men and wealth at rates like these required a tremendous mobilization of resources throughout the world, and could not fail to have far-reaching effects on the patterns of thought and modes of action of people forced to undergo such a strain.
text_raw:
Obviously,  expenditures  of  men  and  wealth  at  rates  like  these  required  a  tremendous
mobilization  of  resources  throughout  the  world,  and  could  not  fail  to  have  far-reaching
effects  on  the  patterns  of  thought  and  modes  of  action  of  people  forced  to  undergo  such  a
strain.

text: Some states were destroyed or permanently crippled.
text_raw: Some  states  were  destroyed  or  permanently  crippled.

text: There were profound modifications in finance, in economic life, in social relations, in intellectual outlook, and in emotional patterns.
text_raw:
There  were  profound
modifications  in  finance,  in  economic  life,  in  social  relations,  in  intellectual  outlook,  and
in  emotional  patterns.

text: Nevertheless, two facts should be recognized.
text_raw: Nevertheless,  two  facts  should  be  recognized.

text: The war brought nothing really new into the world; rather it sped up processes of change which had been going on for a considerable period and would have continued anyway, with the result that changes which would have taken place over a period of thirty or even fifty years in peacetime were brought about in five years during the war.
text_raw:
The  war  brought
nothing  really  new  into  the  world;  rather  it  sped  up  processes  of  change  which  had  been
going  on  for  a  considerable  period  and  would  have  continued  anyway,  with  the  result  that
changes  which  would  have  taken  place  over  a  period  of  thirty  or  even  fifty  years  in
peacetime  were  brought  about  in  five  years  during  the  war.

text: Also, the changes were much greater in objective facts and in the organization of society than they were in men's ideas of these facts or organization.
text_raw:
Also,  the  changes  were  much
greater  in  objective  facts  and  in  the  organization  of  society  than  they  were  in  men's  ideas
of  these  facts  or  organization.

text: It was as if the changes were too rapid for men's minds to accept them, or, what is more likely, that men, seeing the great changes which were occurring on all sides, recognized them, but assumed that they were merely temporary wartime aberrations, and that, when peace came, they would pass away and everyone could go back to the slow, pleasant world of 1913.
text_raw:
It  was  as  if  the  changes  were  too  rapid  for  men's  minds  to
accept  them,  or,  what  is  more  likely,  that  men,  seeing  the  great  changes  which  were
occurring  on  all  sides,  recognized  them,  but  assumed  that  they  were  merely  temporary
wartime  aberrations,  and  that,  when  peace  came,  they  would  pass  away  and  everyone
could  go  back  to  the  slow,  pleasant  world  of  1913.

text: This point of view, which dominated the thinking of the 1920's, was widespread and very dangerous.
text_raw:
This  point  of  view,  which  dominated
the  thinking  of  the  1920's,  was  widespread  and  very  dangerous.

text: In their efforts to go back to 1913, men refused to recognize that the wartime changes were more or less permanent, and, instead of trying to solve the problems arising from these changes, set up a false facade of pretense, painted to look like 1913, to cover up the great changes which had taken place.
text_raw:
In  their  efforts  to  go  back
to  1913,  men  refused  to  recognize  that  the  wartime  changes  were  more  or  less  permanent,
and,  instead  of  trying  to  solve  the  problems  arising  from  these  changes,  set  up  a  false
facade  of  pretense,  painted  to  look  like  1913,  to  cover  up  the  great  changes  which  had
taken  place.

text: Then, by acting as if this facade were reality, and by neglecting the maladjusted reality which was moving beneath it, the people of the 1920'S drifted in a hectic world of unreality until the world depression of 1929-1935, and the international crises which followed, tore away the facade and showed the horrible, long-neglected reality beneath it.
text_raw:
Then,  by  acting  as  if  this  facade  were  reality,  and  by  neglecting  the
maladjusted  reality  which  was  moving  beneath  it,  the  people  of  the  1920'S  drifted  in  a
hectic  world  of  unreality  until  the  world  depression  of  1929-1935,  and  the  international
crises  which  followed,  tore  away  the  facade  and  showed  the  horrible,  long-neglected
reality  beneath  it.

text: The magnitude of the war and the fact that it might last for more than six months were quite unexpected for both sides and were impressed upon them only gradually.
text_raw:
The  magnitude  of  the  war  and  the  fact  that  it  might  last  for  more  than  six  months  were
quite  unexpected  for  both  sides  and  were  impressed  upon  them  only  gradually.

text: It first became clear in regard to consumption of supplies, especially ammunition, and in the problem of how to pay for these supplies.
text_raw:
It  first
became  clear  in  regard  to  consumption  of  supplies,  especially  ammunition,  and  in  the
problem  of  how  to  pay  for  these  supplies.

text: In July 1914, the military men were confident that a decision would be reached in six months because their military plans and the examples of 1866 and 1870 indicated an immediate decision.
text_raw:
In  July  1914,  the  military  men  were  confident
that  a  decision  would  be  reached  in  six  months  because  their  military  plans  and  the
examples  of  1866  and  1870  indicated  an  immediate  decision.

text: This belief was supported by the financial experts who, while greatly underestimating the cost of fighting, were confident that the financial resources of all states would be exhausted in six months.
text_raw:
This  belief  was  supported
by  the  financial  experts  who,  while  greatly  underestimating  the  cost  of  fighting,  were
confident  that  the  financial  resources  of  all  states  would  be  exhausted  in  six  months.

text: By "financial resources" they meant the gold reserves of the various nations.
text_raw:
By
"financial  resources"  they  meant  the  gold  reserves  of  the  various  nations.

text: These were clearly limited; all the Great Powers were on the gold standard under which bank notes and paper money could be converted into gold on demand.
text_raw:
These  were
clearly  limited;  all  the  Great  Powers  were  on  the  gold  standard  under  which  bank  notes
and  paper  money  could  be  converted  into  gold  on  demand.

text: However, each country suspended the gold standard at the outbreak of war.
text_raw:
However,  each  country
suspended  the  gold  standard  at  the  outbreak  of  war.

text: This removed the automatic
text_raw: This  removed  the  automatic

text: limitation on the supply of paper money.
text_raw: limitation  on  the  supply  of  paper  money.

text: Then each country proceeded to pay for the war by borrowing from the banks.
text_raw:
Then  each  country  proceeded  to  pay  for  the  war
by  borrowing  from  the  banks.

text: The banks created the money which they lent by merely giving the government a deposit of any size against which the government could draw checks.
text_raw:
The  banks  created  the  money  which  they  lent  by  merely
giving  the  government  a  deposit  of  any  size  against  which  the  government  could  draw
checks.

text: The banks were no longer limited in the amount of credit they could create because they no longer had to pay out gold for checks on demand.
text_raw:
The  banks  were  no  longer  limited  in  the  amount  of  credit  they  could  create
because  they  no  longer  had  to  pay  out  gold  for  checks  on  demand.

text: Thus the creation of money in the form of credit by the banks was limited only by the demands of its borrowers.
text_raw:
Thus  the  creation  of
money  in  the  form  of  credit  by  the  banks  was  limited  only  by  the  demands  of  its
borrowers.

text: Naturally, as governments borrowed to pay for their needs, private businesses borrowed in order to be able to fill the government's orders.
text_raw:
Naturally,  as  governments  borrowed  to  pay  for  their  needs,  private  businesses
borrowed  in  order  to  be  able  to  fill  the  government's  orders.

text: The gold which could no longer be demanded merely rested in the vaults, except where some of it was exported to pay for supplies from neutral countries or from fellow belligerents.
text_raw:
The  gold  which  could  no
longer  be  demanded  merely  rested  in  the  vaults,  except  where  some  of  it  was  exported  to
pay  for  supplies  from  neutral  countries  or  from  fellow  belligerents.

text: As a result, the percentage of outstanding bank notes covered by gold reserves steadily fell, and the percentage of bank credit covered by either gold or bank notes fell even further.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  the
percentage  of  outstanding  bank  notes  covered  by  gold  reserves  steadily  fell,  and  the
percentage  of  bank  credit  covered  by  either  gold  or  bank  notes  fell  even  further.

text: Naturally, when the supply of money was increased in this fashion faster than the supply of goods, prices rose because a larger supply of money was competing for a smaller supply of goods.
text_raw:
Naturally,  when  the  supply  of  money  was  increased  in  this  fashion  faster  than  the
supply  of  goods,  prices  rose  because  a  larger  supply  of  money  was  competing  for  a
smaller  supply  of  goods.

text: This effect was made worse by the fact that the supply of goods tended to be reduced by wartime destruction.
text_raw:
This  effect  was  made  worse  by  the  fact  that  the  supply  of  goods
tended  to  be  reduced  by  wartime  destruction.

text: People received money for making capital goods, consumers' goods, and munitions, but they could spend their money only to buy consumers' goods, since capital goods and munitions were not offered for sale.
text_raw:
People  received  money  for  making  capital
goods,  consumers'  goods,  and  munitions,  but  they  could  spend  their  money  only  to  buy
consumers'  goods,  since  capital  goods  and  munitions  were  not  offered  for  sale.

text: Since governments tried to reduce the supply of consumers' goods while increasing the supply of the other two products, the problem of rising prices (inflation) became acute.
text_raw:
Since
governments  tried  to  reduce  the  supply  of  consumers'  goods  while  increasing  the  supply
of  the  other  two  products,  the  problem  of  rising  prices  (inflation)  became  acute.

text: At the same time the problem of public debt became steadily worse because governments were financing such a large part of their activities by bank credit.
text_raw:
At  the
same  time  the  problem  of  public  debt  became  steadily  worse  because  governments  were
financing  such  a  large  part  of  their  activities  by  bank  credit.

text: These two problems, inflation and public debt, continued to grow, even after the fighting stopped, because of the continued disruption of economic life and the need to pay for past activities.
text_raw:
These  two  problems,
inflation  and  public  debt,  continued  to  grow,  even  after  the  fighting  stopped,  because  of
the  continued  disruption  of  economic  life  and  the  need  to  pay  for  past  activities.

text: Only in the period 1920-1925 did these two stop increasing in most countries, and they remained problems long after that.
text_raw:
Only  in
the  period  1920-1925  did  these  two  stop  increasing  in  most  countries,  and  they  remained
problems  long  after  that.

text: Inflation indicates not only an increase in the prices of goods but also a decrease in the value of money (since it will buy less goods).
text_raw:
Inflation  indicates  not  only  an  increase  in  the  prices  of  goods  but  also  a  decrease  in  the
value  of  money  (since  it  will  buy  less  goods).

text: Accordingly, people in an inflation seek to get goods and to get rid of money.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  people  in  an  inflation  seek  to
get  goods  and  to  get  rid  of  money.

text: Thus inflation increases production and purchases for consumption or hoarding, but it reduces saving or creation of capital.
text_raw:
Thus  inflation  increases  production  and  purchases  for
consumption  or  hoarding,  but  it  reduces  saving  or  creation  of  capital.

text: It benefits debtors (by making a fixed-money debt less of a burden) but injures creditors (by reducing the value of their savings and credits).
text_raw:
It  benefits  debtors
(by  making  a  fixed-money  debt  less  of  a  burden)  but  injures  creditors  (by  reducing  the
value  of  their  savings  and  credits).

text: Since the middle classes of European society, with their bank savings, checking deposits, mortgages, insurance, and bond holdings, were the creditor class, they were injured and even ruined by the wartime inflation.
text_raw:
Since  the  middle  classes  of  European  society,  with
their  bank  savings,  checking  deposits,  mortgages,  insurance,  and  bond  holdings,  were  the
creditor  class,  they  were  injured  and  even  ruined  by  the  wartime  inflation.

text: In Germany, Poland, Hungary, and Russia, where the inflation went so far that the monetary unit became completely valueless by 1924, the middle classes were largely destroyed, and their members were driven to desperation or at least to an almost psychopathic hatred of the form of government or the social class that they believed to be responsible for their plight.
text_raw:
In  Germany,
Poland,  Hungary,  and  Russia,  where  the  inflation  went  so  far  that  the  monetary  unit
became  completely  valueless  by  1924,  the  middle  classes  were  largely  destroyed,  and
their  members  were  driven  to  desperation  or  at  least  to  an  almost  psychopathic  hatred  of
the  form  of  government  or  the  social  class  that  they  believed  to  be  responsible  for  their
plight.

text: Since the last stages of inflation which dealt the fatal blow to the middle classes occurred after the war rather than during it (in 1923 in Germany), this hatred was directed against the parliamentary governments which were functioning after 1918 rather than against the monarchical governments which functioned in 1914-1918.
text_raw:
Since  the  last  stages  of  inflation  which  dealt  the  fatal  blow  to  the  middle  classes
occurred  after  the  war  rather  than  during  it  (in  1923  in  Germany),  this  hatred  was  directed
against  the  parliamentary  governments  which  were  functioning  after  1918  rather  than
against  the  monarchical  governments  which  functioned  in  1914-1918.

text: In France and Italy, where the inflation went so far that the franc or fire was reduced permanently to one-fifth of its prewar value, the hatred of the injured middle classes was directed against
text_raw:
In  France  and
Italy,  where  the  inflation  went  so  far  that  the  franc  or  fire  was  reduced  permanently  to
one-fifth  of  its  prewar  value,  the  hatred  of  the  injured  middle  classes  was  directed  against

text: the parliamentary regime which had functioned both during and after the war and against the working class which they felt had profited by their misfortunes.
text_raw:
the  parliamentary  regime  which  had  functioned  both  during  and  after  the  war  and  against
the  working  class  which  they  felt  had  profited  by  their  misfortunes.

text: These things were not true in Britain or the United States, where the inflation was brought under control and the monetary unit restored to most of its prewar value.
text_raw:
These  things  were  not
true  in  Britain  or  the  United  States,  where  the  inflation  was  brought  under  control  and  the
monetary  unit  restored  to  most  of  its  prewar  value.

text: Even in these countries, prices rose by 200 to 300 percent, while public debts rose about 1,000 percent.
text_raw:
Even  in  these  countries,  prices  rose  by
200  to  300  percent,  while  public  debts  rose  about  1,000  percent.

text: The economic effects of the war were more complicated.
text_raw: The  economic  effects  of  the  war  were  more  complicated.

text: Resources of all kinds, including land, labor, and raw materials, had to be diverted from peacetime purposes to wartime production; or, in some cases, resources previously not used at all had to be brought into the productive system.
text_raw:
Resources  of  all  kinds,
including  land,  labor,  and  raw  materials,  had  to  be  diverted  from  peacetime  purposes  to
wartime  production;  or,  in  some  cases,  resources  previously  not  used  at  all  had  to  be
brought  into  the  productive  system.

text: Before the war, the allotment of resources to production had been made by the automatic processes of the price system; labor and raw materials going, for example, to manufacture those goods which were most profitable rather than to those goods which were most serviceable or socially beneficial, or in best taste.
text_raw:
Before  the  war,  the  allotment  of  resources  to
production  had  been  made  by  the  automatic  processes  of  the  price  system;  labor  and  raw
materials  going,  for  example,  to  manufacture  those  goods  which  were  most  profitable
rather  than  to  those  goods  which  were  most  serviceable  or  socially  beneficial,  or  in  best
taste.

text: In wartime, however, governments had to have certain specific goods for military purposes; they tried to get these goods produced by making them more profitable than nonmilitary goods using the same resources, but they were not always successful.
text_raw:
In  wartime,  however,  governments  had  to  have  certain  specific  goods  for  military
purposes;  they  tried  to  get  these  goods  produced  by  making  them  more  profitable  than
nonmilitary  goods  using  the  same  resources,  but  they  were  not  always  successful.

text: The excess of purchasing power in the hands of consumers caused a great rise in demand for goods of a semi-luxury nature, like white cotton shirts for laborers.
text_raw:
The
excess  of  purchasing  power  in  the  hands  of  consumers  caused  a  great  rise  in  demand  for
goods  of  a  semi-luxury  nature,  like  white  cotton  shirts  for  laborers.

text: This frequently made it more profitable for manufacturers to use cotton for making shirts to sell at high prices than to use it to make explosives.
text_raw:
This  frequently  made
it  more  profitable  for  manufacturers  to  use  cotton  for  making  shirts  to  sell  at  high  prices
than  to  use  it  to  make  explosives.

text: Situations such as these made it necessary for governments to intervene directly in the economic process to secure those results which could not be obtained by the free price system or to reduce those evil effects which emerged from wartime disruption.
text_raw:
Situations  such  as  these  made  it  necessary  for  governments  to  intervene  directly  in  the
economic  process  to  secure  those  results  which  could  not  be  obtained  by  the  free  price
system  or  to  reduce  those  evil  effects  which  emerged  from  wartime  disruption.

text: They appealed to the patriotism of manufacturers to make things that were needed rather than things which were profitable, or to the patriotism of consumers to put their money into government bonds rather than into goods in short supply.
text_raw:
They
appealed  to  the  patriotism  of  manufacturers  to  make  things  that  were  needed  rather  than
things  which  were  profitable,  or  to  the  patriotism  of  consumers  to  put  their  money  into
government  bonds  rather  than  into  goods  in  short  supply.

text: They began to build government-owned plants for war production, either using them for such purposes themselves or leasing them out to private manufacturers at attractive terms.
text_raw:
They  began  to  build
government-owned  plants  for  war  production,  either  using  them  for  such  purposes
themselves  or  leasing  them  out  to  private  manufacturers  at  attractive  terms.

text: They began to ration consumers' goods which were in short supply, like articles of food.
text_raw:
They  began
to  ration  consumers'  goods  which  were  in  short  supply,  like  articles  of  food.

text: They began to monopolize essential raw materials and allot them to manufacturers who had war contracts rather than allow them to flow where prices w ere highest.
text_raw:
They  began
to  monopolize  essential  raw  materials  and  allot  them  to  manufacturers  who  had  war
contracts  rather  than  allow  them  to  flow  where  prices  w  ere  highest.

text: The materials so treated were generally fuels, steel, rubber, copper, wool, cotton, nitrates, and such, although they varied from country to country, depending upon the supply.
text_raw:
The  materials  so
treated  were  generally  fuels,  steel,  rubber,  copper,  wool,  cotton,  nitrates,  and  such,
although  they  varied  from  country  to  country,  depending  upon  the  supply.

text: Governments began to regulate imports and exports in order to ensure that necessary materials staved in the country and, above all, did not go to enemy states.
text_raw:
Governments
began  to  regulate  imports  and  exports  in  order  to  ensure  that  necessary  materials  staved  in
the  country  and,  above  all,  did  not  go  to  enemy  states.

text: This ]ed to the British blockade of Europe, the rationing of exports to neutrals, and complicated negotiations to see that goods in neutral countries were not re-exported to enemy countries.
text_raw:
This  ]ed  to  the  British  blockade  of
Europe,  the  rationing  of  exports  to  neutrals,  and  complicated  negotiations  to  see  that
goods  in  neutral  countries  were  not  re-exported  to  enemy  countries.

text: Bribery, bargaining, and even force came into these negotiations, as when the British set quotas on the imports of Holland based on the figures for prewar years or cut down necessary shipments of British coal to Sweden until they obtained the concessions they wished regarding sales of Swedish goods to Germany.
text_raw:
Bribery,  bargaining,
and  even  force  came  into  these  negotiations,  as  when  the  British  set  quotas  on  the  imports
of  Holland  based  on  the  figures  for  prewar  years  or  cut  down  necessary  shipments  of
British  coal  to  Sweden  until  they  obtained  the  concessions  they  wished  regarding  sales  of
Swedish  goods  to  Germany.

text: Shipping and railroad transportation had to be taken over almost completely in most countries in order to ensure that the inadequate space for cargo and freight would be used as effectively as possible, that loading and unloading would be speeded up, and that goods essential to the war effort would be shipped earlier and faster than less essential goods.
text_raw:
Shipping  and  railroad  transportation  had  to  be  taken  over
almost  completely  in  most  countries  in  order  to  ensure  that  the  inadequate  space  for  cargo
and  freight  would  be  used  as  effectively  as  possible,  that  loading  and  unloading  would  be
speeded  up,  and  that  goods  essential  to  the  war  effort  would  be  shipped  earlier  and  faster
than  less  essential  goods.

text: Labor had to be regulated and directed into essential activities.
text_raw: Labor  had  to  be  regulated  and  directed  into  essential  activities.

text: The rapid rise in prices led to demands for raises in wages.
text_raw: The  rapid  rise  in  prices  led  to  demands  for  raises  in  wages.

text: This led to a growth and strengthening of labor unions and increasing threats of strikes.
text_raw:
This  led  to  a  growth  and
strengthening  of  labor  unions  and  increasing  threats  of  strikes.

text: There was no guarantee that the wages of essential workers would go up faster than the wages of nonessential workers.
text_raw:
There  was  no  guarantee
that  the  wages  of  essential  workers  would  go  up  faster  than  the  wages  of  nonessential
workers.

text: Certainly the wages of soldiers, who were the most essential of all, went up very little.
text_raw:
Certainly  the  wages  of  soldiers,  who  were  the  most  essential  of  all,  went  up  very
little.

text: Thus there was no guarantee that labor, if left solely to the influence of wage levels, as was usual before 1914, would flow to the occupations where it was most urgently needed.
text_raw:
Thus  there  was  no  guarantee  that  labor,  if  left  solely  to  the  influence  of  wage  levels,
as  was  usual  before  1914,  would  flow  to  the  occupations  where  it  was  most  urgently
needed.

text: Accordingly, the governments began to intervene in labor problems, seeking to avoid strikes but also to direct the flow of labor to more essential activities.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  the  governments  began  to  intervene  in  labor  problems,  seeking  to
avoid  strikes  but  also  to  direct  the  flow  of  labor  to  more  essential  activities.

text: There were general registrations of men in most countries, at first as part of the draft of men for military service, but later to control services in essential activities.
text_raw:
There  were
general  registrations  of  men  in  most  countries,  at  first  as  part  of  the  draft  of  men  for
military  service,  but  later  to  control  services  in  essential  activities.

text: Generally, the right to leave an essential job was restricted, and eventually people were directed into essential jobs from nonessential activities.
text_raw:
Generally,  the  right  to
leave  an  essential  job  was  restricted,  and  eventually  people  were  directed  into  essential
jobs  from  nonessential  activities.

text: The high wages and shortage of labor brought into the labor market many persons who would not have been in it in peacetime, such as old persons, youths, clergy, and, above all, women.
text_raw:
The  high  wages  and  shortage  of  labor  brought  into  the
labor  market  many  persons  who  would  not  have  been  in  it  in  peacetime,  such  as  old
persons,  youths,  clergy,  and,  above  all,  women.

wanted  to  pursue  a  policy  of  "national  interest,"  by  which  they  meant  emphasis  on
strengthening  the  empire,  conducting  an  aggressive  commercial  policy  against  outsiders,
and  adopting  relative  isolationism  in  general  policy  with  no  European  political
commitments  except  west  of  the  Rhine  (where  Britain's  interests  were  immediate).

text: The groups of the Left were in office in Britain for only about two years in the twenty years 1919-1939 and then only as a minority government (1924, 1929-1931); the groups of the Right were in power for eighteen of these twenty years, usually with an absolute majority.

The
groups  of  the  Left  were  in  office  in  Britain  for  only  about  two  years  in  the  twenty  years
1919-1939  and  then  only  as  a  minority  government  (1924,  1929-1931);  the  groups  of  the

text: However, during these twenty years the people of Britain were generally sympathetic to the point of view of the Left in foreign policy, although they generally voted in elections on the basis of domestic rather than foreign politics.

text: This means that the people were in favor of revision of Versailles, of collective security, of international cooperation, and of disarmament.

the  people  were  in  favor  of  revision  of  Versailles,  of  collective  security,  of  international

text: Knowing this, the British governments of the Right began to follow a double policy: a public policy in which they spoke loudly in support of what we have called the foreign policy of the Left, and a secret policy in which they acted in support of what we have called the foreign policy of the Right.
text_raw:
Knowing  this,  the  British  governments  of  the  Right  began  to  follow  a  double  policy:  a
public  policy  in  which  they  spoke  loudly  in  support  of  what  we  have  called  the  foreign
policy  of  the  Left,  and  a  secret  policy  in  which  they  acted  in  support  of  what  we  have
called  the  foreign  policy  of  the  Right.

text: Thus the stated policy of the government and the policy of the British people were based on support of the League of Nations, of international cooperation, and of disarmament.
text_raw:
Thus  the  stated  policy  of  the  government  and  the
policy  of  the  British  people  were  based  on  support  of  the  League  of  Nations,  of

text: Yet the real policy was quite different.
text_raw: Yet  the  real  policy  was  quite  different.

text: Lord Curzon, who was foreign secretary for four years (1919-1923) called the League of Nations "a good joke";
text_raw:

text: Also, after 1935, the policies of both Right and Left were changed, the Left becoming anti- revisionist as early as 1934, continuing to support disarmament until (in some cases) 1939, and strengthening its insistence on collective security, while the Right became more insistent on revisionism (by that time called "appeasement") and opposition to the Soviet Union.

Also,
after  1935,  the  policies  of  both  Right  and  Left  were  changed,  the  Left  becoming  anti-

text: In France the contrasts between Right and Left were less sharp than in Britain and the exceptions more numerous, not only because of the comparative complexity of French political parties and political ideology, but also because foreign policy in France was not an academic or secondary issue but was an immediate, frightening concern of every Frenchman.
text_raw:
In  France  the  contrasts  between  Right  and  Left  were  less  sharp  than  in  Britain  and  the
exceptions  more  numerous,  not  only  because  of  the  comparative  complexity  of  French
political  parties  and  political  ideology,  but  also  because  foreign  policy  in  France  was  not
an  academic  or  secondary  issue  but  was  an  immediate,  frightening  concern  of  every
Frenchman.

text: Consequently, differences of opinion, however noisy and intense, were really rather slight.
text_raw:
Consequently,  differences  of  opinion,  however  noisy  and  intense,  were  really
rather  slight.

text: One thing all Frenchmen agreed upon:
text_raw: One  thing  all  Frenchmen  agreed  upon:

text: "It must not happen again." Never again must the Hun be permitted to become strong enough to assault France as in 1870 and in 1914.
text_raw:
"It  must  not  happen  again."  Never
again  must  the  Hun  be  permitted  to  become  strong  enough  to  assault  France  as  in  1870
and  in  1914.

text: To prevent this, the Right and the Left agreed, there were two methods: by the collective action of all nations and by France's own military power.
text_raw:
To  prevent  this,  the  Right  and  the  Left  agreed,  there  were  two  methods:  by
the  collective  action  of  all  nations  and  by  France's  own  military  power.

text: The two sides differed in the order in which these two should be used, the Left wanting to use collective action first and France's own power as a supplement or a substitute, the Right wanting to use France's own power first, with support from the League or other allies as a supplement.
text_raw:
The  two  sides
differed  in  the  order  in  which  these  two  should  be  used,  the  Left  wanting  to  use  collective
action  first  and  France's  own  power  as  a  supplement  or  a  substitute,  the  Right  wanting  to
use  France's  own  power  first,  with  support  from  the  League  or  other  allies  as  a
supplement.

text: In addition, the Left tried to distinguish between the old imperial Germany and the new republican Germany, hoping to placate the latter and turn its mind away from revisionism by cooperative friendship and collective action.
text_raw:
In  addition,  the  Left  tried  to  distinguish  between  the  old  imperial  Germany
and  the  new  republican  Germany,  hoping  to  placate  the  latter  and  turn  its  mind  away
from  revisionism  by  cooperative  friendship  and  collective  action.

text: The Right, on the other hand, found it impossible to distinguish one Germany from another or even one German from another, believing that all were equally incapable of understanding any policy but force.
text_raw:
The  Right,  on  the  other
hand,  found  it  impossible  to  distinguish  one  Germany  from  another  or  even  one  German
from  another,  believing  that  all  were  equally  incapable  of  understanding  any  policy  but
force.

text: Accordingly, the Right wanted to use force to compel Germany to fulfill the Treaty of Versailles, even if France had to act alone.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  the  Right  wanted  to  use  force  to  compel  Germany  to  fulfill  the  Treaty
of  Versailles,  even  if  France  had  to  act  alone.

text: The policy of the Right was the policy of Poincare and Barthou; the policy of the Left was the policy of Briand.
text_raw:
The  policy  of  the  Right  was  the  policy  of  Poincare  and  Barthou;  the  policy  of  the  Left
was  the  policy  of  Briand.

text: The former was used in 1918-1924 and, briefly, in 1934-1935; the latter was used in 1924-1929.
text_raw:
The  former  was  used  in  1918-1924  and,  briefly,  in  1934-1935;
the  latter  was  used  in  1924-1929.

text: The policy of the Right failed in 1924 when Poincare's occupation of the Ruhr in order to force Germany to pay reparations was ended.
text_raw:
The  policy  of  the  Right  failed  in  1924  when  Poincare's
occupation  of  the  Ruhr  in  order  to  force  Germany  to  pay  reparations  was  ended.

text: This showed that France could not act alone even against a weak Germany because of the opposition of Britain and the danger of alienating world opinion.

This
showed  that  France  could  not  act  alone  even  against  a  weak  Germany  because  of  the
opposition  of  Britain  and  the  danger  of  alienating  world  opinion.

text: Accordingly, France turned to a policy of the Left (1924-1929).
text_raw:
Accordingly,  France
turned  to  a  policy  of  the  Left  (1924-1929).

text: In this period, which is known as the "Period of Fulfillment," Briand, as foreign minister of France, and Stresemann, as foreign minister of Germany, cooperated in friendly terms.
text_raw:
In  this  period,  which  is  known  as  the  "Period
of  Fulfillment,"  Briand,  as  foreign  minister  of  France,  and  Stresemann,  as  foreign
minister  of  Germany,  cooperated  in  friendly  terms.

text: This period ended in 1929, not, as is usually said, because Stresemann died and Briand fell from office, but because of a growing realization that the whole policy of fulfillment (1924-1929) had been based on a misunderstanding.
text_raw:
This  period  ended  in  1929,  not,  as  is
usually  said,  because  Stresemann  died  and  Briand  fell  from  office,  but  because  of  a
growing  realization  that  the  whole  policy  of  fulfillment  (1924-1929)  had  been  based  on  a
misunderstanding.

text: Briand followed a policy of conciliation toward Germany in order to win Germany from any desire to revise Versailles;
text_raw:
Briand  followed  a  policy  of  conciliation  toward  Germany  in  order  to
win  Germany  from  any  desire  to  revise  Versailles;

text: Stresemann followed his policy of fulfillment toward France in order to win from France a revision of the treaty.
text_raw:
Stresemann  followed  his  policy  of
fulfillment  toward  France  in  order  to  win  from  France  a  revision  of  the  treaty.

text: It was a relationship of cross-purposes, because on the crucial issue (revision of Versailles) Briand stood adamant, like most Frenchmen, and Stresemann was irreconcilable, like most Germans.
text_raw:
It  was  a
relationship  of  cross-purposes,  because  on  the  crucial  issue  (revision  of  Versailles)
Briand  stood  adamant,  like  most  Frenchmen,  and  Stresemann  was  irreconcilable,  like
most  Germans.

text: In France, as a result of the failure of the policy of the Right in 1924 and of the policy of the Left in 1929, it became clear that France could not act alone toward Germany.
text_raw:
In  France,  as  a  result  of  the  failure  of  the  policy  of  the  Right  in  1924  and  of  the  policy
of  the  Left  in  1929,  it  became  clear  that  France  could  not  act  alone  toward  Germany.

text: It became clear that France did not have freedom of action in foreign affairs and was dependent on Britain for its security.
text_raw:
It
became  clear  that  France  did  not  have  freedom  of  action  in  foreign  affairs  and  was
dependent  on  Britain  for  its  security.

text: To win this support, which Britain always held out as a bait but did not give until 1939, Britain forced France to adopt the policy of appeasement of the British Right after 1935.
text_raw:
To  win  this  support,  which  Britain  always  held  out
as  a  bait  but  did  not  give  until  1939,  Britain  forced  France  to  adopt  the  policy  of
appeasement  of  the  British  Right  after  1935.

text: This policy forced France to give away every advantage which it held over Germany:
text_raw:
This  policy  forced  France  to  give  away
every  advantage  which  it  held  over  Germany:

text: Germany was allowed to rearm (1935);
text_raw: Germany  was  allowed  to  rearm  (1935);

text: Germany was allowed to remilitarize the Rhineland (1936);
text_raw: Germany  was  allowed  to  remilitarize  the  Rhineland  (1936);

text: Italy was alienated (1935);
text_raw: Italy  was  alienated  (1935);

text: France lost its last secure land frontier (Spain, 1936-1939);
text_raw: France  lost  its  last  secure  land  frontier  (Spain,  1936-1939);

France  lost  all  her  allies  to  the

text: France had to accept the union of Austria with Germany which she had vetoed in 1931 (March 1938); the power and prestige of the League of Nations was broken and the whole system of collective security abandoned (1931-1939); the Soviet Union, which had allied with France and Czechoslovakia against Germany in 1935, was treated as a pariah among nations and lost to the anti-German coalition (1937-1939).
text_raw:
France  had
to  accept  the  union  of  Austria  with  Germany  which  she  had  vetoed  in  1931  (March
1938);  the  power  and  prestige  of  the  League  of  Nations  was  broken  and  the  whole  system

text: And finally, when all these had been lost, public opinion in England forced the British government to abandon the Right's policy of appeasement and adopt the old French policy of resistance.
text_raw:
And  finally,  when  all  these
had  been  lost,  public  opinion  in  England  forced  the  British  government  to  abandon  the
Right's  policy  of  appeasement  and  adopt  the  old  French  policy  of  resistance.

text: This change was made on a poor issue (Poland, 1939) after the possibility of using the policy of resistance had been destroyed by Britain and after France itself had almost abandoned it.
text_raw:
This  change
was  made  on  a  poor  issue  (Poland,  1939)  after  the  possibility  of  using  the  policy  of
resistance  had  been  destroyed  by  Britain  and  after  France  itself  had  almost  abandoned  it.

text: In France, as in Britain, there were changes in the foreign policies of the Right and the Left after Hitler came to power in Germany (1933).
text_raw:
In  France,  as  in  Britain,  there  were  changes  in  the  foreign  policies  of  the  Right  and  the
Left  after  Hitler  came  to  power  in  Germany  (1933).

text: The Left became more anti-German and abandoned Briand's policy of conciliation, while the Right, in some sections, sought to make a virtue of necessity and began to toy with the idea that, if Germany was to become strong anyway, a solution to the French problem of security might be found by turning Germany against the Soviet Union.
text_raw:
The  Left  became  more  anti-German
and  abandoned  Briand's  policy  of  conciliation,  while  the  Right,  in  some  sections,  sought
to  make  a  virtue  of  necessity  and  began  to  toy  with  the  idea  that,  if  Germany  was  to
become  strong  anyway,  a  solution  to  the  French  problem  of  security  might  be  found  by
turning  Germany  against  the  Soviet  Union.

text: This idea, which already had adherents in the Right in Britain, was more acceptable to the Right than to the Left in France, because, while the Right was conscious of the political threat from Germany, it was equally conscious of the social and economic threat from Bolshevism.
text_raw:
This  idea,  which  already  had  adherents  in  the
Right  in  Britain,  was  more  acceptable  to  the  Right  than  to  the  Left  in  France,  because,
while  the  Right  was  conscious  of  the  political  threat  from  Germany,  it  was  equally
conscious  of  the  social  and  economic  threat  from  Bolshevism.

text: Some members of the Right in France even went so far as to picture France as an ally of Germany in the assault on the Soviet Union.
text_raw:
Some  members  of  the
Right  in  France  even  went  so  far  as  to  picture  France  as  an  ally  of  Germany  in  the  assault

text: On the other hand, many persons of the Right in France continued to insist that the chief, or even the only, threat to France was from the danger of German aggression.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  many  persons  of  the  Right  in  France  continued  to
insist  that  the  chief,  or  even  the  only,  threat  to  France  was  from  the  danger  of  German
aggression.

text: In France, as in Britain, there appeared a double policy but only after 1935, and, even then, it was more of an attempt to pretend that France was following a policy of her own instead of a policy made in Britain than it was an attempt to pretend it was following a policy of loyalty to collective security and French allies rather than a policy of appeasement.
text_raw:
In  France,  as  in  Britain,  there  appeared  a  double  policy  but  only  after  1935,  and,  even
then,  it  was  more  of  an  attempt  to  pretend  that  France  was  following  a  policy  of  her  own
instead  of  a  policy  made  in  Britain  than  it  was  an  attempt  to  pretend  it  was  following  a
policy  of  loyalty  to  collective  security  and  French  allies  rather  than  a  policy  of
appeasement.

text: While France continued to talk of her international obligations, of collective security, and of the sanctity of treaties (especially Versailles), this was largely for public consumption, for in fact from the autumn of 1935 to the spring of 1940 France had no policy in Europe independent of Britain's policy of appeasement.
text_raw:
While  France  continued  to  talk  of  her  international  obligations,  of
collective  security,  and  of  the  sanctity  of  treaties  (especially  Versailles),  this  was  largely
for  public  consumption,  for  in  fact  from  the  autumn  of  1935  to  the  spring  of  1940  France
had  no  policy  in  Europe  independent  of  Britain's  policy  of  appeasement.

text: Thus French foreign policy in the whole period 1919-1939 was dominated by the problem of security.
text_raw:
Thus  French  foreign  policy  in  the  whole  period  1919-1939  was  dominated  by  the

text: The French feeling that they lacked security was so powerful in 1919 that they were quite willing to sacrifice the sovereignty of the French state and its freedom of action in order to get a League of Nations possessing the powers of a world government.
text_raw:
The  French  feeling  that  they  lacked  security  was  so  powerful  in  1919  that  they  were
quite  willing  to  sacrifice  the  sovereignty  of  the  French  state  and  its  freedom  of  action  in
order  to  get  a  League  of  Nations  possessing  the  powers  of  a  world  government.

text: Accordingly, at the first meeting of the League of Nations Committee at the Paris Peace Conference in 1919, the French tried to establish a League with its own army, its own general staff, and its own powers of police action against aggressors without the permission of the member states.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  at  the  first  meeting  of  the  League  of  Nations  Committee  at  the  Paris  Peace
Conference  in  1919,  the  French  tried  to  establish  a  League  with  its  own  army,  its  own
general  staff,  and  its  own  powers  of  police  action  against  aggressors  without  the
permission  of  the  member  states.

text: The Anglo-Americans were horrified at what they regarded as an inexcusable example of "power politics and militarism." They rode roughshod over the French and drew up their own draft Covenant in which there was no sacrifice of state sovereignty and where the new world organization had no powers of its own and no right to take action without the consent of the parties concerned.
text_raw:
The  Anglo-Americans  were  horrified  at  what  they
regarded  as  an  inexcusable  example  of  "power  politics  and  militarism."  They  rode
roughshod  over  the  French  and  drew  up  their  own  draft  Covenant  in  which  there  was  no
sacrifice  of  state  sovereignty  and  where  the  new  world  organization  had  no  powers  of  its
own  and  no  right  to  take  action  without  the  consent  of  the  parties  concerned.

text: War was not outlawed but merely subjected to certain procedural delays in making it, nor were peaceful procedures for settling international disputes made compulsory but instead were merely provided for those who wished to use them.
text_raw:
War  was  not
outlawed  but  merely  subjected  to  certain  procedural  delays  in  making  it,  nor  were
peaceful  procedures  for  settling  international  disputes  made  compulsory  but  instead  were
merely  provided  for  those  who  wished  to  use  them.

text: Finally, no real political sanctions were provided to force nations to use peaceful procedures or even to use the delaying procedures of the Covenant itself.
text_raw:
Finally,  no  real  political  sanctions
were  provided  to  force  nations  to  use  peaceful  procedures  or  even  to  use  the  delaying
procedures  of  the  Covenant  itself.

text: Economic sanctions were expected to be used by member nations against aggressor states which violated the delaying procedures of the Covenant, but no military sanctions could be used except as contributed by each state itself.
text_raw:
Economic  sanctions  were  expected  to  be  used  by
member  nations  against  aggressor  states  which  violated  the  delaying  procedures  of  the
Covenant,  but  no  military  sanctions  could  be  used  except  as  contributed  by  each  state
itself.

text: The League was thus far from being a world government, although both its friends and its enemies, for opposite reasons, tried to pretend that it was more powerful, and more important, than it really was.
text_raw:
The  League  was  thus  far  from  being  a  world  government,  although  both  its  friends
and  its  enemies,  for  opposite  reasons,  tried  to  pretend  that  it  was  more  powerful,  and
more  important,  than  it  really  was.

text: The Covenant, especially the critical articles 1 o- 16, had been worded by a skillful British lawyer, Cecil Hurst, who filled it with loopholes cleverly concealed under a mass of impressive verbiage, so that no state's freedom of action was vitally restricted by the document.
text_raw:
The  Covenant,  especially  the  critical  articles  1  o-  16,
had  been  worded  by  a  skillful  British  lawyer,  Cecil  Hurst,  who  filled  it  with  loopholes
cleverly  concealed  under  a  mass  of  impressive  verbiage,  so  that  no  state's  freedom  of
action  was  vitally  restricted  by  the  document.

text: The politicians knew this, although it was not widely publicized and, from the beginning, those states which wanted a real international organization began to seek to amend the Covenant, to "plug the loopholes" in it.
text_raw:
The  politicians  knew  this,  although  it  was
not  widely  publicized  and,  from  the  beginning,  those  states  which  wanted  a  real
international  organization  began  to  seek  to  amend  the  Covenant,  to  "plug  the  loopholes"
in  it.

text: Any real international political organization needed three things:
text_raw: Any  real  international  political  organization  needed  three  things:

text: (1) peaceful procedures for settling all disputes, (2) outlawry of non-peaceful procedures for this purpose, and (3) effective military sanctions to compel use of the peaceful procedures and to prevent the use of warlike procedures.
text_raw:
(1)  peaceful
procedures  for  settling  all  disputes,  (2)  outlawry  of  non-peaceful  procedures  for  this
purpose,  and  (3)  effective  military  sanctions  to  compel  use  of  the  peaceful  procedures  and
to  prevent  the  use  of  warlike  procedures.

text: The League of Nations consisted of three parts:
text_raw: The  League  of  Nations  consisted  of  three  parts:

text: (1) the Assembly of all members of the League, meeting generally in September of each year;
text_raw:

text: Conceived in the same London circles which had been opposing France, supporting Germany, and sabotaging the League, the Locarno Pacts were the result of a complex international intrigue in which General Smuts played a chief role.

text: On the face of it, these agreements appeared to guarantee the Rhine frontiers, to provide peaceful procedures for all disputes between Germany and her neighbors, and to admit Germany to the League of Nations on a basis of equality with the Great Powers.
text_raw:
On  the  face  of  it,  these  agreements
appeared  to  guarantee  the  Rhine  frontiers,  to  provide  peaceful  procedures  for  all  disputes
between  Germany  and  her  neighbors,  and  to  admit  Germany  to  the  League  of  Nations  on
a  basis  of  equality  with  the  Great  Powers.

text: The Pacts consisted of nine documents of which four were arbitration treaties between Germany and her neighbors (Belgium, France, Poland and Czechoslovakia); two were treaties between France and her eastern allies (Poland and Czechoslovakia); the seventh was a note releasing Germany from any need to apply the sanctions clause of the Covenant against any aggressor nation on the grounds that Germany, being disarmed by the Treaty of Versailles, could not be expected to assume the same obligations as other members of the League; the eighth document v.:as a general introduction to the Pacts j and the ninth document was the "Rhine Pact," the real heart of the agreement.

The  Pacts  consisted  of  nine  documents  of
which  four  were  arbitration  treaties  between  Germany  and  her  neighbors  (Belgium,
France,  Poland  and  Czechoslovakia);  two  were  treaties  between  France  and  her  eastern

need  to  apply  the  sanctions  clause  of  the  Covenant  against  any  aggressor  nation  on  the
grounds  that  Germany,  being  disarmed  by  the  Treaty  of  Versailles,  could  not  be  expected
to  assume  the  same  obligations  as  other  members  of  the  League;  the  eighth  document
v.:as  a  general  introduction  to  the  Pacts  j  and  the  ninth  document  was  the  "Rhine  Pact,"

text: This "Rhine Pact" guaranteed the frontier between Germany and Belgium-France against attack from either side.
text_raw:
This  "Rhine  Pact"  guaranteed  the  frontier  between
Germany  and  Belgium-France  against  attack  from  either  side.

text: The guarantee was signed by Britain and Italy, as well as by the three states directly concerned, and covered the demilitarized condition of the Rhineland as established in 1919.

The  guarantee  was  signed

text: This meant that if any one of the three frontier Powers violated the frontier or the demilitarized zone, this violation would bring the four other Powers into action against the violator.

text: The Locarno Pacts were designed by Britain to give France the security against Germany on the Rhine which France so urgently desired and at the same time (since the guarantee worked both ways) to prevent France from ever occupying the Ruhr or any other part of Germany, as had been done over the violent objections of Britain in 1923- 1924.
text_raw:
The  Locarno  Pacts  were  designed  by  Britain  to  give  France  the  security  against
Germany  on  the  Rhine  which  France  so  urgently  desired  and  at  the  same  time  (since  the
guarantee  worked  both  ways)  to  prevent  France  from  ever  occupying  the  Ruhr  or  any
other  part  of  Germany,  as  had  been  done  over  the  violent  objections  of  Britain  in  1923-
1924.

text: Moreover, by refusing to guarantee Germany's eastern frontier with Poland and Czechoslovakia, Britain established in law the distinction between peace in the east and peace in the west, on which she had been insisting since 1919, and greatly weakened the French alliances with Poland and Czechoslovakia by making it almost impossible for France to honor her alliances with these two countries or to put pressure on Germany in the west if Germany began to put pressure on these French allies in the east, unless Britain consented.
text_raw:
Moreover,  by  refusing  to  guarantee  Germany's  eastern  frontier  with  Poland  and
Czechoslovakia,  Britain  established  in  law  the  distinction  between  peace  in  the  east  and
peace  in  the  west,  on  which  she  had  been  insisting  since  1919,  and  greatly  weakened  the
French  alliances  with  Poland  and  Czechoslovakia  by  making  it  almost  impossible  for
France  to  honor  her  alliances  with  these  two  countries  or  to  put  pressure  on  Germany  in
the  west  if  Germany  began  to  put  pressure  on  these  French  allies  in  the  east,  unless
Britain  consented.

text: Thus, the Locarno Pacts, which were presented at the time throughout the English-speaking world as a sensational contribution to the peace and stability of Europe, really formed the background for the events of 1938 when Czechoslovakia was destroyed at Munich.
text_raw:
Thus,  the  Locarno  Pacts,  which  were  presented  at  the  time  throughout
the  English-speaking  world  as  a  sensational  contribution  to  the  peace  and  stability  of
Europe,  really  formed  the  background  for  the  events  of  1938  when  Czechoslovakia  was
destroyed  at  Munich.

text: The only reason why France accepted the Locarno Pacts was that they guaranteed explicitly the demilitarized condition of the Rhineland.

they  guaranteed  explicitly  the  demilitarized  condition  of  the  Rhineland.

text: So long as this condition continued, France held a complete veto over any movement of Germany either east or west because Germany's chief industrial districts in the Ruhr were unprotected.

text: Unfortunately, as we have indicated, when the guarantee of Locarno became due in March 1936 Britain dishonored its agreement, the Rhine was remilitarized, and the way was opened for Germany to move eastward.

Unfortunately,  as  we  have  indicated,  when  the  guarantee  of  Locarno  became  due  in

text: Poland protested violently, issued a long legal justification of her own frontiers, sent her foreign minister to take up residence in Paris, and signed three agreements with Czechoslovakia (ending the dispute over Teschen, as well as a commercial treaty and an arbitration convention).

text: The Kellogg-Briand Pact (1928) was a weak and rather hypocritical document and advanced further toward the destruction of international law as it had existed in 1900.

The  Kellogg-Briand  Pact  (1928)  was  a  weak  and  rather  hypocritical  document  and

text: We have seen that the First World War did much to destroy the legal distinctions between belligerents and neutrals and between combatants and noncombatants.

have  seen  that  the  First  World  War  did  much  to  destroy  the  legal  distinctions  between

text: The Kellogg- Briand Pact took one of the first steps toward destroying the legal distinction between war and peace, since the Powers, having renounced the use of war, began to wage wars without declaring them, as was done by Japan in China in 1937, by Italy in Spain in 1936-1939, and by everyone in Korea in 1950.
text_raw:
The  Kellogg-
Briand  Pact  took  one  of  the  first  steps  toward  destroying  the  legal  distinction  between
war  and  peace,  since  the  Powers,  having  renounced  the  use  of  war,  began  to  wage  wars
without  declaring  them,  as  was  done  by  Japan  in  China  in  1937,  by  Italy  in  Spain  in
1936-1939,  and  by  everyone  in  Korea  in  1950.

text: The Kellogg-Briand Pact was signed by fifteen nations which were invited to do so, while forty-eight nations were invited to adhere to its terms.

text: The Litvinoff Protocol was one of the first concrete evidences of a shift in Soviet foreign policy which occurred about 1927-1928 Previously, Russia had refused to cooperate with any system of collective security or disarmament on the grounds that these were just "capitalistic tricks." text: The "realists," on the other hand, including most of the countries in Europe, led by France and the Little Entente, argued that armaments are caused by war and the fear of war and that the proper way to disarm is to make nations secure.

text: The reasons for this difference of opinion are to be found in the fact that the nations which advocated the direct method, like Britain, the United States, and Japan, already had security and could proceed directly to the problem of disarmament, while the nations which felt insecure were bound to seek security before they would bind themselves to reduce the armaments they had.

task  of  reaching  a  disarmament  agreement  was  turned  over  to  a  purely  technical  group,
the  Permanent  Advisory  Commission  on  Disarmament  of  the  League  of  Nations.

text: This group, which consisted exclusively of officers of the various armed services, was unable to reach agreement on any important issues: it could not find any method of measuring armaments or even of defining them; it could not distinguish actual from potential armaments or defensive from offensive.
text_raw:
This
group,  which  consisted  exclusively  of  officers  of  the  various  armed  services,  was  unable

armaments  or  even  of  defining  them;  it  could  not  distinguish  actual  from  potential

text: The Japanese were already attacking China; the French and Germans were deadlocked in a violent controversy, the former insisting on security and the latter on arms equality; and the world depression was growing steadily worse, with several governments coming to believe that only a policy of government spending (including spending on arms) could provide the purchasing power needed for economic revival.

(including  spending  on  arms)  could  provide  the  purchasing  power  needed  for  economic

text: Once again, the French desire for an international police force was rebuffed, although supported by seventeen states; the British desire to outlaw certain "aggressive" armaments (like gas, submarines, and bombing planes) was rejected by the French, although accepted by thirty states (including the Soviet Union and Italy).

text: Scheme to Enrich Themselves
text_raw: Scheme  to  Enrich  Themselves

text: The attitudes of bankers were revealed most clearly in England, where every move was dictated by efforts to protect their own position and to profit from it rather than by considerations of economic mobilization for war or the welfare of the British people.
text_raw:
The  attitudes  of  bankers  were  revealed  most  clearly  in  England,  where  every  move
was  dictated  by  efforts  to  protect  their  own  position  and  to  profit  from  it  rather  than  by
considerations  of  economic  mobilization  for  war  or  the  welfare  of  the  British  people.

text: The outbreak of war on August 4, 1914, found the British banking system insolvent in the sense that its funds, created by the banking system for profit and rented out to the economic system to permit it to operate, could not be covered by the existing volume of gold reserves or by collateral which could be liquidated rapidly.
text_raw:
The
outbreak  of  war  on  August  4,  1914,  found  the  British  banking  system  insolvent  in  the
sense  that  its  funds,  created  by  the  banking  system  for  profit  and  rented  out  to  the
economic  system  to  permit  it  to  operate,  could  not  be  covered  by  the  existing  volume  of
gold  reserves  or  by  collateral  which  could  be  liquidated  rapidly.

text: Accordingly, the bankers secretly devised a scheme by which their obligations could be met by fiat money (so- called Treasury Notes), but, as soon as that crisis was over, they then insisted that the government must pay for the war without recourse to fiat money (which was always damned by bankers as immoral), but by taxation and by borrowing at high interest rates from bankers.
