export  of  gold  were  suspended,  but  every  effort  was  made  to  keep  gold  reserves  up  to  a
respectable  percentage  of  notes,  and  exchanges  were  controlled  to  keep  them  as  near
parity  as  possible.

text: These attributes were achieved in some cases by deceptive methods.
text_raw: These  attributes  were  achieved  in  some  cases  by  deceptive  methods.

text: In Britain, for example, the gold reserve against notes fell from 52 percent to 18 percent in the month July- August 1914; then the situation was concealed, partly by moving assets of local banks into the Bank of England and using them as reserves for both, partly by issuing a new kind of notes (called Currency Notes) which had no real reserve and little gold backing.
text_raw:
In
Britain,  for  example,  the  gold  reserve  against  notes  fell  from  52  percent  to  18  percent  in
the  month  July- August  1914;  then  the  situation  was  concealed,  partly  by  moving  assets  of
local  banks  into  the  Bank  of  England  and  using  them  as  reserves  for  both,  partly  by
issuing  a  new  kind  of  notes  (called  Currency  Notes)  which  had  no  real  reserve  and  little
gold  backing.

text: In the United States the percentage of reserves required by law in commercial banks was reduced in 1914, and the reserve requirements both for notes and deposits were cut in June 1917; a new system of "depositary banks" was set up which required no reserves against government deposits created in them in return for government bonds.
text_raw:
In  the  United  States  the  percentage  of  reserves  required  by  law  in
commercial  banks  was  reduced  in  1914,  and  the  reserve  requirements  both  for  notes  and
deposits  were  cut  in  June  1917;  a  new  system  of  "depositary  banks"  was  set  up  which
required  no  reserves  against  government  deposits  created  in  them  in  return  for
government  bonds.

text: Such efforts were made in all countries, but everywhere the ratio of gold reserves to notes fell drastically during the war: in France from 60 percent to 1 1 percent; in Germany from 59 percent to 10 percent; in Russia from 98 percent to 2 percent; in Italy from 60 percent to 13 percent; in Britain from 53 percent to 32 percent.
text_raw:
Such  efforts  were  made  in  all  countries,  but  everywhere  the  ratio  of
gold  reserves  to  notes  fell  drastically  during  the  war:  in  France  from  60  percent  to  1 1
percent;  in  Germany  from  59  percent  to  10  percent;  in  Russia  from  98  percent  to  2
percent;  in  Italy  from  60  percent  to  13  percent;  in  Britain  from  53  percent  to  32  percent.

text: Inflation and Public Debts Continue after the War
text_raw: Inflation  and  Public  Debts  Continue  after  the  War

text: The inflation and increase in public debts continued after the war ended.
text_raw: The  inflation  and  increase  in  public  debts  continued  after  the  war  ended.

text: The causes for this were complicated, and varied from country to country.
text_raw:
The  causes
for  this  were  complicated,  and  varied  from  country  to  country.

text: In general, (1) price fixing and rationing regulations were ended too soon, before the output of peacetime goods had risen to a level high enough to absorb the accumulated purchasing power in the hands of consumers from their efforts in war production; thus, the slowness of reconversion from war production to peace production caused a short supply at a time of high demand;
text_raw:
In  general,  (1)  price  fixing
and  rationing  regulations  were  ended  too  soon,  before  the  output  of  peacetime  goods  had
risen  to  a  level  high  enough  to  absorb  the  accumulated  purchasing  power  in  the  hands  of
consumers  from  their  efforts  in  war  production;  thus,  the  slowness  of  reconversion  from
war  production  to  peace  production  caused  a  short  supply  at  a  time  of  high  demand;

text: (2) the Allied exchanges, which had been controlled during the war, were unpegged in March 1919 and at once fell to levels revealing the great price disequilibrium between countries;
text_raw:
(2)
the  Allied  exchanges,  which  had  been  controlled  during  the  war,  were  unpegged  in
March  1919  and  at  once  fell  to  levels  revealing  the  great  price  disequilibrium  between
countries;

text: (3) purchasing power held back during the war suddenly came into the market;
text_raw: (3)  purchasing  power  held  back  during  the  war  suddenly  came  into  the  market;

text: (4) there was an expansion of bank credit because of postwar optimism;
text_raw: (4)  there  was  an  expansion  of  bank  credit  because  of  postwar  optimism;

text: (5) budgets remained out of balance because of reconstruction requirements (as in France or Belgium), reparations (as in Germany), demobilization expenses (as in the United States, Italy, and so on); and (6) production of peacetime goods was disrupted by revolutions (as in Hungary, Russia, and so on) or strikes (as in the United States, Italy, France, and so on).
text_raw:
(5)  budgets
remained  out  of  balance  because  of  reconstruction  requirements  (as  in  France  or
Belgium),  reparations  (as  in  Germany),  demobilization  expenses  (as  in  the  United  States,
Italy,  and  so  on);  and  (6)  production  of  peacetime  goods  was  disrupted  by  revolutions  (as
in  Hungary,  Russia,  and  so  on)  or  strikes  (as  in  the  United  States,  Italy,  France,  and  so
on).

text: Postwar Inflation Had Evil Results
text_raw: Postwar  Inflation  Had  Evil  Results

text: Unfortunately, this postwar inflation, which could have accomplished much good (by increasing output of real wealth) was wasted (by increasing prices of existing goods) and had evil results (by destroying capital accumulations and savings, and overturning economic class lines).
text_raw:
Unfortunately,  this  postwar  inflation,  which  could  have  accomplished  much  good  (by
increasing  output  of  real  wealth)  was  wasted  (by  increasing  prices  of  existing  goods)  and
had  evil  results  (by  destroying  capital  accumulations  and  savings,  and  overturning
economic  class  lines).

text: This failure was caused by the fact that the inflation, though unwanted everywhere, was uncontrolled because few persons in positions of power had the courage to take the steps necessary to curtail it.
text_raw:
This  failure  was  caused  by  the  fact  that  the  inflation,  though
unwanted  everywhere,  was  uncontrolled  because  few  persons  in  positions  of  power  had
the  courage  to  take  the  steps  necessary  to  curtail  it.

text: In the defeated and revolutionary countries (Russia, Poland, Hungary, Austria, and Germany), the inflation went so far that the former monetary units became valueless, and ceased to exist.
text_raw:
In  the  defeated  and  revolutionary
countries  (Russia,  Poland,  Hungary,  Austria,  and  Germany),  the  inflation  went  so  far  that
the  former  monetary  units  became  valueless,  and  ceased  to  exist.

text: In a second group of countries (like France, Belgium, and Italy), the value of the monetary unit was so reduced that it became a different thing, although the same name was still used.
text_raw:
In  a  second  group  of
countries  (like  France,  Belgium,  and  Italy),  the  value  of  the  monetary  unit  was  so  reduced
that  it  became  a  different  thing,  although  the  same  name  was  still  used.

text: In a third group of countries (Britain, the United States, and Japan), the situation was kept under control.
text_raw:
In  a  third  group  of
countries  (Britain,  the  United  States,  and  Japan),  the  situation  was  kept  under  control.

text: Public Debt and Economic Depression in America
text_raw: Public  Debt  and  Economic  Depression  in  America

text: As far as Europe was concerned, the intensity of the inflation increased as one moved geographically from west to east.
text_raw:
As  far  as  Europe  was  concerned,  the  intensity  of  the  inflation  increased  as  one  moved
geographically  from  west  to  east.

text: Of the three groups of countries above, the second (moderate inflation) group was the most fortunate.
text_raw:
Of  the  three  groups  of  countries  above,  the  second
(moderate  inflation)  group  was  the  most  fortunate.

text: In the first (extreme inflation) group the inflation wiped out all public debts, all savings, and all claims on wealth, since the monetary unit became valueless.
text_raw:
In  the  first  (extreme  inflation)  group
the  inflation  wiped  out  all  public  debts,  all  savings,  and  all  claims  on  wealth,  since  the
monetary  unit  became  valueless.

text: In the moderate-inflation group, the burden of the public debt was reduced, and private debts and savings were reduced by the same proportion.
text_raw:
In  the  moderate-inflation  group,  the  burden  of  the  public
debt  was  reduced,  and  private  debts  and  savings  were  reduced  by  the  same  proportion.

text: In the United States and Britain the effort to fight inflation took the form of a deliberate movement toward deflation.
text_raw:
In
the  United  States  and  Britain  the  effort  to  fight  inflation  took  the  form  of  a  deliberate
movement  toward  deflation.

text: This preserved savings but increased the burden of the public debt and gave economic depression.
text_raw:
This  preserved  savings  but  increased  the  burden  of  the
public  debt  and  gave  economic  depression.

text: As soon as the war was finished, governments began to turn their attention to the problem of restoring the prewar financial system.
text_raw:
As  soon  as  the  war  was  finished,  governments  began  to  turn  their  attention  to  the
problem  of  restoring  the  prewar  financial  system.

text: Since the essential element in that system was believed to be the gold standard with its stable exchanges, this movement was called "stabilization." Because of their eagerness to restore the prewar financial situation, the "experts" closed their eyes to the tremendous changes which had resulted from the war.
text_raw:
Since  the  essential  element  in  that
system  was  believed  to  be  the  gold  standard  with  its  stable  exchanges,  this  movement
was  called  "stabilization."  Because  of  their  eagerness  to  restore  the  prewar  financial
situation,  the  "experts"  closed  their  eyes  to  the  tremendous  changes  which  had  resulted
from  the  war.

text: These changes were so great in production, in commerce, and in financial habits that any effort to restore the prewar conditions or even stabilize on the gold standard was impossible and inadvisable.
text_raw:
These  changes  were  so  great  in  production,  in  commerce,  and  in  financial
habits  that  any  effort  to  restore  the  prewar  conditions  or  even  stabilize  on  the  gold
standard  was  impossible  and  inadvisable.

text: Instead of seeking a financial system adapted to the new economic and commercial world which had emerged from the war, the experts tried to ignore this world, and established a financial system which looked, superficially, as much like the prewar system as possible.
text_raw:
Instead  of  seeking  a  financial  system  adapted  to
the  new  economic  and  commercial  world  which  had  emerged  from  the  war,  the  experts
tried  to  ignore  this  world,  and  established  a  financial  system  which  looked,  superficially,
as  much  like  the  prewar  system  as  possible.

text: This system, however, was not the prewar system.
text_raw:
This  system,  however,  was  not  the  prewar
system.

text: Neither was it adapted to the new economic conditions.
text_raw: Neither  was  it  adapted  to  the  new  economic  conditions.

text: When the experts began to have vague glimmerings of this last fact, they did not begin to modify their goals, but insisted on the same goals, and voiced incantations and exhortations against the existing conditions which made the attainment of their goals impossible.
text_raw:
When  the  experts  began
to  have  vague  glimmerings  of  this  last  fact,  they  did  not  begin  to  modify  their  goals,  but
insisted  on  the  same  goals,  and  voiced  incantations  and  exhortations  against  the  existing
conditions  which  made  the  attainment  of  their  goals  impossible.

text: These changed economic conditions could not be controlled or exorcised by incantations.
text_raw:
These  changed  economic  conditions  could  not  be  controlled  or  exorcised  by
incantations.

text: They were basically not results of the war at all, but normal outcomes of the economic development of the world in the nineteenth century.
text_raw:
They  were  basically  not  results  of  the  war  at  all,  but  normal  outcomes  of  the
economic  development  of  the  world  in  the  nineteenth  century.

text: All that the war had done
text_raw: All  that  the  war  had  done

text: was to speed up the rate of this development.
text_raw: was  to  speed  up  the  rate  of  this  development.

text: The economic changes which in 1925 made it so difficult to restore the financial system of 1914 were already discernible in 1890 and clearly evident by 1910.
text_raw:
The  economic  changes  which  in  1925  made
it  so  difficult  to  restore  the  financial  system  of  1914  were  already  discernible  in  1890  and
clearly  evident  by  1910.

text: Britain's Supremacy as the Financial Center of the World Is Threatened
text_raw:
Britain's  Supremacy  as  the  Financial  Center  of  the
World  Is  Threatened

text: The chief item in these changes was the decline of Britain.
text_raw: The  chief  item  in  these  changes  was  the  decline  of  Britain.

text: What had happened was that the Industrial Revolution was spreading beyond Britain to Europe and the United States and by 1910 to South America and Asia.
text_raw:
What  had  happened  was
that  the  Industrial  Revolution  was  spreading  beyond  Britain  to  Europe  and  the  United
States  and  by  1910  to  South  America  and  Asia.

text: As a result, these areas became less dependent on Britain for manufactured goods, less eager to sell their raw materials and food products to her, and became her competitors both in selling to and in buying from those colonial areas to which industrialism had not yet spread.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  these  areas  became  less
dependent  on  Britain  for  manufactured  goods,  less  eager  to  sell  their  raw  materials  and
food  products  to  her,  and  became  her  competitors  both  in  selling  to  and  in  buying  from
those  colonial  areas  to  which  industrialism  had  not  yet  spread.

text: By 1914 Britain's supremacy as financial center, as commercial market, as creditor, and as merchant shipper was being threatened.
text_raw:
By  1914  Britain's
supremacy  as  financial  center,  as  commercial  market,  as  creditor,  and  as  merchant
shipper  was  being  threatened.

text: A less obvious threat arose from long-run shifts in demand â€” shifts from the products of heavy industry to the products of more highly specialized branches of production (like chemicals), from cereals to fruits and dairy products, from cotton and wool to silk and rayon, from leather to rubber, and so on.
text_raw:
A  less  obvious  threat  arose  from  long-run  shifts  in
demand â€” shifts  from  the  products  of  heavy  industry  to  the  products  of  more  highly
specialized  branches  of  production  (like  chemicals),  from  cereals  to  fruits  and  dairy
products,  from  cotton  and  wool  to  silk  and  rayon,  from  leather  to  rubber,  and  so  on.

text: These changes presented Britain with a fundamental choice â€” either to yield her supremacy in the world or reform her industrial and commercial system to cope with the new conditions.
text_raw:
These  changes  presented  Britain  with  a  fundamental  choice â€” either  to  yield  her
supremacy  in  the  world  or  reform  her  industrial  and  commercial  system  to  cope  with  the
new  conditions.

text: The latter was difficult because Britain had allowed her industrial system to become lopsided under the influence of free trade and international division of labor.
text_raw:
The  latter  was  difficult  because  Britain  had  allowed  her  industrial  system
to  become  lopsided  under  the  influence  of  free  trade  and  international  division  of  labor.

text: Over half the employed persons in Britain were engaged in the manufacture of textiles and ferrous metals.
text_raw:
Over  half  the  employed  persons  in  Britain  were  engaged  in  the  manufacture  of  textiles
and  ferrous  metals.

text: Textiles accounted for over one-third of her exports, and textiles, along with iron and steel, for over one-half.
text_raw:
Textiles  accounted  for  over  one-third  of  her  exports,  and  textiles,
along  with  iron  and  steel,  for  over  one-half.

text: At the same time, newer industrial nations (Germany, the United States, and Japan) were growing rapidly with industrial systems better adapted to the trend of the times; and these were also cutting deeply into Britain's supremacy in merchant shipping.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  newer  industrial  nations
(Germany,  the  United  States,  and  Japan)  were  growing  rapidly  with  industrial  systems
better  adapted  to  the  trend  of  the  times;  and  these  were  also  cutting  deeply  into  Britain's
supremacy  in  merchant  shipping.

text: America Becomes the World's Greatest Creditor
text_raw: America  Becomes  the  World's  Greatest  Creditor

text: At this critical stage in Britain's development, the World War occurred.
text_raw: At  this  critical  stage  in  Britain's  development,  the  World  War  occurred.

text: This had a double result as far as this subject is concerned.
text_raw:
This  had  a
double  result  as  far  as  this  subject  is  concerned.

text: It forced Britain to postpone indefinitely any reform of her industrial system to adjust it to more modern trends; and it speeded up the development of these trends so that what might have occurred in twenty years was done instead in five.
text_raw:
It  forced  Britain  to  postpone  indefinitely
any  reform  of  her  industrial  system  to  adjust  it  to  more  modern  trends;  and  it  speeded  up
the  development  of  these  trends  so  that  what  might  have  occurred  in  twenty  years  was
done  instead  in  five.

text: In the period 1910-1920, Britain's merchant fleet fell by 6 percent in number of vessels, while that of the United States went up 57 percent, that of Japan up 130 percent, and that of the Netherlands up 58 percent.
text_raw:
In  the  period  1910-1920,  Britain's  merchant  fleet  fell  by  6  percent  in
number  of  vessels,  while  that  of  the  United  States  went  up  57  percent,  that  of  Japan  up
130  percent,  and  that  of  the  Netherlands  up  58  percent.

text: Her position as the world's greatest creditor was lost to the United States, and a large quantity of good foreign credits was replaced by a smaller amount of poorer risks.
text_raw:
Her  position  as  the  world's
greatest  creditor  was  lost  to  the  United  States,  and  a  large  quantity  of  good  foreign  credits
was  replaced  by  a  smaller  amount  of  poorer  risks.

text: In addition, she became a debtor to the United States to the amount of over $4 billion.
text_raw:
In  addition,  she  became  a  debtor  to  the
United  States  to  the  amount  of  over  $4  billion.

text: The change in the positions of the two countries can be summarized briefly.
text_raw:
The  change  in  the  positions  of  the  two
countries  can  be  summarized  briefly.

text: The war changed the position of the United States in respect to the rest of the world from that of a debtor owing about $3 billion to that of a creditor owed $4 billion.
text_raw:
The  war  changed  the  position  of  the  United  States
in  respect  to  the  rest  of  the  world  from  that  of  a  debtor  owing  about  $3  billion  to  that  of  a
creditor  owed  $4  billion.

text: This does not include intergovernmental debts of about $10 billion owed to the United States as a result of the war.
text_raw:
This  does  not  include  intergovernmental  debts  of  about  $10
billion  owed  to  the  United  States  as  a  result  of  the  war.

text: At the same time, Britain's
text_raw: At  the  same  time,  Britain's

text: position changed from a creditor owed about $18 billion to a creditor owed about $13.5 billion.
text_raw:
position  changed  from  a  creditor  owed  about  $18  billion  to  a  creditor  owed  about  $13.5
billion.

text: In addition, Britain was owed about $8 billion in war debts from her Allies and an unknown sum in reparations from Germany, and owed to the United States war debts of well over 54 billion.
text_raw:
In  addition,  Britain  was  owed  about  $8  billion  in  war  debts  from  her  Allies  and  an
unknown  sum  in  reparations  from  Germany,  and  owed  to  the  United  States  war  debts  of
well  over  54  billion.

text: Most of these war debts and reparations were sharply reduced after 1920, but the net result for Britain was a drastic change in her position in respect to the United States.
text_raw:
Most  of  these  war  debts  and  reparations  were  sharply  reduced  after
1920,  but  the  net  result  for  Britain  was  a  drastic  change  in  her  position  in  respect  to  the
United  States.

text: Modification of the Basic Economic Organization of the World
text_raw: Modification  of  the  Basic  Economic  Organization  of  the  World

text: The basic economic organization of the world was modified in other ways.
text_raw: The  basic  economic  organization  of  the  world  was  modified  in  other  ways.

text: As a result of the war, the old organization of relatively free commerce among countries specializing in different types of production was replaced by a situation in which a larger number of countries sought economic self-sufficiency by placing restrictions on commerce.
text_raw:
As  a  result
of  the  war,  the  old  organization  of  relatively  free  commerce  among  countries  specializing
in  different  types  of  production  was  replaced  by  a  situation  in  which  a  larger  number  of
countries  sought  economic  self-sufficiency  by  placing  restrictions  on  commerce.

text: In addition, productive capacity in both agriculture and industry had been increased by the artificial demand of the war period to a degree far beyond the ability of normal domestic demand to buy the products of that capacity.
text_raw:
In
addition,  productive  capacity  in  both  agriculture  and  industry  had  been  increased  by  the
artificial  demand  of  the  war  period  to  a  degree  far  beyond  the  ability  of  normal  domestic
demand  to  buy  the  products  of  that  capacity.

text: And, finally, the more backward areas of Europe and the world had been industrialized to a great degree and were unwilling to fall back to a position in which they would obtain industrial products from Britain, Germany, or the United States in return for their raw materials and food.
text_raw:
And,  finally,  the  more  backward  areas  of
Europe  and  the  world  had  been  industrialized  to  a  great  degree  and  were  unwilling  to  fall
back  to  a  position  in  which  they  would  obtain  industrial  products  from  Britain,  Germany,
or  the  United  States  in  return  for  their  raw  materials  and  food.

text: This refusal was made more painful for both sides by the fact that these backward areas had increased their outputs of raw materials and food so greatly that the total could hardly have been sold even if they had been willing to buy all their industrial products from their prewar sources.
text_raw:
This  refusal  was  made
more  painful  for  both  sides  by  the  fact  that  these  backward  areas  had  increased  their
outputs  of  raw  materials  and  food  so  greatly  that  the  total  could  hardly  have  been  sold
even  if  they  had  been  willing  to  buy  all  their  industrial  products  from  their  prewar
sources.

text: These prewar sources in turn had increased their industrial capacity so greatly that the product could hardly have been sold if they had been able to recapture entirely all their prewar markets.
text_raw:
These  prewar  sources  in  turn  had  increased  their  industrial  capacity  so  greatly
that  the  product  could  hardly  have  been  sold  if  they  had  been  able  to  recapture  entirely  all
their  prewar  markets.

text: The result was a situation where all countries were eager to sell and reluctant to buy, and sought to achieve these mutually irreconcilable ends by setting up subsidies and bounties on exports, tariffs, and restrictions on imports, with disastrous results on world trade.
text_raw:
The  result  was  a  situation  where  all  countries  were  eager  to  sell  and
reluctant  to  buy,  and  sought  to  achieve  these  mutually  irreconcilable  ends  by  setting  up
subsidies  and  bounties  on  exports,  tariffs,  and  restrictions  on  imports,  with  disastrous
results  on  world  trade.

text: The only sensible solution to this problem of excessive productive capacity would have been a substantial rise in domestic standards of living, but this would have required a fundamental reapportionment of the national income so that claims to the product of the excess capacity would go to those masses eager to consume, rather than continue to go to the minority desiring to save.
text_raw:
The  only  sensible  solution  to  this  problem  of  excessive  productive
capacity  would  have  been  a  substantial  rise  in  domestic  standards  of  living,  but  this
would  have  required  a  fundamental  reapportionment  of  the  national  income  so  that  claims
to  the  product  of  the  excess  capacity  would  go  to  those  masses  eager  to  consume,  rather
than  continue  to  go  to  the  minority  desiring  to  save.

text: Such a reform was rejected by the ruling groups in both "advanced" and "backward" countries, so that this solution was reached only to a relatively small degree in a relatively few countries (chiefly the United States and Germany in the period 1925-1929)
text_raw:
Such  a  reform  was  rejected  by  the
ruling  groups  in  both  "advanced"  and  "backward"  countries,  so  that  this  solution  was
reached  only  to  a  relatively  small  degree  in  a  relatively  few  countries  (chiefly  the  United
States  and  Germany  in  the  period  1925-1929)

text: International Bankers Began to Set Gold Aside
text_raw: International  Bankers  Began  to  Set  Gold  Aside

text: Changes in the basic productive and commercial organization of the world in the period 1914-1919 were made more difficult to adjust by other less tangible changes in financial practices and business psychology.
text_raw:
Changes  in  the  basic  productive  and  commercial  organization  of  the  world  in  the
period  1914-1919  were  made  more  difficult  to  adjust  by  other  less  tangible  changes  in
financial  practices  and  business  psychology.

text: The spectacular postwar inflations in eastern Europe had intensified the traditional fear of inflation among bankers.

text: And they who control the credit of the nation direct the policy of Governments and hold in the hollow of their hands the destiny of the people." In that same year, Sir Drummond Fraser, vice-president of the Institute of Bankers, stated, "The Governor of the Bank of England must be the autocrat who dictates the terms upon which alone the Government can obtain borrowed money." On September 26, 1921, The Financial Times wrote, "Half a dozen men at the top of the Big Five Banks could upset the whole fabric of government finance by refraining from renewing Treasury Bills." Vincent Vickers, who had been a director of the bank for nine years, said, "Since 1919 the monetary policy of the Government has been the policy of the Bank of England and the policy of the Bank of England has been the policy of Mr. Montagu Norman." On November II, 1927, the Wall Street Journal called Mr. Norman "the currency dictator of Europe." This fact was admitted by Mr. Norman himself before the court of the bank on March 21, 1930, and before the Macmillan Committee five days later.

text: In the 1920's, they were determined to use the financial power of Britain and of the United States to force all the major countries of the world to go on the gold standard and to operate it through central banks free from all political control, with all questions of international finance to be settled by agreements by such central banks without interference from governments.
text_raw:
In  the  1920's,  they  were  determined  to  use  the  financial  power  of  Britain  and  of  the
United  States  to  force  all  the  major  countries  of  the  world  to  go  on  the  gold  standard  and
to  operate  it  through  central  banks  free  from  all  political  control,  with  all  questions  of
international  finance  to  be  settled  by  agreements  by  such  central  banks  without
interference  from  governments.

text: Norman and Strong Were Mere Agents of the Powerful Bankers Who Remained Behind the Scenes and Operated in Secret
text_raw:
Norman  and  Strong  Were  Mere  Agents  of  the  Powerful  Bankers
Who  Remained  Behind  the  Scenes  and  Operated  in  Secret

text: It must not be felt that these heads of the world's chief central banks were themselves substantive powers in world finance.
text_raw:
It  must  not  be  felt  that  these  heads  of  the  world's  chief  central  banks  were  themselves
substantive  powers  in  world  finance.

text: They were not.
text_raw: They  were  not.

text: Rather, they were the technicians and agents of the dominant investment bankers of their own countries, who had raised them up and were perfectly capable of throwing them down.
text_raw:
Rather,  they  were  the  technicians
and  agents  of  the  dominant  investment  bankers  of  their  own  countries,  who  had  raised
them  up  and  were  perfectly  capable  of  throwing  them  down.

text: The substantive financial powers of the world were in the hands of these investment bankers (also called "international" or "merchant" bankers) who remained largely behind the scenes in their own unincorporated private banks.
text_raw:
The  substantive  financial
powers  of  the  world  were  in  the  hands  of  these  investment  bankers  (also  called
"international"  or  "merchant"  bankers)  who  remained  largely  behind  the  scenes  in  their
own  unincorporated  private  banks.

text: These formed a system of international cooperation and national dominance which was more private, more powerful, and more secret than that of their agents in the central banks.
text_raw:
These  formed  a  system  of  international  cooperation
and  national  dominance  which  was  more  private,  more  powerful,  and  more  secret  than
that  of  their  agents  in  the  central  banks.

text: This dominance of investment bankers was based on their control over the flows of credit and investment funds in their own countries and throughout the world.
text_raw:
This  dominance  of  investment  bankers  was  based
on  their  control  over  the  flows  of  credit  and  investment  funds  in  their  own  countries  and
throughout  the  world.

text: They could dominate the financial and industrial systems of their own countries by their influence over the flow of current funds through bank loans, the discount rate, and the re-discounting of commercial debts; they could dominate governments by their control over current government loans and the play of the international exchanges.
text_raw:
They  could  dominate  the  financial  and  industrial  systems  of  their
own  countries  by  their  influence  over  the  flow  of  current  funds  through  bank  loans,  the
discount  rate,  and  the  re-discounting  of  commercial  debts;  they  could  dominate
governments  by  their  control  over  current  government  loans  and  the  play  of  the
international  exchanges.

text: Almost all of this power was exercised by the personal influence and prestige of men who had demonstrated their ability in the past to bring off successful financial coupe, to keep their word, to remain cool in a crisis, and to share their winning opportunities with their associates.
text_raw:
Almost  all  of  this  power  was  exercised  by  the  personal  influence
and  prestige  of  men  who  had  demonstrated  their  ability  in  the  past  to  bring  off  successful
financial  coupe,  to  keep  their  word,  to  remain  cool  in  a  crisis,  and  to  share  their  winning
opportunities  with  their  associates.

text: Government Reports and Conferences
text_raw: Government  Reports  and  Conferences

text: The bankers' point of view was clearly expressed in a series of government reports and international conferences from 1918 to 1933.
text_raw:
The  bankers'  point  of  view  was  clearly  expressed  in  a  series  of  government  reports  and
international  conferences  from  1918  to  1933.

text: Among these were the reports of the Cunliffe Committee of Great Britain (August 1918), that of the Brussels Conference of Experts (September 1920), that of the Genoa Conference of the Supreme Council (January 1922), the First World Economic Conference (at Geneva, May 1927), the report of the Macmillan Committee on Finance and Industry (of 1931), and the various statements released by the World Economic Conference (at London in 1933).
text_raw:
Among  these  were  the  reports  of  the
Cunliffe  Committee  of  Great  Britain  (August  1918),  that  of  the  Brussels  Conference  of
Experts  (September  1920),  that  of  the  Genoa  Conference  of  the  Supreme  Council
(January  1922),  the  First  World  Economic  Conference  (at  Geneva,  May  1927),  the  report
of  the  Macmillan  Committee  on  Finance  and  Industry  (of  1931),  and  the  various
statements  released  by  the  World  Economic  Conference  (at  London  in  1933).

text: These and many other statements and reports called vainly for a free international gold standard, for balanced budgets, for restoration of the exchange rates and reserve ratios customary before 1914, for reductions in taxes and government spending, and for a cessation of all government interference in economic activity either domestic or international.
text_raw:
These  and
many  other  statements  and  reports  called  vainly  for  a  free  international  gold  standard,  for
balanced  budgets,  for  restoration  of  the  exchange  rates  and  reserve  ratios  customary
before  1914,  for  reductions  in  taxes  and  government  spending,  and  for  a  cessation  of  all
government  interference  in  economic  activity  either  domestic  or  international.

text: But none of these studies made any effort to assess the fundamental changes in economic, commercial, and political life since 1914.
text_raw:
But  none
of  these  studies  made  any  effort  to  assess  the  fundamental  changes  in  economic,
commercial,  and  political  life  since  1914.

text: And none gave any indication of a realization that a financial system must adapt itself to such changes.
text_raw:
And  none  gave  any  indication  of  a  realization
that  a  financial  system  must  adapt  itself  to  such  changes.

text: Instead, they all implied that if
text_raw: Instead,  they  all  implied  that  if

text: men would only give up their evil ways and impose the financial system of 1914 on the world, the changes would be compelled to reverse their direction and go back to the conditions of 1914.
text_raw:
men  would  only  give  up  their  evil  ways  and  impose  the  financial  system  of  1914  on  the
world,  the  changes  would  be  compelled  to  reverse  their  direction  and  go  back  to  the
conditions  of  1914.

text: Restoration of the Gold Standard of 1914
text_raw: Restoration  of  the  Gold  Standard  of  1914

text: Accordingly, the financial efforts of the period after 1918 became concentrated on a very simple (and superficial) goal â€” to get back to the gold standard â€” not "a" gold standard but "the" gold standard, by which was meant the identical exchange ratios and gold contents that monetary units had had in 1914.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  the  financial  efforts  of  the  period  after  1918  became  concentrated  on  a
very  simple  (and  superficial)  goal â€” to  get  back  to  the  gold  standard â€” not  "a"  gold
standard  but  "the"  gold  standard,  by  which  was  meant  the  identical  exchange  ratios  and
gold  contents  that  monetary  units  had  had  in  1914.

text: Restoration of the gold standard was not something which could be done by a mere act of government.
text_raw:
Restoration  of  the  gold  standard  was  not  something  which  could  be  done  by  a  mere  act
of  government.

text: It was admitted even by the most ardent advocates of the gold standard that certain financial relationships would require adjustment before the gold standard could be restored.
text_raw:
It  was  admitted  even  by  the  most  ardent  advocates  of  the  gold  standard
that  certain  financial  relationships  would  require  adjustment  before  the  gold  standard
could  be  restored.

text: There were three chief relationships involved.
text_raw: There  were  three  chief  relationships  involved.

text: These were (1) the problem of inflation, or the relationship between money and goods;
text_raw:
These  were  (1)  the
problem  of  inflation,  or  the  relationship  between  money  and  goods;

text: (2) the problem of public debts, or the relationship between governmental income and expenditure; and (3) the problem of price parities, or the relationship between price levels of different countries.
text_raw:
(2)  the  problem  of
public  debts,  or  the  relationship  between  governmental  income  and  expenditure;  and  (3)
the  problem  of  price  parities,  or  the  relationship  between  price  levels  of  different
countries.

text: That these three problems existed was evidence of a fundamental disequilibrium between real wealth and claims on wealth, caused by a relative decrease in the former and increase in the latter.
text_raw:
That  these  three  problems  existed  was  evidence  of  a  fundamental
disequilibrium  between  real  wealth  and  claims  on  wealth,  caused  by  a  relative  decrease  in
the  former  and  increase  in  the  latter.

text: Paying the Public Debt
text_raw: Paying  the  Public  Debt

text: The problem of public debts arose from the fact that as money (credit) was created during the war period, it was usually made in such a way that it was not in the control of the state or the community but was in the control of private financial institutions which demanded real wealth at some future date for the creation of claims on wealth in the present.
text_raw:
The  problem  of  public  debts  arose  from  the  fact  that  as  money  (credit)  was  created
during  the  war  period,  it  was  usually  made  in  such  a  way  that  it  was  not  in  the  control  of
the  state  or  the  community  but  was  in  the  control  of  private  financial  institutions  which
demanded  real  wealth  at  some  future  date  for  the  creation  of  claims  on  wealth  in  the
present.

text: The problem of public debt could have been met in one or more of several fashions:
text_raw:
The  problem  of  public  debt  could  have  been  met  in  one  or  more  of  several
fashions:

text: (a) by increasing the amount of real wealth in the community so that its price would fall and the value of money would rise.
text_raw:
(a)  by  increasing  the  amount  of  real  wealth  in  the  community  so  that  its  price
would  fall  and  the  value  of  money  would  rise.

text: This would restore the old equilibrium (and price level) between real wealth and claims on wealth and, at the same time, would permit payment of the public debt with no increase in the tax rates;
(b) by devaluation â€” that is, reduce the gold content of the monetary unit so that the government's holdings of gold would be worth a greatly increased number of monetary units.
text_raw:
(b)  by  devaluation â€”
that  is,  reduce  the  gold  content  of  the  monetary  unit  so  that  the  government's  holdings  of
gold  would  be  worth  a  greatly  increased  number  of  monetary  units.

text: These latter could be applied to the public debt;
text_raw:
These  latter  could  be
applied  to  the  public  debt;

text: (c) by repudiation â€” that is, a simple cancellation of the public debt by a refusal to pay it;
text_raw:
(c)  by  repudiation â€” that  is,  a  simple  cancellation  of  the  public
debt  by  a  refusal  to  pay  it;

text: (d) by taxation â€” that is, by increasing the tax rate to a level high enough to yield enough income to pay off the public debt;
text_raw:
(d)  by  taxation â€” that  is,  by  increasing  the  tax  rate  to  a  level
high  enough  to  yield  enough  income  to  pay  off  the  public  debt;

text: (e) by the issuance of fiat money and the payment of the debt by such money.
text_raw:
(e)  by  the  issuance  of  fiat
money  and  the  payment  of  the  debt  by  such  money.

text: These methods were not mutually exclusive, and in some cases overlapped.
text_raw: These  methods  were  not  mutually  exclusive,  and  in  some  cases  overlapped.

text: It might, for example, be argued that devaluation or use of fiat money were forms of partial repudiation.
text_raw:
It  might,
for  example,  be  argued  that  devaluation  or  use  of  fiat  money  were  forms  of  partial
repudiation.

text: Nor were all these methods equally practical.
text_raw: Nor  were  all  these  methods  equally  practical.

text: For example, the first (increase real wealth) was by far the soundest method to achieve a re-stabilization....
text_raw:
For  example,  the  first  (increase
real  wealth)  was  by  far  the  soundest  method  to  achieve  a  re-stabilization....

text: The fourth (taxation) would have put a burden on the economic system so great as to be self- defeating.
text_raw:
The  fourth
(taxation)  would  have  put  a  burden  on  the  economic  system  so  great  as  to  be  self-
defeating.

text: In Britain, the public debt could have been paid only by a tax of 25 percent for
text_raw: In  Britain,  the  public  debt  could  have  been  paid  only  by  a  tax  of  25  percent  for

text: about three hundred years.
text_raw: about  three  hundred  years.

text: Such heavy taxes might have had such a depressing effect on production of real wealth that national income would decline faster than tax rates rose, making payment by taxation impossible.
text_raw:
Such  heavy  taxes  might  have  had  such  a  depressing  effect  on
production  of  real  wealth  that  national  income  would  decline  faster  than  tax  rates  rose,
making  payment  by  taxation  impossible.

text: Nor were all these alternative methods of paying the public debt of equal practicality in respect to their effects on the two other financial problems occupying the minds of experts and statesmen.
text_raw:
Nor  were  all  these  alternative  methods  of  paying
the  public  debt  of  equal  practicality  in  respect  to  their  effects  on  the  two  other  financial
problems  occupying  the  minds  of  experts  and  statesmen.

text: These other two problems were inflation and price parities.
text_raw:
These  other  two  problems  were
inflation  and  price  parities.

text: These problems were just as urgent as the public debt, and the effects upon them of the different methods for paying the public debt could have been completely different.
text_raw:
These  problems  were  just  as  urgent  as  the  public  debt,  and  the
effects  upon  them  of  the  different  methods  for  paying  the  public  debt  could  have  been
completely  different.

text: Efforts to pay the public debt by fiat money would have made the inflation problem and perhaps the price-parity problem worse.
text_raw:
Efforts  to  pay  the  public  debt  by  fiat  money  would  have  made  the
inflation  problem  and  perhaps  the  price-parity  problem  worse.

text: Taxation and increasing real wealth, on the other hand, would have reduced the inflation problem at the same time as they reduced the public debt, since both would have increased the value of money (that is, they were deflationary).
text_raw:
Taxation  and  increasing
real  wealth,  on  the  other  hand,  would  have  reduced  the  inflation  problem  at  the  same  time
as  they  reduced  the  public  debt,  since  both  would  have  increased  the  value  of  money  (that
is,  they  were  deflationary).

text: Their effects on the problem of price parity would differ from case to case.
text_raw:
Their  effects  on  the  problem  of  price  parity  would  differ  from
case  to  case.

text: Use of Taxation to Pay Public Debt
text_raw: Use  of  Taxation  to  Pay  Public  Debt

text: Finally, these methods of paying the public debt were not of equal value in theory.
text_raw: Finally,  these  methods  of  paying  the  public  debt  were  not  of  equal  value  in  theory.

text: Orthodox theory rejected repudiation, devaluation, and fiat money as solutions to the problem, and, since it showed no way of increasing the production of real wealth, only taxation was left as a possible method of paying public debts.
text_raw:
Orthodox  theory  rejected  repudiation,  devaluation,  and  fiat  money  as  solutions  to  the
problem,  and,  since  it  showed  no  way  of  increasing  the  production  of  real  wealth,  only
taxation  was  left  as  a  possible  method  of  paying  public  debts.

text: But the theorists, as we have shown, could call taxation a possible way only if they neglected the economic consequences.
text_raw:
But  the  theorists,  as  we
have  shown,  could  call  taxation  a  possible  way  only  if  they  neglected  the  economic
consequences.

text: These consequences in most countries were so disastrous that taxation, if tried, soon had to be supplemented by other, unorthodox, methods.
text_raw:
These  consequences  in  most  countries  were  so  disastrous  that  taxation,  if
tried,  soon  had  to  be  supplemented  by  other,  unorthodox,  methods.

text: Great Britain and the United States were the only Great Powers which continued to use taxation as the chief method of paying the public debt.
text_raw:
Great  Britain  and  the
United  States  were  the  only  Great  Powers  which  continued  to  use  taxation  as  the  chief
method  of  paying  the  public  debt.

text: The Problem of Inflation
text_raw: The  Problem  of  Inflation

text: The second problem which had to be faced before stabilization was possible was the problem of inflation.
text_raw:
The  second  problem  which  had  to  be  faced  before  stabilization  was  possible  was  the
problem  of  inflation.

text: This was caused by the great increase in claims on wealth (money), and showed itself in a drastic increase in prices.
text_raw:
This  was  caused  by  the  great  increase  in  claims  on  wealth  (money),
and  showed  itself  in  a  drastic  increase  in  prices.

text: There were three possible solutions:
text_raw: There  were  three  possible  solutions:

text: (a) to increase the production of real wealth;
text_raw:
(a)
to  increase  the  production  of  real  wealth;

text: (b) to decrease the quantity of money; or (c) to devaluate, or make each unit of money equal to a smaller amount of wealth (specifically gold).
text_raw:
(b)  to  decrease  the  quantity  of  money;  or  (c)  to
devaluate,  or  make  each  unit  of  money  equal  to  a  smaller  amount  of  wealth  (specifically
gold).

text: The first two would have forced prices back to the lower prewar level but would have done it in entirely different ways, one resulting in prosperity and a great rise in standards of living, the second resulting in depression and a great fall in standards of living.
text_raw:
The  first  two  would  have  forced  prices  back  to  the  lower  prewar  level  but  would
have  done  it  in  entirely  different  ways,  one  resulting  in  prosperity  and  a  great  rise  in
standards  of  living,  the  second  resulting  in  depression  and  a  great  fall  in  standards  of
living.

text: The third method (devaluation) was essentially a recognition and acceptance of the existing situation, and would have left prices at the higher postwar level permanently.
text_raw:
The  third  method  (devaluation)  was  essentially  a  recognition  and  acceptance  of
the  existing  situation,  and  would  have  left  prices  at  the  higher  postwar  level  permanently.

text: This would have involved a permanent reduction in the value of money, and also would have given different parities in foreign exchanges (unless there was international agreement that countries devaluate by the same ratio).
text_raw:
This  would  have  involved  a  permanent  reduction  in  the  value  of  money,  and  also  would
have  given  different  parities  in  foreign  exchanges  (unless  there  was  international
agreement  that  countries  devaluate  by  the  same  ratio).

text: But it would have made possible prosperity and a rising standard of living and would have accepted as permanent the redistribution of wealth from creditors to debtors brought about by the wartime inflation.
text_raw:
But  it  would  have  made  possible
prosperity  and  a  rising  standard  of  living  and  would  have  accepted  as  permanent  the
redistribution  of  wealth  from  creditors  to  debtors  brought  about  by  the  wartime  inflation.

text: International Bankers Regarded Deflation as a Good Thing
text_raw: International  Bankers  Regarded  Deflation  as  a  Good  Thing

text: Since the third method (devaluation) was rejected by orthodox theorists, and no one could see how to get the first (increase of real wealth), only the second (deflation) was left as a possible method for dealing with the problem of inflation.
text_raw:
Since  the  third  method  (devaluation)  was  rejected  by  orthodox  theorists,  and  no  one
could  see  how  to  get  the  first  (increase  of  real  wealth),  only  the  second  (deflation)  was
left  as  a  possible  method  for  dealing  with  the  problem  of  inflation.

text: To many people it seemed axiomatic that the cure for inflation was deflation, especially since bankers regarded deflation as a good thing in itself.
text_raw:
To  many  people  it
seemed  axiomatic  that  the  cure  for  inflation  was  deflation,  especially  since  bankers
regarded  deflation  as  a  good  thing  in  itself.

text: Moreover, deflation as a method for dealing with the problem of inflation went hand in hand with taxation as a method for dealing with the problem of public debts.
text_raw:
Moreover,  deflation  as  a  method  for  dealing
with  the  problem  of  inflation  went  hand  in  hand  with  taxation  as  a  method  for  dealing
with  the  problem  of  public  debts.

text: Theorists did not stop to think what the effects of both would be on the production of real wealth and on the prosperity of the world.
text_raw:
Theorists  did  not  stop  to  think  what  the  effects  of  both
would  be  on  the  production  of  real  wealth  and  on  the  prosperity  of  the  world.

text: The Problem of Price Parities
text_raw: The  Problem  of  Price  Parities

text: The third financial problem which had to be solved before stabilization became practical was the problem of price parities.
text_raw:
The  third  financial  problem  which  had  to  be  solved  before  stabilization  became
practical  was  the  problem  of  price  parities.

text: This differed because it was primarily an international question while the other two problems were primarily domestic.
text_raw:
This  differed  because  it  was  primarily  an
international  question  while  the  other  two  problems  were  primarily  domestic.

text: By suspending the gold standard and establishing artificial control of foreign exchanges at the outbreak of war, the belligerent countries made it possible for prices to rise at different rates in different countries.
text_raw:
By
suspending  the  gold  standard  and  establishing  artificial  control  of  foreign  exchanges  at
the  outbreak  of  war,  the  belligerent  countries  made  it  possible  for  prices  to  rise  at
different  rates  in  different  countries.

text: This can be seen in the fact that prices in Britain rose 200 percent in seven years (1913-1920), while in the United States they rose only 100 percent.
text_raw:
This  can  be  seen  in  the  fact  that  prices  in  Britain  rose
200  percent  in  seven  years  (1913-1920),  while  in  the  United  States  they  rose  only  100
percent.

text: The resulting disequilibrium had to be rectified before the two countries went back on the old gold standard, or the currencies would be valued in law in a ratio quite different from their value in goods.
text_raw:
The  resulting  disequilibrium  had  to  be  rectified  before  the  two  countries  went
back  on  the  old  gold  standard,  or  the  currencies  would  be  valued  in  law  in  a  ratio  quite
different  from  their  value  in  goods.

text: By going back on gold at the old ratios, one ounce of fine gold would, by law, become equal to $20.67 in the United States and about 84s.
text_raw:
By  going  back  on  gold  at  the  old  ratios,  one  ounce  of
fine  gold  would,  by  law,  become  equal  to  $20.67  in  the  United  States  and  about  84s.

The  ounce  of  gold  in  the  United
States  would  be  much  more  valuable  than  in  Britain,  so  that  foreigners  (and  British)
would  prefer  to  buy  in  the  United  States  rather  than  in  Britain,  and  gold  would  tend  to
flow  to  the  United  States  from  Britain  with  goods  flowing  in  the  opposite  direction.

text: In such conditions it would be said that the pound was overvalued and the dollar undervalued.
text_raw:
In
such  conditions  it  would  be  said  that  the  pound  was  overvalued  and  the  dollar
undervalued.

text: The overvaluation would bring depression to Britain, while the United States would tend to be prosperous.
text_raw:
The  overvaluation  would  bring  depression  to  Britain,  while  the  United
States  would  tend  to  be  prosperous.

text: Such disequilibrium of price parities could be adjusted either by a fall of prices in the country whose currency was overvalued or by a rise in prices in the country whose currency was undervalued (or by both).
text_raw:
Such  disequilibrium  of  price  parities  could  be
adjusted  either  by  a  fall  of  prices  in  the  country  whose  currency  was  overvalued  or  by  a
rise  in  prices  in  the  country  whose  currency  was  undervalued  (or  by  both).

text: Such an adjustment would be largely automatic, but at the cost of a considerable flow of gold from the country whose currency was overvalued.
text_raw:
Such  an
adjustment  would  be  largely  automatic,  but  at  the  cost  of  a  considerable  flow  of  gold
from  the  country  whose  currency  was  overvalued.

text: Because the problem of price parities would either adjust itself or would require international agreement for its adjustment, no real attention was paid to it when governments turned their attention to the task of stabilization.
text_raw:
Because  the  problem  of  price  parities  would  either  adjust  itself  or  would  require
international  agreement  for  its  adjustment,  no  real  attention  was  paid  to  it  when
governments  turned  their  attention  to  the  task  of  stabilization.

text: Instead, they concentrated on the other two problems and, above all, devoted attention to the task of building up sufficient gold reserves to permit them to carry out the methods chosen in respect to these two problems.
text_raw:
Instead,  they  concentrated
on  the  other  two  problems  and,  above  all,  devoted  attention  to  the  task  of  building  up
sufficient  gold  reserves  to  permit  them  to  carry  out  the  methods  chosen  in  respect  to  these
two  problems.

text: America Returns to the Gold Standard
text_raw: America  Returns  to  the  Gold  Standard

text: Most countries were in a hurry to stabilize their currencies when peace was signed in 1919.
text_raw:
Most  countries  were  in  a  hurry  to  stabilize  their  currencies  when  peace  was  signed  in
1919.

text: The difficulties of the three problems we have mentioned made it necessary to postpone the step for years.
text_raw:
The  difficulties  of  the  three  problems  we  have  mentioned  made  it  necessary  to
postpone  the  step  for  years.

text: The process of stabilization was stretched over more than a decade from 1919 to 1931.
text_raw:
The  process  of  stabilization  was  stretched  over  more  than  a
decade  from  1919  to  1931.

text: Only the United States was able to return to the gold standard at once, and this was the result of a peculiar combination of circumstances which existed only in that country.
text_raw:
Only  the  United  States  was  able  to  return  to  the  gold  standard
at  once,  and  this  was  the  result  of  a  peculiar  combination  of  circumstances  which  existed
only  in  that  country.

text: The United States had a plentiful supply of gold.
text_raw: The  United  States  had  a  plentiful  supply  of  gold.

text: In addition it had a technological structure quite different from that of any other country, except perhaps Japan.
text_raw:
In  addition  it  had  a
technological  structure  quite  different  from  that  of  any  other  country,  except  perhaps
Japan.

text: American technology was advancing so rapidly in the period 1922-1928 that even with falling prices there was prosperity, since costs of production fell even faster.
text_raw:
American  technology  was  advancing  so  rapidly  in  the  period  1922-1928  that  even
with  falling  prices  there  was  prosperity,  since  costs  of  production  fell  even  faster.

text: This situation was helped by the fact that prices of raw materials and food fell faster than prices of industrial products, so that production of these latter was very profitable.
text_raw:
This
situation  was  helped  by  the  fact  that  prices  of  raw  materials  and  food  fell  faster  than
prices  of  industrial  products,  so  that  production  of  these  latter  was  very  profitable.

text: As a result, America achieved to a degree greater than any other country a solution of inflation and public debt which all theorists had recognized as possible, but which none had known how to obtain â€” the solution to be found in a great increase in real wealth.
text_raw:
As  a
result,  America  achieved  to  a  degree  greater  than  any  other  country  a  solution  of  inflation
and  public  debt  which  all  theorists  had  recognized  as  possible,  but  which  none  had
known  how  to  obtain â€” the  solution  to  be  found  in  a  great  increase  in  real  wealth.

text: This increase made it possible simultaneously to pay off the public debt and reduce taxes; it also made it possible to have deflation without depression.
text_raw:
This
increase  made  it  possible  simultaneously  to  pay  off  the  public  debt  and  reduce  taxes;  it
also  made  it  possible  to  have  deflation  without  depression.

text: A happier solution of the postwar problems could hardly have been found â€” for a time, at least.
text_raw:
A  happier  solution  of  the
postwar  problems  could  hardly  have  been  found â€” for  a  time,  at  least.

text: In the long run, the situation had its drawbacks, since the fact that costs fell faster than prices and that prices of agricultural products and raw materials fell faster than prices of industrial products meant that in the long run the community would not have sufficient purchasing power to buy the products of the industrial organization.
text_raw:
In  the  long  run,  the
situation  had  its  drawbacks,  since  the  fact  that  costs  fell  faster  than  prices  and  that  prices
of  agricultural  products  and  raw  materials  fell  faster  than  prices  of  industrial  products
meant  that  in  the  long  run  the  community  would  not  have  sufficient  purchasing  power  to
buy  the  products  of  the  industrial  organization.

text: This problem was postponed for a considerable period by the application of easy credit and installment selling to the domestic market and by the extension to foreign countries of huge loans which made it possible for these countries to buy the products of American industry without sending their own goods into the American market in return.
text_raw:
This  problem  was  postponed  for  a
considerable  period  by  the  application  of  easy  credit  and  installment  selling  to  the
domestic  market  and  by  the  extension  to  foreign  countries  of  huge  loans  which  made  it
possible  for  these  countries  to  buy  the  products  of  American  industry  without  sending
their  own  goods  into  the  American  market  in  return.

text: Thus, from a most unusual group of circumstances, the United States obtained an unusual boom of prosperity.
text_raw:
Thus,  from  a  most  unusual  group  of
circumstances,  the  United  States  obtained  an  unusual  boom  of  prosperity.

text: These circumstances were, however, in many ways a postponement of difficulties rather than a solution of them, as the theoretical understanding of what was going on was still lacking.
text_raw:
These
circumstances  were,  however,  in  many  ways  a  postponement  of  difficulties  rather  than  a
solution  of  them,  as  the  theoretical  understanding  of  what  was  going  on  was  still  lacking.

text: Taxation as a Cure for Public Debts
text_raw: Taxation  as  a  Cure  for  Public  Debts

text: In other countries the stabilization period was not so happy.
text_raw: In  other  countries  the  stabilization  period  was  not  so  happy.

text: In Britain, stabilization was reached by orthodox paths â€” that is, taxation as a cure for public debts and deflation as a cure for inflation.
text_raw:
In  Britain,  stabilization
was  reached  by  orthodox  paths â€” that  is,  taxation  as  a  cure  for  public  debts  and  deflation
as  a  cure  for  inflation.

text: These cures were believed necessary in order to go back on the old gold parity.
text_raw:
These  cures  were  believed  necessary  in  order  to  go  back  on  the  old
gold  parity.

text: Since Britain did not have an adequate supply of gold, the policy of deflation had to be pushed ruthlessly in order to reduce the volume of money in circulation to a quantity small enough to be superimposed on the small base of available gold at the old ratios.
text_raw:
Since  Britain  did  not  have  an  adequate  supply  of  gold,  the  policy  of  deflation
had  to  be  pushed  ruthlessly  in  order  to  reduce  the  volume  of  money  in  circulation  to  a
quantity  small  enough  to  be  superimposed  on  the  small  base  of  available  gold  at  the  old
ratios.

text: At the same time, the policy was intended to drive British prices down to the level of world prices.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  the  policy  was  intended  to  drive  British  prices  down  to  the  level
of  world  prices.

text: The currency notes which had been used to supplement bank notes were retired, and credit was curtailed by raising the discount rate to panic level.
text_raw:
The  currency  notes  which  had  been  used  to  supplement  bank  notes  were
retired,  and  credit  was  curtailed  by  raising  the  discount  rate  to  panic  level.

text: The results were horrible.
text_raw:
The  results
were  horrible.

text: Business activity fell drastically, and unemployment rose to well over a million and a half.
text_raw:
Business  activity  fell  drastically,  and  unemployment  rose  to  well  over  a
million  and  a  half.

text: The drastic fall in prices (from 307 in 1920 to 197 in 1921) made production unprofitable unless costs were driven down even faster.
text_raw:
The  drastic  fall  in  prices  (from  307  in  1920  to  197  in  1921)  made
production  unprofitable  unless  costs  were  driven  down  even  faster.

text: This could not be achieved because labor unions were determined that the burden of the deflationary policy should not be pushed onto them by forcing down wages.
text_raw:
This  could  not  be
achieved  because  labor  unions  were  determined  that  the  burden  of  the  deflationary  policy
should  not  be  pushed  onto  them  by  forcing  down  wages.

text: The outcome was a great wave of strikes and industrial unrest.
text_raw:
The  outcome  was  a  great  wave
of  strikes  and  industrial  unrest.

text: Britain Goes Back on the Gold Standard
text_raw: Britain  Goes  Back  on  the  Gold  Standard

text: The British government could measure the success of their deflation only by comparing their price level with world price levels.
text_raw:
The  British  government  could  measure  the  success  of  their  deflation  only  by
comparing  their  price  level  with  world  price  levels.

text: This was done by means of the exchange ratio between the pound and the dollar.
text_raw:
This  was  done  by  means  of  the
exchange  ratio  between  the  pound  and  the  dollar.

text: At that time the dollar was the only important currency on gold.
text_raw:
At  that  time  the  dollar  was  the  only
important  currency  on  gold.

text: It was expected that the forcing down of prices in Britain would be reflected in an increase in the value of the pound in terms of dollars on the foreign exchange market.
text_raw:
It  was  expected  that  the  forcing  down  of  prices  in  Britain
would  be  reflected  in  an  increase  in  the  value  of  the  pound  in  terms  of  dollars  on  the
foreign  exchange  market.

text: Thus as the pound rose gradually upward toward the pre-war rate of $4.86, this rise would measure the fall in British prices downward to the American (or the world) price level.
text_raw:
Thus  as  the  pound  rose  gradually  upward  toward  the  pre-war
rate  of  $4.86,  this  rise  would  measure  the  fall  in  British  prices  downward  to  the  American
(or  the  world)  price  level.

text: In general terms, this was true, but it failed to take into consideration the speculators who, knowing that the value of the pound was rising, sold dollars to buy pounds, thus pushing the dollar down and the pound upward faster than was justified in terms of the changes in price levels in the two countries.
text_raw:
In  general  terms,  this  was  true,  but  it  failed  to  take  into
consideration  the  speculators  who,  knowing  that  the  value  of  the  pound  was  rising,  sold
dollars  to  buy  pounds,  thus  pushing  the  dollar  down  and  the  pound  upward  faster  than
was  justified  in  terms  of  the  changes  in  price  levels  in  the  two  countries.

text: Thus the pound rose to $4.86, while the British price level had not yet fallen to the American price level, but the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Winston Churchill, judging the price level by the exchange rate, believed that it had and went back on the gold standard at that point.
text_raw:
Thus  the  pound
rose  to  $4.86,  while  the  British  price  level  had  not  yet  fallen  to  the  American  price  level,
but  the  Chancellor  of  the  Exchequer,  Winston  Churchill,  judging  the  price  level  by  the
exchange  rate,  believed  that  it  had  and  went  back  on  the  gold  standard  at  that  point.

text: As a result, sterling was overvalued and Britain found itself economically isolated on a price plateau above the world market on which she was economically dependent.
text_raw:
As  a
result,  sterling  was  overvalued  and  Britain  found  itself  economically  isolated  on  a  price
plateau  above  the  world  market  on  which  she  was  economically  dependent.

text: These higher British prices served to increase imports, decrease exports, and encourage an outflow of gold which made gold reserves dangerously low.
text_raw:
These  higher
British  prices  served  to  increase  imports,  decrease  exports,  and  encourage  an  outflow  of
gold  which  made  gold  reserves  dangerously  low.

text: To maintain the gold reserve at all, it was necessary to keep the discount rate at a level so high (4 Vi percent or more) that business activity was discouraged.
text_raw:
To  maintain  the  gold  reserve  at  all,  it
was  necessary  to  keep  the  discount  rate  at  a  level  so  high  (4  Vi  percent  or  more)  that
business  activity  was  discouraged.

text: The only solution which the British government could see to this situation was continued deflation.
text_raw:
The  only  solution  which  the  British  government  could
see  to  this  situation  was  continued  deflation.

text: This effort to drive down prices failed because the unions were able to prevent the drastic cutting of costs (chiefly wages) necessary to permit profitable production on such a deflationary market.
text_raw:
This  effort  to  drive  down  prices  failed
because  the  unions  were  able  to  prevent  the  drastic  cutting  of  costs  (chiefly  wages)
necessary  to  permit  profitable  production  on  such  a  deflationary  market.

text: Nor could the alternative method of deflation â€” by heavy taxation â€” be imposed to the necessary degree on the upper classes who were in control of the' government.
text_raw:
Nor  could  the
alternative  method  of  deflation â€” by  heavy  taxation â€” be  imposed  to  the  necessary  degree
on  the  upper  classes  who  were  in  control  of  the'  government.

text: The showdown on the deflationary policy came in the General Strike of 1926.
text_raw:
The  showdown  on  the
deflationary  policy  came  in  the  General  Strike  of  1926.

text: The unions lost the strike â€” that is, they could not prevent the policy of deflation â€” but they made it impossible for the government to continue the reduction of costs to the extent necessary to restore business profits and the export trade.
text_raw:
The  unions  lost  the  strike â€” that
is,  they  could  not  prevent  the  policy  of  deflation â€” but  they  made  it  impossible  for  the
government  to  continue  the  reduction  of  costs  to  the  extent  necessary  to  restore  business
profits  and  the  export  trade.

text: Britain Goes into Financial Bondage to France
text_raw: Britain  Goes  into  Financial  Bondage  to  France

text: As a result of this financial policy, Britain found herself faced with deflation and depression for the whole period 1920-1933.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  this  financial  policy,  Britain  found  herself  faced  with  deflation  and
depression  for  the  whole  period  1920-1933.

text: These effects were drastic in 1920-1922, moderate in 1922-1929, and drastic again in -1933.
text_raw:
These  effects  were  drastic  in  1920-1922,
moderate  in  1922-1929,  and  drastic  again  in  -1933.

text: The wholesale price index (1913=100) fell from 307 in 1920 to 197 in 1921, then declined slowly to 137 in 1928.
text_raw:
The  wholesale  price  index
(1913=100)  fell  from  307  in  1920  to  197  in  1921,  then  declined  slowly  to  137  in  1928.

text: Then it fell rapidly to 120 in 1929 and go in 1933.
text_raw: Then  it  fell  rapidly  to  120  in  1929  and  go  in  1933.

text: The number of unemployed averaged about 13/4 millions for each of the thirteen years of 1921-1932 and reached 3 million in 1931.
text_raw:
The  number  of  unemployed  averaged
about  13/4  millions  for  each  of  the  thirteen  years  of  1921-1932  and  reached  3  million  in
1931.

text: At the same time, the inadequacy of the British gold reserve during most of the period placed Britain in financial subjection to France (which had a plentiful supply of gold because of her different financial policy).
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  the  inadequacy  of  the  British  gold  reserve  during  most  of  the
period  placed  Britain  in  financial  subjection  to  France  (which  had  a  plentiful  supply  of
gold  because  of  her  different  financial  policy).

text: This subjection served to balance the political subjection of France to Britain arising from French insecurity, and ended only with Britain's abandonment of the gold standard in 1931.
text_raw:
This  subjection  served  to  balance  the
political  subjection  of  France  to  Britain  arising  from  French  insecurity,  and  ended  only
with  Britain's  abandonment  of  the  gold  standard  in  1931.

text: Britain was the only important European country which reached stabilization through deflation.
text_raw:
Britain  was  the  only  important  European  country  which  reached  stabilization  through
deflation.

text: East of her, a second group of countries, including Belgium, France, and Italy, reached stabilization through devaluation.
text_raw:
East  of  her,  a  second  group  of  countries,  including  Belgium,  France,  and  Italy,
reached  stabilization  through  devaluation.

text: This was a far better method.
text_raw: This  was  a  far  better  method.

text: It was adopted, however, not because of superior intelligence but because of financial weakness.
text_raw:
It  was  adopted,
however,  not  because  of  superior  intelligence  but  because  of  financial  weakness.

text: In these countries, the burden of war-damage reconstruction made it impossible to balance a budget, and this made deflation difficult.
text_raw:
In  these
countries,  the  burden  of  war-damage  reconstruction  made  it  impossible  to  balance  a
budget,  and  this  made  deflation  difficult.

text: These countries accepted orthodox financial ideas and tried to deflate in 1920-1921, but, after the depression which resulted, they gave up the task.
text_raw:
These  countries  accepted  orthodox  financial
ideas  and  tried  to  deflate  in  1920-1921,  but,  after  the  depression  which  resulted,  they
gave  up  the  task.

text: Belgium stabilized once at 107 francs to the pound sterling, but could not hold this level and had to devaluate further to 175 to the pound (October 1926).
text_raw:
Belgium  stabilized  once  at  107  francs  to  the  pound  sterling,  but  could
not  hold  this  level  and  had  to  devaluate  further  to  175  to  the  pound  (October  1926).

text: France stabilized at 124.21 francs to the pound at the end of 1926, although the stabilization was made de jure only in June 1928.
text_raw:
France  stabilized  at  124.21  francs  to  the  pound  at  the  end  of  1926,  although  the
stabilization  was  made  de  jure  only  in  June  1928.

text: Italy stabilized at 92.46 fire to the pound sterling in December 1927.
text_raw:
Italy  stabilized  at  92.46  fire  to  the
pound  sterling  in  December  1927.

text: Achieving Stabilization through Devaluation
text_raw: Achieving  Stabilization  through  Devaluation

text: The group of countries which reached stabilization through devaluation prospered in contrast with those who reached stabilization through deflation.
text_raw:
The  group  of  countries  which  reached  stabilization  through  devaluation  prospered  in
contrast  with  those  who  reached  stabilization  through  deflation.

text: The prosperity was roughly equal to the degree of devaluation.
text_raw:
The  prosperity  was
roughly  equal  to  the  degree  of  devaluation.

text: Of the three Latin countries â€” Belgium, France, and Italy â€” Belgium devalued the most and was most prosperous.
text_raw:
Of  the  three  Latin  countries â€” Belgium,
France,  and  Italy â€” Belgium  devalued  the  most  and  was  most  prosperous.

text: Her stabilization was at a price level below the world level so that the belga was undervalued by about one-fifth.
text_raw:
Her
stabilization  was  at  a  price  level  below  the  world  level  so  that  the  belga  was  undervalued
by  about  one-fifth.

text: This served to encourage exports.
text_raw: This  served  to  encourage  exports.

text: For an industrial country such as Belgium, this made it possible for her to profit by the misfortunes of Britain.
text_raw:
For  an  industrial  country  such  as
Belgium,  this  made  it  possible  for  her  to  profit  by  the  misfortunes  of  Britain.

text: France was in a somewhat similar position.
text_raw:
France  was
in  a  somewhat  similar  position.

text: Italy, on the contrary, stabilized at a figure which made the lira considerably overvalued.
text_raw:
Italy,  on  the  contrary,  stabilized  at  a  figure  which  made
the  lira  considerably  overvalued.

text: This was done for purposes of prestige â€” Mussolini being determined to stabilize the lira at a value higher than that of the French franc.
text_raw:
This  was  done  for  purposes  of  prestige â€” Mussolini
being  determined  to  stabilize  the  lira  at  a  value  higher  than  that  of  the  French  franc.

text: The effects of this overvaluation of the lira on the Italian economy were extremely adverse.
text_raw:
The
effects  of  this  overvaluation  of  the  lira  on  the  Italian  economy  were  extremely  adverse.

text: Italy was never as prosperous after stabilization as she had been immediately before it.
text_raw: Italy  was  never  as  prosperous  after  stabilization  as  she  had  been  immediately  before  it.

text: Not only did the countries which undervalued their money prosper; they decreased the disequilibrium between wealth and money; they were able to use the inflation to increase production; they escaped high taxes; they moderated or escaped the stabilization crisis and the deflationary depression; they improved their positions in the world market in respect to high-cost countries like Britain; and they replenished their gold stocks.
text_raw:
Not  only  did  the  countries  which  undervalued  their  money  prosper;  they  decreased  the
disequilibrium  between  wealth  and  money;  they  were  able  to  use  the  inflation  to  increase
production;  they  escaped  high  taxes;  they  moderated  or  escaped  the  stabilization  crisis
and  the  deflationary  depression;  they  improved  their  positions  in  the  world  market  in
respect  to  high-cost  countries  like  Britain;  and  they  replenished  their  gold  stocks.

text: America Rebuilds the Industrial Structure of Germany
text_raw: America  Rebuilds  the  Industrial  Structure  of  Germany

text: through the Dawes Plan
text_raw: through  the  Dawes  Plan

text_raw: A  third  group  of  countries  reached  stabilization  through  reconstruction.

text_raw:
These  were
the  countries  in  which  the  old  monetary  unit  had  been  wiped  out  and  had  to  be  replaced
