text: The real key to the shift rested on the control of money flows, especially of investment funds.
text_raw:
The  real  key  to  the  shift  rested  on  the
control  of  money  flows,  especially  of  investment  funds.

text: These controls, which were held by investment bankers in 1900, were eclipsed by other sources of funds and capital, such as insurance, retirement and investment funds, and, above all, by those flows resulting from the fiscal policies of governments.
text_raw:
These  controls,  which  were  held
by  investment  bankers  in  1900,  were  eclipsed  by  other  sources  of  funds  and  capital,  such
as  insurance,  retirement  and  investment  funds,  and,  above  all,  by  those  flows  resulting
from  the  fiscal  policies  of  governments.

text: Efforts by the older private investment bankers to control these new channels of funds had varying degrees of success, but, in general, financial capitalism was destroyed by two events:
text_raw:
Efforts  by  the  older  private  investment  bankers
to  control  these  new  channels  of  funds  had  varying  degrees  of  success,  but,  in  general,
financial  capitalism  was  destroyed  by  two  events:

text: (1) the ability of industry to finance its own capital needs because of the increased profits arising from the decreased competition established by financial capitalism, and (2) the economic crisis engendered by the deflationary policies resulting from financial capitalism's obsession with the gold standard.
text_raw:
(1)  the  ability  of  industry  to  finance  its
own  capital  needs  because  of  the  increased  profits  arising  from  the  decreased  competition
established  by  financial  capitalism,  and  (2)  the  economic  crisis  engendered  by  the
deflationary  policies  resulting  from  financial  capitalism's  obsession  with  the  gold
standard.

text: The period of stabilization cannot be clearly distinguished from the period of deflation.
text_raw:
The  period  of  stabilization  cannot  be  clearly  distinguished  from  the  period  of
deflation.

text: In most countries, the period of deflation began in 1921 and, after about four or five years, became more rapid in its development, reaching after 1929 a degree which
text_raw:
In  most  countries,  the  period  of  deflation  began  in  1921  and,  after  about  four  or
five  years,  became  more  rapid  in  its  development,  reaching  after  1929  a  degree  which

text: could be called acute.
text_raw: could  be  called  acute.

text: In the first part of this period (1921-1925), the dangerous economic implications of deflation were concealed by a structure of self-deception which pretended that a great period of economic progress would be inaugurated as soon as the task of stabilization had been accomplished.
text_raw:
In  the  first  part  of  this  period  (1921-1925),  the  dangerous  economic
implications  of  deflation  were  concealed  by  a  structure  of  self-deception  which  pretended
that  a  great  period  of  economic  progress  would  be  inaugurated  as  soon  as  the  task  of
stabilization  had  been  accomplished.

text: This psychological optimism was completely unwarranted by the economic facts, even in the United States where these economic facts were (for the short term, at least) more promising than anywhere else.
text_raw:
This  psychological  optimism  was  completely
unwarranted  by  the  economic  facts,  even  in  the  United  States  where  these  economic  facts
were  (for  the  short  term,  at  least)  more  promising  than  anywhere  else.

text: After 1925, when the deflation became more deep-rooted and economic conditions worsened, the danger from these conditions was concealed by a continuation of unwarranted optimism.
text_raw:
After  1925,  when
the  deflation  became  more  deep-rooted  and  economic  conditions  worsened,  the  danger
from  these  conditions  was  concealed  by  a  continuation  of  unwarranted  optimism.

text: The chief symptom of the unsoundness of the underlying economic reality â€” the steady fall in prices â€” was concealed in the later period (1925-1929) by a steady rise in security prices (which was erroneously regarded as a good sign) and by the excessive lending abroad of the United States (which amounted to almost ten billion dollars in the period 1920-1931, bringing our total foreign investment to almost 27 billion dollars by the end of 1930).
text_raw:
The
chief  symptom  of  the  unsoundness  of  the  underlying  economic  reality â€” the  steady  fall  in
prices â€” was  concealed  in  the  later  period  (1925-1929)  by  a  steady  rise  in  security  prices
(which  was  erroneously  regarded  as  a  good  sign)  and  by  the  excessive  lending  abroad  of
the  United  States  (which  amounted  to  almost  ten  billion  dollars  in  the  period  1920-1931,
bringing  our  total  foreign  investment  to  almost  27  billion  dollars  by  the  end  of  1930).

text: This foreign lending of the United States was the chief reason why the maladjusted economic conditions could be kept concealed for so many years.
text_raw:
This  foreign  lending  of  the  United  States  was  the  chief  reason  why  the  maladjusted
economic  conditions  could  be  kept  concealed  for  so  many  years.

text: Before the World War, the United States had been a debtor nation and, to pay these debts, had developed an exporting economy.
text_raw:
Before  the  World  War,
the  United  States  had  been  a  debtor  nation  and,  to  pay  these  debts,  had  developed  an
exporting  economy.

text: The combination of debtor and exporter is a feasible one.
text_raw: The  combination  of  debtor  and  exporter  is  a  feasible  one.

text: The war made the United States a creditor nation and also made her a greater exporter than ever by building up her acreage of cotton and wheat and her capacity to produce ships, steel, textiles, and so on.
text_raw:
The  war
made  the  United  States  a  creditor  nation  and  also  made  her  a  greater  exporter  than  ever
by  building  up  her  acreage  of  cotton  and  wheat  and  her  capacity  to  produce  ships,  steel,
textiles,  and  so  on.

text: The resulting combination of creditor and exporter was not feasible.
text_raw: The  resulting  combination  of  creditor  and  exporter  was  not  feasible.

text: The United States refused to accept either necessary alternative â€” to reduce debts owed to her or to increase her imports.
text_raw:
The  United  States  refused  to  accept  either  necessary  alternative â€” to  reduce  debts  owed  to
her  or  to  increase  her  imports.

text: Instead, she raised tariffs against imports and temporarily filled the gap with huge foreign loans.
text_raw:
Instead,  she  raised  tariffs  against  imports  and  temporarily
filled  the  gap  with  huge  foreign  loans.

text: But this was hopeless as a permanent solution.
text_raw: But  this  was  hopeless  as  a  permanent  solution.

text: As a temporary solution, it permitted the United States to be both creditor and exporter; it permitted Germany to pay reparations with neither a budgetary surplus nor a favorable balance of trade; it permitted dozens of minor countries to adopt a gold standard they could not hold; it permitted France, Britain, Italy, and others to pay war debts to the United States without sending goods.
text_raw:
As
a  temporary  solution,  it  permitted  the  United  States  to  be  both  creditor  and  exporter;  it
permitted  Germany  to  pay  reparations  with  neither  a  budgetary  surplus  nor  a  favorable
balance  of  trade;  it  permitted  dozens  of  minor  countries  to  adopt  a  gold  standard  they
could  not  hold;  it  permitted  France,  Britain,  Italy,  and  others  to  pay  war  debts  to  the
United  States  without  sending  goods.

text: In a word, it permitted the world to live in a fairyland of self-delusions remote from economic realities.
text_raw:
In  a  word,  it  permitted  the  world  to  live  in  a
fairyland  of  self-delusions  remote  from  economic  realities.

text: Economic Realities
text_raw: Economic  Realities

text: These realities were characterized by (a) fundamental maladjustments, both economic and financial, which made it impossible for the financial system to function as it had in 1914, and (b) the steady deflation.
text_raw:
These  realities  were  characterized  by  (a)  fundamental  maladjustments,  both  economic
and  financial,  which  made  it  impossible  for  the  financial  system  to  function  as  it  had  in
1914,  and  (b)  the  steady  deflation.

text: The fundamental maladjustments were both economic and financial.
text_raw: The  fundamental  maladjustments  were  both  economic  and  financial.

text: The economic maladjustments were those which we have already indicated: the industrialization of colonial areas; the overproduction of raw materials and food as a result of wartime high prices, the overexpansion of heavy industry as a result of wartime needs, the obsolescence of much of heavy industry in Europe and in Britain which made it impossible to compete with newer equipment or to cope with the shifts in consumer demand, and the steadily increasing disadvantage of producers of raw materials and food in contrast with producers of industrial goods.
text_raw:
The  economic
maladjustments  were  those  which  we  have  already  indicated:  the  industrialization  of
colonial  areas;  the  overproduction  of  raw  materials  and  food  as  a  result  of  wartime  high
prices,  the  overexpansion  of  heavy  industry  as  a  result  of  wartime  needs,  the
obsolescence  of  much  of  heavy  industry  in  Europe  and  in  Britain  which  made  it
impossible  to  compete  with  newer  equipment  or  to  cope  with  the  shifts  in  consumer
demand,  and  the  steadily  increasing  disadvantage  of  producers  of  raw  materials  and  food
in  contrast  with  producers  of  industrial  goods.

text: To these old factors were added new ones such as the great increase in productive efficiency in Germany and the United States, the return of Russia and Germany to the European economy about 1924, and the return of
text_raw:
To  these  old  factors  were  added  new  ones
such  as  the  great  increase  in  productive  efficiency  in  Germany  and  the  United  States,  the
return  of  Russia  and  Germany  to  the  European  economy  about  1924,  and  the  return  of

text: Europe-to the world economy in the period 1925-1927.
text_raw: Europe-to  the  world  economy  in  the  period  1925-1927.

text: Many countries sought to resist these factors, both old and new, by adopting political interference with economic life in the form of tariffs, import quotas, export subsidies, and so on.
text_raw:
Many  countries  sought  to  resist
these  factors,  both  old  and  new,  by  adopting  political  interference  with  economic  life  in
the  form  of  tariffs,  import  quotas,  export  subsidies,  and  so  on.

text: The financial maladjustments served to create an insufficiency of gold and a mal- distribution of gold.
text_raw:
The  financial  maladjustments  served  to  create  an  insufficiency  of  gold  and  a  mal-
distribution of  gold.

text: The inadequacy of the supply of gold arose from several causes.
text_raw: The  inadequacy  of  the  supply  of  gold  arose  from  several  causes.

text: It has been estimated that the world's stock of gold money needed to increase by 3.1 percent per year in the 1920's to support the world's economic development with stable prices on the gold standard.
text_raw:
It
has  been  estimated  that  the  world's  stock  of  gold  money  needed  to  increase  by  3.1  percent
per  year  in  the  1920's  to  support  the  world's  economic  development  with  stable  prices  on
the  gold  standard.

text: The production of new gold after 1920 was below this rate.
text_raw: The  production  of  new  gold  after  1920  was  below  this  rate.

text: Moreover, as a result of the activities of the League of Nations and financial advisers like Professor E.
text_raw:
Moreover,  as  a  result  of  the  activities  of  the  League  of  Nations  and  financial  advisers
like  Professor  E.

text: W.
text_raw: W.

text: Kemmerer of Princeton University, every country was encouraged to get on the gold standard.
text_raw:
Kemmerer  of  Princeton  University,  every  country  was  encouraged  to
get  on  the  gold  standard.

text: This led to a "gold rush" as each country tried to obtain a supply of gold large enough to provide adequate reserves.
text_raw:
This  led  to  a  "gold  rush"  as  each  country  tried  to  obtain  a  supply
of  gold  large  enough  to  provide  adequate  reserves.

text: Because there were more countries on gold in 1928 than in 1914 and because prices in general were higher, more gold was needed in reserves.
text_raw:
Because  there  were  more  countries  on
gold  in  1928  than  in  1914  and  because  prices  in  general  were  higher,  more  gold  was
needed  in  reserves.

text: The efforts to get around this by using a gold exchange standard rather than a gold standard were helpful in dealing with the problem of inadequate supplies of gold but increased the difficulty of the problem of mal-distribution of gold, since the gold exchange standard did not respond to the flow of gold as readily and thus did not serve so well to stem such flows of gold.
text_raw:
The  efforts  to  get  around  this  by  using  a  gold  exchange  standard  rather  than  a  gold
standard  were  helpful  in  dealing  with  the  problem  of  inadequate  supplies  of  gold  but
increased  the  difficulty  of  the  problem  of  mal-distribution  of  gold,  since  the  gold
exchange  standard  did  not  respond  to  the  flow  of  gold  as  readily  and  thus  did  not  serve  so
well  to  stem  such  flows  of  gold.

text: The need for gold was made greater by the existence of large floating balances of political or panic funds which might well move from one market to another independent of economic conditions.
text_raw:
The  need  for  gold  was  made  greater  by  the  existence  of
large  floating  balances  of  political  or  panic  funds  which  might  well  move  from  one
market  to  another  independent  of  economic  conditions.

text: The need was increased by the fact that in 1920 there were three major financial centers which had to make payments by shipments of gold in contrast to the single financial center of 1914 where payments could be made by bookkeeping transactions.
text_raw:
The  need  was  increased  by  the
fact  that  in  1920  there  were  three  major  financial  centers  which  had  to  make  payments  by
shipments  of  gold  in  contrast  to  the  single  financial  center  of  1914  where  payments  could
be  made  by  bookkeeping  transactions.

text: To rectify this problem to some degree, the Bank for International Settlements was created in 1929....
text_raw:
To  rectify  this  problem  to  some  degree,  the  Bank
for  International  Settlements  was  created  in  1929....

text: Finally, the need for gold was increased by the enormous growth in foreign indebtedness, much of it of a political nature such as the war debts and reparations.
text_raw:
Finally,  the  need  for  gold  was
increased  by  the  enormous  growth  in  foreign  indebtedness,  much  of  it  of  a  political
nature  such  as  the  war  debts  and  reparations.

text: The Financial System of 1914 Had Broken Down
text_raw: The  Financial  System  of  1914  Had  Broken  Down

text: On top of this insufficiency of gold was superimposed a drastic mal-distribution of gold.
text_raw:
On  top  of  this  insufficiency  of  gold  was  superimposed  a  drastic  mal-distribution  of
gold.

text: This was conclusive proof that the financial system of 1914 had broken down, for the old system would have operated automatically to distribute gold evenly.
text_raw:
This  was  conclusive  proof  that  the  financial  system  of  1914  had  broken  down,  for
the  old  system  would  have  operated  automatically  to  distribute  gold  evenly.

text: This mal- distribution resulted from the fact that when gold flowed into certain countries the automatic results of such a flow (such as rising prices or falling interest rates) which would have restored equilibrium in 1914 were prevented from acting in 1928.
text_raw:
This  mal-
distribution resulted  from  the  fact  that  when  gold  flowed  into  certain  countries  the
automatic  results  of  such  a  flow  (such  as  rising  prices  or  falling  interest  rates)  which
would  have  restored  equilibrium  in  1914  were  prevented  from  acting  in  1928.

text: In this period, about four-fifths of the world's gold supply was in five countries, and over half was in two, the United States and France.

In  this
period,  about  four-fifths  of  the  world's  gold  supply  was  in  five  countries,  and  over  half
was  in  two,  the  United  States  and  France.

text: The gold had been brought to these two for quite different reasons â€” to the United States because it was the world's greatest creditor and to France because of its devaluation of the franc.

The  gold  had  been  brought  to  these  two  for
quite  different  reasons â€” to  the  United  States  because  it  was  the  world's  greatest  creditor
and  to  France  because  of  its  devaluation  of  the  franc.

Britain,  on  the  other  hand,  had
floating  balances  of  about  Â£800  million,  and  handled  each  year  Â£20,000  million  in

text: To them sovereignty had not only all the legal and political connotations it had always held, but in addition had to include economic independence.

To  them  sovereignty  had  not  only  all  the  legal  and  political  connotations  it

text: Since such economic independence could, according to the theory, be obtained only by the Great Powers, the lesser states were to be deprived of sovereignty in its fullest sense and be reduced to a kind of vassal or client condition in respect to the Great Powers.

Since  such
economic  independence  could,  according  to  the  theory,  be  obtained  only  by  the  Great

The Rise of Economic Nationalism
text_raw: The  Rise  of  Economic  Nationalism

text: The economic nationalism which arose from the need to act in a crisis â€” and to act unilaterally because of the lack of any organ able to act multilaterally (that is, internationally) was intensified after the breakdown in finance and economics of 1931- 1933 by several developments.
text_raw:
The  economic  nationalism  which  arose  from  the  need  to  act  in  a  crisis â€” and  to  act
unilaterally  because  of  the  lack  of  any  organ  able  to  act  multilaterally  (that  is,
internationally)  was  intensified  after  the  breakdown  in  finance  and  economics  of  1931-
1933  by  several  developments.

text: In the first place, it was increased by the discovery, by Germany in 1932, by Italy in 1934, by Japan in 1936, and by the United States in 1938, that deflation could be prevented by rearming.
text_raw:
In  the  first  place,  it  was  increased  by  the  discovery,  by
Germany  in  1932,  by  Italy  in  1934,  by  Japan  in  1936,  and  by  the  United  States  in  1938,
that  deflation  could  be  prevented  by  rearming.

text: In the second place, it was increased by the realization that political activity was more powerful and more fundamental than economic activity â€” a realization which became clear when it was found that every step toward a unilateral economic solution resulted in reprisals from other nations which canceled out that step and made necessary another step, which, in its turn, called forth new reprisals; this soon showed that except in a nation capable of self-sufficiency such actions in the economic sphere could accomplish little and that unilateral action, if taken at all, must be accompanied by political steps (which would permit no reprisals).
text_raw:
In  the  second  place,  it  was  increased  by
the  realization  that  political  activity  was  more  powerful  and  more  fundamental  than

canceled  out  that  step  and  made  necessary  another  step,  which,  in  its  turn,  called  forth

actions  in  the  economic  sphere  could  accomplish  little  and  that  unilateral  action,  if  taken
at  all,  must  be  accompanied  by  political  steps  (which  would  permit  no  reprisals).

text: In the third place, economic nationalism was increased, and internationalism reduced, by the great increase in political insecurity, since the preservation of an international economic organization involved entrusting one's economic fate, to some degree, to the hands of another.
text_raw:
In  the
third  place,  economic  nationalism  was  increased,  and  internationalism  reduced,  by  the
great  increase  in  political  insecurity,  since  the  preservation  of  an  international  economic
organization  involved  entrusting  one's  economic  fate,  to  some  degree,  to  the  hands  of
another.

text: Rather than this, economic nationalism was increased in the name of autarky, security, economic mobilization, and so on.
text_raw:
Rather  than  this,  economic  nationalism  was  increased  in  the  name  of  autarky,
security,  economic  mobilization,  and  so  on.

text: Self-sufficiency, even if it involved a lower standard of living, was held preferable to international division of labor, on the grounds that political security was more important than a high â€” and insecure â€” standard of living.

standard  of  living,  was  held  preferable  to  international  division  of  labor,  on  the  grounds

text_raw: Britain's  New  Trade  Policy

Britain  sought  debt  collection  and  increase
of  exports  through  bilateralism.

chapter_title: Chapter  23 â€” The  International  Socialist  Movement
text: Unfortunately, as economic and social developments in advanced industrial countries moved in the un-Marxian directions we have mentioned, the unionized laborers and their Social Democratic political parties continued to accept the Marxist ideology or at least to utter the old Marxist war cries of "Down with the capitalists!" or "Long live the revolution" or "Workers of the world, unite!" Since the Marxist ideology and the Marxist war cries were more easily observed than the social realities they served to conceal, especially when labor leaders sought all publicity for what they said and profound secrecy for what they did, many capitalists, some workers, and almost all outsiders missed the new developments completely and continued to believe that a workers' revolution was just around the corner.

text: As the process of industrialization advanced, however, wages became a decreasing portion of productive costs, and other costs, especially the costs of equipment for mass production, for the technical management required by such equipment, and for the advertising and merchandising costs required for mass consumption, became more and more important.

chapter_title: Chapter  24 â€” The  Bolshevik  Revolution  to  1924

chapter_title: Chapter  24 â€” The  Bolshevik  Revolution  to  1924

chapter_title: Chapter  24 â€” The  Bolshevik  Revolution  to  1924

chapter_title: Chapter  24 â€” The  Bolshevik  Revolution  to  1924
text: By that time Stalin held the reins of government firmly in his own hands.
text_raw:
By  that  time  Stalin  held  the  reins  of  government
firmly  in  his  own  hands.

text: As Stalin gradually strengthened his internal control of the Soviet Union after Lenin's death in 1924, it became possible to turn, with increasing energy, to other matters.
text_raw:
As  Stalin  gradually  strengthened  his  internal  control  of  the  Soviet  Union  after  Lenin's
death  in  1924,  it  became  possible  to  turn,  with  increasing  energy,  to  other  matters.

text: The New Economic Policy, which Lenin had adopted in 1921, performed so successfully that the Soviet Union experienced a phenomenal recovery from the depths to which "War Communism" had dragged it in 1918-1921.
text_raw:
The
New  Economic  Policy,  which  Lenin  had  adopted  in  1921,  performed  so  successfully  that
the  Soviet  Union  experienced  a  phenomenal  recovery  from  the  depths  to  which  "War
Communism"  had  dragged  it  in  1918-1921.

text: Unfortunately for the economic theorists of the Soviet Union, the NEP was not really a "policy" at all, and it certainly was not Communism.
text_raw:
Unfortunately  for  the  economic  theorists  of  the  Soviet  Union,  the  NEP  was  not  really
a  "policy"  at  all,  and  it  certainly  was  not  Communism.

text: By reestablishing a new monetary system based on gold, in which one of the new gold rubles was equal to 50,000 of the old, inflated paper rubles, a firm financial basis was provided for recovery.
text_raw:
By  reestablishing  a  new  monetary
system  based  on  gold,  in  which  one  of  the  new  gold  rubles  was  equal  to  50,000  of  the
old,  inflated  paper  rubles,  a  firm  financial  basis  was  provided  for  recovery.

text: Except for a continuance of government regulation in international trade and in large-scale heavy industry, a regime of freedom was permitted.
text_raw:
Except  for  a
continuance  of  government  regulation  in  international  trade  and  in  large-scale  heavy
industry,  a  regime  of  freedom  was  permitted.

text: Agricultural production rose, commercial activities flourished, and the lighter industrial activities devoted to consumers' goods began to recover.
text_raw:
Agricultural  production  rose,  commercial
activities  flourished,  and  the  lighter  industrial  activities  devoted  to  consumers'  goods
began  to  recover.

text: Distinctions of wealth reappeared among the peasants, the richer ones (called "kulaks") being regarded with suspicion by the regime and with envy by their less fortunate neighbors.
text_raw:
Distinctions  of  wealth  reappeared  among  the  peasants,  the  richer  ones
(called  "kulaks")  being  regarded  with  suspicion  by  the  regime  and  with  envy  by  their  less
fortunate  neighbors.

text: At the same time, those who made their fortunes in commerce (called "nepmen") were sporadically persecuted by the regime as enemies of Socialism.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  those  who  made  their  fortunes  in  commerce
(called  "nepmen")  were  sporadically  persecuted  by  the  regime  as  enemies  of  Socialism.

text: Nonetheless, the economic system flourished.
text_raw: Nonetheless,  the  economic  system  flourished.

text: Acreage under cultivation rose from 148 million acres in 1921 to 222 million in 1927; grain collections, after the famine of 1922 had passed, approximately doubled in 1923-1927; coal production doubled in three years, while production of cotton textiles quadrupled.
text_raw:
Acreage  under  cultivation  rose  from  148
million  acres  in  1921  to  222  million  in  1927;  grain  collections,  after  the  famine  of  1922
had  passed,  approximately  doubled  in  1923-1927;  coal  production  doubled  in  three  years,
while  production  of  cotton  textiles  quadrupled.

text: As a consequence of such recovery, the Russian economic system in 1927 was, once again, back to its 1913 level, although, since population had gone up by ten million persons, the per capita income was lower.
text_raw:
As  a  consequence  of  such  recovery,  the
Russian  economic  system  in  1927  was,  once  again,  back  to  its  1913  level,  although,  since
population  had  gone  up  by  ten  million  persons,  the  per  capita  income  was  lower.

text: In spite of the economic recovery of the NEP, it gave rise to important problems.
text_raw: In  spite  of  the  economic  recovery  of  the  NEP,  it  gave  rise  to  important  problems.

text: Just as the free agricultural economy produced kulaks, and the free commercial system produced nepmen, so the mixed industrial system had undesirable consequences.
text_raw:
Just
as  the  free  agricultural  economy  produced  kulaks,  and  the  free  commercial  system
produced  nepmen,  so  the  mixed  industrial  system  had  undesirable  consequences.

text: Under this mixed system industries concerned with national defense were under direct state control; heavy industry was controlled by monopolistic trusts, which were owned by the state, but operated under separate budgets and were expected to be profitable; small industry w as free.
text_raw:
Under
this  mixed  system  industries  concerned  with  national  defense  were  under  direct  state
control;  heavy  industry  was  controlled  by  monopolistic  trusts,  which  were  owned  by  the
state,  but  operated  under  separate  budgets  and  were  expected  to  be  profitable;  small
industry  w  as  free.

text: One bad result of this was that small industry was squeezed in its efforts to obtain labor, materials, or credit, and its products were in scarce supply at high prices.
text_raw:
One  bad  result  of  this  was  that  small  industry  was  squeezed  in  its
efforts  to  obtain  labor,  materials,  or  credit,  and  its  products  were  in  scarce  supply  at  high
prices.

text: Another result was that agricultural prices, being free and competitive, fell lower and lower as agricultural production recovered, but industrial prices, being monopolistic, or in short supply, remained high.
text_raw:
Another  result  was  that  agricultural  prices,  being  free  and  competitive,  fell  lower
and  lower  as  agricultural  production  recovered,  but  industrial  prices,  being  monopolistic,
or  in  short  supply,  remained  high.

text: The result was a "scissors crisis," as it is called in Europe (or "parity prices," as it is called in America).
text_raw:
The  result  was  a  "scissors  crisis,"  as  it  is  called  in
Europe  (or  "parity  prices,"  as  it  is  called  in  America).

text: This meant that the goods farmers sold were at low prices, while the goods they bought were at high prices, and scarce.
text_raw:
This  meant  that  the  goods  farmers
sold  were  at  low  prices,  while  the  goods  they  bought  were  at  high  prices,  and  scarce.

text: Thus, in 1923, agricultural prices were at 58 percent of the 1913 level, while industrial prices were at 187 percent of their 1913 level, so that peasants could obtain only one- third as much manufactured goods for their crops as they had been able to obtain in 1913.
text_raw:
Thus,  in  1923,  agricultural  prices  were  at  58  percent  of  the  1913  level,  while  industrial
prices  were  at  187  percent  of  their  1913  level,  so  that  peasants  could  obtain  only  one-
third  as  much  manufactured  goods  for  their  crops  as  they  had  been  able  to  obtain  in  1913.

text: By withholding credit from industry, the government was able to force factories to liquidate their stocks of goods by lowering prices.
text_raw:
By  withholding  credit  from  industry,  the  government  was  able  to  force  factories  to
liquidate  their  stocks  of  goods  by  lowering  prices.

text: As a consequence, by 1924 industrial prices fell to 141 percent of 1913, while agricultural prices rose to 77 percent of 1913.
text_raw:
As  a  consequence,  by  1924  industrial
prices  fell  to  141  percent  of  1913,  while  agricultural  prices  rose  to  77  percent  of  1913.

text: The peasant's position was improved from one-third to one-half of his 1913 position, but at no time did he regain his 1913 parity level.
text_raw:
The  peasant's  position  was  improved  from  one-third  to  one-half  of  his  1913  position,  but
at  no  time  did  he  regain  his  1913  parity  level.

text: This gave rise to a great deal of agrarian discontent and to numerous peasant disturbances during the latter part of the NEP.
text_raw:
This  gave  rise  to  a  great  deal  of  agrarian
discontent  and  to  numerous  peasant  disturbances  during  the  latter  part  of  the  NEP.

text: Lenin had insisted that the weakness of the proletariat in Russia made it necessary to maintain an alliance with the peasantry.
text_raw:
Lenin  had  insisted  that  the  weakness  of  the  proletariat  in  Russia  made  it  necessary  to
maintain  an  alliance  with  the  peasantry.

text: This had been done during the period of state capitalism (November 1917-June 1918), but the alliance had been largely destroyed in the period of "War Communism" (June 1918-April 1921).
text_raw:
This  had  been  done  during  the  period  of  state
capitalism  (November  1917-June  1918),  but  the  alliance  had  been  largely  destroyed  in
the  period  of  "War  Communism"  (June  1918-April  1921).

text: Under the NEP this alliance was reestablished, but the "scissors crisis" once again destroyed it.
text_raw:
Under  the  NEP  this  alliance
was  reestablished,  but  the  "scissors  crisis"  once  again  destroyed  it.

text: Then it was reestablished only partially.
text_raw:
Then  it  was
reestablished  only  partially.

text: Stalin's victory over Trotsky and his personal inclination for terroristic methods of government led to decisions which marked the end of these cycles of peasant discontent.
text_raw:
Stalin's  victory  over  Trotsky  and  his  personal  inclination  for
terroristic  methods  of  government  led  to  decisions  which  marked  the  end  of  these  cycles
of  peasant  discontent.

text: The decision to build Socialism in a single country made it necessary, it was felt, to emphasize the predominance of heavy industry in order to obtain, as quickly as possible, the basis for the manufacture of armaments (chiefly iron, steel, coal, and electrical power projects).
text_raw:
The  decision  to  build  Socialism  in  a  single  country  made  it
necessary,  it  was  felt,  to  emphasize  the  predominance  of  heavy  industry  in  order  to
obtain,  as  quickly  as  possible,  the  basis  for  the  manufacture  of  armaments  (chiefly  iron,
steel,  coal,  and  electrical  power  projects).

text: Such projects required great masses of labor to be concentrated together and fed.
text_raw:
Such  projects  required  great  masses  of  labor  to
be  concentrated  together  and  fed.

text: Both the labor and the food would have to be drawn from the peasantry, but the emphasis on heavy industrial production rather than on light industry meant that there would be few consumers' goods to give to the peasantry in return for the food taken from them.
text_raw:
Both  the  labor  and  the  food  would  have  to  be  drawn
from  the  peasantry,  but  the  emphasis  on  heavy  industrial  production  rather  than  on  light
industry  meant  that  there  would  be  few  consumers'  goods  to  give  to  the  peasantry  in
return  for  the  food  taken  from  them.

text: Moreover, the drain of manpower from the peasantry to form urban labor forces would mean that those who continued to be peasants must greatly improve their methods of agricultural production in order to supply, with a smaller proportion of peasants, food for themselves, for the new urban laborers, for the growing party bureaucracy, and for the growing Red Army which was regarded as essential to defend "Socialism in a single country.".
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  drain  of  manpower  from  the  peasantry
to  form  urban  labor  forces  would  mean  that  those  who  continued  to  be  peasants  must
greatly  improve  their  methods  of  agricultural  production  in  order  to  supply,  with  a
smaller  proportion  of  peasants,  food  for  themselves,  for  the  new  urban  laborers,  for  the
growing  party  bureaucracy,  and  for  the  growing  Red  Army  which  was  regarded  as
essential  to  defend  "Socialism  in  a  single  country.".

text: The problem of obtaining increasing supplies of food from fewer peasants without offering them consumers' industrial goods in exchange could not, according to Stalin, be worked in a peasant regime based on freedom of commerce, as under the NEP of 1921- 1927, or in one based on individual farmers, as in the "War Communism" of 1918-1921; the former of these required that the peasants be given goods in exchange while the latter could be made a failure by peasant refusals to produce more food than was required by their own needs.
text_raw:
The  problem  of  obtaining  increasing  supplies  of  food  from  fewer  peasants  without
offering  them  consumers'  industrial  goods  in  exchange  could  not,  according  to  Stalin,  be
worked  in  a  peasant  regime  based  on  freedom  of  commerce,  as  under  the  NEP  of  1921-
1927,  or  in  one  based  on  individual  farmers,  as  in  the  "War  Communism"  of  1918-1921;
the  former  of  these  required  that  the  peasants  be  given  goods  in  exchange  while  the  latter
could  be  made  a  failure  by  peasant  refusals  to  produce  more  food  than  was  required  by
their  own  needs.

text: The NEP could not find a solution to this problem.
text_raw: The  NEP  could  not  find  a  solution  to  this  problem.

text: In spite of the closing of the scissors in 1923-1927, industrial prices remained higher than farm prices, peasants were reluctant to supply food to the cities since they could not get the cities' products they wanted in return, and the amount of peasants' grain which was sold remained about 13 percent of the grain raised in 1927 compared to 26 percent in 1913.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  the
closing  of  the  scissors  in  1923-1927,  industrial  prices  remained  higher  than  farm  prices,
peasants  were  reluctant  to  supply  food  to  the  cities  since  they  could  not  get  the  cities'
products  they  wanted  in  return,  and  the  amount  of  peasants'  grain  which  was  sold
remained  about  13  percent  of  the  grain  raised  in  1927  compared  to  26  percent  in  1913.

text: Such a system might provide a high standard of living for the peasants, but it could never provide the highly industrialized basis necessary to support "Socialism in a single country."
text_raw:
Such  a  system  might  provide  a  high  standard  of  living  for  the  peasants,  but  it  could  never
provide  the  highly  industrialized  basis  necessary  to  support  "Socialism  in  a  single
country."

text: The new direction which Russia's development took after 1927 and which we call "Stalinism" is a consequence of numerous factors.
text_raw:
The  new  direction  which  Russia's  development  took  after  1927  and  which  we  call
"Stalinism"  is  a  consequence  of  numerous  factors.

text: Three of these factors were (1) the bloodthirsty and paranoiac ambitions of Stalin and his associates, (2) a return of Russia to its older traditions, but on a new level and a new intensity, and (3) a theory of social, political, and economic developments which is included under the phrase "Socialism in a single country." This theory was embraced with such an insane fanaticism by the rulers of the new Russia, and provided such powerful motivations for Soviet foreign and domestic politics, that it must be analyzed at some length.
text_raw:
Three  of  these  factors  were  (1)  the
bloodthirsty  and  paranoiac  ambitions  of  Stalin  and  his  associates,  (2)  a  return  of  Russia  to
its  older  traditions,  but  on  a  new  level  and  a  new  intensity,  and  (3)  a  theory  of  social,
political,  and  economic  developments  which  is  included  under  the  phrase  "Socialism  in  a
single  country."  This  theory  was  embraced  with  such  an  insane  fanaticism  by  the  rulers  of
the  new  Russia,  and  provided  such  powerful  motivations  for  Soviet  foreign  and  domestic
politics,  that  it  must  be  analyzed  at  some  length.

text: The rivalry between Stalin and Trotsky in the mid-1920's was fought with slogans as well as with more violent weapons.
text_raw:
The  rivalry  between  Stalin  and  Trotsky  in  the  mid-1920's  was  fought  with  slogans  as
well  as  with  more  violent  weapons.

text: Trotsky called for "world revolution," while Stalin wanted "Communism in a single country." According to Trotsky, Russia was economically too weak and too backward to be able to establish a Communist system alone.
text_raw:
Trotsky  called  for  "world  revolution,"  while  Stalin
wanted  "Communism  in  a  single  country."  According  to  Trotsky,  Russia  was
economically  too  weak  and  too  backward  to  be  able  to  establish  a  Communist  system
alone.

text: Such a system, all agreed, could not exist except in a fully industrialized country.
text_raw: Such  a  system,  all  agreed,  could  not  exist  except  in  a  fully  industrialized  country.

text: Russia, which was so far from being industrialized, could obtain the necessary capital only by borrowing it abroad or by accumulating it from its own people.
text_raw:
Russia,  which  was  so  far  from  being  industrialized,  could  obtain  the  necessary  capital
only  by  borrowing  it  abroad  or  by  accumulating  it  from  its  own  people.

text: In either case, it would be taken, in the long run, from Russia's peasants by political duress, in the one case being exported to pay for foreign loans and, in the other case, being given, as food and raw materials, to the industrial workers in the city.
text_raw:
In  either  case,  it
would  be  taken,  in  the  long  run,  from  Russia's  peasants  by  political  duress,  in  the  one
case  being  exported  to  pay  for  foreign  loans  and,  in  the  other  case,  being  given,  as  food
and  raw  materials,  to  the  industrial  workers  in  the  city.

text: Both cases would be fraught with dangers; foreign countries, because their own economic systems were capitalistic, would not stand idly by and allow a rival Socialistic system to reach successful achievement in Russia; moreover, in either case, there would be a dangerously high level of peasant discontent, since the necessary food and raw materials would have to be taken from Russia's peasantry by political duress, without economic return.
text_raw:
Both  cases  would  be  fraught  with
dangers;  foreign  countries,  because  their  own  economic  systems  were  capitalistic,  would
not  stand  idly  by  and  allow  a  rival  Socialistic  system  to  reach  successful  achievement  in
Russia;  moreover,  in  either  case,  there  would  be  a  dangerously  high  level  of  peasant
discontent,  since  the  necessary  food  and  raw  materials  would  have  to  be  taken  from
Russia's  peasantry  by  political  duress,  without  economic  return.

text: This followed from the Soviet theory that the enmity of foreign capitalist countries would require Russia's new industry to emphasize heavy industrial products able to support the manufacture of armaments rather than light industrial products able to provide consumers' goods which could be given to the peasants in return for their produce.
text_raw:
This  followed  from  the
Soviet  theory  that  the  enmity  of  foreign  capitalist  countries  would  require  Russia's  new
industry  to  emphasize  heavy  industrial  products  able  to  support  the  manufacture  of
armaments  rather  than  light  industrial  products  able  to  provide  consumers'  goods  which
could  be  given  to  the  peasants  in  return  for  their  produce.

text: The Bolsheviks assumed, as an axiom, that capitalistic countries would not allow the Soviet Union to build up a successful Socialistic system which would make all capitalism obsolete.
text_raw:
The  Bolsheviks  assumed,  as  an  axiom,  that  capitalistic  countries  would  not  allow  the
Soviet  Union  to  build  up  a  successful  Socialistic  system  which  would  make  all  capitalism
obsolete.

text: This idea was strengthened by a theory, to which Lenin made a chief contribution, that "imperialism is the last stage of capitalism." According to this theory, a fully industrialized capitalistic country enters upon a period of economic depression which leads it to embrace a program of warlike aggression.
text_raw:
This  idea  was  strengthened  by  a  theory,  to  which  Lenin  made  a  chief
contribution,  that  "imperialism  is  the  last  stage  of  capitalism."  According  to  this  theory,  a
fully  industrialized  capitalistic  country  enters  upon  a  period  of  economic  depression
which  leads  it  to  embrace  a  program  of  warlike  aggression.

text: The theory insisted that the distribution of income in a capitalistic society would become so inequitable that the masses of the people would not obtain sufficient income to buy the goods being produced by the industrial plants.
text_raw:
The  theory  insisted  that  the
distribution  of  income  in  a  capitalistic  society  would  become  so  inequitable  that  the
masses  of  the  people  would  not  obtain  sufficient  income  to  buy  the  goods  being  produced
by  the  industrial  plants.

text: As such unsold goods accumulated with decreasing profits and deepening depression, there would be a shift toward the production of armaments to provide profits and produce goods which could be sold and there would be an increasingly aggressive foreign policy in order to obtain markets for unsold goods in backward or undeveloped countries.
text_raw:
As  such  unsold  goods  accumulated  with  decreasing  profits  and
deepening  depression,  there  would  be  a  shift  toward  the  production  of  armaments  to
provide  profits  and  produce  goods  which  could  be  sold  and  there  would  be  an
increasingly  aggressive  foreign  policy  in  order  to  obtain  markets  for  unsold  goods  in
backward  or  undeveloped  countries.

text: Such aggressive imperialism, it seemed to Soviet thinkers, would inevitably make Russia a target of aggression in order to prevent a successful Communist system there from becoming an attractive model for the discontented proletariat in capitalistic countries.
text_raw:
Such  aggressive  imperialism,  it  seemed  to  Soviet
thinkers,  would  inevitably  make  Russia  a  target  of  aggression  in  order  to  prevent  a
successful  Communist  system  there  from  becoming  an  attractive  model  for  the
discontented  proletariat  in  capitalistic  countries.

text: According to Trotsky, all these truths made it quite obvious that "Socialism in a single country" was an impossible idea, especially if that single country was as poor and backward as Russia.
text_raw:
According  to  Trotsky,  all  these  truths
made  it  quite  obvious  that  "Socialism  in  a  single  country"  was  an  impossible  idea,
especially  if  that  single  country  was  as  poor  and  backward  as  Russia.

text: To Trotsky and his friends it seemed quite clear that the salvation of the Soviet system must be sought in a world revolution which would bring other countries, especially such an advanced industrial country as Germany, to Russia's side as allies.
text_raw:
To  Trotsky  and  his
friends  it  seemed  quite  clear  that  the  salvation  of  the  Soviet  system  must  be  sought  in  a
world  revolution  which  would  bring  other  countries,  especially  such  an  advanced
industrial  country  as  Germany,  to  Russia's  side  as  allies.

text: While the internal struggle between Trotsky and Stalin was wending its weary way in 1923-1927, it became quite clear not only that world revolution was impossible and that Germany was not going either to a Communist revolution or an alliance with the Soviet, it also became equally clear that "oppressed colonial" areas such as China were not going
text_raw:
While  the  internal  struggle  between  Trotsky  and  Stalin  was  wending  its  weary  way  in
1923-1927,  it  became  quite  clear  not  only  that  world  revolution  was  impossible  and  that
Germany  was  not  going  either  to  a  Communist  revolution  or  an  alliance  with  the  Soviet,
it  also  became  equally  clear  that  "oppressed  colonial"  areas  such  as  China  were  not  going

text: to ally with the Soviet Union.
text_raw: to  ally  with  the  Soviet  Union.

text: "Communism in a single country" had to be adopted as Russia's policy simply because there was no alternative.
text_raw:
"Communism  in  a  single  country"  had  to  be  adopted  as
Russia's  policy  simply  because  there  was  no  alternative.

text: Communism in Russia alone required, according to Bolshevik thinkers, that the country must be industrialized with breakneck speed, whatever the waste and hardships, and must emphasize heavy industry and armaments rather than rising standards of living.
text_raw:
Communism  in  Russia  alone  required,  according  to  Bolshevik  thinkers,  that  the
country  must  be  industrialized  with  breakneck  speed,  whatever  the  waste  and  hardships,
and  must  emphasize  heavy  industry  and  armaments  rather  than  rising  standards  of  living.

text: This meant that the goods produced by the peasants must be taken from them, by political duress, without any economic return, and that the ultimate in authoritarian terror must be used to prevent the peasants from reducing their level of production to their own consumption needs, as they had done in the period of "War Communism" in 1918-1921.
text_raw:
This  meant  that  the  goods  produced  by  the  peasants  must  be  taken  from  them,  by  political
duress,  without  any  economic  return,  and  that  the  ultimate  in  authoritarian  terror  must  be
used  to  prevent  the  peasants  from  reducing  their  level  of  production  to  their  own
consumption  needs,  as  they  had  done  in  the  period  of  "War  Communism"  in  1918-1921.

text: This meant that the first step toward the industrialization of Russia required that the peasantry be broken by terror and reorganized from a capitalistic basis of private farms to a Socialistic system of collective farms.
text_raw:
This  meant  that  the  first  step  toward  the  industrialization  of  Russia  required  that  the
peasantry  be  broken  by  terror  and  reorganized  from  a  capitalistic  basis  of  private  farms  to
a  Socialistic  system  of  collective  farms.

text: Moreover, to prevent imperialist capitalistic countries from taking advantage of the inevitable unrest this program would create in Russia, it was necessary to crush all kinds of foreign espionage, resistance to the Bolshevik state, independent thought, or public discontent.
text_raw:
Moreover,  to  prevent  imperialist  capitalistic
countries  from  taking  advantage  of  the  inevitable  unrest  this  program  would  create  in
Russia,  it  was  necessary  to  crush  all  kinds  of  foreign  espionage,  resistance  to  the
Bolshevik  state,  independent  thought,  or  public  discontent.

text: These must be crushed by terror so that the whole of Russia could be formed into a monolithic structure of disciplined proletariat who would obey their leaders with such unquestioning obedience that it would strike fear in the hearts of every potential aggressor.
text_raw:
These  must  be  crushed  by
terror  so  that  the  whole  of  Russia  could  be  formed  into  a  monolithic  structure  of
disciplined  proletariat  who  would  obey  their  leaders  with  such  unquestioning  obedience
that  it  would  strike  fear  in  the  hearts  of  every  potential  aggressor.

text: The steps in this theory followed one another like the steps of a geometrical proposition: failure of the revolution in industrially advanced Germany required that Communism be established in backward Russia; this demanded rapid industrialization with emphasis on heavy industry; this meant that the peasants could not obtain consumers' goods for their food and raw materials; this meant that the peasants must be reduced by terroristic duress to collective farms where they could neither resist nor reduce their levels of production: this required that all discontent and independence be crushed under a despotic police state to prevent foreign capitalistic imperialists from exploiting the discontent or social unrest in Russia.
text_raw:
The  steps  in  this  theory  followed  one  another  like  the  steps  of  a  geometrical
proposition:  failure  of  the  revolution  in  industrially  advanced  Germany  required  that
Communism  be  established  in  backward  Russia;  this  demanded  rapid  industrialization
with  emphasis  on  heavy  industry;  this  meant  that  the  peasants  could  not  obtain
consumers'  goods  for  their  food  and  raw  materials;  this  meant  that  the  peasants  must  be
reduced  by  terroristic  duress  to  collective  farms  where  they  could  neither  resist  nor
reduce  their  levels  of  production:  this  required  that  all  discontent  and  independence  be
crushed  under  a  despotic  police  state  to  prevent  foreign  capitalistic  imperialists  from
exploiting  the  discontent  or  social  unrest  in  Russia.

text: To the rulers in the Kremlin the final proof of the truth of this proposition appeared when Germany, which had not gone Communist but had remained capitalistic, attacked Russia in 1941.
text_raw:
To  the  rulers  in  the  Kremlin  the  final
proof  of  the  truth  of  this  proposition  appeared  when  Germany,  which  had  not  gone
Communist  but  had  remained  capitalistic,  attacked  Russia  in  1941.

text: A historian, who might question the assumptions or the stages in this theory, would also see that the theory made it possible for Bolshevik Russia to abandon most of the influences of Western ideology in Marxism (such as its humanitarianism, its equality, or its anti-militarist, anti-state bias) and allow it to fall back into the Russian tradition of a despotic police state resting on espionage and terror, in which there was a profound gulf in ideology and manner of living between the rulers and the ruled.
text_raw:
A  historian,  who  might  question  the  assumptions  or  the  stages  in  this  theory,  would
also  see  that  the  theory  made  it  possible  for  Bolshevik  Russia  to  abandon  most  of  the
influences  of  Western  ideology  in  Marxism  (such  as  its  humanitarianism,  its  equality,  or
its  anti-militarist,  anti-state  bias)  and  allow  it  to  fall  back  into  the  Russian  tradition  of  a
despotic  police  state  resting  on  espionage  and  terror,  in  which  there  was  a  profound  gulf
in  ideology  and  manner  of  living  between  the  rulers  and  the  ruled.

text: It should also be evident that a new regime, such as Bolshevism was in Russia, would have no traditional methods of social recruitment or circulation of elites; these would be based on intrigue and violence and would inevitably bring to the top the most decisive, most merciless, most unprincipled, and most violent of its members.
text_raw:
It  should  also  be
evident  that  a  new  regime,  such  as  Bolshevism  was  in  Russia,  would  have  no  traditional
methods  of  social  recruitment  or  circulation  of  elites;  these  would  be  based  on  intrigue
and  violence  and  would  inevitably  bring  to  the  top  the  most  decisive,  most  merciless,
most  unprincipled,  and  most  violent  of  its  members.

text: Such a group, forming around Stalin, began the process of establishing "Communism in a single country" in 1927-1929, and continued it until interrupted by the approach of war in 1941.
text_raw:
Such  a  group,  forming  around  Stalin,
began  the  process  of  establishing  "Communism  in  a  single  country"  in  1927-1929,  and
continued  it  until  interrupted  by  the  approach  of  war  in  1941.

text: This program of heavy industrialization was organized in a series of "Five- Year Plans," of which the first covered the years 1928-1932.
text_raw:
This  program  of  heavy
industrialization  was  organized  in  a  series  of  "Five- Year  Plans,"  of  which  the  first
covered  the  years  1928-1932.

text: The chief elements in the First Five- Year Plan were the collectivization of agriculture and the creation of a basic system of heavy industry.
text_raw:
The  chief  elements  in  the  First  Five- Year  Plan  were  the  collectivization  of  agriculture
and  the  creation  of  a  basic  system  of  heavy  industry.

text: In order to increase the supply of food and industrial labor in the cities, Stalin forced the peasants off their own lands (worked by their own animals and their own tools) onto large communal farms, worked cooperatively with lands, tools, and animals owned in common, or onto huge state farms, run as state-owned enterprises by wage-earning employees using lands, tools, and animals owned by the government.
text_raw:
In  order  to  increase  the  supply  of
food  and  industrial  labor  in  the  cities,  Stalin  forced  the  peasants  off  their  own  lands
(worked  by  their  own  animals  and  their  own  tools)  onto  large  communal  farms,  worked
cooperatively  with  lands,  tools,  and  animals  owned  in  common,  or  onto  huge  state  farms,
run  as  state-owned  enterprises  by  wage-earning  employees  using  lands,  tools,  and
animals  owned  by  the  government.

text: In communal farms the crops were owned jointly by the members and were divided, after certain amounts had been set aside for taxes, purchases, and other payments which directed food to the cities.
text_raw:
In  communal  farms  the  crops  were  owned  jointly  by
the  members  and  were  divided,  after  certain  amounts  had  been  set  aside  for  taxes,
purchases,  and  other  payments  which  directed  food  to  the  cities.

text: In state farms the crops were owned outright by the state, after the necessary costs had been paid.
text_raw:
In  state  farms  the  crops
were  owned  outright  by  the  state,  after  the  necessary  costs  had  been  paid.

text: In time, experience showed that the costs of the state farms were so high and their operations so inefficient that they were hardly worthwhile, although they continued to be created.
text_raw:
In  time,
experience  showed  that  the  costs  of  the  state  farms  were  so  high  and  their  operations  so
inefficient  that  they  were  hardly  worthwhile,  although  they  continued  to  be  created.

text: The shift to the new system came slowly in 1927-1929 and then was put violently into full operation in 1930.
text_raw:
The  shift  to  the  new  system  came  slowly  in  1927-1929  and  then  was  put  violently  into
full  operation  in  1930.

text: In the space of six weeks (February-March 1930) collective farms increased from 59,400, with 4,400,000 families, to 110,200 farms, with 14,300,000 families.
text_raw:
In  the  space  of  six  weeks  (February-March  1930)  collective  farms
increased  from  59,400,  with  4,400,000  families,  to  110,200  farms,  with  14,300,000
families.

text: All peasants who resisted were treated with violence; their property was confiscated, they were beaten or sent into exile in remote areas; many were killed.
text_raw:
All  peasants  who  resisted  were  treated  with  violence;  their  property  was
confiscated,  they  were  beaten  or  sent  into  exile  in  remote  areas;  many  were  killed.

text: This process, known as "the liquidation of the kulaks" (since the richer peasantry resisted most vigorously), affected five million kulak families.
text_raw:
This
process,  known  as  "the  liquidation  of  the  kulaks"  (since  the  richer  peasantry  resisted  most
vigorously),  affected  five  million  kulak  families.

text: Rather than give up their animals to the collective farms, many peasants killed them.
text_raw:
Rather  than  give  up  their  animals  to  the
collective  farms,  many  peasants  killed  them.

text: As a result, the number of cattle was reduced from 30.7 million in 1928 to 19.6 million in 1933, while, in the same five years, sheep and goats fell from 146.7 million to 50.2 million, hogs from 26 to 12.1 million, and horses from 33.5 to 16.6 million.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  the  number  of  cattle  was
reduced  from  30.7  million  in  1928  to  19.6  million  in  1933,  while,  in  the  same  five  years,
sheep  and  goats  fell  from  146.7  million  to  50.2  million,  hogs  from  26  to  12.1  million,  and
horses  from  33.5  to  16.6  million.

text: Moreover, the planting season of 1930 was entirely disrupted, and the agricultural activities of later years continued to be disturbed so that food production decreased drastically.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  planting  season  of  1930  was  entirely
disrupted,  and  the  agricultural  activities  of  later  years  continued  to  be  disturbed  so  that
food  production  decreased  drastically.

text: Since the government insisted on taking the food needed to support the urban population, the rural areas were left with inadequate food, and at least three million peasants starved in 1931-1933.
text_raw:
Since  the  government  insisted  on  taking  the  food
needed  to  support  the  urban  population,  the  rural  areas  were  left  with  inadequate  food,
and  at  least  three  million  peasants  starved  in  1931-1933.

text: Twelve years later, in 1945, Stalin told Winston Churchill that twelve million peasants died in this reorganization of agriculture.
text_raw:
Twelve  years  later,  in  1945,
Stalin  told  Winston  Churchill  that  twelve  million  peasants  died  in  this  reorganization  of
agriculture.

text: To compensate for these setbacks, large areas of previously uncultivated lands, many of them semiarid, were brought under cultivation, mostly in Siberia, as state farms.
text_raw:
To  compensate  for  these  setbacks,  large  areas  of  previously  uncultivated  lands,  many
of  them  semiarid,  were  brought  under  cultivation,  mostly  in  Siberia,  as  state  farms.

text: Considerable research was done on new crop varieties to increase yields, and to utilize the drier lands of the south and the shorter growing season in the north.
text_raw:
Considerable  research  was  done  on  new  crop  varieties  to  increase  yields,  and  to  utilize
the  drier  lands  of  the  south  and  the  shorter  growing  season  in  the  north.

text: As a consequence, the area under cultivation increased by 21 percent in 1927-1938.
text_raw:
As  a
consequence,  the  area  under  cultivation  increased  by  21  percent  in  1927-1938.

text: However, the fact that the Soviet population rose, in the same eleven years, from 150 million to 170 million persons, meant that the cultivated acreage per capita rose only from 1.9 to 2.0 acres.
text_raw:
However,
the  fact  that  the  Soviet  population  rose,  in  the  same  eleven  years,  from  150  million  to  170
million  persons,  meant  that  the  cultivated  acreage  per  capita  rose  only  from  1.9  to  2.0
acres.

text: The use of semiarid lands required a considerable extension of irrigation; thus there was an increase of about 50 percent in the acreage irrigated in the decade 1928-1938 (from ro.6 million acres to 15.2 million acres).
text_raw:
The  use  of  semiarid  lands  required  a  considerable  extension  of  irrigation;  thus  there
was  an  increase  of  about  50  percent  in  the  acreage  irrigated  in  the  decade  1928-1938
(from  ro.6  million  acres  to  15.2  million  acres).

text: Some of these irrigation projects combined irrigation with the generation of electricity by waterpower, and provided improved water transportation facilities, as in our Tennessee Valley Authority; this was true of the famous project at Dnepropetrovsk on the lower Dnieper River, which had a capacity of half ,a million kilowatts ( 1935).
text_raw:
Some  of  these  irrigation  projects
combined  irrigation  with  the  generation  of  electricity  by  waterpower,  and  provided
improved  water  transportation  facilities,  as  in  our  Tennessee  Valley  Authority;  this  was
true  of  the  famous  project  at  Dnepropetrovsk  on  the  lower  Dnieper  River,  which  had  a

text: The reduction in farm animals, which was not made up by 1941, combined with the efforts to develop heavy industry, resulted in increased use of tractors and other mechanized equipment in agriculture.
text_raw:
The  reduction  in  farm  animals,  which  was  not  made  up  by  1941,  combined  with  the
efforts  to  develop  heavy  industry,  resulted  in  increased  use  of  tractors  and  other
mechanized  equipment  in  agriculture.

text: The number of tractors rose from 26.7 thousand in 1928 to 483.5 thousand in 1938, while in the same decade the percentage of plowing done by tractors increased from I percent to 7, percent.
text_raw:
The  number  of  tractors  rose  from  26.7  thousand  in
1928  to  483.5  thousand  in  1938,  while  in  the  same  decade  the  percentage  of  plowing
done  by  tractors  increased  from  I  percent  to  7,  percent.

text: Harvesting was increasingly done by combines, the number of these increasing from almost none in 1928 to 182,000 in 1940.
text_raw:
Harvesting  was  increasingly  done
by  combines,  the  number  of  these  increasing  from  almost  none  in  1928  to  182,000  in
1940.

text: Such complicated machinery was not owned by the collective farms but by independent machine-tractor stations scattered about the country; they had to be hired from these as they were needed.
text_raw:
Such  complicated  machinery  was  not  owned  by  the  collective  farms  but  by
independent  machine-tractor  stations  scattered  about  the  country;  they  had  to  be  hired
from  these  as  they  were  needed.

text: The introduction of mechanized farming of this type was not an unmixed success, as many machines were ruined by inexperienced help and the costs of upkeep and fuel were very high.
text_raw:
The  introduction  of  mechanized  farming  of  this  type  was
not  an  unmixed  success,  as  many  machines  were  ruined  by  inexperienced  help  and  the
costs  of  upkeep  and  fuel  were  very  high.

text: Nevertheless, the trend toward mechanization continued, partly from a desire to copy the United States and partly from a rather childish enthusiasm for modern technology.
text_raw:
Nevertheless,  the  trend  toward  mechanization
continued,  partly  from  a  desire  to  copy  the  United  States  and  partly  from  a  rather  childish
enthusiasm  for  modern  technology.

text: These two impulses combined, at times, to produce a "gigantomania," or enthusiasm for large size rather than for efficiency or a satisfactory way of life.
text_raw:
These  two  impulses  combined,  at  times,  to  produce  a
"gigantomania,"  or  enthusiasm  for  large  size  rather  than  for  efficiency  or  a  satisfactory
way  of  life.

text: In agriculture this gave rise to many enormous state farms of hundreds of thousands of acres which were notoriously inefficient.
text_raw:
In  agriculture  this  gave  rise  to  many  enormous  state  farms  of  hundreds  of
thousands  of  acres  which  were  notoriously  inefficient.

text: Moreover, the shift to such large- scale mechanized agriculture, in contrast to the old czarist agriculture organized in scattered peasant plots cultivated in a three-year, fallow-rotation system, greatly increased such problems as spreading drought, losses to insect pests, and decreasing soil fertility, requiring the use of artificial fertilizers.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  shift  to  such  large-
scale  mechanized  agriculture,  in  contrast  to  the  old  czarist  agriculture  organized  in
scattered  peasant  plots  cultivated  in  a  three-year,  fallow-rotation  system,  greatly
increased  such  problems  as  spreading  drought,  losses  to  insect  pests,  and  decreasing  soil
fertility,  requiring  the  use  of  artificial  fertilizers.

text: In spite of all these problems, Soviet agriculture, without ever becoming successful or even adequate, provided a steadily expanding base for the growth of Soviet industry, until both were disrupted by the invasion of Hitler's hordes in the summer of 1941.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  all  these  problems,  Soviet
agriculture,  without  ever  becoming  successful  or  even  adequate,  provided  a  steadily
expanding  base  for  the  growth  of  Soviet  industry,  until  both  were  disrupted  by  the
invasion  of  Hitler's  hordes  in  the  summer  of  1941.

text: The industrial portion of the First Five- Year Plan was pursued with the same ruthless drive as the collectivization of agriculture and had similar spectacular results: impressive physical accomplishment, large-scale waste, lack of integration, ruthless disregard of personal comfort and standards of living, constant purges of opposition elements, of scapegoats, and of the inefficient, all to the accompaniment of blasts of propaganda inflating the plan's real achievements to incredible dimensions, attacking opposition groups (sometimes real and frequently imaginary) within the Soviet Union, or mixing scorn with fear in verbal assaults on foreign "capitalist imperialist" countries and their secret "saboteurs" within Russia.
text_raw:
The  industrial  portion  of  the  First  Five- Year  Plan  was  pursued  with  the  same  ruthless
drive  as  the  collectivization  of  agriculture  and  had  similar  spectacular  results:  impressive
physical  accomplishment,  large-scale  waste,  lack  of  integration,  ruthless  disregard  of
personal  comfort  and  standards  of  living,  constant  purges  of  opposition  elements,  of
scapegoats,  and  of  the  inefficient,  all  to  the  accompaniment  of  blasts  of  propaganda
inflating  the  plan's  real  achievements  to  incredible  dimensions,  attacking  opposition
groups  (sometimes  real  and  frequently  imaginary)  within  the  Soviet  Union,  or  mixing
scorn  with  fear  in  verbal  assaults  on  foreign  "capitalist  imperialist"  countries  and  their
secret  "saboteurs"  within  Russia.

text: The First Five- Year Plan of 1928-1932 was followed by a Second Plan of 1933-1937 and a Third Plan of 1938-1942.
text_raw:
The  First  Five- Year  Plan  of  1928-1932  was  followed  by  a  Second  Plan  of  1933-1937
and  a  Third  Plan  of  1938-1942.

text: The last of these was completely disrupted by the German invasion of June 1941, and had, from the beginning, undergone periodic modifications which changed its targets in the direction of an increased emphasis on armaments because of the rising international tensions.
text_raw:
The  last  of  these  was  completely  disrupted  by  the
German  invasion  of  June  1941,  and  had,  from  the  beginning,  undergone  periodic
modifications  which  changed  its  targets  in  the  direction  of  an  increased  emphasis  on
armaments  because  of  the  rising  international  tensions.

text: Because of the inadequacies of the available Soviet statistics, it is not easy to make any definite statements about the success of these plans.
text_raw:
Because  of  the  inadequacies  of
the  available  Soviet  statistics,  it  is  not  easy  to  make  any  definite  statements  about  the
success  of  these  plans.

text: There can be no doubt that there was a great increase in the physical output of industrial goods and that this output was very largely in capital equipment rather than in consumers' goods.
text_raw:
There  can  be  no  doubt  that  there  was  a  great  increase  in  the
physical  output  of  industrial  goods  and  that  this  output  was  very  largely  in  capital
equipment  rather  than  in  consumers'  goods.

text: It is also clear that much of this advance was uncoordinated and spotty and that, while Soviet national income was rising, the standard of living of the Russian peoples was declining from its 1928 level.
text_raw:
It  is  also  clear  that  much  of  this  advance  was
uncoordinated  and  spotty  and  that,  while  Soviet  national  income  was  rising,  the  standard
of  living  of  the  Russian  peoples  was  declining  from  its  1928  level.

text: There can be little doubt that this ... industrialization made it possible for the Soviet system to withstand the German assault in 1941.
text_raw:
There  can  be  little  doubt  that  this  ...  industrialization  made  it  possible  for  the  Soviet
