text: At the same time the magnitude of the achievement produced great distortions and tensions in Soviet life.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time  the  magnitude  of  the
achievement  produced  great  distortions  and  tensions  in  Soviet  life.

text: Millions of persons moved from villages to cities (some of these entirely new) to find inadequate housing, inadequate food, and violent psychological tensions.
text_raw:
Millions  of  persons
moved  from  villages  to  cities  (some  of  these  entirely  new)  to  find  inadequate  housing,
inadequate  food,  and  violent  psychological  tensions.

text: On the other hand, the same move opened to them wide opportunities in ... education, for themselves and for their children, as well as opportunities to rise in the social, economic, and party structures.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  the  same  move
opened  to  them  wide  opportunities  in  ...  education,  for  themselves  and  for  their  children,
as  well  as  opportunities  to  rise  in  the  social,  economic,  and  party  structures.

text: As a consequence of such opportunities, class distinctions reappeared in the Soviet Union, the privileged leaders of the secret police and the Red Army, as well as the leaders of the party and certain favored writers, musicians, ballet dancers, and actors, obtaining
text_raw:
As  a
consequence  of  such  opportunities,  class  distinctions  reappeared  in  the  Soviet  Union,  the
privileged  leaders  of  the  secret  police  and  the  Red  Army,  as  well  as  the  leaders  of  the
party  and  certain  favored  writers,  musicians,  ballet  dancers,  and  actors,  obtaining

text: incomes so far above those of the ordinary Russian that they lived in quite a different world.
text_raw:
incomes  so  far  above  those  of  the  ordinary  Russian  that  they  lived  in  quite  a  different
world.

text: The ordinary Russian had inadequate food and housing, was subject to extended rationing, having to stand in line for scarce consumers' items or even to go without them for long periods, and was reduced to living, with his family, in a single room, or even, in many cases, to a corner of a single room shared with other families.
text_raw:
The  ordinary  Russian  had  inadequate  food  and  housing,  was  subject  to  extended
rationing,  having  to  stand  in  line  for  scarce  consumers'  items  or  even  to  go  without  them
for  long  periods,  and  was  reduced  to  living,  with  his  family,  in  a  single  room,  or  even,  in
many  cases,  to  a  corner  of  a  single  room  shared  with  other  families.

text: The privileged rulers and their favorites had the best of everything, including foods and wines, the use of vacation villas in the country or in the Crimea, the use of official cars in the city, the right to live in old czarist palaces and mansions, and the right to obtain tickets to the best seats at the musical or dramatic performances.
text_raw:
The  privileged  rulers
and  their  favorites  had  the  best  of  everything,  including  foods  and  wines,  the  use  of
vacation  villas  in  the  country  or  in  the  Crimea,  the  use  of  official  cars  in  the  city,  the  right
to  live  in  old  czarist  palaces  and  mansions,  and  the  right  to  obtain  tickets  to  the  best  seats
at  the  musical  or  dramatic  performances.

text: These privileges of the ruling group, however, were obtained at a terrible price: at the cost of complete insecurity, for even the highest party officials were under constant surveillance by the secret police and inevitably would be purged, sooner or later, to exile or to death.
text_raw:
These  privileges  of  the  ruling  group,  however,
were  obtained  at  a  terrible  price:  at  the  cost  of  complete  insecurity,  for  even  the  highest
party  officials  were  under  constant  surveillance  by  the  secret  police  and  inevitably  would
be  purged,  sooner  or  later,  to  exile  or  to  death.

text: The growth of inequality was increasingly rapid under the Five- Year plans and was embodied in law.
text_raw:
The  growth  of  inequality  was  increasingly  rapid  under  the  Five- Year  plans  and  was
embodied  in  law.

text: All restrictions on maximum salaries were removed; variations in salaries grew steadily wider and were made greater by the non-monetary privileges extended to the favored upper ranks.
text_raw:
All  restrictions  on  maximum  salaries  were  removed;  variations  in
salaries  grew  steadily  wider  and  were  made  greater  by  the  non-monetary  privileges
extended  to  the  favored  upper  ranks.

text: Special stores were established where the privileged could obtain scarce goods at low prices; two or even three restaurants, with entirely different menus, were set up in industrial plants for different levels of employees; housing discrimination became steadily wider; all wages were put on a piecework basis even when this was quite impractical; work quotas and work minimums were steadily raised.
text_raw:
Special  stores  were  established  where  the  privileged
could  obtain  scarce  goods  at  low  prices;  two  or  even  three  restaurants,  with  entirely
different  menus,  were  set  up  in  industrial  plants  for  different  levels  of  employees;
housing  discrimination  became  steadily  wider;  all  wages  were  put  on  a  piecework  basis
even  when  this  was  quite  impractical;  work  quotas  and  work  minimums  were  steadily
raised.

text: Much of this differentiation of wages was justified under a fraudulent propaganda system known as Stakhanovism.
text_raw:
Much  of  this  differentiation  of  wages  was  justified  under  a  fraudulent  propaganda
system  known  as  Stakhanovism.

text: In September 1935, a miner named Stakhanov mined 102 tons of coal in a day, fourteen times the usual output.
text_raw:
In  September  1935,  a  miner  named  Stakhanov  mined  102  tons  of  coal  in  a  day,
fourteen  times  the  usual  output.

text: Similar exploits were arranged in other activities for propaganda purposes and used to justify speedup, raising of production quotas, and wage differences.
text_raw:
Similar  exploits  were  arranged  in  other  activities  for
propaganda  purposes  and  used  to  justify  speedup,  raising  of  production  quotas,  and  wage
differences.

text: At the same time, the standard of living of the ordinary worker was steadily reduced not only by raising quotas but also by a systematic policy of segmented inflation.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  the  standard  of  living  of  the  ordinary  worker  was  steadily
reduced  not  only  by  raising  quotas  but  also  by  a  systematic  policy  of  segmented  inflation.

text: Food was purchased from the collective farms at lo\v prices and then sold to the public at high prices.
text_raw:
Food  was  purchased  from  the  collective  farms  at  lo\v  prices  and  then  sold  to  the  public  at
high  prices.

text: The gap between these two was steadily widened year by year.
text_raw: The  gap  between  these  two  was  steadily  widened  year  by  year.

text: At the same time the amount of produce taken from the peasants was gradually increased by one technique or another.
text_raw:
At  the  same
time  the  amount  of  produce  taken  from  the  peasants  was  gradually  increased  by  one
technique  or  another.

text: When collective farms had to shift to tractors and combines these were taken from the farms themselves and centralized in machine-tractor stations controlled by the government.
text_raw:
When  collective  farms  had  to  shift  to  tractors  and  combines  these
were  taken  from  the  farms  themselves  and  centralized  in  machine-tractor  stations
controlled  by  the  government.

text: They had to be hired at rates which approached one-fifth of the total output of the collective farm.
text_raw:
They  had  to  be  hired  at  rates  which  approached  one-fifth
of  the  total  output  of  the  collective  farm.

text: One of the chief sources of governmental income was a turnover tax (sales tax) on consumers' goods; this varied from item to item, but was generally about 60 percent or more.
text_raw:
One  of  the  chief  sources  of  governmental
income  was  a  turnover  tax  (sales  tax)  on  consumers'  goods;  this  varied  from  item  to  item,
but  was  generally  about  60  percent  or  more.

text: It was not imposed on producers' goods, which were, on the contrary, subsidized to the extent of half the government's expenditures.
text_raw:
It  was  not  imposed  on  producers'  goods,
which  were,  on  the  contrary,  subsidized  to  the  extent  of  half  the  government's
expenditures.

text: Price segmentation was so great that in the period 1927-1948 consumers' prices went up thirty-fold, wages went up eleven-fold, while prices of producers' goods and armaments went up less than threefold.
text_raw:
Price  segmentation  was  so  great  that  in  the  period  1927-1948  consumers'
prices  went  up  thirty-fold,  wages  went  up  eleven-fold,  while  prices  of  producers'  goods
and  armaments  went  up  less  than  threefold.

text: This served to reduce consumption and to falsify the statistical picture of the national income, standards of living, and the breakdown between consumers' goods, capital goods, and armaments.
text_raw:
This  served  to  reduce  consumption  and  to
falsify  the  statistical  picture  of  the  national  income,  standards  of  living,  and  the
breakdown  between  consumers'  goods,  capital  goods,  and  armaments.

text: As public discontent and social tensions grew in the period of the Five- Year plans and the collectivization of agriculture, the use of spying, purges, torture, and murder increased out of all proportion.
text_raw:
As  public  discontent  and  social  tensions  grew  in  the  period  of  the  Five- Year  plans  and
the  collectivization  of  agriculture,  the  use  of  spying,  purges,  torture,  and  murder
increased  out  of  all  proportion.

text: Every wave of discontent, every discovery of inefficiency, every recognition of some past mistake of the authorities resulted in new waves of police activity.
text_raw:
Every  wave  of  discontent,  every  discovery  of
inefficiency,  every  recognition  of  some  past  mistake  of  the  authorities  resulted  in  new
waves  of  police  activity.

text: When the meat supplies of the cities almost vanished, after the collectivization of agriculture in the early 1930's, more than a dozen of the high officials in charge of meat supplies in Moscow were arrested and shot, although they were in no way responsible for the shortage.
text_raw:
When  the  meat  supplies  of  the  cities  almost  vanished,  after  the
collectivization  of  agriculture  in  the  early  1930's,  more  than  a  dozen  of  the  high  officials
in  charge  of  meat  supplies  in  Moscow  were  arrested  and  shot,  although  they  were  in  no
way  responsible  for  the  shortage.

text: By the middle 1930's the search for "saboteurs" and for "enemies of the state" became an all-enveloping mania which left hardly a family untouched.
text_raw:
By  the  middle  1930's  the  search  for  "saboteurs"  and  for
"enemies  of  the  state"  became  an  all-enveloping  mania  which  left  hardly  a  family
untouched.

text: Hundreds of thousands were killed, frequently on completely false charges, while millions were arrested and exiled to Siberia or put into huge slave-labor camps.
text_raw:
Hundreds  of  thousands  were  killed,  frequently  on  completely  false  charges,
while  millions  were  arrested  and  exiled  to  Siberia  or  put  into  huge  slave-labor  camps.

text: In these camps, under conditions of semi- starvation and incredible cruelty, millions toiled in mines, in logging camps in the Arctic, or building new railroads, new canals, or new cities.
text_raw:
In
these  camps,  under  conditions  of  semi- starvation  and  incredible  cruelty,  millions  toiled  in
mines,  in  logging  camps  in  the  Arctic,  or  building  new  railroads,  new  canals,  or  new
cities.

text: Estimates of the number of persons in such slave-labor camps in the period just before Hitler's attack in 1941 vary from as low as two million to as high as twenty million.
text_raw:
Estimates  of  the  number  of  persons  in  such  slave-labor  camps  in  the  period  just
before  Hitler's  attack  in  1941  vary  from  as  low  as  two  million  to  as  high  as  twenty
million.

text: The majority of these prisoners had done nothing against the Soviet state or the Communist system, but consisted of the relatives, associates, and friends of persons who had been arrested on more serious charges.
text_raw:
The  majority  of  these  prisoners  had  done  nothing  against  the  Soviet  state  or  the
Communist  system,  but  consisted  of  the  relatives,  associates,  and  friends  of  persons  who
had  been  arrested  on  more  serious  charges.

text: Many of these charges were completely false, having been trumped up to provide labor in remote areas, scapegoats for administrative breakdowns, and to eliminate possible rivals in the control of the Soviet system, or simply because of the constantly growing mass paranoidal suspicion which enveloped the upper levels of the regime.
text_raw:
Many  of  these  charges  were  completely  false,
having  been  trumped  up  to  provide  labor  in  remote  areas,  scapegoats  for  administrative
breakdowns,  and  to  eliminate  possible  rivals  in  the  control  of  the  Soviet  system,  or
simply  because  of  the  constantly  growing  mass  paranoidal  suspicion  which  enveloped  the
upper  levels  of  the  regime.

text: In many cases, incidental events led to large-scale reprisals for personal grudges far beyond any scope justified by the event itself.
text_raw:
In  many  cases,  incidental  events  led  to  large-scale  reprisals  for
personal  grudges  far  beyond  any  scope  justified  by  the  event  itself.

text: In most cases these "liquidations" took place in the cells of the secret police, in the middle of the night, with no public announcements except the most laconic.
text_raw:
In  most  cases  these
"liquidations"  took  place  in  the  cells  of  the  secret  police,  in  the  middle  of  the  night,  with
no  public  announcements  except  the  most  laconic.

text: But, in a few cases, spectacular public trials were staged in which the accused, usually famous Soviet leaders, were berated and reviled, volubly confessed their own dastardly activities, and, after conviction' were taken out and shot.
text_raw:
But,  in  a  few  cases,  spectacular  public
trials  were  staged  in  which  the  accused,  usually  famous  Soviet  leaders,  were  berated  and
reviled,  volubly  confessed  their  own  dastardly  activities,  and,  after  conviction'  were  taken
out  and  shot.

text: These purges and trials kept the Soviet Union in an uproar and kept the rest of the world in a state of continuous amazement throughout the period of the Five- Year plans.
text_raw:
These  purges  and  trials  kept  the  Soviet  Union  in  an  uproar  and  kept  the  rest  of  the
world  in  a  state  of  continuous  amazement  throughout  the  period  of  the  Five- Year  plans.

text: In 1929 a large group of party leaders who objected to the ruthless exploitation of the peasantry (the so-called "Rightist opposition"), led by the party's most expert theoretician of the Marxist ideology, Nikolai Bukharin, was purged.
text_raw:
In  1929  a  large  group  of  party  leaders  who  objected  to  the  ruthless  exploitation  of  the
peasantry  (the  so-called  "Rightist  opposition"),  led  by  the  party's  most  expert  theoretician
of  the  Marxist  ideology,  Nikolai  Bukharin,  was  purged.

text: In 1933 about a third of the members of the party (at least a million names) were expelled from the party.
text_raw:
In  1933  about  a  third  of  the
members  of  the  party  (at  least  a  million  names)  were  expelled  from  the  party.

text: In 1935, following upon the murder of a Stalinist supporter, Serge Kirov, by the secret police, many of the "Old Bolsheviks," including Zinoviev and Kamenev, were tried for treason.
text_raw:
In  1935,
following  upon  the  murder  of  a  Stalinist  supporter,  Serge  Kirov,  by  the  secret  police,
many  of  the  "Old  Bolsheviks,"  including  Zinoviev  and  Kamenev,  were  tried  for  treason.

neurological  systems  were  a  consequence  of  the  coziness  of  German  childhood,  which,
contrary  to  popular  impression,  was  not  a  condition  of  misery  and  personal  cruelty  (as  it
often  is  in  England),  but  a  warm,  affectionate,  and  externally  disciplined  situation  of
secure  relationships.

text: After all, Santa Claus and the child-centered Christmas is Germanic.
text_raw: After  all,  Santa  Claus  and  the  child-centered  Christmas  is  Germanic.

text: This is the situation the adult German, face to face with what seems an alien world, is constantly seeking to recapture.
text_raw:
This  is  the  situation  the  adult  German,  face  to  face  with  what  seems  an  alien  world,  is
constantly  seeking  to  recapture.

text: To the German it is Gemiitlichkeit; but to outsiders it may be suffocating.
text_raw:
To  the  German  it  is  Gemiitlichkeit;  but  to  outsiders  it
may  be  suffocating.

text: In any case it gives rise among adult Germans to two additional traits of German character: the need for external discipline and the quality of egocentricity.
text_raw:
In  any  case  it  gives  rise  among  adult  Germans  to  two  additional  traits
of  German  character:  the  need  for  external  discipline  and  the  quality  of  egocentricity.

text: The Englishman is disciplined from within so that he takes his self-discipline, embedded in his neurological system, with him wherever he goes, even to situations where all the external forms of discipline are lacking.
text_raw:
The  Englishman  is  disciplined  from  within  so  that  he  takes  his  self-discipline,
embedded  in  his  neurological  system,  with  him  wherever  he  goes,  even  to  situations
where  all  the  external  forms  of  discipline  are  lacking.

text: As a consequence the Englishman
text_raw: As  a  consequence  the  Englishman

text: is the most completely socialized of Europeans, as the Frenchman is the most completely civilized, the Italian most completely gregarious, or the Spaniard most completely individualistic.

is  the  most  completely  socialized  of  Europeans,  as  the  Frenchman  is  the  most  completely
civilized,  the  Italian  most  completely  gregarious,  or  the  Spaniard  most  completely

text: But the German by seeking external discipline shows his unconscious desire to recapture the externally disciplined world of his childhood.

But  the  German  by  seeking  external  discipline  shows  his  unconscious

text: With such discipline he may be the best behaved of citizens, but without it he may be a beast.

With  such  discipline
he  may  be  the  best  behaved  of  citizens,  but  without  it  he  may  be  a  beast.

text: A second notable carryover from childhood to adult German life was egocentricity.
text_raw: A  second  notable  carryover  from  childhood  to  adult  German  life  was  egocentricity.

text: The whole world seems to any child to revolve around it, and most societies have provided ways in which the adolescent is disabused of this error.
text_raw:
The  whole  world  seems  to  any  child  to  revolve  around  it,  and  most  societies  have
provided  ways  in  which  the  adolescent  is  disabused  of  this  error.

text: The German leaves childhood so abruptly that he rarely learns this fact of the universe, and spends the rest of his life creating a network of established relationships centering on himself.
text_raw:
The  German  leaves
childhood  so  abruptly  that  he  rarely  learns  this  fact  of  the  universe,  and  spends  the  rest  of
his  life  creating  a  network  of  established  relationships  centering  on  himself.

text: Since this is his aim in life, he sees no need to make any effort to see anything from any point of view other than his own.
text_raw:
Since  this  is
his  aim  in  life,  he  sees  no  need  to  make  any  effort  to  see  anything  from  any  point  of  view
other  than  his  own.

text: The consequence is a most damaging inability to do this.
text_raw: The  consequence  is  a  most  damaging  inability  to  do  this.

text: Each class or group is totally unsympathetic to any point of view except the egocentric one of the viewer himself.
text_raw:
Each  class
or  group  is  totally  unsympathetic  to  any  point  of  view  except  the  egocentric  one  of  the
viewer  himself.

text: His union, his company, his composer, his poet, his party, his neighborhood are the best, almost the only acceptable, examples of the class, and all others must be denigrated.

neighborhood  are  the  best,  almost  the  only  acceptable,  examples  of  the  class,  and  all

text: As part of this process a German usually chooses for himself his favorite flower, musical composition, beer, club, painting, or opera, and sees little value or merit in any other.

his  favorite  flower,  musical  composition,  beer,  club,  painting,  or  opera,  and  sees  little

text: Yet at the same time he insists that his myopic or narrow- angled vision of the universe must be universalized, because no people are more insistent on the role of the absolute or the universal as the framework of their own egocentricity.

text: One deplorable consequence of this has been the social animosities rampant in a Germany which has loudly proclaimed its rigid solidarity.

One  deplorable  consequence  of  this  has  been  the  social  animosities  rampant  in  a

text: With an individual personality structure such as this, the German was painfully uncomfortable in the totally different, and to him totally unfriendly, world of nineteenth- century individualism, liberalism, competitive atomism, democratic equality, and self- reliant dynamicism.

The  late  arrival  of  these  achievements,  especially  national
unity  and  industrialism,  in  Germany  left  the  average  German  with  a  feeling  of  inferiority

Few  Germans  were  willing  to  compete  as  individuals  with  British

As  a  consequence  Germany  never  had  a  clearly  competitive,  liberal

text: The failure to achieve democracy was reflected in public law.
text_raw: The  failure  to  achieve  democracy  was  reflected  in  public  law.

text: The German Parliament was more of an advisory than a legislative body; the judiciary was not under popular control; and the executive (the chancellor and the Cabinet) were responsible to the emperor rather than to Parliament.
text_raw:
The  German  Parliament
was  more  of  an  advisory  than  a  legislative  body;  the  judiciary  was  not  under  popular
control;  and  the  executive  (the  chancellor  and  the  Cabinet)  were  responsible  to  the

text: Moreover, the constitution, because of a peculiar suffrage system, was weighted to give undue importance to Prussia (which was the stronghold of the army, the landlords, the bureaucracy, and the industrialists).

Moreover,  the  constitution,  because  of  a  peculiar
suffrage  system,  was  weighted  to  give  undue  importance  to  Prussia  (which  was  the
stronghold  of  the  army,  the  landlords,  the  bureaucracy,  and  the  industrialists).

text: Within Prussia the elections were weighted to give undue influence to these same groups.
text_raw:
Within
Prussia  the  elections  were  weighted  to  give  undue  influence  to  these  same  groups.

text: Above all, the army was subject to no democratic or even governmental control, but was dominated by the Prussian Officers' Corps whose members were recruited by regimental
text_raw:
Above
all,  the  army  was  subject  to  no  democratic  or  even  governmental  control,  but  was
dominated  by  the  Prussian  Officers'  Corps  whose  members  were  recruited  by  regimental

This  Officers'  Corps  thus  came  to  resemble  a  fraternity  rather  than  an

text: By 1890, when he retired from office, Bismarck had built up an unstable balance of forces within Germany similar to the unstable balance of powers which he had established in Europe as a whole.
text_raw:
By  1890,  when  he  retired  from  office,  Bismarck  had  built  up  an  unstable  balance  of
forces  within  Germany  similar  to  the  unstable  balance  of  powers  which  he  had
established  in  Europe  as  a  whole.

text: His cynical and materialistic view of human motivations had driven all idealistic and humanitarian forces from the German political scene and had remodeled the political parties almost completely into economic and social pressure groups which he played off, one against another.
text_raw:
His  cynical  and  materialistic  view  of  human
motivations  had  driven  all  idealistic  and  humanitarian  forces  from  the  German  political
scene  and  had  remodeled  the  political  parties  almost  completely  into  economic  and  social
pressure  groups  which  he  played  off,  one  against  another.

text: The chief of these forces were the landlords (Conservative Party), the industrialists (National Liberal Party), the Catholics (Center Party), and the workers (Social Democratic Party).
text_raw:
The  chief  of  these  forces  were
the  landlords  (Conservative  Party),  the  industrialists  (National  Liberal  Party),  the
Catholics  (Center  Party),  and  the  workers  (Social  Democratic  Party).

text: In addition, the army and the bureaucracy were expected to be politically neutral, but they did not hesitate to exert pressures on the government without the intermediary of any political party.
text_raw:
In  addition,  the
army  and  the  bureaucracy  were  expected  to  be  politically  neutral,  but  they  did  not
hesitate  to  exert  pressures  on  the  government  without  the  intermediary  of  any  political
party.

text: Thus there existed a precarious and dangerous balance of forces which only a genius could manipulate.
text_raw:
Thus  there  existed  a  precarious  and  dangerous  balance  of  forces  which  only  a
genius  could  manipulate.

text: Bismarck was followed by no genius.
text_raw: Bismarck  was  followed  by  no  genius.

text: The Kaiser, William II (1888-1918), was an incapable neurotic, and the system of recruitment to government service was such as to exclude any but mediocrities.
text_raw:
The  Kaiser,  William  II
(1888-1918),  was  an  incapable  neurotic,  and  the  system  of  recruitment  to  government
service  was  such  as  to  exclude  any  but  mediocrities.

text: As a result, the precarious structure left by Bismarck was not managed but was merely hidden from public view by a facade of nationalistic, anti-foreign, anti-Semitic, imperialistic, and chauvinistic propaganda of which the emperor was the center.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  the  precarious  structure
left  by  Bismarck  was  not  managed  but  was  merely  hidden  from  public  view  by  a  facade

which  the  emperor  was  the  center.

text: The dichotomy in Germany between appearance and reality, between propaganda and structure, between economic prosperity and political and social weakness was put to the test in World War I, and failed completely.
text_raw:
The  dichotomy  in  Germany  between  appearance  and  reality,  between  propaganda  and
structure,  between  economic  prosperity  and  political  and  social  weakness  was  put  to  the
test  in  World  War  I,  and  failed  completely.

text: The events of 191 4- 1919 revealed that Germany was not a democracy in which all men were legally equal.
text_raw:
The  events  of  191 4- 1919  revealed  that
Germany  was  not  a  democracy  in  which  all  men  were  legally  equal.

text: Instead, the ruling groups formed some strange animal fording it over a host of lesser animals.
text_raw:
Instead,  the  ruling
groups  formed  some  strange  animal  fording  it  over  a  host  of  lesser  animals.

text: In this strange creature the monarchy represented the body, which was supported by four legs: the army, the landlords, the bureaucracy, and the industrialists.
text_raw:
In  this
strange  creature  the  monarchy  represented  the  body,  which  was  supported  by  four  legs:
the  army,  the  landlords,  the  bureaucracy,  and  the  industrialists.

text: This glimpse of reality was not welcome to any important group in Germany, with the result that it was covered over, almost at once, by another misleading facade: the "revolution" of 1918 was not really a revolution at all, because it did not radically change this situation; it removed the monarchy, but it left the quartet of legs.
text_raw:
This  glimpse  of  reality  was  not  welcome  to  any  important  group  in  Germany,  with  the
result  that  it  was  covered  over,  almost  at  once,  by  another  misleading  facade:  the
"revolution"  of  1918  was  not  really  a  revolution  at  all,  because  it  did  not  radically  change
this  situation;  it  removed  the  monarchy,  but  it  left  the  quartet  of  legs.

text: This Quartet was not the creation of a moment, rather it was the result of a long process of development whose last stages were reached only in the twentieth century.
text_raw:
This  Quartet  was  not  the  creation  of  a  moment,  rather  it  was  the  result  of  a  long
process  of  development  whose  last  stages  were  reached  only  in  the  twentieth  century.

text: In these last stages the industrialists were adopted into the ruling clique by conscious acts of agreement.
text_raw:
In
these  last  stages  the  industrialists  were  adopted  into  the  ruling  clique  by  conscious  acts  of

text: These acts culminated in the years 1898-1905 in a deal by which the Junkers accepted the industrialists' navy-building program (which they detested) in return for the industrialists' acceptance of the Junkers' high tariff on grains.

accepted  the  industrialists'  navy-building  program  (which  they  detested)  in  return  for  the
industrialists'  acceptance  of  the  Junkers'  high  tariff  on  grains.

text: The Junkers were anti-navy because they, with their few numbers and close alliance with the army, were opposed to any venture into the fields of colonialism or overseas imperialism, and were determined not to jeopardize Germany's continental position by alienating England.
text_raw:
The  Junkers  were  anti-navy
because  they,  with  their  few  numbers  and  close  alliance  with  the  army,  were  opposed  to

not  to  jeopardize  Germany's  continental  position  by  alienating  England.

text: In fact, the policy of the Junkers was not only a continental one; on the Continent it was klein- deutsch.

In  fact,  the
policy  of  the  Junkers  was  not  only  a  continental  one;  on  the  Continent  it  was  klein-

text: The reasons for this situation are important.
text_raw: The  reasons  for  this  situation  are  important.

text: The Quartet, with the monarchy, made the war of 1914-1918, and were incapable of winning it.
text_raw:

Democrats  and  the  Center  (Catholic)  Party.

The  former  was  doctrinaire  in  its  attitude,
being  anticapitalist,  pledged  to  the  international  brotherhood  of  labor,  pacifist,

text_raw: These  two  opposition  parties  underwent  considerable  change  during  the  war.

text: This extremist group, under Karl Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg, became known as the Spartacist Union and (after 1919) as the Communists.

The  rest  of  the
Social  Democrats  supported  the  war  and  the  old  monarchial  system  until  November  1918

text: The Center Party was aggressive and nationalist until 1917 when it became pacifist.
text_raw: The  Center  Party  was  aggressive  and  nationalist  until  1917  when  it  became  pacifist.

Under  Matthias  Erzberger  it  allied  with  the  Social  Democrats  to  push  through  the

text: The position of these various groups on the issue of aggressive nationalism was sharply revealed in the voting to ratify the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk imposed by the militarists, Junkers, and industrialists on a prostrate Russia.

The  position  of  these  various  groups  on  the
issue  of  aggressive  nationalism  was  sharply  revealed  in  the  voting  to  ratify  the  Treaty  of
Brest-Litovsk  imposed  by  the  militarists,  Junkers,  and  industrialists  on  a  prostrate  Russia.

text: The Center Party voted to ratify; the Social Democrats abstained from voting; the Independents voted No.
text_raw:
The  Center  Party  voted  to  ratify;  the  Social  Democrats  abstained  from  voting;  the
Independents  voted  No.

text: The "revolution" of November 1918 would have been a real revolution except for the opposition of the Social Democrats and the Center Party, for the Quartet in the crucial days of November and December 1918 were discouraged, discredited, and helpless.
text_raw:
The  "revolution"  of  November  1918  would  have  been  a  real  revolution  except  for  the

text: These two small groups were the "indiscriminate nationalists" and the "mercenaries." The indiscriminate nationalists were those men, like Hitler, who were not able to distinguish between the German nation and the old monarchial system.

These  two  small  groups  were  the
"indiscriminate  nationalists"  and  the  "mercenaries."  The  indiscriminate  nationalists  were

These  persons,  because  of  their  loyalty  to  the  nation,  were

text: They not only left the Quartet in their positions of responsibility and power â€” the landlords on their estates, the officers in their commands, the industrialists in control of their factories, and the bureaucracy in control of the police, the courts, and the administration â€” but they increased the influence of these groups because the actions of the Quartet were not restrained under the republic by that sense of honor or loyalty to the system which had restrained the use of their power under the monarchy.

text: As early as November 10,1918, Friedrich Ebert, chief figure of the Social Democratic Party, made an agreement with the Officers' Corps in which he promised not to use the power of the new government to democratize the army if the officers would support the new government against the threat of the Independents and the Spartacists to establish a soviet system.

soviet  system.

text: This drift, as we shall see, was delayed by only two influences: the need for foreign loans and political concessions from the Western Powers and the recognition that both of these could be obtained better by a government which seemed to be republican and democratic in inclination than by a government which was obviously hand in glove with the Quartet.

delayed  by  only  two  influences:  the  need  for  foreign  loans  and  political  concessions  from

government  which  seemed  to  be  republican  and  democratic  in  inclination  than  by  a
government  which  was  obviously  hand  in  glove  with  the  Quartet.

text: At the end of the war in 1918 the Socialists were in control, not because the Germans were Socialistic (for the party was not really Socialist) but because this was the only party which had been traditionally in opposition to the imperial system.
text_raw:
At  the  end  of  the  war  in  1918  the  Socialists  were  in  control,  not  because  the  Germans
were  Socialistic  (for  the  party  was  not  really  Socialist)  but  because  this  was  the  only
party  which  had  been  traditionally  in  opposition  to  the  imperial  system.

text: A committee of six men was set up: three from the Social Democrats (Ebert, Philip Scheidemann, and Otto Landsberg) and three from the Independent Socialists (Hugo Haase, Wilhelm Dittman, and Emil Barth).

six  men  was  set  up:  three  from  the  Social  Democrats  (Ebert,  Philip  Scheidemann,  and

and  had  the  regular  secretaries  of  state  as  their  subordinates.

text: These men did nothing to consolidate the republic or democracy and were opposed to any effort to take any steps toward Socialism.

consolidate  the  republic  or  democracy  and  were  opposed  to  any  effort  to  take  any  steps
toward  Socialism.

was  generally  expected.

text: Instead they wasted the opportunity by busying themselves with typical trade-union problems such as the eight- hour day (November 12, 1918) and collective bargaining methods (December 23, 1918).

typical  trade-union  problems  such  as  the  eight- hour  day  (November  12,  1918)  and
collective  bargaining  methods  (December  23,  1918).

text: The critical problem was the form of government, with the choice resting between workers' and peasants' councils (soviets), already widely established, and a national assembly to set up an ordinary parliamentary system.
text_raw:
The  critical  problem  was  the  form  of  government,  with  the  choice  resting  between
workers'  and  peasants'  councils  (soviets),  already  widely  established,  and  a  national
assembly  to  set  up  an  ordinary  parliamentary  system.

text: The Socialist group preferred the latter, and were willing to use the regular army to enforce this choice.
text_raw:
The  Socialist  group  preferred  the
latter,  and  were  willing  to  use  the  regular  army  to  enforce  this  choice.

text: On this basis a counterrevolutionary agreement was made between Ebert and the General Staff.
text_raw:
On  this  basis  a
counterrevolutionary  agreement  was  made  between  Ebert  and  the  General  Staff.

text: As a consequence of this agreement, the army attacked a Spartacist parade in Berlin on December 6, 1918, and liquidated the rebellious People's Naval Division on December 24, 1918.
text_raw:
As  a
consequence  of  this  agreement,  the  army  attacked  a  Spartacist  parade  in  Berlin  on
December  6,  1918,  and  liquidated  the  rebellious  People's  Naval  Division  on  December
24,  1918.

text: In protest at this violence the three Independent members of the government resigned.
text_raw:
In  protest  at  this  violence  the  three  Independent  members  of  the  government
resigned.

text: Their example was followed by other Independents throughout Germany, with the exception of Kurt Eisner in Munich.
text_raw:
Their  example  was  followed  by  other  Independents  throughout  Germany,  with
the  exception  of  Kurt  Eisner  in  Munich.

text: The next day the Spartacists formed the German Communist Party with a non-revolutionary program.
text_raw:
The  next  day  the  Spartacists  formed  the  German
Communist  Party  with  a  non-revolutionary  program.

text: Their declaration read, in part:
text_raw: Their  declaration  read,  in  part:

text: "The
text_raw: "The

text: Spartacist Union will never assume governmental power except in response to the plain and unmistakable wish of the great majority of the proletarian masses in Germany; and only as a result of a definite agreement of these masses with the aims and methods of the Spartacist Union."
text_raw:
Spartacist  Union  will  never  assume  governmental  power  except  in  response  to  the  plain
and  unmistakable  wish  of  the  great  majority  of  the  proletarian  masses  in  Germany;  and
only  as  a  result  of  a  definite  agreement  of  these  masses  with  the  aims  and  methods  of  the
Spartacist  Union."

text: This pious expression, however, was the program of the leaders; the masses of the new party, and possibly the members of the Independent Socialist group as well, were enraged at the conservatism of the Social Democrats and began to get out of hand.
text_raw:
This  pious  expression,  however,  was  the  program  of  the  leaders;  the  masses  of  the
new  party,  and  possibly  the  members  of  the  Independent  Socialist  group  as  well,  were
enraged  at  the  conservatism  of  the  Social  Democrats  and  began  to  get  out  of  hand.

text: The issue was joined on the question of councils versus National Assembly.
text_raw:
The
issue  was  joined  on  the  question  of  councils  versus  National  Assembly.

text: The government, under Noske's direction, used regular troops in a bloody suppression of the Left (January 5-15), ending up with the murder of Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht, the Communist leaders.
text_raw:
The  government,
under  Noske's  direction,  used  regular  troops  in  a  bloody  suppression  of  the  Left  (January
5-15),  ending  up  with  the  murder  of  Rosa  Luxemburg  and  Karl  Liebknecht,  the
Communist  leaders.

text: The result was exactly as the Quartet wanted: the Communists and many non-Communist workers were permanently alienated from the Socialists and from the parliamentary republic.
text_raw:
The  result  was  exactly  as  the  Quartet  wanted:  the  Communists  and
many  non-Communist  workers  were  permanently  alienated  from  the  Socialists  and  from
the  parliamentary  republic.

text: The Communist Party, deprived of leaders of its own, became a tool of Russian Communism.
text_raw:
The  Communist  Party,  deprived  of  leaders  of  its  own,  became
a  tool  of  Russian  Communism.

text: As a result of this repression, the army was able to disarm the workers at the very moment when it was beginning to arm reactionary private bands (Free Corps) of the Right.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  this  repression,  the  army  was  able  to  disarm
the  workers  at  the  very  moment  when  it  was  beginning  to  arm  reactionary  private  bands
(Free  Corps)  of  the  Right.

text: Both of these developments were encouraged by Ebert and Noske.
text_raw:
Both  of  these  developments  were  encouraged  by  Ebert  and
Noske.

text: Only in Bavaria was the alienation of Communist and Socialist and the disarmament of the former not carried out;
text_raw:
Only  in  Bavaria  was  the  alienation  of  Communist  and  Socialist  and  the  disarmament
of  the  former  not  carried  out;

text: Kurt Eisner, the Independent Socialist minister-president in Munich, prevented it.
text_raw:
Kurt  Eisner,  the  Independent  Socialist  minister-president  in
Munich,  prevented  it.

text: Accordingly, Eisner was murdered by Count Anton von Arco- Valley on February Zl, 1919.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  Eisner  was  murdered  by  Count  Anton  von  Arco-
Valley  on  February  Zl,  1919.

text: When the workers of Munich revolted, they were crushed by a combination of regular army and Free Corps amid scenes of horrible violence from both sides.
text_raw:
When  the  workers  of  Munich  revolted,  they  were  crushed
by  a  combination  of  regular  army  and  Free  Corps  amid  scenes  of  horrible  violence  from
both  sides.

text: Eisner was replaced as premier by a Social Democrat, Adolph Hoffman.
text_raw: Eisner  was  replaced  as  premier  by  a  Social  Democrat,  Adolph  Hoffman.

text: Hoffman, on the night of March 13, 1920, was thrown out by a military coup which replaced him by a government of the Right under Gustav von Kahr.
text_raw:
Hoffman,  on  the  night  of  March  13,  1920,  was  thrown  out  by  a  military  coup  which
replaced  him  by  a  government  of  the  Right  under  Gustav  von  Kahr.

text: In the meantime, the National Assembly elected on June 19, 1919, drew up a parliamentary constitution under the guidance of Professor Hugo Preuss.
text_raw:
In  the  meantime,  the  National  Assembly  elected  on  June  19,  1919,  drew  up  a
parliamentary  constitution  under  the  guidance  of  Professor  Hugo  Preuss.

text: This constitution provided for a president elected for seven years to be head of the state, a bicameral legislature, and a Cabinet responsible to the lower house of the legislature.
text_raw:
This
constitution  provided  for  a  president  elected  for  seven  years  to  be  head  of  the  state,  a
bicameral  legislature,  and  a  Cabinet  responsible  to  the  lower  house  of  the  legislature.

text: The upper house, or Reichsrat, consisted of representatives of eighteen German states and had, in legislative matters, a suspensive veto which could be overcome by a two-thirds vote of the lower chamber.
text_raw:
The
upper  house,  or  Reichsrat,  consisted  of  representatives  of  eighteen  German  states  and
had,  in  legislative  matters,  a  suspensive  veto  which  could  be  overcome  by  a  two-thirds
vote  of  the  lower  chamber.

text: This lower chamber, or Reichstag, had 608 members, elected by a system of proportional representation on a party basis.
text_raw:
This  lower  chamber,  or  Reichstag,  had  608  members,  elected
by  a  system  of  proportional  representation  on  a  party  basis.

text: The head of the government, to whom the president gave a mandate to form a Cabinet, was called the chancellor.
text_raw:
The  head  of  the  government,
to  whom  the  president  gave  a  mandate  to  form  a  Cabinet,  was  called  the  chancellor.

text: The chief weaknesses of the constitution were the provisions for proportional representation and other provisions, by articles 25 and 48, which allowed the president to suspend constitutional guarantees and rule by decree, in periods of "national emergency." As early as 1925 the parties of the Right were planning to destroy the republic by the use of these powers.
text_raw:
The
chief  weaknesses  of  the  constitution  were  the  provisions  for  proportional  representation
and  other  provisions,  by  articles  25  and  48,  which  allowed  the  president  to  suspend
constitutional  guarantees  and  rule  by  decree,  in  periods  of  "national  emergency."  As  early
as  1925  the  parties  of  the  Right  were  planning  to  destroy  the  republic  by  the  use  of  these
powers.

text: A direct challenge to the republic from the Right came in March 1920, when Captain Ehrhardt's Brigade of the Free Corps marched into Berlin, forced the government to flee to Dresden, and set up a government under Wolfgang Kapp, an ultra-nationalist.
text_raw:
A  direct  challenge  to  the  republic  from  the  Right  came  in  March  1920,  when  Captain
Ehrhardt's  Brigade  of  the  Free  Corps  marched  into  Berlin,  forced  the  government  to  flee
to  Dresden,  and  set  up  a  government  under  Wolfgang  Kapp,  an  ultra-nationalist.

text: Kapp
text_raw: Kapp

text: was supported by the army commander in the Berlin area, Baron Walther von Liittwitz, who became Reichswehr minister in Kapp's government.
text_raw:
was  supported  by  the  army  commander  in  the  Berlin  area,  Baron  Walther  von  Liittwitz,
who  became  Reichswehr  minister  in  Kapp's  government.

text: Since General Hans von Seeckt, chief of staff, refused to support the legal government, it was helpless, and was saved only by a general strike of the workers in Berlin and a great proletarian rising in the industrial regions of western Germany.
text_raw:
Since  General  Hans  von  Seeckt,
chief  of  staff,  refused  to  support  the  legal  government,  it  was  helpless,  and  was  saved
only  by  a  general  strike  of  the  workers  in  Berlin  and  a  great  proletarian  rising  in  the
industrial  regions  of  western  Germany.

text: The Kapp government was unable to function, and collapsed, while the army proceeded to violate the territorial disarmament clauses of the Treaty of Versailles by invading the Ruhr in order to crush the workers' uprising in that area.
text_raw:
The  Kapp  government  was  unable  to  function,
and  collapsed,  while  the  army  proceeded  to  violate  the  territorial  disarmament  clauses  of
the  Treaty  of  Versailles  by  invading  the  Ruhr  in  order  to  crush  the  workers'  uprising  in
that  area.

text: Seeckt was rewarded for his non-cooperation by being appointed commander in chief in May 1920.
text_raw:
Seeckt  was  rewarded  for  his  non-cooperation  by  being  appointed  commander  in
chief  in  May  1920.

text: As a consequence of these disturbances, the general election of July 1920 went against the "Weimar Coalition." A new government came in which was completely middle-class in its alignment, the Socialists of the Weimar Coalition being replaced by the party of big business, the German People's Party.
text_raw:
As  a  consequence  of  these  disturbances,  the  general  election  of  July  1920  went  against
the  "Weimar  Coalition."  A  new  government  came  in  which  was  completely  middle-class
in  its  alignment,  the  Socialists  of  the  Weimar  Coalition  being  replaced  by  the  party  of  big
business,  the  German  People's  Party.

text: Noske was replaced as Reichswehr minister by Otto Gessler, a willing tool of the Officers' Corps.
text_raw:
Noske  was  replaced  as  Reichswehr  minister  by  Otto
Gessler,  a  willing  tool  of  the  Officers'  Corps.

text: Gessler, who held this critical position from March 1920 to January 1928, made no effort to subject the army to democratic, or even civilian, control, but cooperated in every way with Seeckt's secret efforts to evade the disarmament provisions of the peace treaties.
text_raw:
Gessler,  who  held  this  critical  position  from
March  1920  to  January  1928,  made  no  effort  to  subject  the  army  to  democratic,  or  even
civilian,  control,  but  cooperated  in  every  way  with  Seeckt's  secret  efforts  to  evade  the
disarmament  provisions  of  the  peace  treaties.

text: German armaments factories were moved to Turkey, Russia, Sweden, the Netherlands, and Switzerland.
text_raw:
German  armaments  factories  were  moved
to  Turkey,  Russia,  Sweden,  the  Netherlands,  and  Switzerland.

text: German officers were drilled in prohibited weapons in Russia and China.
text_raw:
German  officers  were
drilled  in  prohibited  weapons  in  Russia  and  China.

text: Inside Germany, secret armaments were prepared on a considerable scale, and troops in excess of the treaty limits were organized in a "Black Reichswehr" which was supported by secret funds of the regular Reichswehr.
text_raw:
Inside  Germany,  secret  armaments
were  prepared  on  a  considerable  scale,  and  troops  in  excess  of  the  treaty  limits  were
organized  in  a  "Black  Reichswehr"  which  was  supported  by  secret  funds  of  the  regular
Reichswehr.

text: The Reichstag had no control over either organization.
text_raw: The  Reichstag  had  no  control  over  either  organization.

text: When the Western Powers in 1920 demanded that the Free Corps be disbanded, these groups went underground and formed a parallel organization to the Black Reichswehr, being supplied with protection, funds, information, and arms from the Reichswehr and Conservatives.
text_raw:
When  the  Western
Powers  in  1920  demanded  that  the  Free  Corps  be  disbanded,  these  groups  went
underground  and  formed  a  parallel  organization  to  the  Black  Reichswehr,  being  supplied
with  protection,  funds,  information,  and  arms  from  the  Reichswehr  and  Conservatives.

text: In return the Free Corps engaged in large-scale conspiracy and murder on behalf of the Conservatives.
text_raw:
In
return  the  Free  Corps  engaged  in  large-scale  conspiracy  and  murder  on  behalf  of  the
Conservatives.

text: According to The Times of London, the Free Corps murdered four hundred victims of the Left and Center in one year.
text_raw:
According  to  The  Times  of  London,  the  Free  Corps  murdered  four
hundred  victims  of  the  Left  and  Center  in  one  year.

text: The middle-class Cabinet of Konstantin Fehrenbach resigned on May 4, 1921 and allowed the Weimar Coalition of Socialists, Democrats, and Center to take office to receive the reparations ultimatum of the Allied governments on May 5th.
text_raw:
The  middle-class  Cabinet  of  Konstantin  Fehrenbach  resigned  on  May  4,  1921  and
allowed  the  Weimar  Coalition  of  Socialists,  Democrats,  and  Center  to  take  office  to
receive  the  reparations  ultimatum  of  the  Allied  governments  on  May  5th.

text: Thus, the democratic regime was further discredited in the eyes of Germans as an instrument of weakness, hardship, and shame.
text_raw:
Thus,  the
democratic  regime  was  further  discredited  in  the  eyes  of  Germans  as  an  instrument  of
weakness,  hardship,  and  shame.

text: As soon as the job was done, the Socialists were replaced by the People's Party, and the Wirth Cabinet was succeeded by a purely middle-class government under Wilhelm Cuno, general manager of the Hamburg-American Steamship Line.
text_raw:
As  soon  as  the  job  was  done,  the  Socialists  were  replaced
by  the  People's  Party,  and  the  Wirth  Cabinet  was  succeeded  by  a  purely  middle-class
government  under  Wilhelm  Cuno,  general  manager  of  the  Hamburg-American  Steamship
Line.

text: It was this government which "managed" the hyperinflation of 1923 and the passive resistance against the French forces in the Ruhr.
text_raw:
It  was  this  government  which  "managed"  the  hyperinflation  of  1923  and  the  passive
resistance  against  the  French  forces  in  the  Ruhr.

text: The inflation, which was a great benefit to the Quartet, destroyed the economic position of the middle classes and oYver middle classes and permanently alienated them from the republic.
text_raw:
The  inflation,  which  was  a  great  benefit
to  the  Quartet,  destroyed  the  economic  position  of  the  middle  classes  and  oYver  middle
classes  and  permanently  alienated  them  from  the  republic.

text: The Cuno government was ended by a deal between Stresemann and the Socialists.
text_raw: The  Cuno  government  was  ended  by  a  deal  between  Stresemann  and  the  Socialists.

text: The former, on behalf of the People's Party, which had hitherto been resolutely anti- republican, accepted the republic; the Socialists agreed to support a Stresemann Cabinet;
text_raw:
The  former,  on  behalf  of  the  People's  Party,  which  had  hitherto  been  resolutely  anti-
republican,  accepted  the  republic;  the  Socialists  agreed  to  support  a  Stresemann  Cabinet;

text: and a broad coalition was formed for a policy of fulfillment of the Treaty of Versailles.
text_raw: and  a  broad  coalition  was  formed  for  a  policy  of  fulfillment  of  the  Treaty  of  Versailles.

text: This ended the Period of Turmoil (August 1923).
text_raw: This  ended  the  Period  of  Turmoil  (August  1923).

text: The Period of Fulfillment (1923-1930) is associated with the name of Gustav Stresemann, who was in every Cabinet until his death in October 1929.
text_raw:
The  Period  of  Fulfillment  (1923-1930)  is  associated  with  the  name  of  Gustav
Stresemann,  who  was  in  every  Cabinet  until  his  death  in  October  1929.

text: A reactionary Pan-German and economic imperialist in the period before 1919, Stresemann was always a supporter of the Quartet, and the chief creator of the German People's Party, the party of heavy industry.
text_raw:
A  reactionary
Pan-German  and  economic  imperialist  in  the  period  before  1919,  Stresemann  was  always
a  supporter  of  the  Quartet,  and  the  chief  creator  of  the  German  People's  Party,  the  party  of
heavy  industry.

text: In 1923, while still keeping his previous convictions, he decided that it would be good policy to reverse them publicly and adopt a program of support for the republic and fulfillment of treaty obligations.
text_raw:
In  1923,  while  still  keeping  his  previous  convictions,  he  decided  that  it
would  be  good  policy  to  reverse  them  publicly  and  adopt  a  program  of  support  for  the
republic  and  fulfillment  of  treaty  obligations.

text: He did this because he realized that Germany was too weak to do anything else and that she could get stronger only by obtaining release from the more stringent treaty restrictions, by foreign loans from sympathetic British and American financiers, and by secret consolidation of the Quartet.
text_raw:
He  did  this  because  he  realized  that
Germany  was  too  weak  to  do  anything  else  and  that  she  could  get  stronger  only  by
obtaining  release  from  the  more  stringent  treaty  restrictions,  by  foreign  loans  from
sympathetic  British  and  American  financiers,  and  by  secret  consolidation  of  the  Quartet.

text: All these things could be achieved more easily by a policy of fulfillment than by a policy of resistance like Cuno's.
text_raw:
All  these  things  could  be  achieved  more  easily  by  a  policy  of  fulfillment  than  by  a  policy
of  resistance  like  Cuno's.

text: The Bavarian government of the Right, which had been installed under Gustav von Kahr in 1921, refused to accept Stresemann's decision to readmit the Socialists to the Reich government in Berlin.
text_raw:
The  Bavarian  government  of  the  Right,  which  had  been  installed  under  Gustav  von
Kahr  in  1921,  refused  to  accept  Stresemann's  decision  to  readmit  the  Socialists  to  the
Reich  government  in  Berlin.

text: Instead, Kahr assumed dictatorial powers with the title of state commissioner of Bavaria.
text_raw:
Instead,  Kahr  assumed  dictatorial  powers  with  the  title  of
state  commissioner  of  Bavaria.

text: In reply the Stresemann Cabinet invested the executive power of the Reich in the Reichswehr minister, an act which had the effect of making von Seeckt the ruler of Germany.
text_raw:
In  reply  the  Stresemann  Cabinet  invested  the  executive
power  of  the  Reich  in  the  Reichswehr  minister,  an  act  which  had  the  effect  of  making  von
Seeckt  the  ruler  of  Germany.

text: In terror of a rightist coup d'etat (putsch), the Communist International decided to allow the German Communist Party to cooperate with the Socialists in an anti-Right front within the parliamentary regime.
text_raw:
In  terror  of  a  rightist  coup  d'etat  (putsch),  the  Communist
International  decided  to  allow  the  German  Communist  Party  to  cooperate  with  the
Socialists  in  an  anti-Right  front  within  the  parliamentary  regime.

text: This was done at once in the states of Saxony and Thuringia.
text_raw:
This  was  done  at  once
in  the  states  of  Saxony  and  Thuringia.

text: At this the Reichswehr commander in Bavaria, General Otto von Lossow, shifted his allegiance from Seeckt to Kahr.
text_raw:
At  this  the  Reichswehr  commander  in  Bavaria,
General  Otto  von  Lossow,  shifted  his  allegiance  from  Seeckt  to  Kahr.

text: Stresemann-Seeckt in Berlin faced Kahr-Lossow in Munich with the "Red" governments of Saxony and Thuringia in between.
text_raw:
Stresemann-Seeckt
in  Berlin  faced  Kahr-Lossow  in  Munich  with  the  "Red"  governments  of  Saxony  and
Thuringia  in  between.

text: The Reichswehr chiefly obeyed Berlin, while the Black Reichswehr and underground Free Corps (especially Ehrhardt's and Rossbach's) obeyed Munich.
text_raw:
The  Reichswehr  chiefly  obeyed  Berlin,  while  the  Black
Reichswehr  and  underground  Free  Corps  (especially  Ehrhardt's  and  Rossbach's)  obeyed
Munich.

text: Kahr-Lossow, with the support of Hitler and Ludendorff, planned to invade Saxony and Thuringia, overthrow the Red governments on the pretext of suppressing Bolshevism, and then continue northward to overthrow the central government in Berlin.
text_raw:
Kahr-Lossow,  with  the  support  of  Hitler  and  Ludendorff,  planned  to  invade
Saxony  and  Thuringia,  overthrow  the  Red  governments  on  the  pretext  of  suppressing

text: The Reich government headed this plot off by an illegal act:
text_raw: The  Reich  government  headed  this  plot  off  by  an  illegal  act:

The  Reichswohr  forces  of
Seeckt  overthrew  the  constitutional  Red  governments  of  Saxony  and  Thuringia  to

text: As a result, Lossow and Kahr gave up the plans for revolt, while Hitler and Ludendorff refused to do so.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  Lossow  and  Kahr  gave  up  the  plans  for  revolt,  while
Hitler  and  Ludendorff  refused  to  do  so.

text: By the "Beer-Hall" Putsch of November 8, 1923, Hitler and Ludendorff tried to abduct Kahr and Lossow and force them to continue the revolt.
text_raw:
By  the  "Beer-Hall"  Putsch  of  November  8,  1923,
Hitler  and  Ludendorff  tried  to  abduct  Kahr  and  Lossow  and  force  them  to  continue  the

text: They were overcome in a blast of gunfire.
text_raw: They  were  overcome  in  a  blast  of  gunfire.

text: Kahr, Lossow, and Ludendorff were never punished;
text_raw:
Kahr,  Lossow,  and  Ludendorff  were
never  punished;

text: Hermann Goring fled the country;
text_raw: Hermann  Goring  fled  the  country;

text: Hitler and Rudolf Hess were given living quarters in a fortress for a year, profiting by the occasion to write the famous volume Mein Kampf.
text_raw:
Hitler  and  Rudolf  Hess  were  given
living  quarters  in  a  fortress  for  a  year,  profiting  by  the  occasion  to  write  the  famous
volume  Mein  Kampf.

text: In order to deal with the economic crisis and the inflation, Stresemann's government was granted dictatorial powers overriding all constitutional guarantees, except that the Socialists won a promise not to touch the eight-hour day or the social-insurance system.
text_raw:
In  order  to  deal  with  the  economic  crisis  and  the  inflation,  Stresemann's  government
was  granted  dictatorial  powers  overriding  all  constitutional  guarantees,  except  that  the
Socialists  won  a  promise  not  to  touch  the  eight-hour  day  or  the  social-insurance  system.

text: In this way the inflation was curbed, and a new monetary system was established;
text_raw: In  this  way  the  inflation  was  curbed,  and  a  new  monetary  system  was  established;

text: incidentally, the eight-hour day was abolished by decree (1923).
text_raw: incidentally,  the  eight-hour  day  was  abolished  by  decree  (1923).

text: A reparations agreement (the Dawes Plan) was made with the Allied governments, and the Ruhr was successfully evacuated.
text_raw:
A  reparations  agreement
(the  Dawes  Plan)  was  made  with  the  Allied  governments,  and  the  Ruhr  was  successfully
evacuated.

text: In the course of these events the Social Democrats abandoned the Stresemann government in protest at its illegal suppression of the Red government of Saxony, but the Stresemann program continued with the support of the parties of the Center and Right, including, for the first time, the support of the anti-Republican Nationalists.

text: The chief causes of the decision were (1) the realization that industrial plants had been largely rebuilt by foreign loans;
