As  a  consequence  of  this  event,  the  SA  was  reorganized  under  Rohm,
the  word  "Socialism"  in  the  party  name  was  interpreted  to  mean  nationalism  (or  a  society
without  class  conflicts),  and  equality  in  party  and  state  was  replaced  hy  the  "leadership
principle"  and  the  doctrine  of  the  elite.

text: Tn the next two years the party passed through a series of crises of which the chief was the attempted Putsch of November 9, 1923.
text_raw:
Tn  the  next  two  years  the  party  passed  through  a
series  of  crises  of  which  the  chief  was  the  attempted  Putsch  of  November  9,  1923.

text: During this period all kinds of violence and illegality, even murder, were condoned by the Bavarian and Munich authorities.
text_raw:
During
this  period  all  kinds  of  violence  and  illegality,  even  murder,  were  condoned  by  the
Bavarian  and  Munich  authorities.

text: As a result of the failures of this period, especially the abortive Putsch, Hitler became convinced that he must come to power by legal methods rather than by force; he broke with Ludendorff and ceased to be supported by the Reichswehr; he began to receive his chief financial support from the industrialists; he made a tacit alliance with the Bavarian People's Party by which Prime Minister Heinrich Held of Bavaria raised the ban on the Nazi Party in return for Hitler's repudiation of Ludendorff s anti-Christian teachings; and Hitler formed a new armed militia (the SS) to protect himself against Rohm's control of the old armed militia (the SA).
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  the  failures  of  this  period,  especially  the
abortive  Putsch,  Hitler  became  convinced  that  he  must  come  to  power  by  legal  methods
rather  than  by  force;  he  broke  with  Ludendorff  and  ceased  to  be  supported  by  the
Reichswehr;  he  began  to  receive  his  chief  financial  support  from  the  industrialists;  he
made  a  tacit  alliance  with  the  Bavarian  People's  Party  by  which  Prime  Minister  Heinrich
Held  of  Bavaria  raised  the  ban  on  the  Nazi  Party  in  return  for  Hitler's  repudiation  of
Ludendorff  s  anti-Christian  teachings;  and  Hitler  formed  a  new  armed  militia  (the  SS)  to
protect  himself  against  Rohm's  control  of  the  old  armed  militia  (the  SA).

text: In the period 1924-1930 the party continued, without any real growth, as a "lunatic fringe," subsidized by the industrialists.
text_raw:
In  the  period  1924-1930  the  party  continued,  without  any  real  growth,  as  a  "lunatic
fringe,"  subsidized  by  the  industrialists.

text: Among the chief contributors to the party in this period were Carl Bechstein (Berlin piano manufacturer), August Borsig (Berlin locomotive manufacturer), Emil Kirdorf (general manager of the Rhenish-Westphalian Coal Syndicate), Fritz Thyssen (owner of the United Steel Works and president of the German Industrial Council) and Albert Vogler (general manager of the Gelsenkirchen Iron and Steel Company and formerly general manager of United Steel Works).
text_raw:
Among  the  chief  contributors  to  the  party  in  this
period  were  Carl  Bechstein  (Berlin  piano  manufacturer),  August  Borsig  (Berlin
locomotive  manufacturer),  Emil  Kirdorf  (general  manager  of  the  Rhenish-Westphalian
Coal  Syndicate),  Fritz  Thyssen  (owner  of  the  United  Steel  Works  and  president  of  the
German  Industrial  Council)  and  Albert  Vogler  (general  manager  of  the  Gelsenkirchen
Iron  and  Steel  Company  and  formerly  general  manager  of  United  Steel  Works).

text: During this period neither Hitler nor his supporters were seeking to create a mass movement.
text_raw:
During
this  period  neither  Hitler  nor  his  supporters  were  seeking  to  create  a  mass  movement.

text: That did not come until 1930.
text_raw: That  did  not  come  until  1930.

text: But during this earlier period the party itself was steadily centralized, and the Leftish elements (like the Strasser brothers) were weakened or eliminated.
text_raw:
But  during  this  earlier  period  the  party  itself  was  steadily
centralized,  and  the  Leftish  elements  (like  the  Strasser  brothers)  were  weakened  or
eliminated.

text: In April 1927, Hitler spoke to 400 industrialists in Essen; in April 1928, he addressed a similar group of landlords from east of the Elbe; in January 1932 came one of his greatest triumphs when he spoke for 3 hours to the Industrial Club of Diisseldorf and won support and financial contributions from that powerful group.
text_raw:
In  April  1927,  Hitler  spoke  to  400  industrialists  in  Essen;  in  April  1928,  he
addressed  a  similar  group  of  landlords  from  east  of  the  Elbe;  in  January  1932  came  one  of
his  greatest  triumphs  when  he  spoke  for  3  hours  to  the  Industrial  Club  of  Diisseldorf  and
won  support  and  financial  contributions  from  that  powerful  group.

text: By that date he was seeking to build his movement into a mass political party capable of sweeping him into office.
text_raw:
By  that  date  he  was
seeking  to  build  his  movement  into  a  mass  political  party  capable  of  sweeping  him  into
office.

text: This project failed.
text_raw: This  project  failed.

text: As we have indicated, by the end of 1932 much of the financial support from industry had been cut off by Papen, and party membership was falling away, chiefly to the Communists.
text_raw:
As  we  have  indicated,  by  the  end  of  1932  much  of  the
financial  support  from  industry  had  been  cut  off  by  Papen,  and  party  membership  was
falling  away,  chiefly  to  the  Communists.

text: To stop this decline, Hitler agreed to become chancellor in a Cabinet in which there would be only three Nazis among eleven members.
text_raw:
To  stop  this  decline,  Hitler  agreed  to  become
chancellor  in  a  Cabinet  in  which  there  would  be  only  three  Nazis  among  eleven  members.

text: Papen hoped in this way to control the Nazis and to obtain from them the popular support which Papen had so sorely lacked in his own chancellorship in 1932.
text_raw:
Papen  hoped  in  this  way  to  control  the  Nazis  and  to  obtain  from  them  the  popular  support
which  Papen  had  so  sorely  lacked  in  his  own  chancellorship  in  1932.

text: But Papen was far too clever for his own good.
text_raw:
But  Papen  was  far
too  clever  for  his  own  good.

text: He, Hugenberg, Hindenburg, and the rest of the intriguers had underestimated Hitler.
text_raw:
He,  Hugenberg,  Hindenburg,  and  the  rest  of  the  intriguers
had  underestimated  Hitler.

text: The latter, in return for Hugenberg's acceptance of new elections on March 5, 1933, promised that there would be no Cabinet changes whatever the outcome of the voting.
text_raw:
The  latter,  in  return  for  Hugenberg's  acceptance  of  new
elections  on  March  5,  1933,  promised  that  there  would  be  no  Cabinet  changes  whatever
the  outcome  of  the  voting.

text: In spite of the fact that the Nazis obtained only 44 per cent of the ballots in the new election, Hitler became dictator of Germany within eighteen months.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  the  fact  that  the  Nazis  obtained  only  44  per  cent  of
the  ballots  in  the  new  election,  Hitler  became  dictator  of  Germany  within  eighteen
months.

text: One of the chief reasons for this success rests on the position of Prussia within Germany.
text_raw:
One  of  the  chief  reasons  for  this  success  rests  on  the  position  of  Prussia  within
Germany.

text: Prussia was the greatest of the fourteen states of Germany.
text_raw: Prussia  was  the  greatest  of  the  fourteen  states  of  Germany.

text: Covering almost two-thirds of the country, it included both the great rural areas of the east and the great industrial areas of the west.
text_raw:
Covering  almost
two-thirds  of  the  country,  it  included  both  the  great  rural  areas  of  the  east  and  the  great
industrial  areas  of  the  west.

text: Thus it included the most conservative as well as the most progressive portions of Germany.
text_raw:
Thus  it  included  the  most  conservative  as  well  as  the  most
progressive  portions  of  Germany.

text: While its influence was almost as great under the republic as it had been under the empire, this influence was of quite a different character, having changed from the chief bulwark of conservatism in the earlier period to the chief area of progressivism in the later period.
text_raw:
While  its  influence  was  almost  as  great  under  the
republic  as  it  had  been  under  the  empire,  this  influence  was  of  quite  a  different  character,
having  changed  from  the  chief  bulwark  of  conservatism  in  the  earlier  period  to  the  chief
area  of  progressivism  in  the  later  period.

text: This change w as made possible by the large numbers of enlightened groups in the Rhenish areas of Prussia, but chiefly by the fact that the so-called Weimar Coalition of Social Democrats, Center Party, and Liberal Democrats remained unbroken in Prussia from 1918 to 1932.
text_raw:
This  change  w  as  made  possible  by  the  large
numbers  of  enlightened  groups  in  the  Rhenish  areas  of  Prussia,  but  chiefly  by  the  fact  that
the  so-called  Weimar  Coalition  of  Social  Democrats,  Center  Party,  and  Liberal
Democrats  remained  unbroken  in  Prussia  from  1918  to  1932.

text: As a consequence of this alliance, a Social Democrat, Otto Braun. held the position of prime minister of Prussia for almost the whole period 1920 1932, and Prussia was the chief obstacle in the path of the Nazis and of reaction in the critical days after 1930.
text_raw:
As  a  consequence  of  this
alliance,  a  Social  Democrat,  Otto  Braun.  held  the  position  of  prime  minister  of  Prussia  for
almost  the  whole  period  1920  1932,  and  Prussia  was  the  chief  obstacle  in  the  path  of  the
Nazis  and  of  reaction  in  the  critical  days  after  1930.

text: As part of this movement the Prussian Cabinet in 1930 refused to allow either Communists or Nazis to hold municipal offices in Prussia, prohibited Prussian civil servants from holding membership in either of these two parties, and forbade the use of the Nazi uniform.
text_raw:
As  part  of  this  movement  the
Prussian  Cabinet  in  1930  refused  to  allow  either  Communists  or  Nazis  to  hold  municipal
offices  in  Prussia,  prohibited  Prussian  civil  servants  from  holding  membership  in  either
of  these  two  parties,  and  forbade  the  use  of  the  Nazi  uniform.

text: This obstacle to extremism was removed on July 20, 1932, when Hindenburg, by presidential decree based on Article 48, appointed Papen commissioner for Prussia.
text_raw:
This  obstacle  to  extremism  was  removed  on  July  20,  1932,  when  Hindenburg,  by
presidential  decree  based  on  Article  48,  appointed  Papen  commissioner  for  Prussia.

text: Papen at once dismissed the eight members of the Prussian parliamentary Cabinet and granted their governmental functions to men named by himself.
text_raw:
Papen  at  once  dismissed  the  eight  members  of  the  Prussian  parliamentary  Cabinet  and
granted  their  governmental  functions  to  men  named  by  himself.

text: The dismissed ministers were removed from their offices by the power of the army, but at once challenged the legality of this action before the German Supreme Court at Leipzig.
text_raw:
The  dismissed  ministers
were  removed  from  their  offices  by  the  power  of  the  army,  but  at  once  challenged  the
legality  of  this  action  before  the  German  Supreme  Court  at  Leipzig.

text: By its verdict of October 25, 1932, the court decided for the removed officials.
text_raw:
By  its  verdict  of
October  25,  1932,  the  court  decided  for  the  removed  officials.

text: In spite of this decision, Hitler, after only a week in the chancellorship, was able to obtain from Hindenburg a new decree which removed the Prussian ministers from office once more and conferred their powers on the federal vice-chancellor, Papen.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  this  decision,
Hitler,  after  only  a  week  in  the  chancellorship,  was  able  to  obtain  from  Hindenburg  a  new
decree  which  removed  the  Prussian  ministers  from  office  once  more  and  conferred  their
powers  on  the  federal  vice-chancellor,  Papen.

text: Control of the police administration was conferred on Hermann Goring.
text_raw:
Control  of  the  police  administration  was
conferred  on  Hermann  Goring.

text: The Nazis already held, through Wilhelm Frick, control of the Reich Ministry of Interior and thus of the national police powers.
text_raw:
The  Nazis  already  held,  through  Wilhelm  Frick,  control
of  the  Reich  Ministry  of  Interior  and  thus  of  the  national  police  powers.

text: Thus Hitler, by February 7th, had control of the police powers both of the Reich and of Prussia.
text_raw:
Thus  Hitler,  by
February  7th,  had  control  of  the  police  powers  both  of  the  Reich  and  of  Prussia.

text: Using this advantage, the Nazis began a twofold assault on the opposition.
text_raw: Using  this  advantage,  the  Nazis  began  a  twofold  assault  on  the  opposition.

text: Goring and Frick worked under a cloak of legality from above, while Captain Rohm in command of the Nazi Party storm troops worked without pretense of legality from below.
text_raw:
Goring  and
Frick  worked  under  a  cloak  of  legality  from  above,  while  Captain  Rohm  in  command  of
the  Nazi  Party  storm  troops  worked  without  pretense  of  legality  from  below.

text: All uncooperative police officials were retired, removed, or given vacations and were replaced by Nazi substitutes, usually Storm Troop leaders.
text_raw:
All
uncooperative  police  officials  were  retired,  removed,  or  given  vacations  and  were
replaced  by  Nazi  substitutes,  usually  Storm  Troop  leaders.

text: On February 4, 1933,
text_raw: On  February  4,  1933,

text: Hindenburg signed an emergency decree which gave the government the right to prohibit or control any meetings, uniforms, or newspapers.
text_raw:
Hindenburg  signed  an  emergency  decree  which  gave  the  government  the  right  to  prohibit
or  control  any  meetings,  uniforms,  or  newspapers.

text: In this way most opposition meetings and newspapers were prevented from reaching the public.
text_raw:
In  this  way  most  opposition  meetings
and  newspapers  were  prevented  from  reaching  the  public.

text: This attack on the opposition from above was accompanied by a violent assault from below, carried out by the SA.
text_raw:
This  attack  on  the  opposition  from  above  was  accompanied  by  a  violent  assault  from
below,  carried  out  by  the  SA.

text: In desperate attacks in which eighteen Nazis and fifty-one opposition were killed, all Communist, most Socialist, and many Center Party meetings were disrupted.
text_raw:
In  desperate  attacks  in  which  eighteen  Nazis  and  fifty-one
opposition  were  killed,  all  Communist,  most  Socialist,  and  many  Center  Party  meetings
were  disrupted.

text: In spite of all this, it was evident a week before the election that the German people were not convinced.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  all  this,  it  was  evident  a  week  before  the  election  that  the
German  people  were  not  convinced.

text: Accordingly, under circumstances which are still mysterious, a plot was worked out to burn the Reichstag building and blame the Communists.
text_raw:
Accordingly,  under  circumstances  which  are  still
mysterious,  a  plot  was  worked  out  to  burn  the  Reichstag  building  and  blame  the
Communists.

text: Most of the plotters were homosexuals and were able to persuade a degenerate moron from Holland named Van der Lubbe to go with them.
text_raw:
Most  of  the  plotters  were  homosexuals  and  were  able  to  persuade  a
degenerate  moron  from  Holland  named  Van  der  Lubbe  to  go  with  them.

text: After the building was set on fire, Van der Lubbe was left wandering about in it and was arrested by the police.
text_raw:
After  the
building  was  set  on  fire,  Van  der  Lubbe  was  left  wandering  about  in  it  and  was  arrested
by  the  police.

text: The government at once arrested four Communists, including the party leader in the Reichstag (Ernst Torgler).
text_raw:
The  government  at  once  arrested  four  Communists,  including  the  party
leader  in  the  Reichstag  (Ernst  Torgler).

text: The day following the fire (February 28, 1933) Hindenburg signed a decree suspending all civil liberties and giving the government power to invade any personal privacy, including the right to search private homes or confiscate property.
text_raw:
The  day  following  the  fire  (February  28,  1933)  Hindenburg  signed  a  decree
suspending  all  civil  liberties  and  giving  the  government  power  to  invade  any  personal
privacy,  including  the  right  to  search  private  homes  or  confiscate  property.

text: At once all Communist members of the Reichstag, as well as thousands of others, were arrested, and all Communist and Social-Democrat papers were suspended for two weeks.
text_raw:
At  once  all
Communist  members  of  the  Reichstag,  as  well  as  thousands  of  others,  were  arrested,  and
all  Communist  and  Social-Democrat  papers  were  suspended  for  two  weeks.

text: The true story of the Reichstag fire was kept secret only with difficulty.
text_raw: The  true  story  of  the  Reichstag  fire  was  kept  secret  only  with  difficulty.

text: Several persons who knew the truth, including a Nationalist Reichstag member, Dr. Oberfohren, were murdered in March and April to prevent their circulating the true story.
text_raw:
Several
persons  who  knew  the  truth,  including  a  Nationalist  Reichstag  member,  Dr.  Oberfohren,
were  murdered  in  March  and  April  to  prevent  their  circulating  the  true  story.

text: Most of the Nazis who were in on the plot were murdered by Goring during the "blood purge" of June 30, 1934.
text_raw:
Most  of  the
Nazis  who  were  in  on  the  plot  were  murdered  by  Goring  during  the  "blood  purge"  of  June
30,  1934.

text: The four Communists who were directly charged with the crime were acquitted by the regular German courts, although Van der Lubbe was convicted.
text_raw:
The  four  Communists  who  were  directly  charged  with  the  crime  were  acquitted
by  the  regular  German  courts,  although  Van  der  Lubbe  was  convicted.

text: In spite of these drastic measures, the election of March 5, 1933, was a failure from the Nazi point of view.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  these  drastic  measures,  the  election  of  March  5,  1933,  was  a  failure  from
the  Nazi  point  of  view.

text: Hitler's party received only 288 of 647 seats, or 43.9 percent of the total vote.
text_raw:
Hitler's  party  received  only  288  of  647  seats,  or  43.9  percent  of
the  total  vote.

text: The Nationalists obtained only 8 percent.
text_raw: The  Nationalists  obtained  only  8  percent.

text: The Communists obtained 81 seats, a decrease of 19, but the Socialists obtained 125, an increase of 4.
text_raw:
The  Communists  obtained  81
seats,  a  decrease  of  19,  but  the  Socialists  obtained  125,  an  increase  of  4.

text: The Center Party fell from 89 to 74, and the People's Party from 1 1 to 2.
text_raw:
The  Center  Party
fell  from  89  to  74,  and  the  People's  Party  from  1 1  to  2.

text: The Nationalists stayed at 5: seats.
text_raw: The  Nationalists  stayed  at  5:  seats.

text: In the simultaneous election to the Prussian Diet, the Nazis obtained 21 1 and the Nationalists 43 out of 474 seats.
text_raw:
In  the  simultaneous  election  to  the  Prussian  Diet,  the  Nazis  obtained  21 1  and  the
Nationalists  43  out  of  474  seats.

text: The period from the election of March 5, 1933, to the death of Hindenburg on August :, 1934, is generally called the Period of Coordination (Gleichschaltung).
text_raw:
The  period  from  the  election  of  March  5,  1933,  to  the  death  of  Hindenburg  on  August
:,  1934,  is  generally  called  the  Period  of  Coordination  (Gleichschaltung).

text: The process was carried on, like the electoral campaign just finished, by illegal actions from below and legalistic actions from above.
text_raw:
The  process
was  carried  on,  like  the  electoral  campaign  just  finished,  by  illegal  actions  from  below
and  legalistic  actions  from  above.

text: From below, on March 7th throughout Germany, the SA swept away much of the opposition by violence, driving it into hiding.
text_raw:
From  below,  on  March  7th  throughout  Germany,  the
SA  swept  away  much  of  the  opposition  by  violence,  driving  it  into  hiding.

text: They marched to most offices of trade unions, periodicals, and local governments, smashing them up, expelling their occupants, and raising the swastika flag.
text_raw:
They  marched
to  most  offices  of  trade  unions,  periodicals,  and  local  governments,  smashing  them  up,
expelling  their  occupants,  and  raising  the  swastika  flag.

text: Minister of the Interior Wilhelm Frick condoned these actions by naming Nazis as police presidents in various German states (Baden, Saxony, Wurttemburg, Bavaria), including General von Epp in Bavaria.
text_raw:
Minister  of  the  Interior  Wilhelm
Frick  condoned  these  actions  by  naming  Nazis  as  police  presidents  in  various  German
states  (Baden,  Saxony,  Wurttemburg,  Bavaria),  including  General  von  Epp  in  Bavaria.

text: These men then proceeded to use their police powers to seize control of the apparatus of state government.
text_raw:
These  men  then  proceeded  to  use  their  police  powers  to  seize  control  of  the  apparatus  of
state  government.

text: The new Reichstag met on March 23rd at the Kroll Opera House.
text_raw: The  new  Reichstag  met  on  March  23rd  at  the  Kroll  Opera  House.

text: In order to secure a majority, the Nazis excluded from the session all of the Communist and 30 Socialist members, about 109 in all.
text_raw:
In  order  to  secure  a
majority,  the  Nazis  excluded  from  the  session  all  of  the  Communist  and  30  Socialist
members,  about  109  in  all.

text: The rest were asked to pass an "enabling act" which would give the government for four years the right to legislate by decree, without the need for the presidential signature, as in Article 48, and without constitutional restrictions except in respect to the powers of the Reichstag, the Reichsrat, and the presidency.
text_raw:
The  rest  were  asked  to  pass  an  "enabling  act"  which  would
give  the  government  for  four  years  the  right  to  legislate  by  decree,  without  the  need  for
the  presidential  signature,  as  in  Article  48,  and  without  constitutional  restrictions  except
in  respect  to  the  powers  of  the  Reichstag,  the  Reichsrat,  and  the  presidency.

text: Since this law required a two-third majority, it could have been beaten if only a small group of the Center Party had voted against it.
text_raw:
Since  this  law  required  a  two-third  majority,  it  could  have  been  beaten  if  only  a  small
group  of  the  Center  Party  had  voted  against  it.

text: To be sure, Hitler made it very clear that he was prepared to use violence against all who refused to cooperate with him, but his power to do so on a clear-cut constitutional issue in March 1933 was much less than it became later, since violence from him on such a question might well have arrayed the president and the Reichswehr against him.
text_raw:
To  be  sure,  Hitler  made  it  very  clear  that
he  was  prepared  to  use  violence  against  all  who  refused  to  cooperate  with  him,  but  his
power  to  do  so  on  a  clear-cut  constitutional  issue  in  March  1933  was  much  less  than  it
became  later,  since  violence  from  him  on  such  a  question  might  well  have  arrayed  the
president  and  the  Reichswehr  against  him.

text: In spite of Hitler's intimidating speech, Otto Wels of the Social Democrats rose to explain why his party refused to support the bill.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  Hitler's  intimidating  speech,  Otto  Wels  of  the  Social  Democrats  rose  to
explain  why  his  party  refused  to  support  the  bill.

text: He was followed by Monsignor Kaas of the Center Party who explained that his Catholic Group would support it.
text_raw:
He  was  followed  by  Monsignor  Kaas  of
the  Center  Party  who  explained  that  his  Catholic  Group  would  support  it.

text: The vote in favor of the bill was more than sufficient, being 441-94, with the Social Democrats forming the solid minority.
text_raw:
The  vote  in
favor  of  the  bill  was  more  than  sufficient,  being  441-94,  with  the  Social  Democrats
forming  the  solid  minority.

text: Thus, this weak, timid, doctrinaire, and ignorant group redeemed themselves by their courage after the eleventh hour had passed.
text_raw:
Thus,  this  weak,  timid,  doctrinaire,  and  ignorant  group
redeemed  themselves  by  their  courage  after  the  eleventh  hour  had  passed.

text: Under this "Enabling Act" the government issued a series of revolutionary decrees in the next few months.
text_raw:
Under  this  "Enabling  Act"  the  government  issued  a  series  of  revolutionary  decrees  in
the  next  few  months.

text: The diets of all the German states, except Prussia (which had had its own election on March 5th) were reconstituted in the proportions of votes in the national election of March 5th, except that the Communists were thrown out.
text_raw:

election  of  March  5th,  except  that  the  Communists  were  thrown  out.

Each  party  was
given  its  quota  of  members  and  allowed  to  name  the  individual  members  on  a  purely
party  basis.

text: A similar procedure was applied to local governments.
text_raw: A  similar  procedure  was  applied  to  local  governments.

text: Thus the Nazis received a majority in each body.
text_raw:
Thus  the  Nazis
received  a  majority  in  each  body.

text: A decree of April 7th gave the Reich government the right to name a governor of each German state.
text_raw:
A  decree  of  April  7th  gave  the  Reich  government  the  right  to  name  a  governor  of  each
German  state.

text: This was a new official empowered to enforce the policies of the Reich government even to the point of dismissing the state governments, including the prime ministers, diets, and the hitherto irremovable judges.
text_raw:
This  was  a  new  official  empowered  to  enforce  the  policies  of  the  Reich
government  even  to  the  point  of  dismissing  the  state  governments,  including  the  prime
ministers,  diets,  and  the  hitherto  irremovable  judges.

text: This right was used in each state to make a Nazi governor and a Nazi prime minister.
text_raw:
This  right  was  used  in  each  state  to
make  a  Nazi  governor  and  a  Nazi  prime  minister.

text: In Bavaria, for example, the two were Epp and Rohm, while in Prussia the two were Hitler and Goring.
text_raw:
In  Bavaria,  for  example,  the  two  were
Epp  and  Rohm,  while  in  Prussia  the  two  were  Hitler  and  Goring.

text: In many states the governor was the district leader of the Nazi Party, and where he was not, he was subject to that leader's orders.
text_raw:
In  many  states  the
governor  was  the  district  leader  of  the  Nazi  Party,  and  where  he  was  not,  he  was  subject
to  that  leader's  orders.

text: By a later law of January 30, 1934, the diets of the states were abolished; the sovereign powers of the states were transferred to the Reich; and the governors were made subordinates of the Reich Ministry of the Interior.
text_raw:
By  a  later  law  of  January  30,  1934,  the  diets  of  the  states  were
abolished;  the  sovereign  powers  of  the  states  were  transferred  to  the  Reich;  and  the
governors  were  made  subordinates  of  the  Reich  Ministry  of  the  Interior.

text: All the political parties except the Nazis were abolished in May, June, and July 1933.
text_raw: All  the  political  parties  except  the  Nazis  were  abolished  in  May,  June,  and  July  1933.

text: The Communists had been outlawed on February 28th.
text_raw: The  Communists  had  been  outlawed  on  February  28th.

text_raw:
The  Social  Democrats  were
enjoined  from  all  activities  on  June  22nd,  and  were  expelled  from  various  governing

text: bodies on July 7th.

text_raw:
The  German  State  Party  (Democratic  Party)  and  the  German  People's
Party  were  dissolved  on  June  28th  and  July  4th.

text_raw:
The  Bavarian  People's  Party  was
smashed  by  the  Storm  Troopers  on  June  22nd,  and  disbanded  itself  on  July  4th.

The

On  July  22nd  the  same  man  became  president  of  the  German  Industrial
and  Trade  Committee,  which  was  a  union  of  all  the  chambers  of  commerce.

In  Germany

This  last  reversal  resulted  from  the  fact  that  most  of  the
cooperatives  had  come  under  Nazi  control  by  being  taken  over  by  the  Labor  Front  on

text: Labor was coordinated without resistance, except from the Communists.
text_raw: Labor  was  coordinated  without  resistance,  except  from  the  Communists.

government  declared  May  1st  a  national  holiday,  and  celebrated  it  with  a  speech  by  Hitler

The  unions  themselves  were  incorporated  into  a  Nazi  German

The  new  leader,  in  an  article  in  the  Volkischer
Beobachter,  promised  employers  that  henceforth  they  could  be  masters  in  their  own
houses  as  long  as  they  served  the  nation  (that  is,  the  Nazi  Party).

labor  by  reducing  the  work  week  to  forty  hours  (with  a  corresponding  wage  cut),  hy

The  various  land  and  peasant  associations  were  merged  into  a  single

text_raw: Ludwig  Miiller,  in  his  place  (September  27th).

At  the  elections  for  Church  assemblies  in

Prominent  Protestant  leaders,  like  Martin  Niemoller,  who  objected  to

The  Catholic  Church  made  every  effort  to  cooperate  with  the  Nazis,  but  soon  found  it

By  this  agreement  the  state  recognized
freedom  of  religious  belief  and  of  worship,  exemption  of  the  clergy  from  certain  civic
duties,  and  the  right  of  the  Church  to  manage  its  own  affairs  and  to  establish
denominational  schools.

Governors  of  the  German  states  were  given  a  right  to  object  to
nominations  to  the  highest  clerical  posts;  bishops  were  to  take  an  oath  of  loyalty,  and
education  was  to  continue  to  function  as  it  had  been  doing.

text: This agreement with the Church began to break down almost at once.
text_raw: This  agreement  with  the  Church  began  to  break  down  almost  at  once.

Within  ten  days
of  the  signing  of  the  Concordat,  the  Nazis  began  to  attack  the  Catholic  Youth  League  and

Church  schools  were  restricted,  and  members  of  the  clergy  were
arrested  and  tried  on  charges  of  evading  the  monetary  foreign-exchange  regulations  and
of  immorality.

text: The Church condemned the efforts of Nazis like Rosenberg to replace Christianity by a revived German paganism and such laws as that permitting sterilization of socially objectionable persons.

Christianity  by  a  revived  German  paganism  and  such  laws  as  that  permitting  sterilization

The  word  used  here  is  "authoritarian,"  for,  unlike  the

text: It was not totalitarian because two members of the Quartet were not coordinated, a third member was coordinated only incompletely and, unlike Italy or Soviet Russia, the economic system was not ruled by the state but was subject to "self-rule." It  was  not  totalitarian
because  two  members  of  the  Quartet  were  not  coordinated,  a  third  member  was

text: Newspaper men and journalistic writers applied the term "totalitarian" to the Nazi system, and the name has stuck without any real analysis of the facts as they existed.

text: In fact, the Nazi system was not totalitarian either in theory or in practice.

text: The Nazi movement, in its simplest analysis, was an aggregation of gangsters, neurotics, mercenaries, psychopaths, and merely discontented, with a small intermixture of idealists.
text_raw:
The  Nazi  movement,  in  its  simplest  analysis,  was  an  aggregation  of  gangsters,
neurotics,  mercenaries,  psychopaths,  and  merely  discontented,  with  a  small  intermixture
of  idealists.

text: This movement was built up by the Quartet as a counterrevolutionary force against, first, the Weimar Republic, internationalism, and democracy, and against, second, the dangers of social revolution, especially Communism, engendered by the world economic depression.
text_raw:
This  movement  was  built  up  by  the  Quartet  as  a  counterrevolutionary  force
against,  first,  the  Weimar  Republic,  internationalism,  and  democracy,  and  against,
second,  the  dangers  of  social  revolution,  especially  Communism,  engendered  by  the
world  economic  depression.

text: This movement, once it came to power at the behest of the Quartet, took on life and goals of its own quite different from, and, indeed, largely inimical to, the life and goals of the Quartet.
text_raw:
This  movement,  once  it  came  to  power  at  the  behest  of  the
Quartet,  took  on  life  and  goals  of  its  own  quite  different  from,  and,  indeed,  largely
inimical  to,  the  life  and  goals  of  the  Quartet.

text: No showdown or open conflict ever arose between the movement and the Quartet.
text_raw:
No  showdown  or  open  conflict  ever  arose
between  the  movement  and  the  Quartet.

text: Instead, a modus vivendi was worked out by which the two chief members of the Quartet, industry and the army, obtained their desires, while the Nazis obtained the power and privileges for which they yearned.
text_raw:
Instead,  a  modus  vivendi  was  worked  out  by
which  the  two  chief  members  of  the  Quartet,  industry  and  the  army,  obtained  their
desires,  while  the  Nazis  obtained  the  power  and  privileges  for  which  they  yearned.

text: The seeds of conflict continued to exist and even to grow between the movement and its creators, especially because of the fact that the movement worked continually to create a substitute industrial system and a substitute army parallel to the old industrial system and the old Reichswehr.
text_raw:
The  seeds  of  conflict  continued  to  exist  and  even  to  grow  between  the  movement  and
its  creators,  especially  because  of  the  fact  that  the  movement  worked  continually  to  create
a  substitute  industrial  system  and  a  substitute  army  parallel  to  the  old  industrial  system
and  the  old  Reichswehr.

text: Here again the threatening conflict never broke out because the Second World War had the double result that it demonstrated the need for solidarity in the face of the enemy, and it brought great booty and profits to both sides â€” to the industrialists and Reichswehr on one hand and to the party on the other hand.

text: Except for the rise of the party, and the profits, power, and prestige which accrued to the leaders (but not to the ordinary members) of the party, the structure of German society was not drastically changed after 1933.
text_raw:
Except  for  the  rise  of  the  party,  and  the  profits,  power,  and  prestige  which  accrued  to
the  leaders  (but  not  to  the  ordinary  members)  of  the  party,  the  structure  of  German

text: It was still sharply divided into two parts â€” the rulers and the ruled.

It  was  still  sharply  divided  into  two

text: The influence of the landlord group in the earlier period rested on tradition rather than on power.
text_raw:
The  influence  of  the  landlord  group  in  the  earlier  period  rested  on  tradition  rather  than
on  power.

text: It was supported by a number of factors:
text_raw: It  was  supported  by  a  number  of  factors:

text: (1) the close personal connections of the landlords with the emperor, the army, and the bureaucracy;
text_raw:
(1)  the  close  personal  connections  of
the  landlords  with  the  emperor,  the  army,  and  the  bureaucracy;

text: (2) the peculiar voting rules in Germany which gave the landlords undue influence in Prussia and gave the state of Prussia undue influence in Germany;
(3) the economic and social power of the landlords, especially east of the Elbe, a power based on their ability to bring pressure to bear on tenants and agricultural laborers in that area.
text_raw:
(3)  the  economic  and  social  power  of  the
landlords,  especially  east  of  the  Elbe,  a  power  based  on  their  ability  to  bring  pressure  to

text: All these sources of power were weakening, even under the empire.
text_raw: All  these  sources  of  power  were  weakening,  even  under  the  empire.

text: The republic and the Third Reich merely extended a process already well advanced.
text_raw:
The  republic  and
the  Third  Reich  merely  extended  a  process  already  well  advanced.

text: The economic power of the landlords was threatened by the agricultural crisis after 1880 and was clearly evident in their demand for tariff protection after 1895.
text_raw:
The  economic  power
of  the  landlords  was  threatened  by  the  agricultural  crisis  after  1880  and  was  clearly
evident  in  their  demand  for  tariff  protection  after  1895.

text: The bankruptcy of the Junker estates was bound to undermine their political influence even if the state was willing to support them with subsidies and Osthilfe indefinitely.
text_raw:

estates  was  bound  to  undermine  their  political  influence  even  if  the  state  was  willing  to
support  them  with  subsidies  and  Osthilfe  indefinitely.

text: The departure of the emperor and the change in the position of the army and bureaucracy under the republic weakened

The  departure  of  the  emperor  and
the  change  in  the  position  of  the  army  and  bureaucracy  under  the  republic  weakened

text_raw:
The  change  in  the  voting  regulations
after  1918  and  the  ending  of  voting  after  1933,  combined  with  the  increasing  absorption
of  Prussia  and  the  other  Lander  into  a  unified  German  state,  reduced  the  political  power

text: Finally, their social influence was weakened by the migration of German farm laborers from eastern to central and western Germany and their replacement by Slav farm labor.
text_raw:
Finally,  their  social  influence  was  weakened  by  the  migration  of
German  farm  laborers  from  eastern  to  central  and  western  Germany  and  their
replacement  by  Slav  farm  labor.

text: This decrease in the power of the landlord group continued under the Third Reich and was intensified by the fact that this group was the one segment of the Quartet which vv as successfully coordinated.

This  decrease  in  the  power  of  the  landlord  group  continued  under  the  Third  Reich  and
was  intensified  by  the  fact  that  this  group  was  the  one  segment  of  the  Quartet  which  vv  as
successfully  coordinated.

text: The landlords lost most of their economic power because the control of their economic life was not left in the hands of the landlords as was done with industry.
text_raw:
The  landlords  lost  most  of  their  economic  power  because  the
control  of  their  economic  life  was  not  left  in  the  hands  of  the  landlords  as  was  done  with
industry.

text: In both cases economic life was controlled, chiefly by cartels and associations, but in industry these were controlled by industrialists, while in agriculture they were controlled by the state in close cooperation with the party.
text_raw:
In  both  cases  economic  life  was  controlled,  chiefly  by  cartels  and  associations,
but  in  industry  these  were  controlled  by  industrialists,  while  in  agriculture  they  were
controlled  by  the  state  in  close  cooperation  with  the  party.

text: Prices, production, conditions of sale, and, in fact, every detail about agriculture was in control of a government corporation called the Reichsnahrstand which consisted of a complex of groups, associations, and boards.
text_raw:
Prices,  production,  conditions  of  sale,  and,  in  fact,  every  detail  about  agriculture  was
in  control  of  a  government  corporation  called  the  Reichsnahrstand  which  consisted  of  a
complex  of  groups,  associations,  and  boards.

text: The leader of this complex was the minister of food and agriculture, named by Hitler.
text_raw:
The  leader  of  this  complex  was  the  minister
of  food  and  agriculture,  named  by  Hitler.

text: This leader appointed the subordinate leaders of all the member organizations of the Reichsnahrstand, and these, in turn, named their subordinates.
text_raw:
This  leader  appointed  the  subordinate  leaders  of
all  the  member  organizations  of  the  Reichsnahrstand,  and  these,  in  turn,  named  their
subordinates.

text: This process was continued down to the lowest individual, each leader naming his direct subordinates according to the "leadership principle." Every person engaged in any activity concerned with agriculture, food, or raw-material production, including lumber, fishing, dairying, and grazing belonged to one or several associations in the Reichsnahrstand.
text_raw:
This  process  was  continued  down  to  the  lowest  individual,  each  leader
naming  his  direct  subordinates  according  to  the  "leadership  principle."  Every  person
engaged  in  any  activity  concerned  with  agriculture,  food,  or  raw-material  production,
including  lumber,  fishing,  dairying,  and  grazing  belonged  to  one  or  several  associations
in  the  Reichsnahrstand.

text: The associations were organized both on a territorial and on a functional basis.
text_raw:
The  associations  were  organized  both  on  a  territorial  and  on  a
functional  basis.

text: On a functional basis they were organized in both vertical and horizontal associations.
text_raw:
On  a  functional  basis  they  were  organized  in  both  vertical  and  horizontal
associations.

text: On a territorial basis were twenty regional "peasant-ships" (Landesbauernschaften) subdivided into 515 local "peasant-ships" (Kreisbauernschaften).
text_raw:
On  a  territorial  basis  were  twenty  regional  "peasant-ships"
(Landesbauernschaften)  subdivided  into  515  local  "peasant-ships"  (Kreisbauernschaften).

text: On a horizontal basis were associations of persons in the same activity, such as grinding flour, churning butter, growing grain, and so on.
text_raw:
On  a  horizontal  basis  were  associations  of  persons  in  the  same  activity,  such  as  grinding
flour,  churning  butter,  growing  grain,  and  so  on.

text: On a vertical basis were associations of all persons concerned with the production and processing of any single commodity, such as grain or milk.
text_raw:
On  a  vertical  basis  were  associations  of
all  persons  concerned  with  the  production  and  processing  of  any  single  commodity,  such
as  grain  or  milk.

text: These organizations, all formed on the "leadership principle," were chiefly concerned with prices and production quotas.
text_raw:
These  organizations,  all  formed  on  the  "leadership  principle,"  were
chiefly  concerned  with  prices  and  production  quotas.

text: These were controlled by the state, but prices were set at a level sufficient to give a profit to most participants, and quotas were based on assessments estimated by the farmers themselves.
text_raw:
These  were  controlled  by  the  state,
but  prices  were  set  at  a  level  sufficient  to  give  a  profit  to  most  participants,  and  quotas
were  based  on  assessments  estimated  by  the  farmers  themselves.

text: While the landlords lost power in this way, they received economic advantages.
text_raw: While  the  landlords  lost  power  in  this  way,  they  received  economic  advantages.

text: As befitted a counterrevolutionary movement, the Nazis increased the wealth and privileges of the landlords.
text_raw:
As
befitted  a  counterrevolutionary  movement,  the  Nazis  increased  the  wealth  and  privileges
of  the  landlords.

The  report  on  the  Osthilfe  scandal,  which  had  been  made  for  Schleicher
in  1932,  was  permanently  suppressed.

text: The autarky program gave them a stable market for their products, shielding them from the vicissitudes which they had suffered under liberalism with its unstable markets and fluctuating prices.
text_raw:
The  autarky  program  gave  them  a  stable  market
for  their  products,  shielding  them  from  the  vicissitudes  which  they  had  suffered  under
liberalism  with  its  unstable  markets  and  fluctuating  prices.

text: The prices fixed under Nazism were not high but were adequate, especially in combination with other advantages.
text_raw:
The  prices  fixed  under  Nazism
were  not  high  but  were  adequate,  especially  in  combination  with  other  advantages.

text_raw:
By

below  those  of  1925.

text: Larger farms which used hired labor were aided by the prevention of unions, strikes, and rising wages.
text_raw:
Larger  farms  which  used  hired  labor  were  aided  by  the  prevention
of  unions,  strikes,  and  rising  wages.

text: Labor forces were increased by using the labor
text_raw: Labor  forces  were  increased  by  using  the  labor

Payments  for
interest  and  taxes  were  both  reduced,  the  former  from  950  million  marks  in  1929-1930  to

text_raw:
Farmers  were  exempt  completely  from  unemployment-insurance

text: The constant threat of breaking up the bankrupt great estates was removed whether it arose from the state or from private creditors.
text_raw:
The  constant  threat  of
breaking  up  the  bankrupt  great  estates  was  removed  whether  it  arose  from  the  state  or

All  farms  of  over  family  size  were  made  secure  in  possession  of

These  benefits  were  greater  for  larger  units  than  for  smaller  ones,  and  greatest  for  the

While  small  farms  (5  to  50  hectares),  according  to  Max  Sering,  made  a  net

In  1934  the  corresponding  figures  were  28  and  53,  a  gain  of  19  marks  per  hectare

text: As a result of this growth in profitability of large units, the concentration of ownership of land in Germany was increased, thus reversing a trend.

As  a  result  of  this  growth  in
profitability  of  large  units,  the  concentration  of  ownership  of  land  in  Germany  was

text: Both the number and the average size of large units increased.

Both  the  number  and  the  average  size  of  large  units

text: Thus the landlords won great privileges and rewards in the Third Reich, but at the cost of a drastic reduction in their power.
text_raw:
Thus  the  landlords  won  great  privileges  and  rewards  in  the  Third  Reich,  but  at  the  cost

text: They were coordinated, like the rest of society outside the ruling groups, with the result that they became the least important of these groups.

They  were  coordinated,  like  the  rest  of  society
outside  the  ruling  groups,  with  the  result  that  they  became  the  least  important  of  these
groups.

The  bureaucracy  was  not  completely  coordinated,  but  it  found  its  power  greatly

Outside  the  Ministry  of  Economics  the  chief  changes  were  the  ministers

The  newly  created  ministries,  of  course,  had  new

three  sessions  of  the  Commons  over  a  period  of  at  least  two  years.

text: The election of 1910 had so reduced Acquith's plurality that he became dependent on Irish and Labourite support, and, for the next four years, was of necessity compelled to grant both concessions for which he personally had little taste.
text_raw:
The  election  of  1910  had  so  reduced  Acquith's  plurality  that  he  became  dependent  on
Irish  and  Labourite  support,  and,  for  the  next  four  years,  was  of  necessity  compelled  to
grant  both  concessions  for  which  he  personally  had  little  taste.

text: In 1909 the Lords, again as a Supreme Court, declared the use of union funds in political campaigns to be illegal, thus destroying the political weapon to which Labour had been driven by the Taff Vale decision of 1902.
text_raw:
In  1909  the  Lords,  again
as  a  Supreme  Court,  declared  the  use  of  union  funds  in  political  campaigns  to  be  illegal,
thus  destroying  the  political  weapon  to  which  Labour  had  been  driven  by  the  Taff  Vale
decision  of  1902.

text: Asquith was not eager to overthrow this so-called "Osborne Judgement," at least for a while, for as long as union political activities were illegal the Labourite members of the Commons had to support Asquith in order to avoid a general election they could no longer finance.
text_raw:
Asquith  was  not  eager  to  overthrow  this  so-called  "Osborne
Judgement,"  at  least  for  a  while,  for  as  long  as  union  political  activities  were  illegal  the
Labourite  members  of  the  Commons  had  to  support  Asquith  in  order  to  avoid  a  general
election  they  could  no  longer  finance.

text: In order to permit the existing Labour members to live without union funds, the Asquith government in 1911 established payment for members of Parliament for the first time.
text_raw:
In  order  to  permit  the  existing  Labour  members  to
live  without  union  funds,  the  Asquith  government  in  1911  established  payment  for
members  of  Parliament  for  the  first  time.

text: Labour was also rewarded for its support of the Asquith government by the creation of Health and Unemployment Insurance in 191 1, by a Minimum Wage Law in 1912, and by a Trades-Union Act in 1913.
text_raw:
Labour  was  also  rewarded  for  its  support  of  the
Asquith  government  by  the  creation  of  Health  and  Unemployment  Insurance  in  191 1,  by
a  Minimum  Wage  Law  in  1912,  and  by  a  Trades-Union  Act  in  1913.

text: This last item made it legal for labor organizations to finance political activities after approval by a majority of their members and from a special fund to be raised from those union members who did not ask to be exempt.
text_raw:
This  last  item  made
it  legal  for  labor  organizations  to  finance  political  activities  after  approval  by  a  majority
of  their  members  and  from  a  special  fund  to  be  raised  from  those  union  members  who  did
not  ask  to  be  exempt.

text: Assaulted by the supporters of women suffrage, dependent on the votes of Labour and the Irish Nationalists, and under steady pressure from Nonconformist Liberals, the Asquith government had an unpleasant period from 1912- to 1915.
text_raw:
Assaulted  by  the  supporters  of  women  suffrage,  dependent  on  the  votes  of  Labour  and
the  Irish  Nationalists,  and  under  steady  pressure  from  Nonconformist  Liberals,  the
Asquith  government  had  an  unpleasant  period  from  1912- to  1915.

text: The unpleasantness
text_raw: The  unpleasantness

text: culminated in violent controversies over Irish Home Rule and Welsh Disestablishment.
text_raw: culminated  in  violent  controversies  over  Irish  Home  Rule  and  Welsh  Disestablishment.

text: Both bills were finally jammed through without the acceptance of the Lords in September 1914, in both cases with provisions which suspended their application until the end of the war with Germany.
text_raw:
Both  bills  were  finally  jammed  through  without  the  acceptance  of  the  Lords  in  September
1914,  in  both  cases  with  provisions  which  suspended  their  application  until  the  end  of  the
war  with  Germany.

text: Thus the weakness and divisions of the Asquith government and the alarming divisions in Britain itself were swallowed up in the greater problems of waging a modern war of unlimited resources.
text_raw:
Thus  the  weakness  and  divisions  of  the  Asquith  government  and  the
alarming  divisions  in  Britain  itself  were  swallowed  up  in  the  greater  problems  of  waging
a  modern  war  of  unlimited  resources.

text: The problem of waging this war was given eventually to coalition governments, at first (1915-1916) under Asquith and later (1916-1922) under the more vigorous direction of David Lloyd George.
text_raw:
The  problem  of  waging  this  war  was  given  eventually  to  coalition  governments,  at
first  (1915-1916)  under  Asquith  and  later  (1916-1922)  under  the  more  vigorous  direction
of  David  Lloyd  George.

text: The latter coalition was returned to power in the "Khaki Election" of December 1918, on a program promising punishment of German "war criminals," full payment by the defeated powers of the costs of the war, and "homes fit for heroes." Although the Coalition government w as made up of Conservatives, Liberals, and Labour, with an ex-Liberal as prime minister, the Conservatives had a majority of seats in Parliament and were in closest contact with Lloyd George so that the coalition government was, except in name, a Conservative government.
text_raw:
The  latter  coalition  was  returned  to  power  in  the  "Khaki
Election"  of  December  1918,  on  a  program  promising  punishment  of  German  "war
criminals,"  full  payment  by  the  defeated  powers  of  the  costs  of  the  war,  and  "homes  fit
for  heroes."  Although  the  Coalition  government  w  as  made  up  of  Conservatives,  Liberals,
and  Labour,  with  an  ex-Liberal  as  prime  minister,  the  Conservatives  had  a  majority  of
seats  in  Parliament  and  were  in  closest  contact  with  Lloyd  George  so  that  the  coalition
government  was,  except  in  name,  a  Conservative  government.

text: The political history of Britain in the years between 1918 and 1945 is a depressing one, chiefly because of Conservative errors in domestic economic policy and in foreign policy.
text_raw:
The  political  history  of  Britain  in  the  years  between  1918  and  1945  is  a  depressing
one,  chiefly  because  of  Conservative  errors  in  domestic  economic  policy  and  in  foreign
policy.

text: In this period there were seven general elections (1918, 1922, 1923, 1924, 1929, 1931, 1935).
text_raw:
In  this  period  there  were  seven  general  elections  (1918,  1922,  1923,  1924,  1929,
1931,  1935).

text: In only one (1931) did a party receive a majority of the popular vote, but in four the Conservatives obtained a majority of seats in the House of Commons.

In  only  one  (1931)  did  a  party  receive  a  majority  of  the  popular  vote,  but  in
four  the  Conservatives  obtained  a  majority  of  seats  in  the  House  of  Commons.

text: On the basis of these elections Britain had ten governments in the period 1918-1945.
text_raw:
On  the
basis  of  these  elections  Britain  had  ten  governments  in  the  period  1918-1945.

his  own  supporters  and  his  own  political  funds  and  feuds.

text_raw:
Although  technically  a  Liberal,
Lloyd  George  had  split  his  own  party,  so  that  Asquith  was  in  opposition  along  with  the
Labour  party  and  about  an  equal  number  of  Conservatives.

Since  the  80  Irish  Nationalists
and  Irish  Republicans  did  not  take  their  seats,  the  334  Conservatives  in  the  coalition  had  a
majority  of  the  Commons,  but  allowed  Lloyd  George  to  take  the  responsibility  for

text: They waited four years before throwing him out.
text_raw: They  waited  four  years  before  throwing  him  out.

text: During this time domestic affairs were in a turmoil, and foreign affairs were not much better.
text_raw:
During
this  time  domestic  affairs  were  in  a  turmoil,  and  foreign  affairs  were  not  much  better.

text: In the former, the effort to deflate prices in order to go back on the gold standard at the prewar parity was fatal to prosperity and domestic order.
text_raw:
In
the  former,  the  effort  to  deflate  prices  in  order  to  go  back  on  the  gold  standard  at  the
prewar  parity  was  fatal  to  prosperity  and  domestic  order.

text: Unemployment and strikes increased, especially in the coal mines.
text_raw:
Unemployment  and  strikes
increased,  especially  in  the  coal  mines.

text: The Conservatives prevented any realistic attack on these problems, and passed the Emergency Powers Act of 1920, which, for the first time in English history, gave a peacetime government the right to proclaim a state of siege (as was done in 1920, 1921, and 1926).
text_raw:
The  Conservatives  prevented  any  realistic  attack  on  these  problems,  and  passed  the
Emergency  Powers  Act  of  1920,  which,  for  the  first  time  in  English  history,  gave  a
peacetime  government  the  right  to  proclaim  a  state  of  siege  (as  was  done  in  1920,  1921,
and  1926).

text: Unemployment was dealt with by establishment of a "dole," that is, a payment of 20 shillings a week to those unable to find work.
text_raw:
Unemployment  was  dealt  with  by  establishment  of  a  "dole,"  that  is,  a  payment
of  20  shillings  a  week  to  those  unable  to  find  work.

text: The wave of strikes was dealt with by minor concessions, by vague promises, by dilatory investigations, and by playing one group off against another.
text_raw:
The  wave  of  strikes  was  dealt  with  by
minor  concessions,  by  vague  promises,  by  dilatory  investigations,  and  by  playing  one
group  off  against  another.

text: The revolt in Ireland was met by a program of strict repression at the hands of a new militarized police known as "Black and Tans." The protectorate over Egypt was ended in 1922, and a reexamination of imperial relations was made necessary by the refusal of the Dominions to support the United Kingdom in the Near East crisis arising from Lloyd George's opposition to Kemal Atatiirk.
text_raw:
The  revolt  in  Ireland  was  met  by  a  program  of  strict  repression
at  the  hands  of  a  new  militarized  police  known  as  "Black  and  Tans."  The  protectorate
over  Egypt  was  ended  in  1922,  and  a  reexamination  of  imperial  relations  was  made
necessary  by  the  refusal  of  the  Dominions  to  support  the  United  Kingdom  in  the  Near
East  crisis  arising  from  Lloyd  George's  opposition  to  Kemal  Atatiirk.

text: On October 23, 1923, the Conservatives overthrew Lloyd George and set up their own government under Bonar Law.
text_raw:
On  October  23,  1923,  the  Conservatives  overthrew  Lloyd  George  and  set  up  their  own
government  under  Bonar  Law.

text: In the following General Election they obtained 344 of 615 seats, and were able to continue in office.
text_raw:
In  the  following  General  Election  they  obtained  344  of
615  seats,  and  were  able  to  continue  in  office.

text: This Conservative government lasted only fifteen months under Bonar Law and Stanley Baldwin.
text_raw:
This  Conservative  government  lasted  only
fifteen  months  under  Bonar  Law  and  Stanley  Baldwin.

text: In domestic affairs its chief activities were piecemeal action on unemployment and talk about a protective tariff.
text_raw:
In  domestic  affairs  its  chief
activities  were  piecemeal  action  on  unemployment  and  talk  about  a  protective  tariff.

text: On this last issue Baldwin called a General Election in December 1923 and lost his majority, although continuing to have the largest block in Commons, 258 seats to Labour's 191 and the Liberals' 159.
text_raw:
On
this  last  issue  Baldwin  called  a  General  Election  in  December  1923  and  lost  his  majority,
although  continuing  to  have  the  largest  block  in  Commons,  258  seats  to  Labour's  191  and
the  Liberals'  159.

text: Asquith, who held the balance of power, could have thrown his support either way, and decided to throw it to Labour, hoping to give Labour a "fair chance." Thus the first Labour government in history came to office, if not to power.
text_raw:
Asquith,  who  held  the  balance  of  power,  could  have  thrown  his  support
either  way,  and  decided  to  throw  it  to  Labour,  hoping  to  give  Labour  a  "fair  chance."
Thus  the  first  Labour  government  in  history  came  to  office,  if  not  to  power.

text: With an unfriendly House of Lords, an almost completely inexperienced Cabinet, a minority government, a large majority of its members in Commons trade unionists with no parliamentary experience, and a Liberal veto over any effort to carry out a Socialist or even a Labourite program, little could be expected from MacDonald's first government.
text_raw:
With  an  unfriendly  House  of  Lords,  an  almost  completely  inexperienced  Cabinet,  a
minority  government,  a  large  majority  of  its  members  in  Commons  trade  unionists  with
no  parliamentary  experience,  and  a  Liberal  veto  over  any  effort  to  carry  out  a  Socialist  or
even  a  Labourite  program,  little  could  be  expected  from  MacDonald's  first  government.

text: Little was accomplished, nothing of permanent importance at least, and within three months the prime minister was looking about for an excuse to resign.
text_raw:
Little  was  accomplished,  nothing  of  permanent  importance  at  least,  and  within  three
months  the  prime  minister  was  looking  about  for  an  excuse  to  resign.

continued  the  practice  of  piecemeal  solutions  for  unemployment,  began  public  subsidies
for  housing,  lowered  the  taxes  on  necessities  (sugar,  tea,  coffee,  cocoa),  abolished  the

corporation  tax  and  the  wartime  duties  of  33  1/3  percent  on  motorcars,  watches,  clocks,

text: The chief political issue of the day, however, was Communism.
text_raw: The  chief  political  issue  of  the  day,  however,  was  Communism.

text: This rose to a fever heat when MacDonald recognized Soviet Russia and tried to make a commercial treaty with the same country.

This  rose  to  a  fever
heat  when  MacDonald  recognized  Soviet  Russia  and  tried  to  make  a  commercial  treaty
with  the  same  country.

MacDonald  cooperated  with  the  Liberals  with  ill-grace  and
resigned  when  Parliament  decided  to  investigate  the  quashing  of  the  prosecution,  under

text: In the resulting general election the Conservatives played the "red scare" for all it was worth.

In  the  resulting
general  election  the  Conservatives  played  the  "red  scare"  for  all  it  was  worth.

text: They were aided greatly when the permanent officials of the Foreign Office issued, four days before the election, the so-called "Zinoviev Letter." This forged document called upon British subjects to support a violent revolution in behalf of the Third International.

They  were
aided  greatly  when  the  permanent  officials  of  the  Foreign  Office  issued,  four  days  before
the  election,  the  so-called  "Zinoviev  Letter."  This  forged  document  called  upon  British
subjects  to  support  a  violent  revolution  in  behalf  of  the  Third  International.

text: It undoubtedly played some role in gaining the Conservatives their largest majority in many years, 412 out of 615 seats.
text_raw:
It
undoubtedly  played  some  role  in  gaining  the  Conservatives  their  largest  majority  in  many
years,  412  out  of  615  seats.

text: Thus began a Conservative government which was in office under Baldwin for five years.

Thus  began  a  Conservative  government  which  was  in  office  under  Baldwin  for  five

text: Winston Churchill as chancellor of the Exchequer carried out the stabilization policy which put England on the gold standard with the pound sterling at the prewar rate of parity.

text: As we have indicated in Chapter 7, this policy of deflation drove Britain into an economic depression and a period of labor conflict, and the policy was so bungled in its execution that Britain was doomed to semi-depression for almost a decade, was in financial subjection to France until September 1931, and was driven closer to domestic rebellion than she had been at any time since the Chartist movement of 1848.
text_raw:
As  we  have  indicated  in  Chapter  7,  this  policy  of  deflation  drove  Britain  into  an
economic  depression  and  a  period  of  labor  conflict,  and  the  policy  was  so  bungled  in  its
execution  that  Britain  was  doomed  to  semi-depression  for  almost  a  decade,  was  in
financial  subjection  to  France  until  September  1931,  and  was  driven  closer  to  domestic
rebellion  than  she  had  been  at  any  time  since  the  Chartist  movement  of  1848.

text: The recognition of Russia and the trade agreement with Russia were abrogated; the import duties were restored; and the income tax was lowered (although the inheritance tax was raised).

The

text: The, General Strike developed from a strike in the coal mines and from the determination of both sides to bring the class struggle to a showdown.

The,  General  Strike  developed  from  a  strike  in  the  coal  mines  and  from  the

The  British  mines
were  in  bad  condition  because  of  the  nature  of  the  coal  deposits  and  because  of
mismanagement  which  left  them  with  inadequate  and  obsolete  technological  equipment.

text: The deflation resulting from the effort to stabilize the pound hit the mines with special impact, since prices could be cut only if costs were cut first, an action which meant, for the mines above all, cutting of wages.

The  deflation  resulting  from  the  effort  to  stabilize  the  pound  hit  the
mines  with  special  impact,  since  prices  could  be  cut  only  if  costs  were  cut  first,  an  action

text: The loss of the export trade resulting from Germany's efforts to pay reparations in coal, and especially the return of the Ruhr mines to full production after the French evacuation of that area in 1924 made the mines the natural focal point for labor troubles in England.

The  loss  of  the  export  trade
resulting  from  Germany's  efforts  to  pay  reparations  in  coal,  and  especially  the  return  of
the  Ruhr  mines  to  full  production  after  the  French  evacuation  of  that  area  in  1924  made

After  that  conflict
ended,  many  Liberals,  Labourites,  and  the  miners  themselves  wanted  nationalization.

This  attitude  was  reflected  in  the  report  of  a  royal  commission  under  Lord  Sankey  which

text: demanded longer hours and reduced wages.

The  miners  refused,  went  out  on  strike  for
three  months  (March- June  1921),  and  won  a  promise  of  a  government  subsidy  to  raise

In  1925,  as  a  result  of  stabilization,  the  owners

Because  the  miners  objected,  the  government  appointed  a  new

all  willing  to  force  a  showdown,  the  affair  drifted  into  a  crisis  when  the  government

text: German Bankers Consolidate Control of Industrial Corporations
text_raw: German  Bankers  Consolidate  Control  of  Industrial  Corporations

text: These excesses of financial capitalist promotion led to a governmental investigation which resulted in a strict law regulating promotion in 1883.

These  excesses  of  financial  capitalist  promotion  led  to  a  governmental  investigation
which  resulted  in  a  strict  law  regulating  promotion  in  1883.

text: This law made it impossible for German bankers to make fortunes out of promotion and made it necessary for them to seek the same ends by consolidating their control of industrial corporations on a long- term basis.
text_raw:
This  law  made  it  impossible
for  German  bankers  to  make  fortunes  out  of  promotion  and  made  it  necessary  for  them  to
seek  the  same  ends  by  consolidating  their  control  of  industrial  corporations  on  a  long-
term  basis.

text: This was quite different from the United States, where the absence of any legal regulation of promotion previous to the SEC Act of 1933 made it more likely that investment bankers would seek to make short-term "killings" from promotions rather than long-term gains from the control of industrial companies.

This  was  quite  different  from  the  United  States,  where  the  absence  of  any
legal  regulation  of  promotion  previous  to  the  SEC  Act  of  1933  made  it  more  likely  that
investment  bankers  would  seek  to  make  short-term  "killings"  from  promotions  rather
than  long-term  gains  from  the  control  of  industrial  companies.

text: Another result is to be seen in the relatively sounder financing of German corporations through equity capital rather than through the more burdensome (but promoter-favored) method of fixed interest bonds.

seen  in  the  relatively  sounder  financing  of  German  corporations  through  equity  capital

text: The financial capitalism of Germany was at its peak in the years just before 1914.
text_raw: The  financial  capitalism  of  Germany  was  at  its  peak  in  the  years  just  before  1914.

text: It was controlled by a highly centralized oligarchy.
text_raw:
It
was  controlled  by  a  highly  centralized  oligarchy.

text: At the center was the Reichsbank whose control over the other banks was relatively weak at all times.
text_raw:
At  the  center  was  the  Reichsbank  whose
control  over  the  other  banks  was  relatively  weak  at  all  times.

text: This was welcomed by the financial oligarchy, for the Reichsbank, although privately owned, was controlled by the government to a considerable degree.
text_raw:
This  was  welcomed  by  the
financial  oligarchy,  for  the  Reichsbank,  although  privately  owned,  was  controlled  by  the
government  to  a  considerable  degree.

text: The weakness of the Reichsbank's influence over the banking system arose from the weakness of its influence over the two usual instruments of central-banking control â€” the re-discount rate and open-market operations.
text_raw:
The  weakness  of  the  Reichsbank's  influence  over
the  banking  system  arose  from  the  weakness  of  its  influence  over  the  two  usual
instruments  of  central-banking  control â€” the  re-discount  rate  and  open-market  operations.

text: The weakness of the former was based on the fact that the other banks rarely came to the Reichsbank for re-discounts, and usually had a discount rate below that of the Reichsbank.
text_raw:
The  weakness  of  the  former  was  based  on  the  fact  that  the  other  banks  rarely  came  to  the
Reichsbank  for  re-discounts,  and  usually  had  a  discount  rate  below  that  of  the
Reichsbank.

text: A law of 1899 tried to overcome this weakness by forcing the other banks to adjust their discount rates to that of the Reichsbank, but it was never a very effective instrument of control.
text_raw:
A  law  of  1899  tried  to  overcome  this  weakness  by  forcing  the  other  banks  to
adjust  their  discount  rates  to  that  of  the  Reichsbank,  but  it  was  never  a  very  effective
instrument  of  control.

text: Open-market control was also weak because of an official German reluctance "to speculate" in government securities and because the other banks were more responsive to the condition of their portfolios of commercial paper and securities than they were to the size of their gold reserves.

Open-market  control  was  also  weak  because  of  an  official  German
reluctance  "to  speculate"  in  government  securities  and  because  the  other  banks  were  more

In  this  they  were  like  French  rather  than
British  banks.

text_raw: The  Greatest  Bankers  Had  Intimate  Connections  with  Governments

text_raw: Private  Proprietorships  and  Partnerships

corporation  form  of  business  organization  grew  very  slowly  (although  it  was  permitted  by

text_raw: Clash  Between  Two  Economic  Blocs

text: Thus, the struggle between financial capitalism and monopoly capitalism which appeared in most countries was replaced in France by a clash between two economic blocs, both of which were interested in both industry and banking and neither of which was prepared to accept the unorthodox banking procedures which become one of the chief goals of monopoly capitalism.
text_raw:
Thus,  the  struggle  between
financial  capitalism  and  monopoly  capitalism  which  appeared  in  most  countries  was
replaced  in  France  by  a  clash  between  two  economic  blocs,  both  of  which  were  interested
in  both  industry  and  banking  and  neither  of  which  was  prepared  to  accept  the  unorthodox
banking  procedures  which  become  one  of  the  chief  goals  of  monopoly  capitalism.

text: As a result, monopoly capitalism appeared late in France and, when it did, arose between the two great blocs, with ramifications in both, but largely autonomous from the central control of either.
text_raw:

text_raw: The  Center  of  the  Monopolistic  Industrial  Controls

The  Confederation  was  divided  into  sections  for

Rising  Standards  of  Living

text: A rise in the general or average standard of living in modern times is obvious and, with intermittent breaks, goes back for a thousand years.
text_raw:
A  rise  in  the  general  or  average  standard  of  living  in  modern  times  is  obvious
and,  with  intermittent  breaks,  goes  back  for  a  thousand  years.

text: Such progress is welcome, but it obviously brings with it certain accompanying factors which must be understood and accepted.
text_raw:
Such  progress  is  welcome,
but  it  obviously  brings  with  it  certain  accompanying  factors  which  must  be  understood
and  accepted.

text: A rising standard of living, except in its earliest stages, does not involve any increase in consumption of necessities but instead involves an increase in the consumption of luxuries even to the point of replacing basic necessities by luxuries.
text_raw:
A  rising  standard  of  living,  except  in  its  earliest  stages,  does  not  involve
any  increase  in  consumption  of  necessities  but  instead  involves  an  increase  in  the
consumption  of  luxuries  even  to  the  point  of  replacing  basic  necessities  by  luxuries.

text: As average incomes rise, people do not, after a certain level, eat more and more black bread, potatoes, and cabbage, or wear more and more clothing.
text_raw:
As
average  incomes  rise,  people  do  not,  after  a  certain  level,  eat  more  and  more  black  bread,
potatoes,  and  cabbage,  or  wear  more  and  more  clothing.

text: Instead, they replace black bread with wheaten bread and add meat to their diet and replace coarse clothing by finer apparel; they shift their emphasis from energy foods to protective foods.
text_raw:
Instead,  they  replace  black  bread
with  wheaten  bread  and  add  meat  to  their  diet  and  replace  coarse  clothing  by  finer
apparel;  they  shift  their  emphasis  from  energy  foods  to  protective  foods.

text: This process can be continued indefinitely.
text_raw: This  process  can  be  continued  indefinitely.

text: A number of students have divided goods from this point of view into three levels:
text_raw:
A  number  of  students  have  divided
goods  from  this  point  of  view  into  three  levels:

text: (a) necessities, (b) industrial products, and (c) luxuries and services.
text_raw:
(a)  necessities,  (b)  industrial  products,  and
(c)  luxuries  and  services.

text: The first would include food and clothing; the second would include railroads, automobiles, and radios; the third would include movies, books, amusements, yachts, leisure, music, philosophy, and so on.
text_raw:
The  first  would  include  food  and  clothing;  the  second  would
include  railroads,  automobiles,  and  radios;  the  third  would  include  movies,  books,
amusements,  yachts,  leisure,  music,  philosophy,  and  so  on.

text: Naturally, the dividing lines between the three groups are very vague, and the position of any particular item will vary from society to society and even from person to person.
text_raw:
Naturally,  the  dividing  lines
between  the  three  groups  are  very  vague,  and  the  position  of  any  particular  item  will  vary
from  society  to  society  and  even  from  person  to  person.

text: As standards of living rise, decreasing proportions of attention and resources are devoted to primary or secondary types of products, and increasing proportions to secondary and tertiary types of products.
text_raw:
As  standards  of  living  rise,  decreasing  proportions  of  attention  and  resources  are
devoted  to  primary  or  secondary  types  of  products,  and  increasing  proportions  to
secondary  and  tertiary  types  of  products.

text: This has very important economic consequences.
text_raw:
This  has  very  important  economic
consequences.

text: It means that luxuries tend to become relatively more important than necessities.
text_raw:
It  means  that  luxuries  tend  to  become  relatively  more  important  than
necessities.

text: It also means that attention is constantly being shifted from products for which the demand is relatively inelastic to products for which the demand is relatively elastic (that is, expansible).
text_raw:
It  also  means  that  attention  is  constantly  being  shifted  from  products  for
which  the  demand  is  relatively  inelastic  to  products  for  which  the  demand  is  relatively
elastic  (that  is,  expansible).

text: There are exceptions to this.
text_raw: There  are  exceptions  to  this.

text: For example, housing, which is obviously a necessity, is a product for which demand is fairly elastic and might continue to be so until most persons lived in palaces, but, on the whole, the demand for necessities is less elastic than the demand for luxuries.
text_raw:
For  example,  housing,  which  is
obviously  a  necessity,  is  a  product  for  which  demand  is  fairly  elastic  and  might  continue
to  be  so  until  most  persons  lived  in  palaces,  but,  on  the  whole,  the  demand  for  necessities
is  less  elastic  than  the  demand  for  luxuries.

text: A rising standard of living also means an increase in savings (or accumulation of surplus) out of all proportion to the rise in incomes.
text_raw:
A  rising  standard  of  living  also  means  an  increase  in  savings  (or  accumulation  of
surplus)  out  of  all  proportion  to  the  rise  in  incomes.

text: It is a fairly general rule both for societies and for individuals that savings go up faster than incomes as the latter rise, if for no other reason than the fact that a person with an adequate supply of necessities will take time to make up his mind on which luxuries he will expend any increase in income.

It  is  a  fairly  general  rule  both  for
societies  and  for  individuals  that  savings  go  up  faster  than  incomes  as  the  latter  rise,  if  for

text: As a result of this increase in the use of energy per capita, industrial output per man-hour rose significantly (in the United States 96 percent from 1899 to 1929).
