text: The Industrial Revolution did not reach all parts of Europe, or even all parts of any single country, at the same moment.
text_raw:
The  Industrial  Revolution  did  not  reach  all  parts  of  Europe,  or  even  all  parts  of  any
single  country,  at  the  same  moment.

text: In general, it began in England late in the eighteenth century (about 1776) and spread slowly eastward and southward across Europe, reaching France after 1830, Germany after 1850, Italy and Russia after 1890.
text_raw:
In  general,  it  began  in  England  late  in  the  eighteenth
century  (about  1776)  and  spread  slowly  eastward  and  southward  across  Europe,  reaching
France  after  1830,  Germany  after  1850,  Italy  and  Russia  after  1890.

text: This eastward movement of industrialism had many significant results, among them the belief on the part of the newer countries that they were at a disadvantage in comparison with England because of the latter's head start.
text_raw:
This  eastward
movement  of  industrialism  had  many  significant  results,  among  them  the  belief  on  the
part  of  the  newer  countries  that  they  were  at  a  disadvantage  in  comparison  with  England
because  of  the  latter's  head  start.

text: This was untrue, for, from a strictly temporal point of view, these newer countries had an advantage over England, since their newer industrial installations were less obsolescent and less hampered by vested interests.
text_raw:
This  was  untrue,  for,  from  a  strictly  temporal  point  of
view,  these  newer  countries  had  an  advantage  over  England,  since  their  newer  industrial
installations  were  less  obsolescent  and  less  hampered  by  vested  interests.

text: Whatever advantage England had arose from better natural resources, more plentiful supply of capital, and skilled labor.
text_raw:
Whatever
advantage  England  had  arose  from  better  natural  resources,  more  plentiful  supply  of
capital,  and  skilled  labor.

text: Growth of Size of Enterprises
text_raw: Growth  of  Size  of  Enterprises

text: The growth of size of enterprise was a natural result of the process of industrialism.
text_raw:
The  growth  of  size  of  enterprise  was  a  natural  result  of  the  process  of
industrialism.

text: This process required very considerable outlays for fixed capital, especially in the activities most closely associated with the early stages of industrialism, such as railroads, iron foundries, and textile mills.
text_raw:
This  process  required  very  considerable  outlays  for  fixed  capital,  especially
in  the  activities  most  closely  associated  with  the  early  stages  of  industrialism,  such  as
railroads,  iron  foundries,  and  textile  mills.

text: Such great outlays required a new legal structure for enterprise.
text_raw:
Such  great  outlays  required  a  new  legal
structure  for  enterprise.

text: This was found in the corporation or limited-liability joint-stock company.
text_raw:
This  was  found  in  the  corporation  or  limited-liability  joint-stock
company.

text: In this company large capital installations could be constructed and run, with ownership divided into small fractions among a large number of persons.
text_raw:
In  this  company  large  capital  installations  could  be  constructed  and  run,  with
ownership  divided  into  small  fractions  among  a  large  number  of  persons.

text: This increase in size of units was apparent in all countries, but chiefly in the United States, Britain, and Germany.
text_raw:
This  increase  in  size  of  units  was  apparent  in  all  countries,  but  chiefly  in  the  United
States,  Britain,  and  Germany.

text: The statistics on this are incomplete and tricky to use, but, in general, they indicate that, while the number of corporations has been increasing, and the average size of all corporations has been falling, the absolute size of the largest corporations has been increasing rapidly in the twentieth century, and the share of total assets or of total output held h! the largest corporations has been rising.
text_raw:
The  statistics  on  this  are  incomplete  and  tricky  to  use,  but,
in  general,  they  indicate  that,  while  the  number  of  corporations  has  been  increasing,  and
the  average  size  of  all  corporations  has  been  falling,  the  absolute  size  of  the  largest
corporations  has  been  increasing  rapidly  in  the  twentieth  century,  and  the  share  of  total
assets  or  of  total  output  held  h!  the  largest  corporations  has  been  rising.

text: As a result, the output of certain products, notably chemicals, metals, artificial fibers, electrical equipment, and so on, has been dominated in most countries by a few great firms.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  the
output  of  certain  products,  notably  chemicals,  metals,  artificial  fibers,  electrical
equipment,  and  so  on,  has  been  dominated  in  most  countries  by  a  few  great  firms.

text: In the United States, where this process has been studied most carefully, it was found that from 1909 to 1930 the number of billion-dollar corporations rose from 1 to 15, and the share of all corporation assets held by the 200 largest rose from 32 percent to over 49 percent.
text_raw:
In  the  United  States,  where  this  process  has  been  studied  most  carefully,  it  was
found  that  from  1909  to  1930  the  number  of  billion-dollar  corporations  rose  from  1  to  15,
and  the  share  of  all  corporation  assets  held  by  the  200  largest  rose  from  32  percent  to
over  49  percent.

text: By 1939 this figure reached 57 percent.
text_raw: By  1939  this  figure  reached  57  percent.

text: This meant that the largest 200 corporations were growing faster than other corporations (5.4 percent a year compared to 2.0 percent a year) and faster than total national wealth.
text_raw:
This  meant  that  the  largest  200
corporations  were  growing  faster  than  other  corporations  (5.4  percent  a  year  compared  to
2.0  percent  a  year)  and  faster  than  total  national  wealth.

text: As a result, by 1930 these 200 largest corporations had 49.2 percent of all corporate assets (or $81 billion out of $165 billion); they had 38 percent of all business wealth (or $81 billion out of $212 billion); they held 22 percent of all wealth in the country (or $81 billion out of $367 billion).
text_raw:
As  a  result,  by  1930  these  200
largest  corporations  had  49.2  percent  of  all  corporate  assets  (or  $81  billion  out  of  $165
billion);  they  had  38  percent  of  all  business  wealth  (or  $81  billion  out  of  $212  billion);
they  held  22  percent  of  all  wealth  in  the  country  (or  $81  billion  out  of  $367  billion).

text: In fact in 1930, a single corporation (American Telephone and Telegraph) had greater assets than the total wealth in 21 states.
text_raw:
In
fact  in  1930,  a  single  corporation  (American  Telephone  and  Telegraph)  had  greater  assets
than  the  total  wealth  in  21  states.

text: No such figures are available for European countries, but there can be no doubt that similar growth was taking place in most of them during this period.

No  such  figures  are  available  for  European  countries,

text: Dispersal of Ownership of Enterprises
text_raw: Dispersal  of  Ownership  of  Enterprises

text: Dispersal of ownership of enterprise was a natural result of the growth of size of enterprise, and was made possible by the corporate method of organization.
text_raw:
Dispersal  of  ownership  of  enterprise  was  a  natural  result  of  the  growth  of  size  of
enterprise,  and  was  made  possible  by  the  corporate  method  of  organization.

text: As corporations increased in size, it became less and less possible for any individual or small group to own any important fractions of their stocks.
text_raw:
As
corporations  increased  in  size,  it  became  less  and  less  possible  for  any  individual  or  small
group  to  own  any  important  fractions  of  their  stocks.

text: [An individual or family can maintain control of a corporation by holding as little as 5-10 percent of the stock.] In most countries the number of security holders increased faster than the number of outstanding securities.
text_raw:
[An  individual  or  family  can
maintain  control  of  a  corporation  by  holding  as  little  as  5-10  percent  of  the  stock.]  In
most  countries  the  number  of  security  holders  increased  faster  than  the  number  of

text: In the United States the former increased in numbers seven times as fast as the latter from 1900 to 1928.
text_raw:
In  the  United  States  the  former  increased  in  numbers  seven  times
as  fast  as  the  latter  from  1900  to  1928.

text: This was a greater spread than in other countries, but elsewhere there was also a considerable spreading out of corporate ownership.
text_raw:
This  was  a  greater  spread  than  in  other  countries,
but  elsewhere  there  was  also  a  considerable  spreading  out  of  corporate  ownership.

text: This was exactly contrary to the prediction of Karl Marx that the owners of industry would get fewer and fewer as well as richer and richer.
text_raw:
This
was  exactly  contrary  to  the  prediction  of  Karl  Marx  that  the  owners  of  industry  would  get
fewer  and  fewer  as  well  as  richer  and  richer.

text: Separation of Control from Ownership
text_raw: Separation  of  Control  from  Ownership

text: The separation of ownership from control has already been mentioned.
text_raw: The  separation  of  ownership  from  control  has  already  been  mentioned.

text: It was an inevitable counterpart of the advent of the corporate form of business organization; indeed, the corporate form was devised for this very purpose â€” that is, to mobilize the capital owned by many persons into a single enterprise controlled by a few.
text_raw:
It  was  an
inevitable  counterpart  of  the  advent  of  the  corporate  form  of  business  organization;
indeed,  the  corporate  form  was  devised  for  this  very  purpose â€” that  is,  to  mobilize  the
capital  owned  by  many  persons  into  a  single  enterprise  controlled  by  a  few.

text: As we have seen, this inevitable counterpart was carried to a quite unexpected degree by the devices invented by financial capitalism.
text_raw:
As  we  have
seen,  this  inevitable  counterpart  was  carried  to  a  quite  unexpected  degree  by  the  devices

text: Decline of Competition
text_raw: Decline  of  Competition

text: A decline in competition is a natural consequence of the concentration of control.
text_raw:
A  decline  in  competition  is  a  natural  consequence  of  the  concentration  of
control.

text: This decline in competition refers, of course, only to price competition in the market, since this was the mechanism which made the economic system function in the nineteenth century.
text_raw:
This  decline  in  competition  refers,  of  course,  only  to  price  competition  in  the
market,  since  this  was  the  mechanism  which  made  the  economic  system  function  in  the
nineteenth  century.

text: This decline is evident to all students of modern economics, and is one of the most widely discussed aspects of the modern economic system.
text_raw:
This  decline  is  evident  to  all  students  of  modern  economics,  and  is
one  of  the  most  widely  discussed  aspects  of  the  modern  economic  system.

text: It is caused not only by the activities of businessmen but also by the actions of labor unions, of governments, of private social welfare organizations, and even of the herd-like behavior of consumers themselves.
text_raw:
It  is  caused  not
only  by  the  activities  of  businessmen  but  also  by  the  actions  of  labor  unions,  of
governments,  of  private  social  welfare  organizations,  and  even  of  the  herd-like  behavior
of  consumers  themselves.

text: Increasing Disparity in the Distribution of Incomes
text_raw: Increasing  Disparity  in  the  Distribution  of  Incomes

text: The increasing disparity in the distribution of income is the most controversial and least well-established characteristic of the system.
text_raw:
The  increasing  disparity  in  the  distribution  of  income  is  the  most  controversial
and  least  well-established  characteristic  of  the  system.

text: The available statistical evidence is so inadequate in all European countries that the characteristic itself cannot be proved
text_raw:
The  available  statistical  evidence
is  so  inadequate  in  all  European  countries  that  the  characteristic  itself  cannot  be  proved

text: conclusively.
text_raw: conclusively.

text: An extensive study of the subject, using the available materials for both Europe and the United States, with a careful analysis of the much better American materials, will permit the following tentative conclusions.
text_raw:
An  extensive  study  of  the  subject,  using  the  available  materials  for  both
Europe  and  the  United  States,  with  a  careful  analysis  of  the  much  better  American
materials,  will  permit  the  following  tentative  conclusions.

text: Leaving aside all government action, it would appear that the disparity in the distribution of the national income has been getting wider.
text_raw:
Leaving  aside  all  government
action,  it  would  appear  that  the  disparity  in  the  distribution  of  the  national  income  has
been  getting  wider.

text: In the United States, for example, according to the National Industrial Conference Board, the richest one-fifth of the population received 46.2 percent of the national income in 1910, 51.3 percent in 1929, and 48.5 percent in 1937.
text_raw:
In  the  United  States,  for  example,  according  to  the  National  Industrial  Conference
Board,  the  richest  one-fifth  of  the  population  received  46.2  percent  of  the  national  income
in  1910,  51.3  percent  in  1929,  and  48.5  percent  in  1937.

text: In the same three years, the share of the poorest one-fifth of the population fell from 8.3 percent to 5.4 percent to 3.6 percent.
text_raw:
In  the  same  three  years,  the  share
of  the  poorest  one-fifth  of  the  population  fell  from  8.3  percent  to  5.4  percent  to  3.6
percent.

text: Thus the ratios between the portion obtained by the richest one-fifth and that obtained by the poorest one-fifth increased in these three years from 5.6 to 9.3 to 13.5.
text_raw:
Thus  the  ratios  between  the  portion  obtained  by  the  richest  one-fifth  and  that
obtained  by  the  poorest  one-fifth  increased  in  these  three  years  from  5.6  to  9.3  to  13.5.

text: If, instead of one-fifths, we examine the ratios between the percentage obtained by the richest one-tenth and that obtained by the poorest one-tenth, we find that in 1910 the ratio was 10; in 1929 it was 21.7; and in 1937 it was 34.4.
text_raw:
If,
instead  of  one-fifths,  we  examine  the  ratios  between  the  percentage  obtained  by  the
richest  one-tenth  and  that  obtained  by  the  poorest  one-tenth,  we  find  that  in  1910  the  ratio
was  10;  in  1929  it  was  21.7;  and  in  1937  it  was  34.4.

text: This means that the rich in the United States were getting richer relatively and probably absolutely while the poor were getting poorer both relatively and absolutely.
text_raw:
This  means  that  the  rich  in  the
United  States  were  getting  richer  relatively  and  probably  absolutely  while  the  poor  were
getting  poorer  both  relatively  and  absolutely.

text: This last is caused by the fact that the increase in the real national income in the period 1910-1937 was not great enough to compensate for the decrease in percentage going to the poor or for the increase in number of persons in that class.
text_raw:
This  last  is  caused  by  the  fact  that  the
increase  in  the  real  national  income  in  the  period  1910-1937  was  not  great  enough  to
compensate  for  the  decrease  in  percentage  going  to  the  poor  or  for  the  increase  in  number
of  persons  in  that  class.

text: As a result of such an increase in disparity in the distribution of national income, there will be a tendency for savings to rise and for consumers' purchasing power to decline relative to each other.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  such  an  increase  in  disparity  in  the  distribution  of  national  income,  there
will  be  a  tendency  for  savings  to  rise  and  for  consumers'  purchasing  power  to  decline
relative  to  each  other.

text: This is because the savings of a community are largely made by the richer persons in it, and savings increase out of all proportion as incomes rise.
text_raw:
This  is  because  the  savings  of  a  community  are  largely  made  by  the
richer  persons  in  it,  and  savings  increase  out  of  all  proportion  as  incomes  rise.

text: On the other hand, the incomes of the poor class are devoted primarily to expenditures for consumption.
text_raw:
On  the
other  hand,  the  incomes  of  the  poor  class  are  devoted  primarily  to  expenditures  for
consumption.

text: Thus, if it is correct that there is an increasing disparity in the distribution of the national income of a country, there will be a tendency for savings to rise and consumer purchasing power to decline relative to each other.
text_raw:
Thus,  if  it  is  correct  that  there  is  an  increasing  disparity  in  the  distribution
of  the  national  income  of  a  country,  there  will  be  a  tendency  for  savings  to  rise  and
consumer  purchasing  power  to  decline  relative  to  each  other.

text: If this is so, there will be an increasing reluctance on the part of the controllers of savings to invest their savings in new capital equipment, since the existing decline of purchasing power will make it increasingly difficult to sell the products of the existing capital equipment and highly unlikely that the products of any new capital equipment could be sold more easily.
text_raw:
If  this  is  so,  there  will  be  an
increasing  reluctance  on  the  part  of  the  controllers  of  savings  to  invest  their  savings  in
new  capital  equipment,  since  the  existing  decline  of  purchasing  power  will  make  it
increasingly  difficult  to  sell  the  products  of  the  existing  capital  equipment  and  highly
unlikely  that  the  products  of  any  new  capital  equipment  could  be  sold  more  easily.

text: This situation, as we have described it, assumes that the government has not intervened in such a way as to change the distribution of the national income as determined by economic factors.
text_raw:
This  situation,  as  we  have  described  it,  assumes  that  the  government  has  not
intervened  in  such  a  way  as  to  change  the  distribution  of  the  national  income  as
determined  by  economic  factors.

text: If, however, the government does intervene to disturb this distribution, its actions will either increase the disparity in its distribution or will decrease it.
text_raw:
If,  however,  the  government  does  intervene  to  disturb
this  distribution,  its  actions  will  either  increase  the  disparity  in  its  distribution  or  will
decrease  it.

text: If these actions increase it, the problem of the discrepancy to which we have referred between savings, on one hand, and the level of purchasing power and investment, on the other, will be made worse.
text_raw:
If  these  actions  increase  it,  the  problem  of  the  discrepancy  to  which  we  have
referred  between  savings,  on  one  hand,  and  the  level  of  purchasing  power  and
investment,  on  the  other,  will  be  made  worse.

text: If, on the other hand, the government adopts a program which seeks to reduce the disparity in the distribution of the national income, by, for example, adopting a program of taxation which reduces the savings of the rich while increasing the purchasing power of the poor, the same problem of insufficient investment will arise.
text_raw:
If,  on  the  other  hand,  the  government
adopts  a  program  which  seeks  to  reduce  the  disparity  in  the  distribution  of  the  national
income,  by,  for  example,  adopting  a  program  of  taxation  which  reduces  the  savings  of  the
rich  while  increasing  the  purchasing  power  of  the  poor,  the  same  problem  of  insufficient
investment  will  arise.

on  a  graduated  income  tax,  and,  because  of  the  concentration  of  saving  in  the  upper-

situation  is  left  subject  to  purely  economic  factors  or  the  government  takes  steps  to
decrease  the  disparity.

The  only  difference  is  that,  in  the  one  ease,  the  decline  in
investment  may  be  attributed  to  a  leek  of  consumer  purchasing  power,  while,  in  the  other
case,  it  may  be  attributed  to  a  "killing  of  incentive"  by  government  action.

text: Thus, we see that the controversy which has raged in both Europe and America since 1932 between progressives and conservatives in regard to the causes of the lack of investment is an artificial one.
text_raw:
Thus,  we  see
that  the  controversy  which  has  raged  in  both  Europe  and  America  since  1932  between
progressives  and  conservatives  in  regard  to  the  causes  of  the  lack  of  investment  is  an
artificial  one.

text: The progressives, who insisted that the lack of investment was caused by lack of consumer purchasing power, w ere correct.
text_raw:
The  progressives,  who  insisted  that  the  lack  of  investment  was  caused  by
lack  of  consumer  purchasing  power,  w  ere  correct.

text: But the conservatives, who insisted that the lack of investment was caused by a lack of confidence, were also correct.
text_raw:
But  the  conservatives,  who  insisted
that  the  lack  of  investment  was  caused  by  a  lack  of  confidence,  were  also  correct.

text: Each was looking at the opposite side of what is a single continuous cycle.
text_raw:
Each
was  looking  at  the  opposite  side  of  what  is  a  single  continuous  cycle.

text: This cycle runs roughly as follows:
text_raw: This  cycle  runs  roughly  as  follows:

text: (a) purchasing power creates demand for goods;
text_raw:
(a)  purchasing  power  creates  demand  for
goods;

text: (b) demand for goods creates confidence in the minds of investors;
text_raw: (b)  demand  for  goods  creates  confidence  in  the  minds  of  investors;

text: (c) confidence creates new investment; and (d) new investment creates purchasing power, which then creates demand, and so on.
text_raw:
(c)  confidence
creates  new  investment;  and  (d)  new  investment  creates  purchasing  power,  which  then
creates  demand,  and  so  on.

text: To cut this cycle at any point and to insist that the cycle begins at that point is to falsify the situation.
text_raw:
To  cut  this  cycle  at  any  point  and  to  insist  that  the  cycle
begins  at  that  point  is  to  falsify  the  situation.

text: In the 1930's the progressives concentrated attention on stage (a), while the conservatives concentrated attention on stage (c).
text_raw:
In  the  1930's  the  progressives  concentrated
attention  on  stage  (a),  while  the  conservatives  concentrated  attention  on  stage  (c).

text: The progressives, who sought to increase purchasing poYver by some redistribution of the national income, undoubtedly did increase purchasing power under stage (a), but they lost purchasing power under stage (c) by reducing confidence of potential investors.

The
progressives,  who  sought  to  increase  purchasing  poYver  by  some  redistribution  of  the
national  income,  undoubtedly  did  increase  purchasing  power  under  stage  (a),  but  they  lost

text: This decrease of confidence was especially noticeable in countries (like France and the United States) which were still deeply involved in the stage of financial capitalism.
text_raw:
This
decrease  of  confidence  was  especially  noticeable  in  countries  (like  France  and  the  United

text: It would appear that the economic factors alone affected the distribution of incomes in the direction of increasing disparity.
text_raw:
It  would  appear  that  the  economic  factors  alone  affected  the  distribution  of  incomes  in
the  direction  of  increasing  disparity.

text: In no major country, however, were the economic factors alone allowed to determine the issue.
text_raw:
In  no  major  country,  however,  were  the  economic
factors  alone  allowed  to  determine  the  issue.

text: In all countries government action noticeably influenced the distribution....
text_raw:
In  all  countries  government  action
noticeably  influenced  the  distribution....

text: In Italy the economic factors had relatively free rein until after the creation of the corporative state in 1934.
text_raw:
In  Italy  the  economic  factors  had  relatively  free  rein  until  after  the  creation  of  the
corporative  state  in  1934.

text: The effect of government action was to increase the normal economic tendency toward an increasing disparity in distribution of the national income.
text_raw:
The  effect  of  government  action  was  to  increase  the  normal
economic  tendency  toward  an  increasing  disparity  in  distribution  of  the  national  income.

text: This tendency had been allowed to work from an early period until the end of the war in 1918.
text_raw:
This  tendency  had  been  allowed  to  work  from  an  early  period  until  the  end  of  the  war  in
1918.

text: A drastic effort by Leftish influences in the period 1918-1922 resulted in government action which reversed this tendency.
text_raw:
A  drastic  effort  by  Leftish  influences  in  the  period  1918-1922  resulted  in
government  action  which  reversed  this  tendency.

text: As a result, a counterrevolution brought Mussolini to power in October 1922.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  a  counterrevolution  brought
Mussolini  to  power  in  October  1922.

text: The new government suppressed those government actions which had hampered the normal economic tendency, and as a result the trend toward greater disparity in distribution of the national income was resumed.
text_raw:
The  new  government  suppressed  those  government
actions  which  had  hampered  the  normal  economic  tendency,  and  as  a  result  the  trend
toward  greater  disparity  in  distribution  of  the  national  income  was  resumed.

text: This trend
text_raw: This  trend

text: became more drastic after the creation of the dictatorship in 1925, after the stabilization of the lira in 1927, and after the creation of the corporative state in 1934.
text_raw:
became  more  drastic  after  the  creation  of  the  dictatorship  in  1925,  after  the  stabilization
of  the  lira  in  1927,  and  after  the  creation  of  the  corporative  state  in  1934.

text: In Germany the changes in distribution of the national income were similar to those in Italy, although complicated by the efforts to create a social-service state (an effort going back to Bismarck) and by the hyperinflation.
text_raw:
In  Germany  the  changes  in  distribution  of  the  national  income  were  similar  to  those
in  Italy,  although  complicated  by  the  efforts  to  create  a  social-service  state  (an  effort
going  back  to  Bismarck)  and  by  the  hyperinflation.

text: In general, the trend toward increasing disparity in distribution of the national income continued, less rapidly than in Italy, until after 1918.
text_raw:
In  general,  the  trend  toward
increasing  disparity  in  distribution  of  the  national  income  continued,  less  rapidly  than  in
Italy,  until  after  1918.

text: The inflation, by wiping out unemployment for the lower class and by wiping out the savings of the middle class, created a complex situation in which the wealth of the richest class was increased while the poverty of the poorest class was reduced, and the general trend toward increased disparity in income was probably reduced.
text_raw:
The  inflation,  by  wiping  out  unemployment  for  the  lower  class  and
by  wiping  out  the  savings  of  the  middle  class,  created  a  complex  situation  in  which  the
wealth  of  the  richest  class  was  increased  while  the  poverty  of  the  poorest  class  was
reduced,  and  the  general  trend  toward  increased  disparity  in  income  was  probably
reduced.

text: This reduction became great under the social- service state of 1924-1930, but was drastically reversed because of the great increase in poverty in the lower classes after 1929.
text_raw:
This  reduction  became  great  under  the  social- service  state  of  1924-1930,  but
was  drastically  reversed  because  of  the  great  increase  in  poverty  in  the  lower  classes  after
1929.

text: After 1934 the adoption of an unorthodox financial policy and a policy of benefits to monopoly capitalism reinforced the normal trend toward increasing disparity in distribution of income.
text_raw:
After  1934  the  adoption  of  an  unorthodox  financial  policy  and  a  policy  of  benefits
to  monopoly  capitalism  reinforced  the  normal  trend  toward  increasing  disparity  in
distribution  of  income.

text: This was in accord with the desires of the Hitler government, but the full impact of this policy was not apparent on the distribution of incomes until the period of full employment after 1937.
text_raw:
This  was  in  accord  with  the  desires  of  the  Hitler  government,  but
the  full  impact  of  this  policy  was  not  apparent  on  the  distribution  of  incomes  until  the
period  of  full  employment  after  1937.

text: Until 1938 Hitler's policy, although aimed at favoring the high-income classes, raised the standards of living of the lower-income levels even more drastically by shifting them from unemployment with incomes close to nothing into wage-earning positions in industry) so that the disparity in distribution of income was probably even reduced for a short-run period in 1934-1937.
text_raw:
Until  1938  Hitler's  policy,  although  aimed  at  favoring  the  high-income  classes,
raised  the  standards  of  living  of  the  lower-income  levels  even  more  drastically  by  shifting
them  from  unemployment  with  incomes  close  to  nothing  into  wage-earning  positions  in
industry)  so  that  the  disparity  in  distribution  of  income  was  probably  even  reduced  for  a
short-run  period  in  1934-1937.

text: This was not unacceptable to the high-income classes, because it stopped the threat of revolution by the discontented masses and because it was obviously of long-run benefit to them.
text_raw:
This  was  not  unacceptable  to  the  high-income  classes,
because  it  stopped  the  threat  of  revolution  by  the  discontented  masses  and  because  it  was
obviously  of  long-run  benefit  to  them.

text: This long-run benefit began to appear when capacity employment of capital and labor was achieved in 1937.
text_raw:
This  long-run  benefit  began  to  appear  when
capacity  employment  of  capital  and  labor  was  achieved  in  1937.

text: The continuance of the policy of rearmament after 1936 increased the incomes of the high-income groups while decreasing the incomes of the lower-income groups and thus served, from 1937 onward, to reinforce the normal economic tendency toward an increasing disparity int eh distribution of incomes.
text_raw:
The  continuance  of  the
policy  of  rearmament  after  1936  increased  the  incomes  of  the  high-income  groups  while
decreasing  the  incomes  of  the  lower-income  groups  and  thus  served,  from  1937  onward,
to  reinforce  the  normal  economic  tendency  toward  an  increasing  disparity  int  eh
distribution  of  incomes.

text: This, of course, is one of the essential features of a Fascist government, and is obvious not only in Germany since 1937, in Italy since 1927, but also in Spain since 1938.
text_raw:
This,  of  course,  is  one  of  the  essential  features  of  a  Fascist
government,  and  is  obvious  not  only  in  Germany  since  1937,  in  Italy  since  1927,  but  also
in  Spain  since  1938.

text: In France and Britain, the trend toward increasing disparity in the distribution of incomes was reversed in recent decades, although in Britain before 1945 and in France before 1936 there was no conscious effort to achieve this result.
text_raw:
In  France  and  Britain,  the  trend  toward  increasing  disparity  in  the  distribution  of
incomes  was  reversed  in  recent  decades,  although  in  Britain  before  1945  and  in  France
before  1936  there  was  no  conscious  effort  to  achieve  this  result.

text: In France disparity increased until 1913, then decreased chiefly because of the increasing power of labor unions and actions of the government.
text_raw:
In  France  disparity  increased  until  1913,  then  decreased  chiefly  because  of  the
increasing  power  of  labor  unions  and  actions  of  the  government.

text: The inflation and resulting devaluation badly injured the incomes of the possessing class, so that the disparity became less disperse; but the whole level of living standards was declining, savings were declining, and investment was decreasing more rapidly than either.
text_raw:
The  inflation  and
resulting  devaluation  badly  injured  the  incomes  of  the  possessing  class,  so  that  the
disparity  became  less  disperse;  but  the  whole  level  of  living  standards  was  declining,
savings  were  declining,  and  investment  was  decreasing  more  rapidly  than  either.

text: This process became worse after the depression hit France about 1931 and even worse after the Popular Front adopted its welfare program in 1936.
text_raw:
This
process  became  worse  after  the  depression  hit  France  about  1931  and  even  worse  after
the  Popular  Front  adopted  its  welfare  program  in  1936.

text: This decline of the general
text_raw: This  decline  of  the  general

text: economic level continued quite steadily except for a brief revival after 1938, but the disparity in the distribution of incomes very likely became greater in 1940-1942.
text_raw:
economic  level  continued  quite  steadily  except  for  a  brief  revival  after  1938,  but  the
disparity  in  the  distribution  of  incomes  very  likely  became  greater  in  1940-1942.

text: In Britain the disparity became greater, but at a slower rate (because of labor unions), until the First World War, and then almost stabilized, increasing only slightly, because of the severe efforts made in Britain to pay for much of the war's cost by taxation.
text_raw:
In  Britain  the  disparity  became  greater,  but  at  a  slower  rate  (because  of  labor
unions),  until  the  First  World  War,  and  then  almost  stabilized,  increasing  only  slightly,
because  of  the  severe  efforts  made  in  Britain  to  pay  for  much  of  the  war's  cost  by
taxation.

text: The decrease in upper-level incomes by taxation, however, was more than overcome by the decrease in lower-level incomes from unemployment.
text_raw:
The  decrease  in  upper-level  incomes  by  taxation,  however,  was  more  than
overcome  by  the  decrease  in  lower-level  incomes  from  unemployment.

text: This static condition of the disparity in distribution of the national income doubtless continued until after 1931.
text_raw:
This  static
condition  of  the  disparity  in  distribution  of  the  national  income  doubtless  continued  until
after  1931.

text: Since this last date the situation is confused.
text_raw: Since  this  last  date  the  situation  is  confused.

text: The revival of prosperity and the rapid development of new lines of activity combined with the peculiarities of the incidence of British taxation have likely reduced the disparity, but, until 1943, not by anything approaching the degree which one might expect from a first glance at the problem.
text_raw:
The  revival  of  prosperity  and  the
rapid  development  of  new  lines  of  activity  combined  with  the  peculiarities  of  the
incidence  of  British  taxation  have  likely  reduced  the  disparity,  but,  until  1943,  not  by
anything  approaching  the  degree  which  one  might  expect  from  a  first  glance  at  the
problem.

text: Since 1943 and especially since 1946 the tax schedule and the government's social welfare program have drastically reduced the disparity in distribution of income and have also cut investment and even savings by private sources to a considerable degree.
text_raw:
Since  1943  and  especially  since  1946  the  tax  schedule  and  the  government's
social  welfare  program  have  drastically  reduced  the  disparity  in  distribution  of  income
and  have  also  cut  investment  and  even  savings  by  private  sources  to  a  considerable
degree.

text: It would seem that in the twentieth century the disparity in the distribution of national income, which had been increasing for generations, slowed down and reversed as a result of government activities.
text_raw:
It  would  seem  that  in  the  twentieth  century  the  disparity  in  the  distribution  of
national  income,  which  had  been  increasing  for  generations,  slowed  down  and  reversed
as  a  result  of  government  activities.

text: This turning point appeared in different countries at different dates, probably earliest in Denmark and France, later in Germany and Italy, latest in Britain and Spain.
text_raw:
This  turning  point  appeared  in  different  countries  at
different  dates,  probably  earliest  in  Denmark  and  France,  later  in  Germany  and  Italy,
latest  in  Britain  and  Spain.

text: In France and Britain the tendency was reversed by the action of the government, but in a hesitant fashion which was not able, in any decisive way, to overcome the sag in private enterprise by any upswing in government enterprise.
text_raw:
In  France  and  Britain  the  tendency  was  reversed  by  the  action
of  the  government,  but  in  a  hesitant  fashion  which  was  not  able,  in  any  decisive  way,  to
overcome  the  sag  in  private  enterprise  by  any  upswing  in  government  enterprise.

text: In Germany, Italy, and Spain the governments fell into the hands of the possessing classes, and the desires of the peoples of these countries for a more equitable distribution of incomes were frustrated.
text_raw:
In
Germany,  Italy,  and  Spain  the  governments  fell  into  the  hands  of  the  possessing  classes,
and  the  desires  of  the  peoples  of  these  countries  for  a  more  equitable  distribution  of
incomes  were  frustrated.

text: In all three types of conditions, there was a decline in real economic progress until after 1950.
text_raw:
In  all  three  types  of  conditions,  there  was  a  decline  in  real
economic  progress  until  after  1950.

text: Declining Rate of Expansion Leading to Crisis
text_raw: Declining  Rate  of  Expansion  Leading  to  Crisis

text: A declining rate of economic expansion is the last important characteristic of the economic system of Europe in the present century up to 1950.
text_raw:
A  declining  rate  of  economic  expansion  is  the  last  important  characteristic  of  the
economic  system  of  Europe  in  the  present  century  up  to  1950.

text: This decline resulted almost inevitably from the other characteristics which we have already discussed.
text_raw:
This  decline  resulted
almost  inevitably  from  the  other  characteristics  which  we  have  already  discussed.

text: It varied from country to country, the countries of eastern Europe suffering less than those of western Europe on the whole, but chiefly because their previous rate of progress had been so much lower.
text_raw:
It
varied  from  country  to  country,  the  countries  of  eastern  Europe  suffering  less  than  those
of  western  Europe  on  the  whole,  but  chiefly  because  their  previous  rate  of  progress  had
been  so  much  lower.

text: The causes of this decline are basically to be found in a relative increase in the power of the vested interests within the community to defend the status quo against the efforts of the progressive and enterprising members of the community to change it.
text_raw:
The  causes  of  this  decline  are  basically  to  be  found  in  a  relative  increase  in  the  power
of  the  vested  interests  within  the  community  to  defend  the  status  quo  against  the  efforts
of  the  progressive  and  enterprising  members  of  the  community  to  change  it.

text: This was revealed in the market (the central mechanism of the economic system) as a result of a relative increase in savings in respect to investment.
text_raw:
This  was
revealed  in  the  market  (the  central  mechanism  of  the  economic  system)  as  a  result  of  a
relative  increase  in  savings  in  respect  to  investment.

text: Savings have continued or have increased for several reasons.
text_raw:
Savings  have  continued  or  have
increased  for  several  reasons.

text: In the first place, a tradition which placed a high social esteem on savings existed in western Europe from the Protestant Reformation until the
text_raw:
In  the  first  place,  a  tradition  which  placed  a  high  social
esteem  on  savings  existed  in  western  Europe  from  the  Protestant  Reformation  until  the

text: In the second place, there had grown up established institutionalized savings organizations like insurance companies.
text_raw:
In  the  second  place,  there  had  grown  up  established  institutionalized  savings
organizations  like  insurance  companies.

text: In the third place, the rising standards of living increased savings even more rapidly.
text_raw:
In  the  third  place,  the  rising  standards  of  living
increased  savings  even  more  rapidly.

text: In the fourth place, the increasing disparity in the distribution of incomes increased savings.
text_raw:
In  the  fourth  place,  the  increasing  disparity  in  the
distribution  of  incomes  increased  savings.

text: In the fifth place, the increase in size of enterprises and the separation of ownership from control acted to increase the amount of corporate savings (undistributed profits).
text_raw:
In  the  fifth  place,  the  increase  in  size  of
enterprises  and  the  separation  of  ownership  from  control  acted  to  increase  the  amount  of
corporate  savings  (undistributed  profits).

text: On the other hand, the inclination to invest did not rise so rapidly as savings, or even decreased.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  the  inclination  to  invest  did  not  rise  so  rapidly  as  savings,  or
even  decreased.

text: Here, again, the reasons are numerous.
text_raw: Here,  again,  the  reasons  are  numerous.

text: In the first place, the shift in advanced industrial countries from secondary to tertiary production reduces the demand for heavy capital investment.
text_raw:
In  the  first  place,  the  shift  in
advanced  industrial  countries  from  secondary  to  tertiary  production  reduces  the  demand
for  heavy  capital  investment.

text: In the second place, declining rates of population increase, and geographic expansion may adversely affect the demand for investment.
text_raw:
In  the  second  place,  declining  rates  of  population  increase,
and  geographic  expansion  may  adversely  affect  the  demand  for  investment.

text: In the third place, the increasing disparity in the distribution of incomes, whether it is counteracted by government action or not, has a tendency to reduce the demand for investment capital.
text_raw:
In  the  third
place,  the  increasing  disparity  in  the  distribution  of  incomes,  whether  it  is  counteracted
by  government  action  or  not,  has  a  tendency  to  reduce  the  demand  for  investment  capital.

text: In the fourth place, the decrease in competition has served to reduce the amount of investment by making it possible for the controllers of existing capital to maintain its value by curtailing the investment of new capital which would make the existing capital less valuable.
text_raw:
In  the  fourth  place,  the  decrease  in  competition  has  served  to  reduce  the  amount  of
investment  by  making  it  possible  for  the  controllers  of  existing  capital  to  maintain  its
value  by  curtailing  the  investment  of  new  capital  which  would  make  the  existing  capital
less  valuable.

text: This last point may require additional explanation.
text_raw: This  last  point  may  require  additional  explanation.

text: In the past, investment was not only capital-creating but also capital-destroying â€” that is, it made some existing capital worthless by making it obsolete.
text_raw:
In  the  past,  investment  was  not  only  capital-creating  but  also  capital-destroying â€”
that  is,  it  made  some  existing  capital  worthless  by  making  it  obsolete.

text: The creation by investment, for example, of shipyards for making iron-hull steam vessels not only created this new capital but at the same time destroyed the value of the existing yards equipped to make wooden-hull sailing ships.
text_raw:
The  creation  by
investment,  for  example,  of  shipyards  for  making  iron-hull  steam  vessels  not  only  created
this  new  capital  but  at  the  same  time  destroyed  the  value  of  the  existing  yards  equipped  to
make  wooden-hull  sailing  ships.

text: In the past, new investment was made in only one of two cases:
text_raw:
In  the  past,  new  investment  was  made  in  only  one  of  two
cases:

text: (a) if an old investor believed that the new capital would yield sufficient profit to pay for itself and for the old investment now made obsolete, or (b) if the new investor was completely free of the old one, so that the latter could do nothing to prevent the destruction of his existing capital holdings by the new investor.
text_raw:
(a)  if  an  old  investor  believed  that  the  new  capital  would  yield  sufficient  profit  to
pay  for  itself  and  for  the  old  investment  now  made  obsolete,  or  (b)  if  the  new  investor
was  completely  free  of  the  old  one,  so  that  the  latter  could  do  nothing  to  prevent  the
destruction  of  his  existing  capital  holdings  by  the  new  investor.

text: Both of these two alternatives, in the twentieth century tended to become less likely (until 1950), the former by the decline in consumer purchasing power and the latter by the decrease in competition.
text_raw:
Both  of  these  two
alternatives,  in  the  twentieth  century  tended  to  become  less  likely  (until  1950),  the  former
by  the  decline  in  consumer  purchasing  power  and  the  latter  by  the  decrease  in
competition.

text: The way in which the relative decline of investment in respect to savings results in economic crisis is not difficult to see.
text_raw:
The  way  in  which  the  relative  decline  of  investment  in  respect  to  savings  results  in
economic  crisis  is  not  difficult  to  see.

text: In the modern economic community, the sum total of goods and services appearing in the market is at one and the same time the income of the community and the aggregate cost of producing the goods and services in question.
text_raw:
In  the  modern  economic  community,  the  sum  total
of  goods  and  services  appearing  in  the  market  is  at  one  and  the  same  time  the  income  of

North  of  the  Yangtze  River  the  war  lords

text: His program envisaged the achievement of these ideals through three successive stages of development of which the first would be a period of military domination to secure unity and independence, the second would be a period of Kuomintang dictatorship to secure the necessary political education of the masses, and only the third would be one of constitutional democracy.

text: Imposed on November 18, 1935, and accepted by fifty-two nations, these sanctions established an embargo in arms and munitions, on loans and on credit, and on certain key commodities, and established a boycott on purchases of all Italian goods.

different  thing,  and  he  had  constantly  to  give  at  least  verbal  support  to  Britain's  efforts  to
modify  his  encirclement  of  Germany  into  a  Four-Power  Pact  (of  Britain,  France,  Italy,
Germany).

text: This Four- Power Pact, which was the ultimate goal of the anti-Bolshevik group in England, was really an effort to form a united front of Europe against the Soviet Union and, in the eyes of this group, would have been a capstone to unite in one system the encirclement of France (which was the British answer to Barthou's encirclement of Germany) and the Anti-Comintern Pact (which was the German response to the same project).

This  Four- Power  Pact,  which  was  the  ultimate  goal  of  the  anti-Bolshevik

text: The Four-Power Pact reached its fruition at the Munich Conference of September 1938, where these four Powers destroyed Czechoslovakia without consulting Czechoslovakia's ally, the Soviet Union.
text_raw:

1938,  where  these  four  Powers  destroyed  Czechoslovakia  without  consulting

text: But the scorn the dictators had for Britain and France as decadent democracies had by this time reached such a pass that the dictators no longer had even that minimum of respect without which the Four-Power Pact could not function.

But  the  scorn  the  dictators  had  for  Britain  and

text: As a consequence, Hitler in 1939 spurned all Chamberlain's frantic efforts to restore the Four-Power Pact along with his equally frantic and even more secret efforts to win Hitler's attention by offers of colonies in Africa and economic support in eastern Europe.

text: As a result of the failure of the policy of the French Right against Germany in 1924 and the failure of the "policy of fulfillment" of the French Left in 1929-1930, France was left with no policy.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  the  failure  of  the  policy  of  the  French  Right  against  Germany  in  1924
and  the  failure  of  the  "policy  of  fulfillment"  of  the  French  Left  in  1929-1930,  France  was
left  with  no  policy.

text: Convinced that French security depended on British military and naval support in the field before action began (in order to avoid a German wartime occupation of the richest part of France such as existed in 1914-1918), depressed by the growing unbalance of the German population over the French population, and shot through with pacifism and antiwar feeling, the French Army under Petain's influence adopted a purely defensive strategy and built up defensive tactics to support it.
text_raw:
Convinced  that  French  security  depended  on  British  military  and
naval  support  in  the  field  before  action  began  (in  order  to  avoid  a  German  wartime
occupation  of  the  richest  part  of  France  such  as  existed  in  1914-1918),  depressed  by  the

text: In spite of the agitations of Charles de Gaulle (then a colonel) and his parliamentary spokesman, Paul Reynaud, to build up an armored striking force as an offensive weapon, France built a great, and purely defensive, fortified barrier from Montmedy to the Swiss frontier, and retrained many of its tactical units into purely defensive duties within this barrier.

text: The steps which brought France to this destination are clear; they are marked by the Anglo-German Naval Agreement of June 1935; the Ethiopian crisis of September 1935; the remilitarization of the Rhineland in March 1936; the neutralization of Belgium in 1936; the Spanish Civil War of 1936-1939; the destruction of Austria in March 1938; and the Czechoslovak crisis leading up to Munich in September 1938.

The  steps  which  brought  France  to  this  destination  are  clear;  they  are  marked  by  the

text: Along these steps we must continue our story.
