text: From the summer of 1936 to the spring of 1939, Spain was the scene of a bitter conflict of arms, ideologies, and interests.
text_raw:
From  the  summer  of  1936  to  the  spring  of  1939,  Spain  was  the  scene  of  a  bitter
conflict  of  arms,  ideologies,  and  interests.

text: This conflict was both a civil war and an international struggle.
text_raw:
This  conflict  was  both  a  civil  war  and  an
international  struggle.

text: It was a controversial problem at the time and has remained a controversial problem since.
text_raw:
It  was  a  controversial  problem  at  the  time  and  has  remained  a
controversial  problem  since.

text: For twenty or more years, the bitter feelings raised by the struggle remained so intense that it was difficult to determine the facts of the dispute, and anyone who tried to make an objective study of the facts was subjected to abuse from both sides.
text_raw:
For  twenty  or  more  years,  the  bitter  feelings  raised  by  the
struggle  remained  so  intense  that  it  was  difficult  to  determine  the  facts  of  the  dispute,  and
anyone  who  tried  to  make  an  objective  study  of  the  facts  was  subjected  to  abuse  from
both  sides.

text: The historical past of Spain has been so different from that of the rest of Western Civilization that it sometimes seems doubtful if it should be regarded as part of Western Civilization.
text_raw:
The  historical  past  of  Spain  has  been  so  different  from  that  of  the  rest  of  Western
Civilization  that  it  sometimes  seems  doubtful  if  it  should  be  regarded  as  part  of  Western
Civilization.

text: This difference is increased by the fact that, since the late fifteenth century, Spain has refused to share in the experiences of Western Civilization and, if many powerful groups could have had their wish, would have remained in its fifteenth- or sixteenth-century condition.
text_raw:
This  difference  is  increased  by  the  fact  that,  since  the  late  fifteenth  century,
Spain  has  refused  to  share  in  the  experiences  of  Western  Civilization  and,  if  many
powerful  groups  could  have  had  their  wish,  would  have  remained  in  its  fifteenth-  or
sixteenth-century  condition.

text: From the invasion of the Arabs in 71 1 to their final ejection in 1492, Spanish life was dominated by the struggle against this foreign intruder.
text_raw:
From  the  invasion  of  the  Arabs  in  71 1  to  their  final  ejection  in  1492,  Spanish  life  was
dominated  by  the  struggle  against  this  foreign  intruder.

text: From 1525 to 1648, Spain was in a struggle with the new religious movements aroused by Luther.
text_raw:
From  1525  to  1648,  Spain  was  in
a  struggle  with  the  new  religious  movements  aroused  by  Luther.

text: Since 1648 it has been, except for brief intervals and for exceptional personalities, at war with modern rationalism and modern science, with the Enlightenment, the French Revolution, and Napoleon, with modern democracy, modern secularism, modern liberalism, modern constitutionalism, and the bourgeois conception of modern society as a whole.
text_raw:
Since  1648  it  has  been,
except  for  brief  intervals  and  for  exceptional  personalities,  at  war  with  modern
rationalism  and  modern  science,  with  the  Enlightenment,  the  French  Revolution,  and
Napoleon,  with  modern  democracy,  modern  secularism,  modern  liberalism,  modern
constitutionalism,  and  the  bourgeois  conception  of  modern  society  as  a  whole.

text: As a result of more than a thousand years of such struggles, almost all elements of Spanish society, even those which were not, in theory, opposed to the new movements in Western culture,
text_raw:
As  a  result
of  more  than  a  thousand  years  of  such  struggles,  almost  all  elements  of  Spanish  society,
even  those  which  were  not,  in  theory,  opposed  to  the  new  movements  in  Western  culture,

text: have developed a fanatical intolerance, an uncompromising individualism, and a fatal belief that physical force is a solution to all problems, however spiritual.
text_raw:
have  developed  a  fanatical  intolerance,  an  uncompromising  individualism,  and  a  fatal
belief  that  physical  force  is  a  solution  to  all  problems,  however  spiritual.

text: The impact of the bourgeois, liberal, scientific, and industrialized West of the nineteenth century upon Spain w as similar to its impact on other backward political units such as Japan, China, Turkey, or Russia.
text_raw:
The  impact  of  the  bourgeois,  liberal,  scientific,  and  industrialized  West  of  the
nineteenth  century  upon  Spain  w  as  similar  to  its  impact  on  other  backward  political  units
such  as  Japan,  China,  Turkey,  or  Russia.

text: In each case, some elements of these societies wished to resist the political expansion of the West by adopting its industry, science, military organization, and constitutional structures.
text_raw:
In  each  case,  some  elements  of  these  societies
wished  to  resist  the  political  expansion  of  the  West  by  adopting  its  industry,  science,
military  organization,  and  constitutional  structures.

text: Other elements wished to resist all westernization, by passive opposition if nothing more effective could be found, to the death if necessary, and to keep secreted in their hearts and minds the older native attitudes even if their bodies were compelled to yield to alien, Western, patterns of action.
text_raw:
Other  elements  wished  to  resist  all
westernization,  by  passive  opposition  if  nothing  more  effective  could  be  found,  to  the
death  if  necessary,  and  to  keep  secreted  in  their  hearts  and  minds  the  older  native
attitudes  even  if  their  bodies  were  compelled  to  yield  to  alien,  Western,  patterns  of  action.

text: In Spain, Russia, and China this attitude of resistance was sufficiently successful to delay the process of westernization to a date when Western Civilization was beginning to lose its own tradition (or at least its faith in it) and to shift its allegiance (or at least its behavior) to patterns of thought and action which were quite foreign to the main line of Western tradition.
text_raw:
In  Spain,  Russia,  and  China  this  attitude  of  resistance  was  sufficiently  successful  to
delay  the  process  of  westernization  to  a  date  when  Western  Civilization  was  beginning  to
lose  its  own  tradition  (or  at  least  its  faith  in  it)  and  to  shift  its  allegiance  (or  at  least  its
behavior)  to  patterns  of  thought  and  action  which  were  quite  foreign  to  the  main  line  of
Western  tradition.

text: This shift, to which we have referred in the first section of this present chapter, was marked by a loss of the basic element of moderation to be found in the real tradition of the West.
text_raw:
This  shift,  to  which  we  have  referred  in  the  first  section  of  this  present
chapter,  was  marked  by  a  loss  of  the  basic  element  of  moderation  to  be  found  in  the  real
tradition  of  the  West.

text: As ideological intolerance or totalitarian authoritarianism, for example, grew in the West, this was bound to have an adverse effect upon efforts to carry Western democracy, liberalism, or parliamentary constitutionalism to areas like Japan, China, Russia, or, the case in point, Spain.
text_raw:
As  ideological  intolerance  or  totalitarian  authoritarianism,  for
example,  grew  in  the  West,  this  was  bound  to  have  an  adverse  effect  upon  efforts  to  carry
Western  democracy,  liberalism,  or  parliamentary  constitutionalism  to  areas  like  Japan,
China,  Russia,  or,  the  case  in  point,  Spain.

text: During the nineteenth century, the elements willing at least to compromise with the Western way of life were not completely unsuccessful in Spain, probably because they received a certain amount of support from the army, which realized its inability to fight effectively without a largely westernized society to support it.
text_raw:
During  the  nineteenth  century,  the  elements  willing  at  least  to  compromise  with  the
Western  way  of  life  were  not  completely  unsuccessful  in  Spain,  probably  because  they
received  a  certain  amount  of  support  from  the  army,  which  realized  its  inability  to  fight
effectively  without  a  largely  westernized  society  to  support  it.

text: This, however, was destroyed by the efforts of the "Restoration Monarchy" of 1875-1931 to find support among the opponents of modernization and by the Spanish defeat at the hands of the United States in 1898.
text_raw:
This,  however,  was
destroyed  by  the  efforts  of  the  "Restoration  Monarchy"  of  1875-1931  to  find  support
among  the  opponents  of  modernization  and  by  the  Spanish  defeat  at  the  hands  of  the
United  States  in  1898.

text: Alfonso XII ( 1874-1885) came to the throne as a military reaction after a long period of revolutionary confusion.
text_raw:
Alfonso  XII  (  1874-1885)  came  to  the  throne  as  a  military  reaction
after  a  long  period  of  revolutionary  confusion.

text: The defeat by the United States, like the Chinese defeat by Japan in 1894, or the Turkish defeat by Russia in 1877, widened the gap between the "progressive" and "reactionary" groups in Spain (if we may use these terms to indicate a willingness or a refusal to westernize ).
text_raw:
The  defeat  by  the  United  States,  like  the
Chinese  defeat  by  Japan  in  1894,  or  the  Turkish  defeat  by  Russia  in  1877,  widened  the
gap  between  the  "progressive"  and  "reactionary"  groups  in  Spain  (if  we  may  use  these
terms  to  indicate  a  willingness  or  a  refusal  to  westernize  ).

text: Moreover, the war of 1898, by depriving Spain of much of its empire, left its oversized army with little to do and with a reduced area on which to batten.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  war  of  1898,  by  depriving  Spain  of  much  of  its  empire,  left  its
oversized  army  with  little  to  do  and  with  a  reduced  area  on  which  to  batten.

text: Like a vampire octopus, the Spanish Army settled down to drain the lifeblood of Spain and, above all, Morocco.
text_raw:
Like  a
vampire  octopus,  the  Spanish  Army  settled  down  to  drain  the  lifeblood  of  Spain  and,
above  all,  Morocco.

text: This brought the army (meaning the officers) into alignment with the other conservative forces in Spain against the scanty forces of bourgeois liberalism and the rapidly growing forces of proletarian discontent.
text_raw:
This  brought  the  army  (meaning  the  officers)  into  alignment  with  the
other  conservative  forces  in  Spain  against  the  scanty  forces  of  bourgeois  liberalism  and
the  rapidly  growing  forces  of  proletarian  discontent.

text: These conservative forces consisted of the Church (meaning the upper clergy), the landlords, and the monarchists.
text_raw:
These  conservative  forces  consisted
of  the  Church  (meaning  the  upper  clergy),  the  landlords,  and  the  monarchists.

text: The forces of proletarian discontent consisted of the urban workers and the much larger mass of exploited peasants.
text_raw:
The  forces
of  proletarian  discontent  consisted  of  the  urban  workers  and  the  much  larger  mass  of
exploited  peasants.

text: These latter groups, which had no real acquaintance with the Western liberal tradition and found it of little hope when they did, were fertile soil for the agitators
text_raw:
These  latter  groups,  which  had  no  real  acquaintance  with  the  Western
liberal  tradition  and  found  it  of  little  hope  when  they  did,  were  fertile  soil  for  the  agitators

text: of proletarian revolution who were already challenging the bourgeois liberalism of the West.
text_raw:
of  proletarian  revolution  who  were  already  challenging  the  bourgeois  liberalism  of  the
West.

text: To be sure, Spanish individualism, provincialism, and suspicions of the state as an instrument of the possessing classes made any appeal to the totalitarian authoritarianism of Communism relatively weak in Spain.
text_raw:
To  be  sure,  Spanish  individualism,  provincialism,  and  suspicions  of  the  state  as  an
instrument  of  the  possessing  classes  made  any  appeal  to  the  totalitarian  authoritarianism
of  Communism  relatively  weak  in  Spain.

text: On the other hand, the appeal of anarchism, which was both individualist and anti-state, was stronger in Spain than anywhere else on earth (stronger even than in Russia where anarchism received its most complete verbal formulation at the hands of men like Bakunin).
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  the  appeal  of  anarchism,
which  was  both  individualist  and  anti-state,  was  stronger  in  Spain  than  anywhere  else  on
earth  (stronger  even  than  in  Russia  where  anarchism  received  its  most  complete  verbal
formulation  at  the  hands  of  men  like  Bakunin).

text: Finally, the appeal of Socialism was almost as strong as anarchism, and much more effectively organized.
text_raw:
Finally,  the  appeal  of  Socialism  was  almost  as  strong  as  anarchism,  and  much  more
effectively  organized.

text: Socialism to many discontented Spaniards (including many bourgeois intellectuals and professional men) seemed to offer a combination of social reform, economic progress, and a democratic secular state which was better fitted to Spanish needs than anarchism, Bolshevism, or laissez-faire constitutionalism.
text_raw:
Socialism  to  many  discontented  Spaniards  (including  many
bourgeois  intellectuals  and  professional  men)  seemed  to  offer  a  combination  of  social
reform,  economic  progress,  and  a  democratic  secular  state  which  was  better  fitted  to
Spanish  needs  than  anarchism,  Bolshevism,  or  laissez-faire  constitutionalism.

text: The weak link in this Socialist program was that the democratic, non-totalitarian state envisaged by the Socialist intellectuals in Spain was quite compatible with Spanish individualism (and basic democracy) but guise at variance with Spanish intolerance.
text_raw:
The  weak
link  in  this  Socialist  program  was  that  the  democratic,  non-totalitarian  state  envisaged  by
the  Socialist  intellectuals  in  Spain  was  quite  compatible  with  Spanish  individualism  (and
basic  democracy)  but  guise  at  variance  with  Spanish  intolerance.

text: There was a legitimate ground for doubt that any such Socialist state, if it came to power in Spain, would be tolerant enough to permit that intellectual disagreement which is so necessary for a democratic society, even one directing a Socialist economic system.
text_raw:
There  was  a  legitimate
ground  for  doubt  that  any  such  Socialist  state,  if  it  came  to  power  in  Spain,  would  be
tolerant  enough  to  permit  that  intellectual  disagreement  which  is  so  necessary  for  a
democratic  society,  even  one  directing  a  Socialist  economic  system.

text: The bourgeoisie of Spain, relatively few in numbers because of Spain's economic backwardness, were in a difficult position.
text_raw:
The  bourgeoisie  of  Spain,  relatively  few  in  numbers  because  of  Spain's  economic
backwardness,  were  in  a  difficult  position.

text: While the bourgeoisie of England and France had attacked the forces of feudalism, bureaucratic monarchy, militarism, and clericalism, and had created a liberal, secular state and a bourgeois society before they were themselves attacked by the rising forces of proletarian discontent on their Left, the bourgeoisie of Spain could see the proletarian threat from the Left before they were able to overcome the vested interests of the Right.
text_raw:
While  the  bourgeoisie  of  England  and  France
had  attacked  the  forces  of  feudalism,  bureaucratic  monarchy,  militarism,  and  clericalism,
and  had  created  a  liberal,  secular  state  and  a  bourgeois  society  before  they  were
themselves  attacked  by  the  rising  forces  of  proletarian  discontent  on  their  Left,  the
bourgeoisie  of  Spain  could  see  the  proletarian  threat  from  the  Left  before  they  were  able
to  overcome  the  vested  interests  of  the  Right.

text: As a result of this, the bourgeoisie tended to split into two parts.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  this,  the  bourgeoisie  tended  to
split  into  two  parts.

text: On the one hand were industrial and commercial bourgeoisie who supported the liberal ideas of laissez-faire, constitutional parliamentarianism, private property, anti-militarism, anti-bureaucratic freedom, anti-clericalism, and a limited state authority.
text_raw:
On  the  one  hand  were  industrial  and  commercial  bourgeoisie  who
supported  the  liberal  ideas  of  laissez-faire,  constitutional  parliamentarianism,  private
property,  anti-militarism,  anti-bureaucratic  freedom,  anti-clericalism,  and  a  limited  state
authority.

text: On the other hand were the intellectual and professional bourgeoisie who would have added to this program a sufficient degree of social reform, democracy, economic interventionism, and nationalization of property to put them into the Socialist camp.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand  were  the  intellectual  and  professional  bourgeoisie  who
would  have  added  to  this  program  a  sufficient  degree  of  social  reform,  democracy,
economic  interventionism,  and  nationalization  of  property  to  put  them  into  the  Socialist
camp.

text: Both these divisions of the bourgeois group tended to move further to the Right after 1931 as the growing pressure of proletarian revolution threatened both private property and liberal democracy.
text_raw:
Both  these  divisions  of  the  bourgeois  group  tended  to  move  further  to  the  Right
after  1931  as  the  growing  pressure  of  proletarian  revolution  threatened  both  private
property  and  liberal  democracy.

text: The bourgeois liberals feared the loss of private property and, to save it, hastily abandoned their earlier anti-militarism, anti-clericalism, and such; the bourgeois Socialists feared the loss of liberal democracy, but they found nowhere to go because liberal democracy could find no real basis in the fanatical intolerance of Spain, a feature as prevalent on the Right as on the Left.
text_raw:
The  bourgeois  liberals  feared  the  loss  of  private  property
and,  to  save  it,  hastily  abandoned  their  earlier  anti-militarism,  anti-clericalism,  and  such;
the  bourgeois  Socialists  feared  the  loss  of  liberal  democracy,  but  they  found  nowhere  to
go  because  liberal  democracy  could  find  no  real  basis  in  the  fanatical  intolerance  of
Spain,  a  feature  as  prevalent  on  the  Right  as  on  the  Left.

text: In truth, both bourgeois groups were largely crushed out, and their members practically exterminated, by the Right because of their earlier allegiance to anti-militarism, anti-clericalism, and anti- monarchism, and by the Left because of their continued allegiance to private property..
text_raw:
In  truth,  both  bourgeois  groups
were  largely  crushed  out,  and  their  members  practically  exterminated,  by  the  Right
because  of  their  earlier  allegiance  to  anti-militarism,  anti-clericalism,  and  anti-
monarchism,  and  by  the  Left  because  of  their  continued  allegiance  to  private  property..

text: Strangely enough, the only defenders these bourgeois found outside their own group was in the small but well-organized body of Stalinist Communists, whose ideological preconceptions of the natural course of social development were so strong that they insisted that Spain must pass through a period of bourgeois liberal capitalism and industrialization before it would be ripe for the later stage of totalitarian Communism.
text_raw:
Strangely  enough,  the  only  defenders  these  bourgeois  found  outside  their  own  group
was  in  the  small  but  well-organized  body  of  Stalinist  Communists,  whose  ideological
preconceptions  of  the  natural  course  of  social  development  were  so  strong  that  they
insisted  that  Spain  must  pass  through  a  period  of  bourgeois  liberal  capitalism  and
industrialization  before  it  would  be  ripe  for  the  later  stage  of  totalitarian  Communism.

text: This point of view, explicitly stated in Stalin's letter to the Spanish Left-wing Socialist leader, Largo Caballero, on September 21, 1936, warned against premature efforts toward social and economic reforms for which Spain's degree of industrial development made it quite unready, and called for general "anti-fascist" support for a liberal state against the "reactionaries" of the Right.
text_raw:
This  point  of  view,  explicitly  stated  in  Stalin's  letter  to  the  Spanish  Left-wing  Socialist
leader,  Largo  Caballero,  on  September  21,  1936,  warned  against  premature  efforts  toward
social  and  economic  reforms  for  which  Spain's  degree  of  industrial  development  made  it
quite  unready,  and  called  for  general  "anti-fascist"  support  for  a  liberal  state  against  the
"reactionaries"  of  the  Right.

text: In consequence of this point of view, the Communists in Spain were almost as willing to exterminate the revolutionaries of the Left (especially the anarchists, "Trotskyist" Communists, and left-wing Socialists) as they were to eliminate the reactionaries of the Right.
text_raw:
In  consequence  of  this  point  of  view,  the  Communists  in
Spain  were  almost  as  willing  to  exterminate  the  revolutionaries  of  the  Left  (especially  the
anarchists,  "Trotskyist"  Communists,  and  left-wing  Socialists)  as  they  were  to  eliminate
the  reactionaries  of  the  Right.

text: This complex and confused situation in Spain was made even more involved by the struggle between Castilian centralization (which was frequently unenlightened and reactionary) and the supporters of local autonomy and separatism (which were frequently progressive or even revolutionary) in Catalonia, the Basque country, Galicia, and elsewhere.
text_raw:
This  complex  and  confused  situation  in  Spain  was  made  even  more  involved  by  the
struggle  between  Castilian  centralization  (which  was  frequently  unenlightened  and
reactionary)  and  the  supporters  of  local  autonomy  and  separatism  (which  were  frequently
progressive  or  even  revolutionary)  in  Catalonia,  the  Basque  country,  Galicia,  and
elsewhere.

text: This struggle was intensified by the fact that industrialism had grown up only in Catalonia and the Basque provinces, and, accordingly, the strength of the revolutionary proletariat was strongest in the areas where separatism was strongest.
text_raw:
This  struggle  was  intensified  by  the  fact  that  industrialism  had  grown  up  only
in  Catalonia  and  the  Basque  provinces,  and,  accordingly,  the  strength  of  the  revolutionary
proletariat  was  strongest  in  the  areas  where  separatism  was  strongest.

text: Opposed to all these forces was that alignment of officers, upper clergy, landlords, and monarchists which came into existence after 1898 and especially after 1918.
text_raw:
Opposed  to  all  these  forces  was  that  alignment  of  officers,  upper  clergy,  landlords,  and
monarchists  which  came  into  existence  after  1898  and  especially  after  1918.

text: The army was the poorest in Europe and relatively the most expensive.
text_raw:
The  army
was  the  poorest  in  Europe  and  relatively  the  most  expensive.

text: There was a commissioned officer for every six men and a general for every 250 men.
text_raw:
There  was  a  commissioned
officer  for  every  six  men  and  a  general  for  every  250  men.

text: The men were miserably underpaid and mistreated, while the officers squandered fortunes.
text_raw:
The  men  were  miserably
underpaid  and  mistreated,  while  the  officers  squandered  fortunes.

text: The Ministry of War took about a third of the national budget, and most of that went to the officers.
text_raw:
The  Ministry  of  War
took  about  a  third  of  the  national  budget,  and  most  of  that  went  to  the  officers.

text: Money was wasted or stolen, especially in Morocco, in lumps of millions at a time for the benefit of officers and monarchist politicians.
text_raw:
Money
was  wasted  or  stolen,  especially  in  Morocco,  in  lumps  of  millions  at  a  time  for  the  benefit
of  officers  and  monarchist  politicians.

text: Everything was done on a lavish scale.
text_raw: Everything  was  done  on  a  lavish  scale.

text: For example, there were no less than five military academies.
text_raw:
For
example,  there  were  no  less  than  five  military  academies.

text: But the army remained so inefficient that it lost 13,000 men a year for ten years fighting the Riffs in Morocco, and in July 1921 lost 12,000 killed out of 20,000 engaged in one battle.
text_raw:
But  the  army  remained  so
inefficient  that  it  lost  13,000  men  a  year  for  ten  years  fighting  the  Riffs  in  Morocco,  and
in  July  1921  lost  12,000  killed  out  of  20,000  engaged  in  one  battle.

text: The army had the right, incredible as it may seem, to court-martial civilians, and did not hesitate to use this power to prevent criticism of its depredations.
text_raw:
The  army  had  the
right,  incredible  as  it  may  seem,  to  court-martial  civilians,  and  did  not  hesitate  to  use  this
power  to  prevent  criticism  of  its  depredations.

text: Nevertheless, the outcry against corruption and defeats in Morocco resulted in a parliamentary investigation.
text_raw:
Nevertheless,  the  outcry  against  corruption
and  defeats  in  Morocco  resulted  in  a  parliamentary  investigation.

text: To prevent this, a military coup under General Primo de Rivera, with the acquiescence of King Alfonso XIII, took over the government, dissolved the Cortes, and ended civil liberties, with martial law and a strict censorship throughout Spain (1923).
text_raw:
To  prevent  this,  a
military  coup  under  General  Primo  de  Rivera,  with  the  acquiescence  of  King  Alfonso
XIII,  took  over  the  government,  dissolved  the  Cortes,  and  ended  civil  liberties,  with
martial  law  and  a  strict  censorship  throughout  Spain  (1923).

text: The landlords not only monopolized the land but, more important than that, squandered their incomes with little effort to increase the productivity of their estates or to reduce the violent discontent of their peasant tenants and agricultural workers.
text_raw:
The  landlords  not  only  monopolized  the  land  but,  more  important  than  that,
squandered  their  incomes  with  little  effort  to  increase  the  productivity  of  their  estates  or
to  reduce  the  violent  discontent  of  their  peasant  tenants  and  agricultural  workers.

text: Of the 125 million acres of arable land in Spain, about 60 percent was not cultivated, while another 10 percent was left fallow.
text_raw:
Of  the
125  million  acres  of  arable  land  in  Spain,  about  60  percent  was  not  cultivated,  while
another  10  percent  was  left  fallow.

text: The need for irrigation, fertilizers, and new methods was acute, but very little was done to achieve them.
text_raw:
The  need  for  irrigation,  fertilizers,  and  new  methods
was  acute,  but  very  little  was  done  to  achieve  them.

text: On the contrary, while the Spanish
text_raw: On  the  contrary,  while  the  Spanish

text: grandees wasted millions of pesetas in the gambling casinos of the French Riviera, the technical equipment of their estates steadily deteriorated.
text_raw:
grandees  wasted  millions  of  pesetas  in  the  gambling  casinos  of  the  French  Riviera,  the
technical  equipment  of  their  estates  steadily  deteriorated.

text: Making use of the surplus agricultural population, they sought to increase rents and to decrease agricultural wages.
text_raw:
Making  use  of  the  surplus
agricultural  population,  they  sought  to  increase  rents  and  to  decrease  agricultural  wages.

text: To permit this they made every effort to make leases shorter in duration (not over a year) and revocable at the landlord's will and to break up every effort of agricultural workers to seek government or unionized action to raise wages, reduce hours, or improve working conditions.
text_raw:
To  permit  this  they  made  every  effort  to  make  leases  shorter  in  duration  (not  over  a  year)
and  revocable  at  the  landlord's  will  and  to  break  up  every  effort  of  agricultural  workers  to
seek  government  or  unionized  action  to  raise  wages,  reduce  hours,  or  improve  working
conditions.

text: While all this was going on, and while most of Spain was suffering from malnutrition, most of the land was untilled, and the owners refused to use irrigation facilities which had been built by the government.
text_raw:
While  all  this  was  going  on,  and  while  most  of  Spain  was  suffering  from  malnutrition,
most  of  the  land  was  untilled,  and  the  owners  refused  to  use  irrigation  facilities  which  had
been  built  by  the  government.

text: As a result, agricultural yields were the poorest in western Europe.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  agricultural  yields  were  the  poorest  in  western
Europe.

text: While 15 men owned about a million acres, and 15,000 men owned about half of all taxed land, almost 2 million owned the other half, frequently in plots too small for subsistence.
text_raw:
While  15  men  owned  about  a  million  acres,  and  15,000  men  owned  about  half  of
all  taxed  land,  almost  2  million  owned  the  other  half,  frequently  in  plots  too  small  for
subsistence.

text: About 2 million more, who were completely landless, worked 10 to 14 hours a day for about 2.5 pesetas (35 cents) a day for only six months in the year or paid exorbitant rents without any security of tenure.
text_raw:
About  2  million  more,  who  were  completely  landless,  worked  10  to  14  hours
a  day  for  about  2.5  pesetas  (35  cents)  a  day  for  only  six  months  in  the  year  or  paid
exorbitant  rents  without  any  security  of  tenure.

text: In the Church, while the ordinary priests, especially in the villages, shared the poverty and tribulations of the people, and did so with pious devotion, the upper clergy were closely allied with the government and the forces of reaction.
text_raw:
In  the  Church,  while  the  ordinary  priests,  especially  in  the  villages,  shared  the  poverty
and  tribulations  of  the  people,  and  did  so  with  pious  devotion,  the  upper  clergy  were
closely  allied  with  the  government  and  the  forces  of  reaction.

text: The bishops and archbishops were named by the monarchy and were partly supported by an annual grant from the government as a result of the Concordat of 1851.
text_raw:
The  bishops  and
archbishops  were  named  by  the  monarchy  and  were  partly  supported  by  an  annual  grant
from  the  government  as  a  result  of  the  Concordat  of  1851.

text: Moreover, the clergy and the government were inextricably intertwined, the upper clergy having seats in the upper chamber, control of education, censorship, marriage, and the willing ear of the king.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  clergy  and  the
government  were  inextricably  intertwined,  the  upper  clergy  having  seats  in  the  upper
chamber,  control  of  education,  censorship,  marriage,  and  the  willing  ear  of  the  king.

text: In consequence of this alliance of the upper clergy with the government and the forces of reaction, all the animosities built up against the latter came to be directed against the former also.
text_raw:
In
consequence  of  this  alliance  of  the  upper  clergy  with  the  government  and  the  forces  of
reaction,  all  the  animosities  built  up  against  the  latter  came  to  be  directed  against  the
former  also.

text: Although the Spanish people remained universally and profoundly Catholic, and found no attraction whatever in Protestantism and very little attraction in rational skepticism of the French sort, they also became indelibly anti-clerical.
text_raw:
Although  the  Spanish  people  remained  universally  and  profoundly  Catholic,
and  found  no  attraction  whatever  in  Protestantism  and  very  little  attraction  in  rational
skepticism  of  the  French  sort,  they  also  became  indelibly  anti-clerical.

text: This attitude was reflected in the notable reluctance of Spanish men to go to church or receive the sacraments during the interval between confirmation at the age of thirteen and extreme unction on their deathbeds.
text_raw:
This  attitude  was
reflected  in  the  notable  reluctance  of  Spanish  men  to  go  to  church  or  receive  the
sacraments  during  the  interval  between  confirmation  at  the  age  of  thirteen  and  extreme
unction  on  their  deathbeds.

text: It was also reflected in the proclivity of the Spanish people for burning churches.
text_raw:
It  was  also  reflected  in  the  proclivity  of  the  Spanish  people
for  burning  churches.

text: While other peoples expressed turbulent outbursts of anti- governmental feeling in attacks on prisons, post offices, banks, or radio stations, the Spaniards invariably burn churches, and have done so for at least a century.
text_raw:
While  other  peoples  expressed  turbulent  outbursts  of  anti-
governmental  feeling  in  attacks  on  prisons,  post  offices,  banks,  or  radio  stations,  the
Spaniards  invariably  burn  churches,  and  have  done  so  for  at  least  a  century.

text: There were great outbursts of this strange custom in 1808, 1835, 1874, 1909, 1931, and 1936, and it was indulged in by the Right as well as by the Left.
text_raw:
There  were
great  outbursts  of  this  strange  custom  in  1808,  1835,  1874,  1909,  1931,  and  1936,  and  it
was  indulged  in  by  the  Right  as  well  as  by  the  Left.

text: The monarchists were divided into at least two groups.
text_raw: The  monarchists  were  divided  into  at  least  two  groups.

text: One of these, the Renovacion Espanola, supported the dynasty of Isabella II (1833-1868), while the other, the Comunion Tradicionalista, supported the claims of Isabella's uncle, Don Carlos.
text_raw:
One  of  these,  the  Renovacion
Espanola,  supported  the  dynasty  of  Isabella  II  (1833-1868),  while  the  other,  the
Comunion  Tradicionalista,  supported  the  claims  of  Isabella's  uncle,  Don  Carlos.

text: The Renovation group was a clique of wealthy landowners who used their contracts with the government to evade taxes, and to obtain concessions and sinecures for themselves and their friends.
text_raw:
The
Renovation  group  was  a  clique  of  wealthy  landowners  who  used  their  contracts  with  the
government  to  evade  taxes,  and  to  obtain  concessions  and  sinecures  for  themselves  and
their  friends.

text: The Carlists were a fanatically intolerant and murderous group from remote rural regions of Spain, and were almost entirely clerical and reactionary in their aims.
text_raw:
The  Carlists  were  a  fanatically  intolerant  and  murderous  group  from  remote
rural  regions  of  Spain,  and  were  almost  entirely  clerical  and  reactionary  in  their  aims.

text: All these groups, the landlords, officers, higher clergy, and monarchists (except the Carlists), were interest groups seeking to utilize Spain for their own power and profit.
text_raw:
All  these  groups,  the  landlords,  officers,  higher  clergy,  and  monarchists  (except  the
Carlists),  were  interest  groups  seeking  to  utilize  Spain  for  their  own  power  and  profit.

text: The threat to their positions following the First World War and the defeats in Morocco led them to support Primo de Rivera's dictatorship.
text_raw:
The  threat  to  their  positions  following  the  First  World  War  and  the  defeats  in  Morocco
led  them  to  support  Primo  de  Rivera's  dictatorship.

text: However, the general's personal instability and his efforts to appease the industrialists of Catalonia, as well as his unbalanced budgets and his efforts to build up a popular following by cooperating with laboring groups, led to a shift of support, and he was forced to resign in 1930, following an unsuccessful officers' revolt in 1929.
text_raw:
However,  the  general's  personal
instability  and  his  efforts  to  appease  the  industrialists  of  Catalonia,  as  well  as  his
unbalanced  budgets  and  his  efforts  to  build  up  a  popular  following  by  cooperating  with
laboring  groups,  led  to  a  shift  of  support,  and  he  was  forced  to  resign  in  1930,  following
an  unsuccessful  officers'  revolt  in  1929.

text: Realizing the danger to his dynasty from his association with an unpopular dictatorship, Alfonso XIII tried to restore the constitutional government.
text_raw:
Realizing  the  danger  to  his  dynasty  from  his  association  with  an  unpopular
dictatorship,  Alfonso  XIII  tried  to  restore  the  constitutional  government.

text: As a first step, he ordered municipal elections for April 12, 1931.
text_raw:
As  a  first  step,
he  ordered  municipal  elections  for  April  12,  1931.

text: Such elections had been managed successfully by wholesale electoral corruption before 1923, and it was believed that this control could be maintained.
text_raw:
Such  elections  had  been  managed
successfully  by  wholesale  electoral  corruption  before  1923,  and  it  was  believed  that  this
control  could  be  maintained.

text: It was maintained in the rural areas, but, in 46 out of 50 provincial capitals, the anti-monarchical forces were victorious.
text_raw:
It  was  maintained  in  the  rural  areas,  but,  in  46  out  of  50
provincial  capitals,  the  anti-monarchical  forces  were  victorious.

text: When these forces demanded Alfonso's abdication, he called upon General Sanjurjo, commander of the Civil Guard, for support.
text_raw:
When  these  forces
demanded  Alfonso's  abdication,  he  called  upon  General  Sanjurjo,  commander  of  the  Civil
Guard,  for  support.

text: It was refused, and Alfonso fled to France (April 14, 1931).
text_raw: It  was  refused,  and  Alfonso  fled  to  France  (April  14,  1931).

text: The republicans at once began to organize their victory, electing a Constituent Assembly in June 1931, and establishing an ultramodern unicameral, parliamentary government with universal suffrage, separation of Church and State, secularization of education, local autonomy for separatist areas, and power to socialize the great estates or the public utilities.
text_raw:
The  republicans  at  once  began  to  organize  their  victory,  electing  a  Constituent
Assembly  in  June  1931,  and  establishing  an  ultramodern  unicameral,  parliamentary
government  with  universal  suffrage,  separation  of  Church  and  State,  secularization  of
education,  local  autonomy  for  separatist  areas,  and  power  to  socialize  the  great  estates  or
the  public  utilities.

text: Such a government, especially the provisions for a parliamentary regime with universal suffrage, was quite unfitted for Spain with its high illiteracy, its weak middle class, and its great inequalities of economic power.
text_raw:
Such  a  government,  especially  the  provisions  for  a  parliamentary
regime  with  universal  suffrage,  was  quite  unfitted  for  Spain  with  its  high  illiteracy,  its
weak  middle  class,  and  its  great  inequalities  of  economic  power.

text: The republic lasted only five years before the Civil War began on July 18, 1936.
text_raw: The  republic  lasted  only  five  years  before  the  Civil  War  began  on  July  18,  1936.

text: During that period it was challenged constantly from the Right and from the extreme Left, the former offering the greatest test because it commanded economic, military, and ideological power through the landlords, the army, and the Church.
text_raw:
During  that  period  it  was  challenged  constantly  from  the  Right  and  from  the  extreme
Left,  the  former  offering  the  greatest  test  because  it  commanded  economic,  military,  and
ideological  power  through  the  landlords,  the  army,  and  the  Church.

text: During this time the nation was ruled by coalition governments: first by a coalition of the Left from December 1931 to September, 1933; then by the Center from September to October 1934; third, by a coalition of the Right from October 1934 to the Popular Front election of February 1936; and, last, by the Left after February 1936.
text_raw:
During  this  time  the
nation  was  ruled  by  coalition  governments:  first  by  a  coalition  of  the  Left  from  December
1931  to  September,  1933;  then  by  the  Center  from  September  to  October  1934;  third,  by
a  coalition  of  the  Right  from  October  1934  to  the  Popular  Front  election  of  February
1936;  and,  last,  by  the  Left  after  February  1936.

text: These shifts of government resulted from changes in alignments of the multitude of political parties.
text_raw:
These  shifts  of  government  resulted  from
changes  in  alignments  of  the  multitude  of  political  parties.

text: The Right formed a coalition under Jose Maria Gil Robles in February 1933, while the Left formed a coalition under Manuel Azana in February 1936.
text_raw:
The  Right  formed  a  coalition
under  Jose  Maria  Gil  Robles  in  February  1933,  while  the  Left  formed  a  coalition  under
Manuel  Azana  in  February  1936.

text: As a result, the Right coalition won the second parliamentary election in November 1933, while the Left won the third, or Popular Front, election of February 1936.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  the  Right  coalition  won  the  second
parliamentary  election  in  November  1933,  while  the  Left  won  the  third,  or  Popular  Front,
election  of  February  1936.

text: Because of this shifting of governments, the liberal program which was enacted into law in 1931-1933 was annulled or unenforced in 1933-1936.
text_raw:
Because  of  this  shifting  of  governments,  the  liberal  program  which  was  enacted  into
law  in  1931-1933  was  annulled  or  unenforced  in  1933-1936.

text: This program included educational reform, army reform, separation of Church and State, agrarian reform, and social assistance for peasants and workers.
text_raw:
This  program  included
educational  reform,  army  reform,  separation  of  Church  and  State,  agrarian  reform,  and
social  assistance  for  peasants  and  workers.

text: In an effort to reduce illiteracy (which was over 45 percent in 1930), the republic created thousands of new schools and new teachers, raised teachers' salaries to a minimum of about $450 a year (this affected 21,500 out of 37,500 teachers), founded over a thousand new libraries, and encouraged adult education..
text_raw:
In  an  effort  to  reduce  illiteracy  (which  was  over  45  percent  in  1930),  the  republic
created  thousands  of  new  schools  and  new  teachers,  raised  teachers'  salaries  to  a
minimum  of  about  $450  a  year  (this  affected  21,500  out  of  37,500  teachers),  founded
over  a  thousand  new  libraries,  and  encouraged  adult  education..

text: Efforts were made to obtain a smaller, better paid, more efficient army.
text_raw: Efforts  were  made  to  obtain  a  smaller,  better  paid,  more  efficient  army.

text: The 23,000 officers (including 258 generals) were reduced to 9,500 officers (including 86 generals), the surplus being retired on full pay.
text_raw:
The  23,000
officers  (including  258  generals)  were  reduced  to  9,500  officers  (including  86  generals),
the  surplus  being  retired  on  full  pay.

text: The number of enlisted men was reduced to about 100,000 with higher pay.
text_raw:
The  number  of  enlisted  men  was  reduced  to  about
100,000  with  higher  pay.

text: Organization was completely reformed.
text_raw: Organization  was  completely  reformed.

text: As a result, over $14 million was saved on the cost of the army in the first year (1931-1932).
text_raw:
As  a  result,  over  $14
million  was  saved  on  the  cost  of  the  army  in  the  first  year  (1931-1932).

text: Unfortunately, nothing was done to make the army loyal to the new regime.
text_raw:
Unfortunately,
nothing  was  done  to  make  the  army  loyal  to  the  new  regime.

text: Since the choice to retire or stay on active duty was purely voluntary, the republican officers tended to retire, the monarchists to stay on, with the result that the army of the republic was more monarchist in its sympathies than the army had been before 1931.
text_raw:
Since  the  choice  to  retire  or
stay  on  active  duty  was  purely  voluntary,  the  republican  officers  tended  to  retire,  the
monarchists  to  stay  on,  with  the  result  that  the  army  of  the  republic  was  more  monarchist
in  its  sympathies  than  the  army  had  been  before  1931.

text: Although the officers, disgruntled at their narrowing opportunities for enriching themselves, were openly disrespectful and insubordinate toward the republic, almost nothing was done to remedy this.
text_raw:
Although  the  officers,  disgruntled
at  their  narrowing  opportunities  for  enriching  themselves,  were  openly  disrespectful  and
insubordinate  toward  the  republic,  almost  nothing  was  done  to  remedy  this.

text: The Church was subjected to laws establishing complete separation of Church and State.
text_raw:
The  Church  was  subjected  to  laws  establishing  complete  separation  of  Church  and
State.

text: The government gave up its right to nominate the upper clergy, ended the annual grant to the Church, took ownership (but not possession) of Church property, forbade teaching in public schools by the clergy, established religious toleration and civil divorce, and required that all corporations (including religious orders and trade unions) must register with the government and publish financial accounts.
text_raw:
The  government  gave  up  its  right  to  nominate  the  upper  clergy,  ended  the  annual
grant  to  the  Church,  took  ownership  (but  not  possession)  of  Church  property,  forbade
teaching  in  public  schools  by  the  clergy,  established  religious  toleration  and  civil  divorce,
and  required  that  all  corporations  (including  religious  orders  and  trade  unions)  must
register  with  the  government  and  publish  financial  accounts.

text: To assist the peasants and workers, mixed juries were established to hear rural rent disputes; importation of labor from one district to another for wage-breaking purposes was forbidden; and credit was provided for peasants to obtain land, seed, or fertilizers on favorable terms.
text_raw:
To  assist  the  peasants  and  workers,  mixed  juries  were  established  to  hear  rural  rent
disputes;  importation  of  labor  from  one  district  to  another  for  wage-breaking  purposes
was  forbidden;  and  credit  was  provided  for  peasants  to  obtain  land,  seed,  or  fertilizers  on
favorable  terms.

text: Manorial lands, those of monarchists who had fled with Alfonso, and customarily uncultivated lands were expropriated with compensation, to provide farms for a new class of peasant proprietors.
text_raw:
Manorial  lands,  those  of  monarchists  who  had  fled  with  Alfonso,  and
customarily  uncultivated  lands  were  expropriated  with  compensation,  to  provide  farms
for  a  new  class  of  peasant  proprietors.

text: Most of these reforms went into effect only partially or not at all.
text_raw: Most  of  these  reforms  went  into  effect  only  partially  or  not  at  all.

text: The annual contribution to the Church could not be ended, because the Spanish people refused to contribute voluntarily to the Church, and an alternative system of ecclesiastical taxation enforced by the state had to be set up.
text_raw:
The  annual
contribution  to  the  Church  could  not  be  ended,  because  the  Spanish  people  refused  to
contribute  voluntarily  to  the  Church,  and  an  alternative  system  of  ecclesiastical  taxation
enforced  by  the  state  had  to  be  set  up.

text: Few of the abandoned or poorly cultivated estates could be expropriated because of lack of money for compensation.
text_raw:
Few  of  the  abandoned  or  poorly  cultivated  estates
could  be  expropriated  because  of  lack  of  money  for  compensation.

text: The clergy could not be excluded from teaching because of the lack of trained teachers.
text_raw:
The  clergy  could  not
be  excluded  from  teaching  because  of  the  lack  of  trained  teachers.

text: Most expropriated ecclesiastical property was left in the control of the Church either because it was necessary for religious and social services or because it could not be tracked down.
text_raw:
Most  expropriated
ecclesiastical  property  was  left  in  the  control  of  the  Church  either  because  it  was
necessary  for  religious  and  social  services  or  because  it  could  not  be  tracked  down.

text: The conservative groups reacted violently against the republic almost as soon as it began.
text_raw:
The  conservative  groups  reacted  violently  against  the  republic  almost  as  soon  as  it
began.

text: In fact, the monarchists criticized Alfonso for leaving without a struggle, while the upper clergy and landlords ostracized the papal legate for his efforts to make the former adopt a neutral attitude toward the new regime.
text_raw:
In  fact,  the  monarchists  criticized  Alfonso  for  leaving  without  a  struggle,  while  the
upper  clergy  and  landlords  ostracized  the  papal  legate  for  his  efforts  to  make  the  former
adopt  a  neutral  attitude  toward  the  new  regime.

text: As a result, three plots began to be formed against the republic, the one monarchist led by Calvo Sotelo in parliament and by Antonio Goicoechea behind the scenes; the second a parliamentary alliance of landlords
text_raw:
As  a  result,  three  plots  began  to  be
formed  against  the  republic,  the  one  monarchist  led  by  Calvo  Sotelo  in  parliament  and  by
Antonio  Goicoechea  behind  the  scenes;  the  second  a  parliamentary  alliance  of  landlords

text: and clericals under Jose Maria Gil Robles; and the last a conspiracy of officers under Generals Emilio Barrera and Jose Sanjurjo.
text_raw:
and  clericals  under  Jose  Maria  Gil  Robles;  and  the  last  a  conspiracy  of  officers  under
Generals  Emilio  Barrera  and  Jose  Sanjurjo.

text: Sanjurjo led an unsuccessful rebellion at Seville in August 1932.
text_raw:
Sanjurjo  led  an  unsuccessful  rebellion  at
Seville  in  August  1932.

text: When it collapsed from lack of public support, he was arrested, condemned to death, reprieved, and finally released (with all his back pay) in 1934.
text_raw:
When  it  collapsed  from  lack  of  public  support,  he  was  arrested,
condemned  to  death,  reprieved,  and  finally  released  (with  all  his  back  pay)  in  1934.

text: Barrera was arrested but released by the courts.
text_raw: Barrera  was  arrested  but  released  by  the  courts.

text: Both generals began to prepare for the rebellion of 1936.
text_raw:
Both  generals  began  to  prepare  for  the
rebellion  of  1936.

text: In the meantime, the monarchist conspiracy was organized by former King Alfonso from abroad as early as May 1931.
text_raw:
In  the  meantime,  the  monarchist  conspiracy  was  organized  by  former  King  Alfonso
from  abroad  as  early  as  May  1931.

text: As part of this movement a new political party was founded under Sotelo, a "research" organization known as Spanish Action was set up "to publish texts from great thinkers on the legality of revolution," a war chest of 1.5 million pesetas was created, and an underground conspiracy was drawn up under the leadership of Antonio Goicoechea.
text_raw:
As  part  of  this  movement  a  new  political  party  was
founded  under  Sotelo,  a  "research"  organization  known  as  Spanish  Action  was  set  up  "to
publish  texts  from  great  thinkers  on  the  legality  of  revolution,"  a  war  chest  of  1.5  million
pesetas  was  created,  and  an  underground  conspiracy  was  drawn  up  under  the  leadership
of  Antonio  Goicoechea.

text: This last action was taken at a meeting in Paris presided over by Alfonso himself (September 29, 932).
text_raw:
This  last  action  was  taken  at  a  meeting  in  Paris  presided  over  by
Alfonso  himself  (September  29,  932).

text: Goicoechea performed his task with great skill, under the eyes of a government which refused to take preventive action because of its own liberal and legalistic scruples.
text_raw:
Goicoechea  performed  his  task  with  great  skill,  under  the  eyes  of  a  government  which
refused  to  take  preventive  action  because  of  its  own  liberal  and  legalistic  scruples.

text: He organized an alliance of the officers, the Carlists, and his own Alfonsist party.
text_raw:
He
organized  an  alliance  of  the  officers,  the  Carlists,  and  his  own  Alfonsist  party.

text: Four men from these three groups then signed an agreement with Mussolini on March 31, 1934.
text_raw:
Four  men
from  these  three  groups  then  signed  an  agreement  with  Mussolini  on  March  31,  1934.

text: By this agreement the Duce of Fascism promised arms, money, and diplomatic support to the revolutionary movement and gave the conspirators a first-installment payment of 1,500,000 pesetas, 10,000 rifles, 10,000 grenades, and 200 machine guns.
text_raw:
By
this  agreement  the  Duce  of  Fascism  promised  arms,  money,  and  diplomatic  support  to  the
revolutionary  movement  and  gave  the  conspirators  a  first-installment  payment  of
1,500,000  pesetas,  10,000  rifles,  10,000  grenades,  and  200  machine  guns.

text: In return the signers, Lieutenant General Emilio Barrera, Antonio Lizarza, Rafael de Olazabal, and Antonio Goicoechea, promised when they came to power to denounce the existing French-Spanish "secret treaty," and to sign with Mussolini an agreement establishing a joint export policy between Spain and Italy, as well as an agreement to maintain the status quo in the western Mediterranean. ,

text: In the meantime, Gil Robles's coalition, known as CEDA (Spanish Confederation of Autonomous Right Parties), along with his own clerical party (Popular Action) and the Agrarian Party of the big landlords, was able to replace the Left Republican Manuel Azana by the Right Republican Alejandro Lerroux as prime minister (September 1933).
text_raw:
In  the  meantime,  Gil  Robles's  coalition,  known  as  CEDA  (Spanish  Confederation  of
Autonomous  Right  Parties),  along  with  his  own  clerical  party  (Popular  Action)  and  the
Agrarian  Party  of  the  big  landlords,  was  able  to  replace  the  Left  Republican  Manuel
Azana  by  the  Right  Republican  Alejandro  Lerroux  as  prime  minister  (September  1933).

text: It then called new elections in November 1934, and won a victory with 213 seats for the Right, 139 for the Center, and 121 for the Left.
text_raw:
It  then  called  new  elections  in  November  1934,  and  won  a  victory  with  213  seats  for  the
Right,  139  for  the  Center,  and  121  for  the  Left.

text: The Center Cabinet continued in office, supported by the votes of the Right.
text_raw:
The  Center  Cabinet  continued  in  office,
supported  by  the  votes  of  the  Right.

text: It revoked many of the reforms of 1931-1933, allowed most of the rest to go unenforced, released all the Rightist conspirators from prison (including Sanjurjo), gave an amnesty to thousands of monarchist plotters and exiles, and restored their expropriated estates.
text_raw:
It  revoked  many  of  the  reforms  of  1931-1933,
allowed  most  of  the  rest  to  go  unenforced,  released  all  the  Rightist  conspirators  from
prison  (including  Sanjurjo),  gave  an  amnesty  to  thousands  of  monarchist  plotters  and
exiles,  and  restored  their  expropriated  estates.

text: By a process of consolidating portfolios and abolishing Cabinet seats, Gil Robles slowly reduced the Cabinet from thirteen ministers at the end of 1933 to nine two years later.
text_raw:
By  a  process  of  consolidating  portfolios
and  abolishing  Cabinet  seats,  Gil  Robles  slowly  reduced  the  Cabinet  from  thirteen
ministers  at  the  end  of  1933  to  nine  two  years  later.

text: Of these CEDA took three in October 1934 and five in March 1935.
text_raw:
Of  these  CEDA  took  three  in  October
1934  and  five  in  March  1935.

text: The advent to office of CEDA in October 1934 led to a violent agitation which burst into open revolt in the two separatist centers of the Basque country and Catalonia.
text_raw:
The  advent  to  office  of  CEDA  in  October  1934  led  to  a  violent  agitation  which  burst
into  open  revolt  in  the  two  separatist  centers  of  the  Basque  country  and  Catalonia.

text: The latter, led by the bourgeois Left, received little support from the workers, and collapsed at once; the uprising in Asturias, however, spearheaded by anarchist miners hurling
text_raw:
The
latter,  led  by  the  bourgeois  Left,  received  little  support  from  the  workers,  and  collapsed  at

text: dynamite from slings, lasted for nine days.

text: The government used the Foreign Legion and Moors, brought from Morocco by sea, and crushed the rebels without mercy.
text_raw:
The  government  used  the  Foreign  Legion  and
Moors,  brought  from  Morocco  by  sea,  and  crushed  the  rebels  without  mercy.

text: The latter suffered at least 5,000 casualties, of which a third were dead.
text_raw:
The  latter
suffered  at  least  5,000  casualties,  of  which  a  third  were  dead.

text: After the uprising was quelled, all the Socialist press was silenced and 25,000 suspects were thrown into prison.
text_raw:
After  the  uprising  was
quelled,  all  the  Socialist  press  was  silenced  and  25,000  suspects  were  thrown  into  prison.

text: This uprising of October 1934, although crushed, served to split the oligarchy.
text_raw: This  uprising  of  October  1934,  although  crushed,  served  to  split  the  oligarchy.

text: The fact that the government had sent Moors to the most Catholic part of Spain (where they had never penetrated during the Saracen invasions) and the demands of the army, monarchists, and the biggest landlords for a ruthless dictatorship alarmed the leaders of the Church and the president of the republic, Alcala Zamora.
text_raw:
The
fact  that  the  government  had  sent  Moors  to  the  most  Catholic  part  of  Spain  (where  they
had  never  penetrated  during  the  Saracen  invasions)  and  the  demands  of  the  army,
monarchists,  and  the  biggest  landlords  for  a  ruthless  dictatorship  alarmed  the  leaders  of
the  Church  and  the  president  of  the  republic,  Alcala  Zamora.

text: This ultimately blocked Gil Robles's road to power by parliamentary methods.
text_raw:
This  ultimately  blocked  Gil
Robles's  road  to  power  by  parliamentary  methods.

text: After March 1935 he controlled the portfolios of Justice, Industry and Commerce, Labor, and Communications, but could not get the Interior (which controlled the police).
text_raw:
After  March  1935  he  controlled  the
portfolios  of  Justice,  Industry  and  Commerce,  Labor,  and  Communications,  but  could  not
get  the  Interior  (which  controlled  the  police).

text: This was held by Portela Valladares, a moderate close to Zamora.
text_raw:
This  was  held  by  Portela  Valladares,  a
moderate  close  to  Zamora.

text: Gil Robles as minister of war encouraged reactionary control of the army and even put General Franco in as his undersecretary for war, but he could not get rid of Portela Valladares.
text_raw:
Gil  Robles  as  minister  of  war  encouraged  reactionary  control
of  the  army  and  even  put  General  Franco  in  as  his  undersecretary  for  war,  but  he  could
not  get  rid  of  Portela  Valladares.

text: Finally, he demanded that the police be transferred from the Ministry of Interior to his own Ministry of War.
text_raw:
Finally,  he  demanded  that  the  police  be  transferred  from
the  Ministry  of  Interior  to  his  own  Ministry  of  War.

text: When this was refused, he upset the Cabinet, but, instead of getting more from this action, he got less, for Alcala Zamora handed the premier's seat over to moderates (Joaquin Chapaprieta, a businessman, followed by Portela Valladares) and ordered new elections.
text_raw:
When  this  was  refused,  he  upset  the
Cabinet,  but,  instead  of  getting  more  from  this  action,  he  got  less,  for  Alcala  Zamora
handed  the  premier's  seat  over  to  moderates  (Joaquin  Chapaprieta,  a  businessman,
followed  by  Portela  Valladares)  and  ordered  new  elections.

text: For these elections of February 1936, the parties of the Left formed a coalition, the Popular Front, with a published program and plan of action.
text_raw:
For  these  elections  of  February  1936,  the  parties  of  the  Left  formed  a  coalition,  the
Popular  Front,  with  a  published  program  and  plan  of  action.

text: The program was of a moderate Left character, promising a full restoration of the constitution, amnesty for political crimes committed after November 1933, civil liberties, an independent judiciary, minimum wages, protection for tenants, reform of taxation, credit, banking, and the police, and public works.
text_raw:
The  program  was  of  a
moderate  Left  character,  promising  a  full  restoration  of  the  constitution,  amnesty  for
political  crimes  committed  after  November  1933,  civil  liberties,  an  independent  judiciary,
minimum  wages,  protection  for  tenants,  reform  of  taxation,  credit,  banking,  and  the
police,  and  public  works.

text: It repudiated the Socialist program for nationalization of the land, the banks, and industry.
text_raw:
It  repudiated  the  Socialist  program  for  nationalization  of  the
land,  the  banks,  and  industry.

text: The plan of action provided that while all the Popular Front parties would support the government by their votes in the Cortes, only the bourgeois parties would hold seats in the Cabinet, while the workers' parties, such as the Socialists, would remain outside.
text_raw:
The  plan  of  action  provided  that  while  all  the  Popular  Front  parties  would  support  the
government  by  their  votes  in  the  Cortes,  only  the  bourgeois  parties  would  hold  seats  in
the  Cabinet,  while  the  workers'  parties,  such  as  the  Socialists,  would  remain  outside.

text: The election of February 16, 1936 followed a campaign of violence and terrorism in which the worst offenders were the members of a microscopic new political party calling itself the Falange.
text_raw:
The  election  of  February  16,  1936  followed  a  campaign  of  violence  and  terrorism  in
which  the  worst  offenders  were  the  members  of  a  microscopic  new  political  party  calling
itself  the  Falange.

text: Openly Fascist on the Italian model, and consisting largely of a small number of rich and irresponsible youths, this group was led by Primo de Rivera the younger.
text_raw:
Openly  Fascist  on  the  Italian  model,  and  consisting  largely  of  a  small
number  of  rich  and  irresponsible  youths,  this  group  was  led  by  Primo  de  Rivera  the
younger.

text: In the election, the Popular Front captured 266 out of 473 seats, while the Right had 153 and the Center only 54;
text_raw:
In  the  election,  the  Popular  Front  captured  266  out  of  473  seats,  while  the  Right
had  153  and  the  Center  only  54;

text: CEDA had 96, the Socialists 87, Azana's Republican Left 81, the Communists 14.
text_raw:
CEDA  had  96,  the  Socialists  87,  Azana's  Republican
Left  81,  the  Communists  14.

text: The defeated forces of the Right refused to accept the results of this election.
text_raw: The  defeated  forces  of  the  Right  refused  to  accept  the  results  of  this  election.

text: As soon as the results were known, Sotelo tried to persuade Portela Valladares to hand over the government to General Franco.
text_raw:
As  soon
as  the  results  were  known,  Sotelo  tried  to  persuade  Portela  Valladares  to  hand  over  the
government  to  General  Franco.

text: That was rebuffed.
text_raw: That  was  rebuffed.

text: The same day the Falange attacked workers who were celebrating.
text_raw:
The  same  day  the  Falange  attacked
workers  who  were  celebrating.

text_raw:
On  February  20th  the  conspirators  met  and  decided  their
plans  were  not  yet  ripe.

transferred  General  Franco  to  the  Canary  Islands,  General  Manuel  Goded  to  the

The  day  before  Franco  left  Madrid,  he  met
the  chief  conspirators  at  the  home  of  the  monarchist  deputy  Serrano  Delgado.

They
completed  their  plans  for  a  military  revolt  but  fixed  no  date.

text: Property was seized or destroyed, and churches were burned on all sides.

Property  was  seized  or  destroyed,  and  churches  were
burned  on  all  sides.

text: On March 12th the Socialist lawyer who had drafted the constitution of 1931 was fired at from an automobile, and his companion was killed.

On  March  12th  the  Socialist  lawyer  who  had  drafted  the  constitution
of  1931  was  fired  at  from  an  automobile,  and  his  companion  was  killed.

text: Five men were brought to trial; the judge was assassinated (April 13th).
text_raw:
Five  men  were
brought  to  trial;  the  judge  was  assassinated  (April  13th).

text_raw:
The  next  day  a  bomb  exploded
beneath  a  platform  from  which  the  new  Cabinet  was  reviewing  the  troops,  and  a  police

The  mob  retaliated  by  assaults  on  monarchists  and  by

text_raw: On  March  15th  there  was  an  attempt  to  assassinate  Largo  Caballero.

text: By May the monarchist assassins were beginning to concentrate on the officers of the Assault Guards, the only branch of the police which was completely loyal to the republic.

By  May  the  monarchist  assassins  were  beginning  to  concentrate  on  the  officers  of  the

In  May  the  captain  of  this  force,  Faraudo,  was  killed  by  shots  from  a  speeding

The  uprising,  however,  was  already  beginning  in  England  and  in  Italy,
and  broke  out  in  Morocco  on  July  18th..

text: One of the chief figures in the conspiracy in England was Douglas Jerrold, a well- known editor, who has revealed some details in his autobiography.

At  the  end  of  May
1936,  he  obtained  "so  machine  guns  and  a  half  million  rounds  of  S.A.  ammunition"  for

text: These planes went into action in support of the revolt as early as July 27th; on July 30th four such planes, still carrying their orders of July 15th, landed in French Algeria, and were interned.
