These  planes  went  into  action  in
support  of  the  revolt  as  early  as  July  27th;  on  July  30th  four  such  planes,  still  carrying
their  orders  of  July  15th,  landed  in  French  Algeria,  and  were  interned.

text: German intervention was less carefully planned.
text_raw: German  intervention  was  less  carefully  planned.

text: It would appear that Sanjurjo went to Berlin on February 4, 1936, but could get no commitment beyond a promise to provide the necessary transport planes to move the Moroccan forces to Spain if the Spanish fleet made transport by sea dangerous by remaining loyal to the government.
text_raw:
It  would  appear  that  Sanjurjo  went  to
Berlin  on  February  4,  1936,  but  could  get  no  commitment  beyond  a  promise  to  provide
the  necessary  transport  planes  to  move  the  Moroccan  forces  to  Spain  if  the  Spanish  fleet
made  transport  by  sea  dangerous  by  remaining  loyal  to  the  government.

text: As soon as Franco reached Morocco from the Canaries on July 18th, he appealed for these planes through a personal emissary to Hitler and through the German consul at Tetuan.
text_raw:
As  soon  as
Franco  reached  Morocco  from  the  Canaries  on  July  18th,  he  appealed  for  these  planes
through  a  personal  emissary  to  Hitler  and  through  the  German  consul  at  Tetuan.

text: The former met Hitler on July 24th, and was promised assistance.
text_raw:
The
former  met  Hitler  on  July  24th,  and  was  promised  assistance.

text: The plans to intervene were drawn up the same night by Hitler, Goring, and General Werner von Blomberg.
text_raw:
The  plans  to  intervene  were
drawn  up  the  same  night  by  Hitler,  Goring,  and  General  Werner  von  Blomberg.

text: Thirty planes with German crews were sent to Spain by August 8th, and the first one was captured by the Loyalist government the next day.
text_raw:
Thirty
planes  with  German  crews  were  sent  to  Spain  by  August  8th,  and  the  first  one  was
captured  by  the  Loyalist  government  the  next  day.

text: In the meantime, the revolt was a failure.
text_raw: In  the  meantime,  the  revolt  was  a  failure.

text: The navy remained loyal because the crews overthrew their officers; the air force generally remained loyal; the army revolted, along with much of the police, but, except in isolated areas, these rebellious units were overcome.
text_raw:
The  navy  remained  loyal  because  the  crews
overthrew  their  officers;  the  air  force  generally  remained  loyal;  the  army  revolted,  along
with  much  of  the  police,  but,  except  in  isolated  areas,  these  rebellious  units  were
overcome.

text: At the first news of the revolt, the people, led by the labor unions and the militia of the workers' political parties, demanded arms.
text_raw:
At  the  first  news  of  the  revolt,  the  people,  led  by  the  labor  unions  and  the
militia  of  the  workers'  political  parties,  demanded  arms.

text: The government was reluctant because of fear of revolution from the Left as well as the Right and delayed for several days.
text_raw:
The  government  was  reluctant
because  of  fear  of  revolution  from  the  Left  as  well  as  the  Right  and  delayed  for  several
days.

text: Two Cabinets resigned on July 18th and July 19th rather than arm the Left, but a new Cabinet under Jose Giral was willing to do so.
text_raw:
Two  Cabinets  resigned  on  July  18th  and  July  19th  rather  than  arm  the  Left,  but  a
new  Cabinet  under  Jose  Giral  was  willing  to  do  so.

text: However, because arms were lacking, orders were sent at once to France.
text_raw:
However,  because  arms  were  lacking,
orders  were  sent  at  once  to  France.

text: The recognized government in Madrid had the right to buy arms abroad and was even bound to do so to some degree by the existing commercial treaty with France.
text_raw:
The  recognized  government  in  Madrid  had  the  right  to
buy  arms  abroad  and  was  even  bound  to  do  so  to  some  degree  by  the  existing  commercial
treaty  with  France.

text: As a result of the failure of the revolt, the generals found themselves isolated in several different parts of Spain with no mass popular support and with control of none of the three chief industrial areas.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  the  failure  of  the  revolt,  the  generals  found  themselves  isolated  in
several  different  parts  of  Spain  with  no  mass  popular  support  and  with  control  of  none  of
the  three  chief  industrial  areas.

text: The rebels held the extreme northwest (Galicia and Leon), the north (Navarre), and the south (western Andalusia) as well as Morocco and the islands.
text_raw:
The  rebels  held  the  extreme  northwest  (Galicia  and  Leon),
the  north  (Navarre),  and  the  south  (western  Andalusia)  as  well  as  Morocco  and  the
islands.

text: They had the unlimited support of Italy and Portugal, as well as unlimited sympathy and tentative support from Germany.
text_raw:
They  had  the  unlimited  support  of  Italy  and  Portugal,  as  well  as  unlimited
sympathy  and  tentative  support  from  Germany.

text: But the rebel position was desperate by the end of July.
text_raw:
But  the  rebel  position  was  desperate  by
the  end  of  July.

text: On July 25th the German ambassador informed his government that the revolt could not succeed "unless something unforeseen happens." By August 25th the acting state secretary of foreign affairs in Germany, Hans Dieckhoff, wrote, "it is not to be expected that the Franco Government can hold out for long, even after outward successes, without large-scale support from outside."
text_raw:
On  July  25th  the  German  ambassador  informed  his  government  that  the
revolt  could  not  succeed  "unless  something  unforeseen  happens."  By  August  25th  the
acting  state  secretary  of  foreign  affairs  in  Germany,  Hans  Dieckhoff,  wrote,  "it  is  not  to
be  expected  that  the  Franco  Government  can  hold  out  for  long,  even  after  outward
successes,  without  large-scale  support  from  outside."

text: In the meantime, Italian and Portuguese aid kept the rebellion going.
text_raw: In  the  meantime,  Italian  and  Portuguese  aid  kept  the  rebellion  going.

text: The French and British, whose only desire at first was to avoid an open clash arising from the Great Powers' supplying arms and men to opposite sides in the conflict were prepared to sacrifice any interests of their countries to avoid this.
text_raw:
The  French  and
British,  whose  only  desire  at  first  was  to  avoid  an  open  clash  arising  from  the  Great
Powers'  supplying  arms  and  men  to  opposite  sides  in  the  conflict  were  prepared  to
sacrifice  any  interests  of  their  countries  to  avoid  this.

text: Impelled by pacifist sentiments, and a desire to avoid war at any cost, French Premier Leon Blum and French Foreign Minister Yvon Delbos suggested on August 1, 1936, that an agreement not to intervene in Spain should be signed by the chief Powers concerned.
text_raw:
Impelled  by  pacifist  sentiments,  and
a  desire  to  avoid  war  at  any  cost,  French  Premier  Leon  Blum  and  French  Foreign
Minister  Yvon  Delbos  suggested  on  August  1,  1936,  that  an  agreement  not  to  intervene  in
Spain  should  be  signed  by  the  chief  Powers  concerned.

text: This idea was eagerly taken up by Britain and was acceptable to the Popular Front government of France, since it was clear that if there was no intervention, the Spanish government could suppress the rebels.
text_raw:
This  idea  was  eagerly  taken  up  by
Britain  and  was  acceptable  to  the  Popular  Front  government  of  France,  since  it  was  clear
that  if  there  was  no  intervention,  the  Spanish  government  could  suppress  the  rebels.

text: Great Britain accepted the French offer at once, but efforts to get Portugal, Italy, Germany, and Russia into the agreement were difficult because of the delays made by Portugal and Italy, both of which were helping the rebels.
text_raw:
Great
Britain  accepted  the  French  offer  at  once,  but  efforts  to  get  Portugal,  Italy,  Germany,  and
Russia  into  the  agreement  were  difficult  because  of  the  delays  made  by  Portugal  and
Italy,  both  of  which  were  helping  the  rebels.

text: By August 24th all six Powers had agreed, and by August 28th the agreement went into effect.
text_raw:
By  August  24th  all  six  Powers  had  agreed,
and  by  August  28th  the  agreement  went  into  effect.

text: Efforts to establish some kind of supervision by the Nonintervention Committee or by neutral forces were rejected by the rebels and by Portugal, while Britain refused to permit any restrictions to be placed on war materiel going to Portugal at the very moment when it was putting all kinds of pressure on France to restrict any flow of supplies across the Pyrenees to the recognized government of Spain (November 30, 1936).
text_raw:
Efforts  to  establish  some  kind  of  supervision  by  the  Nonintervention  Committee  or  by
neutral  forces  were  rejected  by  the  rebels  and  by  Portugal,  while  Britain  refused  to  permit
any  restrictions  to  be  placed  on  war  materiel  going  to  Portugal  at  the  very  moment  when
it  was  putting  all  kinds  of  pressure  on  France  to  restrict  any  flow  of  supplies  across  the
Pyrenees  to  the  recognized  government  of  Spain  (November  30,  1936).

text: Britain also put pressure on Portugal to stop assistance to the rebels but with little success, as Portugal was determined to see a rebel victory.
text_raw:
Britain  also  put
pressure  on  Portugal  to  stop  assistance  to  the  rebels  but  with  little  success,  as  Portugal
was  determined  to  see  a  rebel  victory.

text: Along with Italy and Germany, Portugal delayed joining the nonintervention agreement until it decided that such an agreement would hurt
text_raw:
Along  with  Italy  and  Germany,  Portugal  delayed
joining  the  nonintervention  agreement  until  it  decided  that  such  an  agreement  would  hurt

text: the Loyalist forces more than the rebels.
text_raw: the  Loyalist  forces  more  than  the  rebels.

text: Even then there was no intention of observing the agreement or permitting any steps to enforce it if such actions would hamper the rebels.
text_raw:
Even  then  there  was  no  intention  of  observing
the  agreement  or  permitting  any  steps  to  enforce  it  if  such  actions  would  hamper  the
rebels.

text: On the other hand, France did little to help the Madrid government, while Britain was positively hostile to it.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  France  did  little  to  help  the  Madrid  government,  while  Britain  was
positively  hostile  to  it.

text: Both governments stopped all shipments of war materiel to Spain in the middle of August.
text_raw:
Both  governments  stopped  all  shipments  of  war  materiel  to  Spain
in  the  middle  of  August.

text: By its insistence on enforcing non-intervention against the Loyalists, while ignoring the systematic and large-scale evasions of the agreement in behalf of the refuels, Britain was neither fair nor neutral, and had to engage in large-scale violations of international law.
text_raw:
By  its  insistence  on  enforcing  non-intervention  against  the
Loyalists,  while  ignoring  the  systematic  and  large-scale  evasions  of  the  agreement  in
behalf  of  the  refuels,  Britain  was  neither  fair  nor  neutral,  and  had  to  engage  in  large-scale
violations  of  international  law.

text: Britain refused to permit any restrictions to be placed on war materiel going to Portugal (in spite of its protests to Portugal for transshipping these to the rebels).
text_raw:
Britain  refused  to  permit  any  restrictions  to  be  placed  on
war  materiel  going  to  Portugal  (in  spite  of  its  protests  to  Portugal  for  transshipping  these
to  the  rebels).

text: It refused to allow the Loyalist Spanish Navy to blockade the seaports held by the rebels, and took immediate action against efforts by the Madrid government to interfere with any kind of shipments to refuel areas, while wholesale assaults by the rebels on British and other neutral ships going to Loyalist areas drew little more than feeble protests from Britain.
text_raw:
It  refused  to  allow  the  Loyalist  Spanish  Navy  to  blockade  the  seaports  held
by  the  rebels,  and  took  immediate  action  against  efforts  by  the  Madrid  government  to
interfere  with  any  kind  of  shipments  to  refuel  areas,  while  wholesale  assaults  by  the
rebels  on  British  and  other  neutral  ships  going  to  Loyalist  areas  drew  little  more  than
feeble  protests  from  Britain.

text: In August 1936, when a Loyalist cruiser intercepted a British freighter carrying supplies to Morocco, the British battle cruiser Repulse went after the Spanish cruiser cleared for action.
text_raw:
In  August  1936,  when  a  Loyalist  cruiser  intercepted  a  British
freighter  carrying  supplies  to  Morocco,  the  British  battle  cruiser  Repulse  went  after  the
Spanish  cruiser  cleared  for  action.

text: On the other hand, the British refusal to recognize the rebel government, or to grant it belligerent status, placed interference with shipping by these forces in the category of piracy; yet Britain did almost nothing when in one year (June 1937-June 1938) 10 British ships were sunk, 10 were captured and held, 28 more were seriously damaged, and at least 12 others were damaged by the rebels out of a total of 140 British ships which went to Spain in that year.
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  the  British  refusal  to  recognize  the
rebel  government,  or  to  grant  it  belligerent  status,  placed  interference  with  shipping  by
these  forces  in  the  category  of  piracy;  yet  Britain  did  almost  nothing  when  in  one  year
(June  1937-June  1938)  10  British  ships  were  sunk,  10  were  captured  and  held,  28  more
were  seriously  damaged,  and  at  least  12  others  were  damaged  by  the  rebels  out  of  a  total
of  140  British  ships  which  went  to  Spain  in  that  year.

text: By the beginning of 1937 Britain was clearly seeking a refuel victory, and, instead of trying to enforce non-intervention or to protect British rights on the seas, was actively supporting the rebel blockade of Loyalist Spain.
text_raw:
By  the  beginning  of  1937  Britain
was  clearly  seeking  a  refuel  victory,  and,  instead  of  trying  to  enforce  non-intervention  or
to  protect  British  rights  on  the  seas,  was  actively  supporting  the  rebel  blockade  of
Loyalist  Spain.

text: This was clearly evident when the British Navy after May 1937 began to intercept British ships headed for Loyalist ports and on some pretext, or simply by force, made them go elsewhere, such as Bordeaux or Gibraltar.
text_raw:
This  was  clearly  evident  when  the  British  Navy  after  May  1937  began  to
intercept  British  ships  headed  for  Loyalist  ports  and  on  some  pretext,  or  simply  by  force,
made  them  go  elsewhere,  such  as  Bordeaux  or  Gibraltar.

text: These tactics were admitted by the First Lord of the Admiralty in the House of Commons on June 29, 1938.
text_raw:
These  tactics  were  admitted  by
the  First  Lord  of  the  Admiralty  in  the  House  of  Commons  on  June  29,  1938.

text: The rebel forces were fewer in numbers than the Loyalists, and fought with less vigor and under poor leadership, according to German secret reports from Spain at the time, but were eventually successful because of their great superiority in artillery, aviation, and tanks, as a result of the one-sided enforcement of the nonintervention agreement.
text_raw:
The  rebel  forces  were  fewer  in  numbers  than  the  Loyalists,  and  fought  with  less  vigor
and  under  poor  leadership,  according  to  German  secret  reports  from  Spain  at  the  time,  but
were  eventually  successful  because  of  their  great  superiority  in  artillery,  aviation,  and
tanks,  as  a  result  of  the  one-sided  enforcement  of  the  nonintervention  agreement.

text: This was admitted by the governments concerned as soon as the war was over, and by General Franco on April 13, 1939.
text_raw:
This
was  admitted  by  the  governments  concerned  as  soon  as  the  war  was  over,  and  by  General
Franco  on  April  13,  1939.

text: We have seen that Italian intervention began even before the revolt broke out and that Portuguese intervention on behalf of the rebels followed soon after.
text_raw:
We  have  seen  that  Italian  intervention  began  even  before  the
revolt  broke  out  and  that  Portuguese  intervention  on  behalf  of  the  rebels  followed  soon
after.

text: German intervention was somewhat slower, although all their sympathies were with the rebels.
text_raw:
German  intervention  was  somewhat  slower,  although  all  their  sympathies  were  with
the  rebels.

text: At the end of July, a German citizen in Morocco organized a Spanish corporation called Hisma to obtain German supplies and assistance for the rebels.
text_raw:
At  the  end  of  July,  a  German  citizen  in  Morocco  organized  a  Spanish
corporation  called  Hisma  to  obtain  German  supplies  and  assistance  for  the  rebels.

text: This firm began to transport the rebel troops from Morocco to Spain on August 2nd.
text_raw:
This
firm  began  to  transport  the  rebel  troops  from  Morocco  to  Spain  on  August  2nd.

text: It soon obtained a monopoly on all German goods sold to rebel Spain and set up a central purchasing office for this purpose in Lisbon, Portugal.
text_raw:
It  soon
obtained  a  monopoly  on  all  German  goods  sold  to  rebel  Spain  and  set  up  a  central
purchasing  office  for  this  purpose  in  Lisbon,  Portugal.

text: By August all important units of the German Navy were in Spanish waters, and their ranking admiral paid a state visit to Franco in his headquarters in Morocco as early as August 3rd.
text_raw:
By  August  all  important  units  of
the  German  Navy  were  in  Spanish  waters,  and  their  ranking  admiral  paid  a  state  visit  to
Franco  in  his  headquarters  in  Morocco  as  early  as  August  3rd.

text: These units gave naval support to the rebellion from then on.
text_raw:
These  units  gave  naval
support  to  the  rebellion  from  then  on.

text: Early in October, General Goring established a corporation called Rowak, with three million reichsmarks credit provided by the German government.
text_raw:
Early  in  October,  General  Goring  established  a  corporation  called  Rowak,  with  three
million  reichsmarks  credit  provided  by  the  German  government.

text: This was given a monopoly on the export of goods to Spain, and orders were issued to the German Navy to protect these goods in transit.
text_raw:
This  was  given  a
monopoly  on  the  export  of  goods  to  Spain,  and  orders  were  issued  to  the  German  Navy  to
protect  these  goods  in  transit.

text: The failure of the Franco forces to capture Madrid led to a joint Italian-German meeting in Berlin on October 20, 1936.
text_raw:
The  failure  of  the  Franco  forces  to  capture  Madrid  led  to  a  joint  Italian-German
meeting  in  Berlin  on  October  20,  1936.

text: There it was decided to embark on a policy of extensive support for Franco.
text_raw:
There  it  was  decided  to  embark  on  a  policy  of
extensive  support  for  Franco.

text: As part of this policy both Powers recognized the Franco government and withdraw their recognition from Madrid on November 1 8, 1936, and Italy signed a secret alliance with the rebel government ten days later.
text_raw:
As  part  of  this  policy  both  Powers  recognized  the  Franco
government  and  withdraw  their  recognition  from  Madrid  on  November  1  8,  1936,  and
Italy  signed  a  secret  alliance  with  the  rebel  government  ten  days  later.

text: Japan recognized the Franco regime early in December, following the signature of the German-Japanese Anti-Comintern Pact of November 25, 1936.
text_raw:
Japan  recognized
the  Franco  regime  early  in  December,  following  the  signature  of  the  German-Japanese
Anti-Comintern  Pact  of  November  25,  1936.

text: As a result of all these actions, Franco received the full support of the aggressor states, while the Loyalist government was obstructed in every way by the "peace-loving" Powers.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  all  these  actions,  Franco  received  the  full  support  of  the  aggressor  states,
while  the  Loyalist  government  was  obstructed  in  every  way  by  the  "peace-loving"
Powers.

text: While the Axis assistance to the rebels was chiefly in the form of supplies and technical assistance, it was also necessary to send a large number of men to work some of this equipment or even to fight as infantry.
text_raw:
While  the  Axis  assistance  to  the  rebels  was  chiefly  in  the  form  of  supplies  and
technical  assistance,  it  was  also  necessary  to  send  a  large  number  of  men  to  work  some  of
this  equipment  or  even  to  fight  as  infantry.

text: In all, Italy sent about 100,000 men and suffered about 50,000 casualties (of which 6,000 were killed).
text_raw:
In  all,  Italy  sent  about  100,000  men  and
suffered  about  50,000  casualties  (of  which  6,000  were  killed).

text: Germany sent about 20,000 men, although this figure is less certain.
text_raw:
Germany  sent  about
20,000  men,  although  this  figure  is  less  certain.

text: The value of the supplies sent to General Franco was estimated by the countries concerned as 500 million reichsmarks by Germany and 14 billion fire by Italy.
text_raw:
The  value  of  the  supplies  sent  to  General
Franco  was  estimated  by  the  countries  concerned  as  500  million  reichsmarks  by  Germany
and  14  billion  fire  by  Italy.

text: Together this amounts to over three-quarters of a billion dollars.
text_raw:
Together  this  amounts  to  over  three-quarters  of  a  billion
dollars.

text: On the other side, the Loyalists were cut off from foreign supplies almost at once because of the embargoes of the Great Powers, and obtained only limited amounts, chiefly from Mexico, Russia, and the United States, before the Nonintervention agreement cut these off.
text_raw:
On  the  other  side,  the  Loyalists  were  cut  off  from  foreign  supplies  almost  at  once
because  of  the  embargoes  of  the  Great  Powers,  and  obtained  only  limited  amounts,
chiefly  from  Mexico,  Russia,  and  the  United  States,  before  the  Nonintervention
agreement  cut  these  off.

text: On January 18, 1937, the American Neutrality Act was revised to apply to civil as well as international wars, and was invoked against Spain immediately, but "unofficial" pressure from the American government prevented exports of this kind to Spain even earlier.
text_raw:
On  January  18,  1937,  the  American  Neutrality  Act  was  revised
to  apply  to  civil  as  well  as  international  wars,  and  was  invoked  against  Spain
immediately,  but  "unofficial"  pressure  from  the  American  government  prevented  exports
of  this  kind  to  Spain  even  earlier.

text: As a result of such actions, shortages of supplies for the Madrid government were evident at the end of August and became acute a few weeks later, while supplies for the rebels were steadily increasing.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  such  actions,  shortages  of  supplies  for  the
Madrid  government  were  evident  at  the  end  of  August  and  became  acute  a  few  weeks
later,  while  supplies  for  the  rebels  were  steadily  increasing.

text: The Madrid government made violent protests against the Axis intervention, both before the Nonintervention Committee in London and before the League of Nations.
text_raw:
The  Madrid  government  made  violent  protests  against  the  Axis  intervention,  both
before  the  Nonintervention  Committee  in  London  and  before  the  League  of  Nations.

text: These were denied by the Axis Powers.
text_raw: These  were  denied  by  the  Axis  Powers.

text: An investigation of these charges was made under Soviet pressure, but the committee reported on November loth that these charges were unproved.
text_raw:
An  investigation  of  these  charges  was  made  under  Soviet  pressure,  but  the  committee
reported  on  November  loth  that  these  charges  were  unproved.

text: Indeed, Anthony Eden, nine days later, went so far as to say in the House of Commons that so far as nonintervention was concerned, "there were other Governments more to blame than either Germany or Italy."
text_raw:
Indeed,  Anthony  Eden,
nine  days  later,  went  so  far  as  to  say  in  the  House  of  Commons  that  so  far  as
nonintervention  was  concerned,  "there  were  other  Governments  more  to  blame  than
either  Germany  or  Italy."

text: Since we have captured large quantities of secret German and Italian documents and have not captured any Soviet documents, it is not possible to fix the date or the degree of Soviet intervention in Spain, but it is conclusively established that it was much later in date and immensely less in quantity than that of either Italy or Germany.
text_raw:
Since  we  have  captured  large  quantities  of  secret  German  and  Italian  documents  and
have  not  captured  any  Soviet  documents,  it  is  not  possible  to  fix  the  date  or  the  degree  of
Soviet  intervention  in  Spain,  but  it  is  conclusively  established  that  it  was  much  later  in
date  and  immensely  less  in  quantity  than  that  of  either  Italy  or  Germany.

text: On October 7, 1936, the Soviet representative informed the Nonintervention Committee that it could not be bound by the nonintervention agreement to a greater extent than the other participants.
text_raw:
On  October  7,
1936,  the  Soviet  representative  informed  the  Nonintervention  Committee  that  it  could  not
be  bound  by  the  nonintervention  agreement  to  a  greater  extent  than  the  other  participants.

text: Soviet intervention appears to have begun at this time, three and a half years after Italian intervention and almost three months after both Italian and German units were fighting with the rebels.
text_raw:
Soviet  intervention  appears  to  have  begun  at  this  time,  three  and  a  half  years  after  Italian
intervention  and  almost  three  months  after  both  Italian  and  German  units  were  fighting
with  the  rebels.

text: Russian military equipment went into action before Madrid in the period October 29â€” November 11, 1936.
text_raw:
Russian  military  equipment  went  into  action  before  Madrid  in  the  period
October  29â€” November  11,  1936.

text: As late as September 28, 1936, the German charge d'affaires in the Soviet Union reported that he could find no reliable proof of violation of the arms embargo by the Soviet government, and on November 16th he reported no evidence of the transport of troops from Odessa.

text: A week later a series of decrees ordered the disarmament of the Heimwehr, created an armed militia for the Fatherland Front as the sole armed militia in the country, ordered that in the future the leader of the Front and the chancellor must be the same person, gave the chancellor the right to appoint the heads of all local political units and to approve their appointments, prohibited all parades and assemblies until September 30th, and declared that the Fatherland Front was "an authoritarian foundation," a legal person, and "the sole instrument for the formation of political will in the state."

text: Thus "strengthened" in Austria, and under pressure from Mussolini to make peace with Hitler, Schuschnigg signed an agreement of July 11, 1936, with Franz von Papen, the German minister.

Thus  "strengthened"  in  Austria,  and  under  pressure  from  Mussolini  to  make  peace

text: According to the published portion of this agreement, Germany recognized Austrian independence and sovereignty; each country promised not to interfere in the domestic politics of the other;
Austria admitted it was a German state; and additional agreements to relieve the existing tension were promised.
text_raw:
Austria  admitted  it  was  a  German  state;  and
additional  agreements  to  relieve  the  existing  tension  were  promised.

text: In secret agreements made at the same time, Austria promised an amnesty for political prisoners, promised to take Nazis into positions of "political responsibility," to allow them the same political rights as other Austrians, and to allow Germans in Austria the same rights to use their national symbols and music as citizens of third states.
text_raw:
In  secret  agreements
made  at  the  same  time,  Austria  promised  an  amnesty  for  political  prisoners,  promised  to
take  Nazis  into  positions  of  "political  responsibility,"  to  allow  them  the  same  political

text: Both states revoked financial and other restrictions on tourists.
text_raw:
Both  states  revoked  financial  and
other  restrictions  on  tourists.

text: Mutual prohibition on each other's newspapers were lifted to the extent that five specifically named German papers could enter Austria and five named Austrian papers could enter Germany.

Mutual  prohibition  on  each  other's  newspapers  were  lifted  to
the  extent  that  five  specifically  named  German  papers  could  enter  Austria  and  five  named

text: Other paragraphs promised mutual concessions in regard to economic and cultural relations.
text_raw:
Other  paragraphs  promised  mutual  concessions  in
regard  to  economic  and  cultural  relations.

text: Austro-German relations for the next eighteen months were dominated by this agreement, Germany, through Papen, trying to extend it bit by bit, while Schuschnigg sought to hold Germany to its recognition of Austrian sovereignty and its promise not to interfere in Austria's domestic political affairs.
text_raw:
Austro-German  relations  for  the  next  eighteen  months  were  dominated  by  this
agreement,  Germany,  through  Papen,  trying  to  extend  it  bit  by  bit,  while  Schuschnigg
sought  to  hold  Germany  to  its  recognition  of  Austrian  sovereignty  and  its  promise  not  to
interfere  in  Austria's  domestic  political  affairs.

text: By the end of that period Germany was insisting that, since the Austrian Nazis were Germans, their desires and activities were not an Austrian, but a German, domestic problem.
text_raw:
By  the  end  of  that  period  Germany  was
insisting  that,  since  the  Austrian  Nazis  were  Germans,  their  desires  and  activities  were
not  an  Austrian,  but  a  German,  domestic  problem.

The  secret  documents  published  since  1945  make  it  quite  clear  that  Germany  had  no
carefully  laid  plans  to  annex  Austria,  and  was  not  encouraging  violence  by  the  Nazis  in

Instead,  every  effort  was  made  to  restrict  the  Austrian  Nazis  to  propaganda  in
order  to  win  places  in  the  Cabinet  and  a  gradual  peaceful  extension  of  Nazi  influence.

text: At the same time, military measures were held in reserve, prepared for use if necessary.
text_raw:
At
the  same  time,  military  measures  were  held  in  reserve,  prepared  for  use  if  necessary.

text: To be sure, wild men on the lower levels of the Nazi Party in Germany were encouraging all kinds of violence in Austria, but this was not true of the real leaders.
text_raw:
To
be  sure,  wild  men  on  the  lower  levels  of  the  Nazi  Party  in  Germany  were  encouraging  all
kinds  of  violence  in  Austria,  but  this  was  not  true  of  the  real  leaders.

text: These ordered von Papen to try to get at least two years of peace in 1936, and they removed the Austrian

Papen  to  try  to  get  at  least  two  years  of  peace  in  1936,  and  they  removed  the  Austrian

In  this  way  the
violent  Tavs  Plan  of  the  Austrian  Nazis  was  replaced  by  the  Keppler  Plan  of  peaceful  and

text: The invasion of Austria as early as March 12, 1938, and the immediate annexation of Austria were a pleasant surprise, even for the Nazi leaders in Germany, and arose from several unexpectedly favorable circumstances.
text_raw:
The  invasion  of  Austria  as  early  as  March  12,  1938,  and  the  immediate  annexation  of
Austria  were  a  pleasant  surprise,  even  for  the  Nazi  leaders  in  Germany,  and  arose  from
several  unexpectedly  favorable  circumstances.

text: Accordingly, the decision to invade was not made before March lo, 1938, and even then was conditional, while the decision to annex was not made until noon on March 12th by Hitler personally and was unknown to both Ribbentrop and Goring as late as 10:30 P.M.

Accordingly,  the  decision  to  invade  was
not  made  before  March  lo,  1938,  and  even  then  was  conditional,  while  the  decision  to

text: On March 12th.

The  circumstances
which  brought  this  unexpected  speedup  in  the  German  plans  were  based  on  two  facts:

(1)

text: As far as obvious political events are concerned, 1937 was the only quiet year after 1933.
text_raw:
As  far  as  obvious  political  events  are  concerned,  1937  was  the  only  quiet  year  after
1933.

text: But the capture and release of various secret documents now make it clear that 1937 was a critical turning point because in that year the German government and the British government made secret decisions which sealed the fate of Austria and Czechoslovakia and dominated the history of the next three years.
text_raw:
But  the  capture  and  release  of  various  secret  documents  now  make  it  clear  that
1937  was  a  critical  turning  point  because  in  that  year  the  German  government  and  the
British  government  made  secret  decisions  which  sealed  the  fate  of  Austria  and
Czechoslovakia  and  dominated  the  history  of  the  next  three  years.

text: The decision made by the German government (that is, by Hitler) was to prepare for open military aggression against Czechoslovakia and Austria and to carry this out before 1943-1945, probably in 1938.
text_raw:
The  decision  made  by  the  German  government  (that  is,  by  Hitler)  was  to  prepare  for
open  military  aggression  against  Czechoslovakia  and  Austria  and  to  carry  this  out  before
1943-1945,  probably  in  1938.

text: This decision was announced by Hitler to a secret meeting of seven persons on November 5, 1937.
text_raw:
This  decision  was  announced  by  Hitler  to  a  secret  meeting
of  seven  persons  on  November  5,  1937.

text: Among those present, besides Hitler and his aide, Colonel Hossback, were the minister of war (Werner von Blomberg), the commanders in chief of the army (Werner von Fritsch), the navy (Erich Raeder), and the air force (Hermann Goring), and the foreign minister (Konstantin von Neurath).
text_raw:
Among  those  present,  besides  Hitler  and  his  aide,
Colonel  Hossback,  were  the  minister  of  war  (Werner  von  Blomberg),  the  commanders  in
chief  of  the  army  (Werner  von  Fritsch),  the  navy  (Erich  Raeder),  and  the  air  force
(Hermann  Goring),  and  the  foreign  minister  (Konstantin  von  Neurath).

text: It is evident from some of Hitler's statements that he had already received certain information about the secret decisions being made by Chamberlain on the British side; for example, he said flatly that Britain wanted to satisfy the colonial ambitions of Germany by giving it non- British areas like Portuguese Angola, something which we now know was in Chamberlain's mind.
text_raw:
It  is  evident  from
some  of  Hitler's  statements  that  he  had  already  received  certain  information  about  the
secret  decisions  being  made  by  Chamberlain  on  the  British  side;  for  example,  he  said
flatly  that  Britain  wanted  to  satisfy  the  colonial  ambitions  of  Germany  by  giving  it  non-
British  areas  like  Portuguese  Angola,  something  which  we  now  know  was  in
Chamberlain's  mind.

text: Hitler further assured his listeners that "almost certainly Britain, and probably France as well, had already tacitly written off the Czechs and were reconciled to the fact that this question would be cleared up in due course by Germany....
text_raw:
Hitler  further  assured  his  listeners  that  "almost  certainly  Britain,  and
probably  France  as  well,  had  already  tacitly  written  off  the  Czechs  and  were  reconciled  to
the  fact  that  this  question  would  be  cleared  up  in  due  course  by  Germany....

text: An attack by France without British support, and with the prospect of the offensive being brought to a standstill on our western fortifications, was hardly probable.

An  attack  by
France  without  British  support,  and  with  the  prospect  of  the  offensive  being  brought  to  a
standstill  on  our  western  fortifications,  was  hardly  probable.

text: Nor was a French march through Belgium and Holland without British support to be expected.".
text_raw:
Nor  was  a  French  march
through  Belgium  and  Holland  without  British  support  to  be  expected.".

text: Hitler thought that, by reducing German support for Franco in Spain, the war there could be extended, and, by encouraging Italy to stay in Spain, especially in the Balearic Islands, the French African troops could be kept from crossing the Mediterranean Sea for use in Europe, and in general that France and Britain would be so tied down in the Mediterranean by Italy that they would take no action against Germany over Czechoslovakia and Austria.
text_raw:
Hitler  thought  that,  by  reducing  German  support  for  Franco  in  Spain,  the  war  there
could  be  extended,  and,  by  encouraging  Italy  to  stay  in  Spain,  especially  in  the  Balearic
Islands,  the  French  African  troops  could  be  kept  from  crossing  the  Mediterranean  Sea  for
use  in  Europe,  and  in  general  that  France  and  Britain  would  be  so  tied  down  in  the
Mediterranean  by  Italy  that  they  would  take  no  action  against  Germany  over
Czechoslovakia  and  Austria.

text: In fact, Hitler was so sure of an Anglo-French war against Italy in 1938 that he was confident Czechoslovakia and Austria could be conquered by Germany in that year..
text_raw:
In  fact,  Hitler  was  so  sure  of  an  Anglo-French  war  against
Italy  in  1938  that  he  was  confident  Czechoslovakia  and  Austria  could  be  conquered  by
Germany  in  that  year..

text: These ideas were completely unacceptable to Blomberg, Fritsch, and Neurath.
text_raw: These  ideas  were  completely  unacceptable  to  Blomberg,  Fritsch,  and  Neurath.

text: They objected that German rearmament was so backward that they did not have a single motorized division capable of movement, that there was no reason to expect an Anglo- French-Italian war in 1938, that Italy, in such a war, could tie down only twenty French divisions, leaving more than enough to attack Germany, and that such an attack would be very dangerous because Germany's fortifications on her western frontier were "insignificant." Hitler brushed these objections aside.
text_raw:
They
objected  that  German  rearmament  was  so  backward  that  they  did  not  have  a  single
motorized  division  capable  of  movement,  that  there  was  no  reason  to  expect  an  Anglo-
French-Italian  war  in  1938,  that  Italy,  in  such  a  war,  could  tie  down  only  twenty  French

text: He "repeated his previous statements that he was convinced of Britain's non-participation, and, therefore, he did not believe in the probability of belligerent action by France against Germany."

He  "repeated  his  previous
statements  that  he  was  convinced  of  Britain's  non-participation,  and,  therefore,  he  did  not
believe  in  the  probability  of  belligerent  action  by  France  against  Germany."

text: As a result of the opposition from Blomberg, Fritsch, and Neurath in this conference of November 1937, Hitler replaced these three by more amenable subordinates in a sudden coup on February 4, 1938.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  the  opposition  from  Blomberg,  Fritsch,  and  Neurath  in  this  conference
of  November  1937,  Hitler  replaced  these  three  by  more  amenable  subordinates  in  a
sudden  coup  on  February  4,  1938.

text: Hitler himself took the posts of minister of war and commander in chief, with General Wilhelm Keitel as chief of staff for all the armed forces of the Reich.

Hitler  himself  took  the  posts  of  minister  of  war  and
commander  in  chief,  with  General  Wilhelm  Keitel  as  chief  of  staff  for  all  the  armed
forces  of  the  Reich.

text: Neurath was replaced in the Foreign Ministry by the fanatical Ribbentrop.
text_raw:
Neurath  was  replaced  in  the  Foreign  Ministry  by  the  fanatical
Ribbentrop.

text: The very able Dirksen was sent to London as ambassador, but his ability was wasted, as Ribbentrop paid no attention to his reports and his well-founded warnings.
text_raw:
The  very  able  Dirksen  was  sent  to  London  as  ambassador,  but  his  ability  was
wasted,  as  Ribbentrop  paid  no  attention  to  his  reports  and  his  well-founded  warnings.

text: In the meantime the British government, especially the small group controlling foreign policy, had reached a seven-point decision regarding their attitude toward Germany:
text_raw:
In  the  meantime  the  British  government,  especially  the  small  group  controlling  foreign
policy,  had  reached  a  seven-point  decision  regarding  their  attitude  toward  Germany:

text: Hitler Germany was the front-line bulwark against the spread of Communism in Europe.
text_raw:
Hitler  Germany  was  the  front-line  bulwark  against  the  spread  of  Communism  in
Europe.

text: A four-Power pact of Britain, France, Italy, and Germany to exclude all Russian influence from Europe was the ultimate aim; accordingly, Britain had no desire to weaken the Rome-Berlin Axis, but regarded it and the Anglo-French Entente as the foundation of a stable Europe.
text_raw:
A  four-Power  pact  of  Britain,  France,  Italy,  and  Germany  to  exclude  all  Russian
influence  from  Europe  was  the  ultimate  aim;  accordingly,  Britain  had  no  desire  to
weaken  the  Rome-Berlin  Axis,  but  regarded  it  and  the  Anglo-French  Entente  as  the
foundation  of  a  stable  Europe.

text: Britain had no objection to German acquisition of Austria, Czechoslovakia, and Danzig.
text_raw:
Britain  had  no  objection  to  German  acquisition  of  Austria,  Czechoslovakia,  and
Danzig.

text: Germany must not use force to achieve its aims in Europe, as this would precipitate a war in which Britain would have to intervene because of the pressure of public opinion in Britain and the French system of alliances; with patience, Germany could get its aims without using force.
text_raw:
Germany  must  not  use  force  to  achieve  its  aims  in  Europe,  as  this  would  precipitate
a  war  in  which  Britain  would  have  to  intervene  because  of  the  pressure  of  public  opinion
in  Britain  and  the  French  system  of  alliances;  with  patience,  Germany  could  get  its  aims
without  using  force.

text: Britain wanted an agreement with Germany restricting the numbers and the use of bombing planes.
text_raw:
Britain  wanted  an  agreement  with  Germany  restricting  the  numbers  and  the  use  of
bombing  planes.

text: Britain was prepared to give Germany colonial areas in south-central Africa, including the Belgian Congo and Portuguese Angola if Germany would renounce its desire to recover Tanganyika, which had been taken from Germany in 1919, and if Germany would sign an international agreement to govern these areas with due regard for the rights of the natives, an "open-door" commercial policy, and under some mechanism of international supervision like the mandates.
text_raw:
Britain  was  prepared  to  give  Germany  colonial  areas  in  south-central  Africa,
including  the  Belgian  Congo  and  Portuguese  Angola  if  Germany  would  renounce  its
desire  to  recover  Tanganyika,  which  had  been  taken  from  Germany  in  1919,  and  if
Germany  would  sign  an  international  agreement  to  govern  these  areas  with  due  regard  for
the  rights  of  the  natives,  an  "open-door"  commercial  policy,  and  under  some  mechanism
of  international  supervision  like  the  mandates.

text: Britain would use pressure on Czechoslovakia and Poland to negotiate with Germany and to be conciliatory to Germany's desires.
text_raw:
Britain  would  use  pressure  on  Czechoslovakia  and  Poland  to  negotiate  with
Germany  and  to  be  conciliatory  to  Germany's  desires.

text: To these seven points we should add an eighth:
text_raw: To  these  seven  points  we  should  add  an  eighth:

text: Britain must rearm in order to maintain its position in a "three-bloc world" and to deter Germany from using force in creating its bloc in Europe.
text_raw:
Britain  must  rearm  in  order  to
maintain  its  position  in  a  "three-bloc  world"  and  to  deter  Germany  from  using  force  in
creating  its  bloc  in  Europe.

text: This point was supported by Chamberlain, who built up the air force which saved Britain in 1940, and by the Round Table Group led by Lord Lothian, Edward Grigg, and Leopold Amery, who put on a campaign to establish compulsory military service.
text_raw:
This  point  was  supported  by  Chamberlain,  who  built  up  the
air  force  which  saved  Britain  in  1940,  and  by  the  Round  Table  Group  led  by  Lord
Lothian,  Edward  Grigg,  and  Leopold  Amery,  who  put  on  a  campaign  to  establish
compulsory  military  service.

text: The first seven points were reiterated to Germany by various spokesmen from 1937 onward.
text_raw:
The  first  seven  points  were  reiterated  to  Germany  by  various  spokesmen  from  1937
onward.

text: They are also to be found in many recently published documents, including the captured archives of the German Foreign Ministry, the documents of the British Foreign Office, and various extracts from diaries and other private papers, especially extracts from Neville Chamberlain's diary and his letters to his sister.
text_raw:

text: The latter's "Karlsbad Demands," enunciated on April 24th after Henlein's conference with Hitler, were extreme.

text: They began with an introduction denouncing the Czechs and the Czechoslovak state, insisting that the country must abandon its foreign policy and cease to be an obstacle to the German "Drive to the East." They then enumerated eight demands.

They  began  with  an  introduction  denouncing  the
Czechs  and  the  Czechoslovak  state,  insisting  that  the  country  must  abandon  its  foreign
policy  and  cease  to  be  an  obstacle  to  the  German  "Drive  to  the  East."  They  then
enumerated  eight  demands.

text: Among these we find (1) complete equality between Czechs and Germans, (2) recognition of the German group as a corporation with legal personality, (3) demarcation of the German areas, (4) full self-government in those areas, (5) legal protection for citizens outside those areas, (6) reparation for damages influenced by the Czechs on the Sudetens since 1918, (7) German officials in German areas, and (8) full freedom to profess German nationality and German political philosophy.

Among  these  we  find  (1)  complete  equality  between  Czechs
and  Germans,  (2)  recognition  of  the  German  group  as  a  corporation  with  legal
personality,  (3)  demarcation  of  the  German  areas,  (4)  full  self-government  in  those  areas,
(5)  legal  protection  for  citizens  outside  those  areas,  (6)  reparation  for  damages  influenced
by  the  Czechs  on  the  Sudetens  since  1918,  (7)  German  officials  in  German  areas,  and  (8)
full  freedom  to  profess  German  nationality  and  German  political  philosophy.

text: In fact, he felt that Germany could impose its will upon Czechoslovakia by economic pressure alone, although he did not go so far as to say, with Sir Nevile Henderson and Lord Halifax, that this method could be successful "in a short time." If Germany did decide to destroy Czechoslovakia, he did not see how this could be prevented.

Accordingly, by putting Anglo-French pressure on the Czechs to negotiate, it would be possible "to save something of Czechoslovakia and in particular to save the existence of the Czechoslovak State." In any case, he was determined not to go to war over it, because nothing could prevent Germany from achieving immediate victory over the Czechs and, even if the Germans were subsequently defeated after a long war, there was no guarantee that Czechoslovakia could be reestablished in its existing form.

text: The mounting horror of the relentless German mobilization was built up day by day, while Britain and France ordered the Czechs not to mobilize in order "not to provoke Germany." text: The blockade was enforced by Britain with little regard for international law or for neutral rights, but there was relatively little protest from the neutrals, because the most influential neutrals were already so deeply committed to one side or to the other that they could hardly be regarded as neutrals and were not prepared to defend such a status.

text: The Soviet Union favored neither side but was very fearful of attack from both; until April 1940, it was more fearful of Britain and France, while after the fall of Norway and France it became increasingly fearful of Germany.

text: After examining the evidence on this problem, the chiefs of the blockade of the Foreign Economic Administration in Washington wrote, "Germany's war production and military operations were never seriously hampered by a shortage of any essential raw materials or industrial products, with the single exception of petroleum â€” and even that shortage resulted from the combined effect of the Soviet Army's capture of Romanian oil fields and the concentrated bombing of Germany's synthetic production rather than directly from economic warfare." The same writers point out that Germany's food supply, in calories per capita, was at the prewar level until the very last months of the war.

text: The ability of the Germans to cope with the blockade was largely due to their high level of engineering skill and their ruthless exploitation of conquered Europe, especially of the manpower of dominated areas.

The  ability  of  the  Germans  to  cope  with  the  blockade  was  largely  due  to  their  high

text: In the early part of the war, the blockade was not effective because of the low level of German mobilization, the slow and faulty fashion in which the blockade was (perhaps necessarily) applied, the large number of neutral and nonbelligerent countries, the leaks to Germany across Soviet Russia and Vichy France, the ineffectiveness of quantitative controls under a limited naval patrol, and the succession of German conquests which brought such valuable assets as the Norwegian iron-ore route, the French iron mines and aluminum industry, the Romanian oil wells, or the Yugoslav copper mines under direct German control.

text: During the "phony war" from September 1939 to April 1940, there were persons in Britain, France, and Germany who were willing to fight to the bitter end and other persons who were eager to make peace.
text_raw:
During  the  "phony  war"  from  September  1939  to  April  1940,  there  were  persons  in
Britain,  France,  and  Germany  who  were  willing  to  fight  to  the  bitter  end  and  other
persons  who  were  eager  to  make  peace.

text: Such persons engaged in extensive intrigues and cross -intrigues in order to negotiate peace or to prevent it.
text_raw:
Such  persons  engaged  in  extensive  intrigues  and
cross -intrigues  in  order  to  negotiate  peace  or  to  prevent  it.

text: One of the most publicized of these efforts gave rise to the so-called "Venlo incident" of November 1939.
text_raw:
One  of  the  most  publicized  of
these  efforts  gave  rise  to  the  so-called  "Venlo  incident"  of  November  1939.

text: On October 8th Hitler ordered his commanding generals to prepare for an immediate attack on the Low Countries and France.

8th  Hitler  ordered  his  commanding  generals  to  prepare  for  an  immediate  attack  on  the

text: Shortly afterward, two members of British military Intelligence in the Netherlands, who were officially attached to the British diplomatic mission at The Hague, were approached by a man whom they believed to be an agent of discontented generals of the German General Staff.
text_raw:
Shortly  afterward,  two  members  of  British  military
Intelligence  in  the  Netherlands,  who  were  officially  attached  to  the  British  diplomatic
mission  at  The  Hague,  were  approached  by  a  man  whom  they  believed  to  be  an  agent  of
discontented  generals  of  the  German  General  Staff.

text: This man, who may have been a "double agent" working for both sides, wished to discuss the possibility of negotiating peace if the German generals removed Hitler and his chief associates by a coup d'etat.
text_raw:
This  man,  who  may  have  been  a
"double  agent"  working  for  both  sides,  wished  to  discuss  the  possibility  of  negotiating
peace  if  the  German  generals  removed  Hitler  and  his  chief  associates  by  a  coup  d'etat.

text: The proposal sounded authentic because the British leaders had been approached with similar offers, which were known to be authentic, since August 1938, and there was, at that very moment, late in 1939, a member of the German General Staff who was passing information (including the date of Hitler's projected attack on Holland) to the Netherlands military attache in Berlin.
text_raw:
The  proposal  sounded  authentic  because  the  British  leaders  had  been  approached  with
similar  offers,  which  were  known  to  be  authentic,  since  August  1938,  and  there  was,  at
that  very  moment,  late  in  1939,  a  member  of  the  German  General  Staff  who  was  passing
information  (including  the  date  of  Hitler's  projected  attack  on  Holland)  to  the  Netherlands
military  attache  in  Berlin.

text: With Lord Halifax's permission, the two British officers, Major Richard Henry Stevens and Captain Sigismund Payne-Best, with an observer from the Netherlands government, Lieutenant Klop, held five meetings on Dutch territory with the German negotiators.
text_raw:
With  Lord  Halifax's  permission,  the  two  British  officers,  Major  Richard  Henry
Stevens  and  Captain  Sigismund  Payne-Best,  with  an  observer  from  the  Netherlands
government,  Lieutenant  Klop,  held  five  meetings  on  Dutch  territory  with  the  German
negotiators.

text: At the fifth meeting, at Venlo on November 8th, the negotiators, who were really members of the Security Police of the S.S., shot Lieutenant Klop, and escaped into Germany with his body, the two British agents, a Dutch chauffeur, and the automobile in which they had been traveling.
text_raw:
At  the  fifth  meeting,  at  Venlo  on  November  8th,  the  negotiators,  who  were
really  members  of  the  Security  Police  of  the  S.S.,  shot  Lieutenant  Klop,  and  escaped  into
Germany  with  his  body,  the  two  British  agents,  a  Dutch  chauffeur,  and  the  automobile  in
which  they  had  been  traveling.

text: The incident aroused great notoriety at the time and, in some circles, was taken to indicate that Britain was really eager to find some way out of the conflict, in spite of its proclaimed determination to fight to a finish.
text_raw:
The  incident  aroused  great  notoriety  at  the  time  and,  in
some  circles,  was  taken  to  indicate  that  Britain  was  really  eager  to  find  some  way  out  of

text: The Venlo incident was but one, and on the whole a rather unimportant one, of a number of unsuccessful efforts to make peace between the Western Powers and Germany in the six months following the defeat of Poland.
text_raw:
The  Venlo  incident  was  but  one,  and  on  the  whole  a  rather  unimportant  one,  of  a
number  of  unsuccessful  efforts  to  make  peace  between  the  Western  Powers  and  Germany
in  the  six  months  following  the  defeat  of  Poland.

text: These efforts combined with the lack of fighting in the "phony war" to convince the leaders of the Soviet Union that the Western Powers had little heart in fighting Germany and would prefer to be fighting Russia.
text_raw:
These  efforts  combined  with  the  lack  of
fighting  in  the  "phony  war"  to  convince  the  leaders  of  the  Soviet  Union  that  the  Western
Powers  had  little  heart  in  fighting  Germany  and  would  prefer  to  be  fighting  Russia.

text: As we shall see, this was probably true of Chamberlain and his close associates and of Daladier and his successor as prime minister of France, Paul Reynaud.
text_raw:
As
we  shall  see,  this  was  probably  true  of  Chamberlain  and  his  close  associates  and  of
Daladier  and  his  successor  as  prime  minister  of  France,  Paul  Reynaud.

text: To avoid or at least postpone an attack, from either the Western Powers or Germany, became the chief aim of Soviet policy, and every effort was made to strengthen Russia's military, strategic, and political position.
text_raw:
To  avoid  or  at
least  postpone  an  attack,  from  either  the  Western  Powers  or  Germany,  became  the  chief
aim  of  Soviet  policy,  and  every  effort  was  made  to  strengthen  Russia's  military,  strategic,
and  political  position.

text: It was felt in the Kremlin, in the period from September to May, that the danger of attack was greater from the Western Powers than it was from Germany, since Germany was in such great need of Russian raw materials that it would probably keep the peace if the Soviet Union made serious efforts to fulfill the economic agreements it had signed with Germany.
text_raw:
It  was  felt  in  the  Kremlin,  in  the  period  from  September  to  May,
that  the  danger  of  attack  was  greater  from  the  Western  Powers  than  it  was  from  Germany,
since  Germany  was  in  such  great  need  of  Russian  raw  materials  that  it  would  probably
keep  the  peace  if  the  Soviet  Union  made  serious  efforts  to  fulfill  the  economic
agreements  it  had  signed  with  Germany.

text: Moreover, the political agreements of August 23rd and September 28th, by giving the Soviet Union a free hand east of a specified line, made it possible for Russia to strengthen its defenses against Germany by advancing its frontiers and military bases up to that line.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  political  agreements  of  August
23rd  and  September  28th,  by  giving  the  Soviet  Union  a  free  hand  east  of  a  specified  line,
made  it  possible  for  Russia  to  strengthen  its  defenses  against  Germany  by  advancing  its
frontiers  and  military  bases  up  to  that  line.

text: Furthermore, the Soviet leaders believed that full economic cooperation with Germany might persuade Hitler to bring pressure on Japan to reduce its pressure on the Soviet Far Eastern frontier.
text_raw:
Furthermore,  the  Soviet  leaders  believed  that
full  economic  cooperation  with  Germany  might  persuade  Hitler  to  bring  pressure  on
Japan  to  reduce  its  pressure  on  the  Soviet  Far  Eastern  frontier.

text: The Japanese pressure on the Soviet Far East reached its peak in the years 1938 and 1939 with two attacks by the Japanese Army on Soviet territory.
text_raw:
The  Japanese  pressure  on  the  Soviet  Far  East  reached  its  peak  in  the  years  1938  and
1939  with  two  attacks  by  the  Japanese  Army  on  Soviet  territory.

text: The second of these attacks, at Nomonhan on the Manchurian-Mongolian frontier, resulted in a major Japanese defeat in which Nippon suffered 52,000 casualties; it was ended by a truce signed on September 16, 1939, only one day before Russian forces began to move into Poland.
text_raw:
The  second  of  these
attacks,  at  Nomonhan  on  the  Manchurian-Mongolian  frontier,  resulted  in  a  major
Japanese  defeat  in  which  Nippon  suffered  52,000  casualties;  it  was  ended  by  a  truce
signed  on  September  16,  1939,  only  one  day  before  Russian  forces  began  to  move  into
Poland.

text: From the diplomatic point of view the Soviet Far Eastern policy was a success, for Hitler, in the years 1939-1941, put pressure on Japan to relax its efforts to expand on the northern part of the Asiastic mainland and to replace this with a movement against British Malaya and the Netherlands East Indies.
text_raw:
From  the  diplomatic  point  of  view  the  Soviet  Far  Eastern  policy  was  a  success,
for  Hitler,  in  the  years  1939-1941,  put  pressure  on  Japan  to  relax  its  efforts  to  expand  on
the  northern  part  of  the  Asiastic  mainland  and  to  replace  this  with  a  movement  against
British  Malaya  and  the  Netherlands  East  Indies.

text: The Japanese defeat at Nomonhan and the fact that the raw materials which Japan needed were to be found in the south rather
text_raw:
The  Japanese  defeat  at  Nomonhan  and
the  fact  that  the  raw  materials  which  Japan  needed  were  to  be  found  in  the  south  rather

text: than in Mongolia, Siberia, or even northern China, persuaded Japan to accept the change of direction.
