The  troubles  in  the  Magyar  state  in  the  summer  of  1956  took  the  same  forms  as  in
Poland,  but  instead  of  being  directed  by  the  Communist  party  secretary,  they  were
directed  against  him.

text: They appeared as agitations against the indefatigable Stalinist Matyas Rakosi and in favor of the mild Imre Nagy, who had been premier in 1953-1955 as Malenkov's choice and had been removed at Khrushchev's order.

They  appeared  as  agitations  against  the  indefatigable  Stalinist
Matyas  Rakosi  and  in  favor  of  the  mild  Imre  Nagy,  who  had  been  premier  in  1953-1955
as  Malenkov's  choice  and  had  been  removed  at  Khrushchev's  order.

On  July  18th
Khrushchev  tried  to  deflate  these  agitations  by  ordering  some  minor  reforms  and
replacing  Rakosi  as  party  secretary  by  his  deputy,  the  uncouth  and  obstinate  Stalinist

text: This simply intensified the agitations, which rose to a crescendo in September, chiefly from the meetings and resolutions of students, workers, and literary groups.
text_raw:
This  simply  intensified  the  agitations,  which  rose  to  a  crescendo  in
September,  chiefly  from  the  meetings  and  resolutions  of  students,  workers,  and  literary
groups.

text: Some of their demands were successful, including, on October 19th, abolition of the compulsory study of the Russian language.
text_raw:
Some  of  their  demands  were  successful,  including,  on  October  19th,  abolition  of
the  compulsory  study  of  the  Russian  language.

text: On October 22nd a meeting of about 4,000 students discussing changes in university life became diverted to political agitations and drew up "Sixteen Points" which they tried to force Radio Budapest to broadcast.
text_raw:
On  October  22nd  a  meeting  of  about  4,000  students  discussing  changes  in  university
life  became  diverted  to  political  agitations  and  drew  up  "Sixteen  Points"  which  they  tried
to  force  Radio  Budapest  to  broadcast.

text: Omission of some of the points, demanding a new economic policy, the withdrawal of Soviet troops, free elections, freedom of the press, and reform of the Communist Party, led to a mass demonstration on October 23rd.
text_raw:
Omission  of  some  of  the  points,  demanding  a  new
economic  policy,  the  withdrawal  of  Soviet  troops,  free  elections,  freedom  of  the  press,
and  reform  of  the  Communist  Party,  led  to  a  mass  demonstration  on  October  23rd.

text: When Gero refused their demands, the students began to riot, smashing to pieces the huge statue of Stalin in the center of the city.
text_raw:
When
Gero  refused  their  demands,  the  students  began  to  riot,  smashing  to  pieces  the  huge  statue
of  Stalin  in  the  center  of  the  city.

text: The security police killed several demonstrators, but when the regular Hungarian troops were called to restore order they joined the agitators.
text_raw:
The  security  police  killed  several  demonstrators,  but
when  the  regular  Hungarian  troops  were  called  to  restore  order  they  joined  the  agitators.

text: By that time Soviet troops began to move from fifty miles away, and arrived in the capital by 2:00 A.M. on October 24th;
text_raw:
By  that  time  Soviet  troops  began  to  move  from  fifty  miles  away,  and  arrived  in  the
capital  by  2:00  A.M.  on  October  24th;

text: Mikoyan had preceded them.
text_raw: Mikoyan  had  preceded  them.

text: It soon became clear
text_raw: It  soon  became  clear

text: that the Soviet tanks could not control the situation, because they could be blocked by overturned streetcars or other obstacles and could not subdue rioters in strong buildings:
text_raw:
that  the  Soviet  tanks  could  not  control  the  situation,  because  they  could  be  blocked  by
overturned  streetcars  or  other  obstacles  and  could  not  subdue  rioters  in  strong  buildings:

text: Mikoyan dismissed Gero and put in, as party secretary, Janos Kadar, until then a known opponent of the Stalinist group.
text_raw:
Mikoyan  dismissed  Gero  and  put  in,  as  party  secretary,  Janos  Kadar,  until  then  a  known
opponent  of  the  Stalinist  group.

text: By that time, October 25th, the revolt had spread through Hungary under the passive eyes of the Soviet troops.
text_raw:
By  that  time,  October  25th,  the  revolt  had  spread  through
Hungary  under  the  passive  eyes  of  the  Soviet  troops.

text: On the following day, Nagy, still in touch with Mikoyan, formed a new government and negotiated a cease-fire.
text_raw:
On  the  following  day,  Nagy,  still  in
touch  with  Mikoyan,  formed  a  new  government  and  negotiated  a  cease-fire.

text: The Russian forces withdrew from Budapest, and negotiations were opened between their officers and the Nagy government for their withdrawal from the country.
text_raw:
The  Russian
forces  withdrew  from  Budapest,  and  negotiations  were  opened  between  their  officers  and
the  Nagy  government  for  their  withdrawal  from  the  country.

text: By that time the whole Communist system in Hungary had collapsed; unofficial elected groups had seized power throughout the country; the secret police and the party had disintegrated; a revolutionary council had taken control of the Hungarian Army, and Colonel Pal Maleter, a leader of the revolt, had been made a major general and minister of defense.
text_raw:
By  that  time  the  whole
Communist  system  in  Hungary  had  collapsed;  unofficial  elected  groups  had  seized  power
throughout  the  country;  the  secret  police  and  the  party  had  disintegrated;  a  revolutionary
council  had  taken  control  of  the  Hungarian  Army,  and  Colonel  Pal  Maleter,  a  leader  of
the  revolt,  had  been  made  a  major  general  and  minister  of  defense.

text: Most significant of all, the one-party system had been ended, and members of the revived non-Communist parties had joined the Cabinet.
text_raw:
Most  significant  of  all,
the  one-party  system  had  been  ended,  and  members  of  the  revived  non-Communist
parties  had  joined  the  Cabinet.

text: On October 31st the official Soviet news agency, Tass, announced that the Kremlin was ready to recognize the new government and negotiate withdrawal of all Soviet troops from the country.
text_raw:
On  October  31st  the  official  Soviet  news  agency,  Tass,
announced  that  the  Kremlin  was  ready  to  recognize  the  new  government  and  negotiate
withdrawal  of  all  Soviet  troops  from  the  country.

text: However, as October ended, large Soviet forces had begun to invade Hungary, crossing into the country on numerous temporary combat bridges.
text_raw:
However,  as  October  ended,  large  Soviet  forces  had  begun  to  invade  Hungary,
crossing  into  the  country  on  numerous  temporary  combat  bridges.

text: On November 1st Kadar, who had pretended to be one of Nagy's closest supporters, fled from Budapest to the Soviet headquarters at Szolnok.
text_raw:
On  November  1st
Kadar,  who  had  pretended  to  be  one  of  Nagy's  closest  supporters,  fled  from  Budapest  to
the  Soviet  headquarters  at  Szolnok.

text: There he set up a new government under Soviet control.
text_raw:
There  he  set  up  a  new  government  under  Soviet
control.

text: The same day Nagy called to the United Nations, appealing for help and announcing Hungary's withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact and its resumption of neutrality.
text_raw:
The  same  day  Nagy  called  to  the  United  Nations,  appealing  for  help  and
announcing  Hungary's  withdrawal  from  the  Warsaw  Pact  and  its  resumption  of
neutrality.

text: In the meantime, the Soviet invasion was in full operation, overrunning the country and smashing into Budapest before dawn on November 4th.
text_raw:
In  the  meantime,  the  Soviet  invasion  was  in  full  operation,  overrunning  the  country
and  smashing  into  Budapest  before  dawn  on  November  4th.

text: Most of the resistance was overwhelmed that day.
text_raw:
Most  of  the  resistance  was
overwhelmed  that  day.

text: As it collapsed, the Nagy government and their families took refuge in the Yugoslav Embassy.
text_raw:
As  it  collapsed,  the  Nagy  government  and  their  families  took
refuge  in  the  Yugoslav  Embassy.

text: The Yugoslavs, including Tito, were obviously confused by Kadar's change of sides, and accepted his promise of safe-conduct to their homes for Nagy and his associates.
text_raw:
The  Yugoslavs,  including  Tito,  were  obviously
confused  by  Kadar's  change  of  sides,  and  accepted  his  promise  of  safe-conduct  to  their
homes  for  Nagy  and  his  associates.

text: However, when these people left the security of the embassy on November 22nd, they were seized by Soviet forces and deported to prisons outside Hungary.
text_raw:
However,  when  these  people  left  the  security  of  the
embassy  on  November  22nd,  they  were  seized  by  Soviet  forces  and  deported  to  prisons
outside  Hungary.

text: By that date the flight of refugees from Hungary was in flood, despite efforts by the Kadar government to prevent it.
text_raw:
By  that  date  the  flight  of  refugees  from  Hungary  was  in  flood,  despite
efforts  by  the  Kadar  government  to  prevent  it.

text: Many were killed as they tried to pass the frontiers, but thousands escaped to the West, where many of them were able to continue their studies in a new way of life.
text_raw:
Many  were  killed  as  they  tried  to  pass  the
frontiers,  but  thousands  escaped  to  the  West,  where  many  of  them  were  able  to  continue
their  studies  in  a  new  way  of  life.

text: The costs of the uprising were catastrophic.
text_raw: The  costs  of  the  uprising  were  catastrophic.

text: On the Hungarian side there were about 2,800 killed, 13,000 wounded, and 4,000 buildings destroyed, but tens of thousands were in exile or in hiding, the country was shattered, and lay, as a conquered country, under the armed forces of its oppressor.
text_raw:
On  the
Hungarian  side  there  were  about  2,800  killed,  13,000  wounded,  and  4,000  buildings
destroyed,  but  tens  of  thousands  were  in  exile  or  in  hiding,  the  country  was  shattered,  and
lay,  as  a  conquered  country,  under  the  armed  forces  of  its  oppressor.

text: The unanticipated consequences of Khrushchev's de-Stalinization efforts in eastern Europe were bound to injure Khrushchev in the Kremlin power struggle.
text_raw:
The  unanticipated  consequences  of  Khrushchev's  de-Stalinization  efforts  in  eastern
Europe  were  bound  to  injure  Khrushchev  in  the  Kremlin  power  struggle.

text: Indeed, they brought him to the brink of final disaster early in 1957.
text_raw:
Indeed,  they
brought  him  to  the  brink  of  final  disaster  early  in  1957.

text: As usual, the shifts of power were indicated by changes in personnel.
text_raw:
As  usual,  the  shifts  of  power  were
indicated  by  changes  in  personnel.

text: Kaganovich, who had been removed from the government on June 5, 1956, was restored as minister of building materials on September 22nd;
Shepilov, who had been Khrushchev's appointee as foreign minister in June, lost
text_raw: Shepilov,  who  had  been  Khrushchev's  appointee  as  foreign  minister  in  June,  lost

text: his other post as secretary to the Central Committee on Christmas Day 1956.
text_raw: his  other  post  as  secretary  to  the  Central  Committee  on  Christmas  Day  1956.

text: Above all, on November 22nd, Molotov was made minister of state control, a post which had budgetary functions in all parts of the state-controlled economy and could have been built up into a state power, in opposition to Khrushchev's party power, in the economic system.
text_raw:
Above  all,
on  November  22nd,  Molotov  was  made  minister  of  state  control,  a  post  which  had
budgetary  functions  in  all  parts  of  the  state-controlled  economy  and  could  have  been  built
up  into  a  state  power,  in  opposition  to  Khrushchev's  party  power,  in  the  economic  system.

text: Moreover, de-Stalinization ceased after July 1956, and even Khrushchev found it necessary to praise the old ogre.
text_raw:
Moreover,  de-Stalinization  ceased  after  July  1956,  and  even  Khrushchev  found  it
necessary  to  praise  the  old  ogre.

text: On December 2 3rd Pravda denied that there had ever been any Stalinism in the Soviet Union.
text_raw:
On  December  2  3rd  Pravda  denied  that  there  had  ever
been  any  Stalinism  in  the  Soviet  Union.

text: Eight days later, Khrushchev said, "We can state with contrition that we are all Stalinists in fact." On January 17, 1957, at the Chinese Embassy in Moscow, he said, "Stalinism, like Stalin himself, is inseparable from Communism....
text_raw:
Eight  days  later,  Khrushchev  said,  "We  can  state
with  contrition  that  we  are  all  Stalinists  in  fact."  On  January  17,  1957,  at  the  Chinese
Embassy  in  Moscow,  he  said,  "Stalinism,  like  Stalin  himself,  is  inseparable  from
Communism....

text: In the fight against the enemies of our class, Stalin defended the cause of Marxism- Leninism."
text_raw:
In  the  fight  against  the  enemies  of  our  class,  Stalin  defended  the  cause  of
Marxism- Leninism."

text: For Khrushchev, as for all the Soviet leaders, the great issue was to prevent Titoism from spreading into the Soviet Union and, if possible, to curtail its spread among the satellites.
text_raw:
For  Khrushchev,  as  for  all  the  Soviet  leaders,  the  great  issue  was  to  prevent  Titoism
from  spreading  into  the  Soviet  Union  and,  if  possible,  to  curtail  its  spread  among  the
satellites.

text: Every effort was made to prevent knowledge of the "Polish October" and the Hungarian revolt from reaching the Soviet people, and the attacks on Tito and Yugoslavia were resumed.
text_raw:
Every  effort  was  made  to  prevent  knowledge  of  the  "Polish  October"  and  the
Hungarian  revolt  from  reaching  the  Soviet  people,  and  the  attacks  on  Tito  and  Yugoslavia
were  resumed.

text: Tito struck back on November 1 1th with the charge that Stalin had taken the domestic and foreign policies of the Soviet Union to dead ends and that his errors were not personal ones but intrinsic in the Soviet system of monolithic authoritarianism.
text_raw:
Tito  struck  back  on  November  1 1th  with  the  charge  that  Stalin  had  taken
the  domestic  and  foreign  policies  of  the  Soviet  Union  to  dead  ends  and  that  his  errors
were  not  personal  ones  but  intrinsic  in  the  Soviet  system  of  monolithic  authoritarianism.

text: He was refuted in Pravda, a week later.
text_raw: He  was  refuted  in  Pravda,  a  week  later.

text: The Hungarian invasion destroyed much of the appeal of Communism to the Leftists of Western Europe and the world; this had already been left in shreds by the "secret speech." Even in the Soviet Union, university students and intellectuals disapproved of the Soviet invasion of Hungary.
text_raw:
The  Hungarian  invasion  destroyed  much  of  the  appeal  of  Communism  to  the  Leftists
of  Western  Europe  and  the  world;  this  had  already  been  left  in  shreds  by  the  "secret
speech."  Even  in  the  Soviet  Union,  university  students  and  intellectuals  disapproved  of
the  Soviet  invasion  of  Hungary.

text: Many literary works written during the de-Stalinization phase in the spring were published the following winter, when the tide had turned again.
text_raw:
Many  literary  works  written  during  the  de-Stalinization
phase  in  the  spring  were  published  the  following  winter,  when  the  tide  had  turned  again.

text: Khrushchev struck hard at these groups and continued to do so for several years, with the result that the alienation of Russian intellectuals from Khrushchev became established.
text_raw:
Khrushchev  struck  hard  at  these  groups  and  continued  to  do  so  for  several  years,  with  the
result  that  the  alienation  of  Russian  intellectuals  from  Khrushchev  became  established.

text: This was reflected in the expulsion from the universities later in 1956 of hundreds of students who refused to applaud the Soviet attack on Hungary.
text_raw:
This  was  reflected  in  the  expulsion  from  the  universities  later  in  1956  of  hundreds  of
students  who  refused  to  applaud  the  Soviet  attack  on  Hungary.

text: The official Soviet line was that most disturbances of this kind arose from the activities of foreign agitators of capitalist aggressors.
text_raw:
The  official  Soviet  line
was  that  most  disturbances  of  this  kind  arose  from  the  activities  of  foreign  agitators  of
capitalist  aggressors.

text: Simultaneously with the Soviet political and intellectual reaction after June 1956, came a series of efforts to alienate the economic stringency: wages were raised, taxes reduced on the poorest payers, social benefits were extended, and the labor unions were urged to protect them; numerous projects in heavy industry under the Five- Year Plan were slowed up and their resources diverted to consumer goods.
text_raw:
Simultaneously  with  the  Soviet  political  and  intellectual  reaction  after  June  1956,
came  a  series  of  efforts  to  alienate  the  economic  stringency:  wages  were  raised,  taxes
reduced  on  the  poorest  payers,  social  benefits  were  extended,  and  the  labor  unions  were
urged  to  protect  them;  numerous  projects  in  heavy  industry  under  the  Five- Year  Plan
were  slowed  up  and  their  resources  diverted  to  consumer  goods.

text: Most significant of all, there was a sharp increase in the influence of state officials and a corresponding decrease in that of party officials.
text_raw:
Most  significant  of  all,
there  was  a  sharp  increase  in  the  influence  of  state  officials  and  a  corresponding  decrease
in  that  of  party  officials.

text: This reversal was fully evident in the Central Committee session of late December 1956, but the following meeting, in February 1957, showed Khrushchev in an aggressive counterattack.
text_raw:
This  reversal  was  fully  evident  in  the  Central  Committee  session  of  late  December
1956,  but  the  following  meeting,  in  February  1957,  showed  Khrushchev  in  an  aggressive
counterattack.

text: This took the form of suggestions for a drastic reorganization of Soviet economic life toward a more decentralized system.
text_raw:
This  took  the  form  of  suggestions  for  a  drastic  reorganization  of  Soviet
economic  life  toward  a  more  decentralized  system.

text: Undoubtedly this plan had considerable merit, but in Khrushchev's eyes it had an additional advantage, since it
text_raw:
Undoubtedly  this  plan  had
considerable  merit,  but  in  Khrushchev's  eyes  it  had  an  additional  advantage,  since  it

text: would remove much of economic life from the influence of the central state ministries and leave it open to increased influence from local party groups.
text_raw:
would  remove  much  of  economic  life  from  the  influence  of  the  central  state  ministries
and  leave  it  open  to  increased  influence  from  local  party  groups.

text: He proposed the division of the Soviet Union into several dozen economic regions, each under an economic council, or sovnarkhozy, of diverse groups, and the devolution to these groups of the economic functions of the majority of the economic ministries in Moscow.
text_raw:
He  proposed  the
division  of  the  Soviet  Union  into  several  dozen  economic  regions,  each  under  an
economic  council,  or  sovnarkhozy,  of  diverse  groups,  and  the  devolution  to  these  groups
of  the  economic  functions  of  the  majority  of  the  economic  ministries  in  Moscow.

text: These ministries would be abolished, along with the State Commission for Current Planning (GEK) and Molotov's Ministry of State Control.
text_raw:
These
ministries  would  be  abolished,  along  with  the  State  Commission  for  Current  Planning
(GEK)  and  Molotov's  Ministry  of  State  Control.

text: This would leave only the long-range economic planning agency (Gosplan) and a few economic ministries at the center, with annual planning and most execution left to the regional or lower groupings.
text_raw:
This  would  leave  only  the  long-range
economic  planning  agency  (Gosplan)  and  a  few  economic  ministries  at  the  center,  with
annual  planning  and  most  execution  left  to  the  regional  or  lower  groupings.

text: This plan had real merits which can hardly be covered here.
text_raw: This  plan  had  real  merits  which  can  hardly  be  covered  here.

text: Clearly, the growing complexity of the Soviet economy, over a widely diverse terrain and people, could not be operated efficiently by uniform regulations from the center.
text_raw:
Clearly,  the  growing
complexity  of  the  Soviet  economy,  over  a  widely  diverse  terrain  and  people,  could  not  be
operated  efficiently  by  uniform  regulations  from  the  center.

text: Moreover, each economic ministry, because of the constant shortages of resources, materials, and labor, sought to build up, within itself, its own sources of supply and also had a constant urge to hoard equipment and parts, even when they were not needed by it and were urgently needed by enterprises of a different ministry in the next street or district.
text_raw:
Moreover,  each  economic
ministry,  because  of  the  constant  shortages  of  resources,  materials,  and  labor,  sought  to
build  up,  within  itself,  its  own  sources  of  supply  and  also  had  a  constant  urge  to  hoard
equipment  and  parts,  even  when  they  were  not  needed  by  it  and  were  urgently  needed  by
enterprises  of  a  different  ministry  in  the  next  street  or  district.

text: This hampered expansion and also resulted in very expensive cross-hauling of the freight of one ministry from remote areas at the very time that a different ministry might be hauling similar resources in the opposite direction.
text_raw:
This  hampered  expansion
and  also  resulted  in  very  expensive  cross-hauling  of  the  freight  of  one  ministry  from
remote  areas  at  the  very  time  that  a  different  ministry  might  be  hauling  similar  resources
in  the  opposite  direction.

text: The serious overworking of the Soviet railway system, a constant weakness in the economy, was intensified by such needless hauling..
text_raw:
The  serious  overworking  of  the  Soviet  railway  system,  a
constant  weakness  in  the  economy,  was  intensified  by  such  needless  hauling..

text: In spite of its merits, the anti-K group in the Presidium was unwilling to adopt this reform because it would drastically weaken centralized state control and strengthen localized party control in the Soviet economy.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  its  merits,  the  anti-K  group  in  the  Presidium  was  unwilling  to  adopt  this
reform  because  it  would  drastically  weaken  centralized  state  control  and  strengthen
localized  party  control  in  the  Soviet  economy.

text: The state hierarchy of Soviets had fallen into decay, partly because of Stalin's use of the party and secret police, partly as a means to avoid use of the fraudulently democratic Soviet constitution and of its federalist features.
text_raw:
The  state  hierarchy  of  Soviets  had  fallen
into  decay,  partly  because  of  Stalin's  use  of  the  party  and  secret  police,  partly  as  a  means
to  avoid  use  of  the  fraudulently  democratic  Soviet  constitution  and  of  its  federalist
features.

text: As a consequence, the state hierarchy lacked effective or flexible control down through its levels, while the party hierarchy had these well developed.
text_raw:
As  a  consequence,  the  state  hierarchy  lacked  effective  or  flexible  control  down
through  its  levels,  while  the  party  hierarchy  had  these  well  developed.

text: Much of the state's power locally was exercised through the economic ministries, which Khrushchev now wished to abolish.
text_raw:
Much  of  the  state's
power  locally  was  exercised  through  the  economic  ministries,  which  Khrushchev  now
wished  to  abolish.

text: And because of his control of the party and through it of the party press, headed by Pravda, Khrushchev could keep up a steady drum of propaganda for his economic reorganization.
text_raw:
And  because  of  his  control  of  the  party  and  through  it  of  the  party
press,  headed  by  Pravda,  Khrushchev  could  keep  up  a  steady  drum  of  propaganda  for  his
economic  reorganization.

text: Every local figure was for it, and it appeared to other rival leaders as an anti-state move.
text_raw:
Every  local  figure  was  for  it,  and  it  appeared  to  other  rival
leaders  as  an  anti-state  move.

text: Khrushchev, on the other hand, could make the opposition seem "anti-party," with all the treasonable overtones Stalin had given to that expression.
text_raw:
Khrushchev,  on  the  other  hand,  could  make  the  opposition
seem  "anti-party,"  with  all  the  treasonable  overtones  Stalin  had  given  to  that  expression.

text: The economic reorganization law was passed on May 10, 1957, abolishing twenty-five economic ministries (retaining nineteen) and devolving their functions to twenty-nine regional sovnarkhozy; the State Economic Commission (GEK) was also abolished, leaving, as the only central economic control, the State Committee for Long-Term Planning under Yosif Kuzmin (a Khrushchev party official), who simultaneously became first deputy prime minister of the Soviet Union.
text_raw:
The  economic  reorganization  law  was  passed  on  May  10,  1957,  abolishing  twenty-five
economic  ministries  (retaining  nineteen)  and  devolving  their  functions  to  twenty-nine
regional  sovnarkhozy;  the  State  Economic  Commission  (GEK)  was  also  abolished,
leaving,  as  the  only  central  economic  control,  the  State  Committee  for  Long-Term
Planning  under  Yosif  Kuzmin  (a  Khrushchev  party  official),  who  simultaneously  became
first  deputy  prime  minister  of  the  Soviet  Union.

text: Shepilov was restored to the secretaryship of the Central Committee, which he had lost in December.
text_raw:
Shepilov  was  restored  to  the
secretaryship  of  the  Central  Committee,  which  he  had  lost  in  December.

text: These changes were pushed through by an alliance of the party, the army, and all the forces of localism, both economic and state.
text_raw:
These  changes
were  pushed  through  by  an  alliance  of  the  party,  the  army,  and  all  the  forces  of  localism,
both  economic  and  state.

text: Khrushchev had won a great victory, which could make the party dominant in economic life.
text_raw:
Khrushchev  had  won  a  great  victory,  which  could  make  the
party  dominant  in  economic  life.

text: Having failed to block Khrushchev's economic plans, his rivals in the Presidium were reduced to a last resort: they had to get rid of the man himself.
text_raw:
Having  failed  to  block  Khrushchev's  economic  plans,  his  rivals  in  the  Presidium  were
reduced  to  a  last  resort:  they  had  to  get  rid  of  the  man  himself.

text: On June 18th, at a meeting of the Presidium, the motion was made to remove Khrushchev as first party secretary.
text_raw:
On  June  18th,  at  a  meeting
of  the  Presidium,  the  motion  was  made  to  remove  Khrushchev  as  first  party  secretary.

text: The discussion grew violent, with Malenkov and Molotov attacking and Khrushchev defending himself.
text_raw:
The  discussion  grew  violent,  with  Malenkov  and  Molotov  attacking  and  Khrushchev
defending  himself.

text: He was accused of practicing a "cult of personality" of his own, of ideological aberrations which threatened the solidarity of Communism, and of economic mismanagement.

text: The orthodox military ideas of the Russians, like everything else, had been stated by Stalin and were not allowed to change, under the impact of new ideas or of new weapons, until after his death.

text: Thus Stalin orthodoxy regarded war as a struggle between whole societies, each with its distinctive way of life, and judged that the outcome would be determined by what was called the "permanently operating factors." These factors emphasized the characteristics of the society, such as industrial strength, morale, level of training, and reserve forces.
text_raw:
Thus  Stalin  orthodoxy  regarded  war  as  a  struggle  between  whole
societies,  each  with  its  distinctive  way  of  life,  and  judged  that  the  outcome  would  be

training,  and  reserve  forces.

text: Other, "accidental," factors, such as weather, surprise, ability of individual commanders (even Napoleon), or the outcome of single battles, were regarded as of little significance.

text: To them, victory was achieved by destruction of the enemy's armed forces by a series of blows and conflicts over a long time, during which the permanent factors, especially the forces of industrial strength and national morale, would be decisive.

text: The Russians generally reject the idea of mutual annihilation or the total destruction of all Civilization in war, and insist that any war, however severe, will leave some remnant of the Soviet Union surviving as victor on the field.

possibility  of  limited  war,  in  a  geographical  sense,  but  have  little  hope  of  any  war  limited

text: A Race between Disaster and Reform
text_raw: A  Race  between  Disaster  and  Reform

text: As time remorselessly moves forward through the second half of the twentieth century, a major problem for the United States is the fate of Latin America, that gigantic portion of the Western Hemisphere that is south of the Rio Grande.
text_raw:
As  time  remorselessly  moves  forward  through  the  second  half  of  the  twentieth
century,  a  major  problem  for  the  United  States  is  the  fate  of  Latin  America,  that  gigantic
portion  of  the  Western  Hemisphere  that  is  south  of  the  Rio  Grande.

text: It is not an area that can continue to be ignored, because it is neither small nor remote, and its problems are both urgent and explosive.
text_raw:
It  is  not  an  area  that
can  continue  to  be  ignored,  because  it  is  neither  small  nor  remote,  and  its  problems  are
both  urgent  and  explosive.

text: Yet, until 1960, it was ignored.
text_raw: Yet,  until  1960,  it  was  ignored.

text: The Latin America that demanded attention in 1960 was twice the size of the United States (7.5 million square miles compared to 3.6 million square miles), with a population about lo percent larger (200 million persons compared to our 180 million in 1960).
text_raw:
The  Latin  America  that  demanded  attention  in  1960  was  twice  the  size  of  the  United
States  (7.5  million  square  miles  compared  to  3.6  million  square  miles),  with  a  population
about  lo  percent  larger  (200  million  persons  compared  to  our  180  million  in  1960).

text: Brazil, which spoke Portuguese rather than Spanish, had almost half the total area with more than a third the total population (75 million in 1960).
text_raw:

more  than  a  third  the  total  population  (75  million  in  1960).

text: In 1960 Brazil reached the end of a decade of economic and population expansion during which its economy was growing at about 7 percent a year while its population was growing over 2.5 percent a year, both close to the fastest rates in the world.

end  of  a  decade  of  economic  and  population  expansion  during  which  its  economy  was

year,  both  close  to  the  fastest  rates  in  the  world.

text: (The population increase of Asia was about 1.8 percent a year, Russia and the United States were less, while Europe was only 0.7 percent a year.) Brazil's rate of economic growth fell to about 3 percent a year after 1960, while its population explosion became worse, apparently trying to catch up with the Brazilian cost of living, which rose 40 percent in 1961, 50 percent in 1962, and 70 percent in 1963.

text: Latin America is not only poverty-ridden, but the distribution of wealth and income is so unequal that the most ostentatious luxury exists for a small group side by side with the most degrading poverty for the overwhelming majority, with a growing but very small group in between.

most  degrading  poverty  for  the  overwhelming  majority,  with  a  growing  but  very  small
group  in  between.

text_raw:
Failure  to  recognize  that  Latin  America's  weaknesses  are  not  based  on  lack  of
substance  but  on  lack  of  constructive  patterns  is  one  of  the  two  chief  reasons  why  the
future  of  Latin  America  looks  so  discouraging.

text: The other reason is failure to recognize that the chief problem in planning Latin America's future is that of establishing a constructive sequence of priorities.
text_raw:
The  other  reason  is  failure  to  recognize
that  the  chief  problem  in  planning  Latin  America's  future  is  that  of  establishing  a
constructive  sequence  of  priorities.

text: In fact, these two problems: obtaining constructive patterns and obtaining a constructive sequence of priorities, are the keys to salvation of all the underdeveloped and backward areas of the globe.
text_raw:
In  fact,  these  two  problems:  obtaining  constructive
patterns  and  obtaining  a  constructive  sequence  of  priorities,  are  the  keys  to  salvation  of
all  the  underdeveloped  and  backward  areas  of  the  globe.

text: We might sum up this general situation by saying that the salvation of our poor, harassed globe depends on structure and sequence (or on patterns and priorities)..
text_raw:
We  might  sum  up  this  general
situation  by  saying  that  the  salvation  of  our  poor,  harassed  globe  depends  on  structure
and  sequence  (or  on  patterns  and  priorities)..

text: In applying these two paradigms to Latin American development, we shall find that the problem of priorities is much easier to solve than the problem of patterns.
text_raw:
In  applying  these  two  paradigms  to  Latin  American  development,  we  shall  find  that
the  problem  of  priorities  is  much  easier  to  solve  than  the  problem  of  patterns.

text: Obviously, the ... food supply must be increased faster than the population.
text_raw:
Obviously,
the  ...  food  supply  must  be  increased  faster  than  the  population.

text: And some provision must be made to provide peasants with capital and know-how before the great landed estates are divided up among them.
text_raw:
And  some  provision  must
be  made  to  provide  peasants  with  capital  and  know-how  before  the  great  landed  estates
are  divided  up  among  them.

text: Equally urgent is the caution that some provision for capital accumulation and its investment in better methods of production must be made before the
text_raw:
Equally  urgent  is  the  caution  that  some  provision  for  capital
accumulation  and  its  investment  in  better  methods  of  production  must  be  made  before  the

text: present accumulation of excess incomes in the hands of the existing oligarchies is destroyed by redistribution of the incomes of the rich (who could invest it) to the poor (who could only consume it).
text_raw:
present  accumulation  of  excess  incomes  in  the  hands  of  the  existing  oligarchies  is
destroyed  by  redistribution  of  the  incomes  of  the  rich  (who  could  invest  it)  to  the  poor
(who  could  only  consume  it).

text: It should be obvious (but unfortunately is not) that a more productive organization of resources should have priority over any effort to raise standards of living.
text_raw:
It  should  be  obvious  (but  unfortunately  is  not)  that  a  more
productive  organization  of  resources  should  have  priority  over  any  effort  to  raise
standards  of  living.

text: And it should be equally obvious that Latin America's own resources (including its own capital accumulation and its own know-how) should be devoted to this effort before the responsibility for Latin American economic development is placed on the resources of North Americans or other outsiders.
text_raw:
And  it  should  be  equally  obvious  that  Latin  America's  own  resources
(including  its  own  capital  accumulation  and  its  own  know-how)  should  be  devoted  to  this
effort  before  the  responsibility  for  Latin  American  economic  development  is  placed  on
the  resources  of  North  Americans  or  other  outsiders.

text: This last point might be amplified.
text_raw: This  last  point  might  be  amplified.

text: We hear a great deal about Latin America's need for American capital and American know-how, when in fact the need for these is much less than the need for utilization of Latin America's own capital and know-how.
text_raw:
We  hear  a  great  deal  about  Latin  America's  need
for  American  capital  and  American  know-how,  when  in  fact  the  need  for  these  is  much
less  than  the  need  for  utilization  of  Latin  America's  own  capital  and  know-how.

text: The wealth and income of Latin America, in absolute quantities, is so great and it is so inequitably controlled and distributed that there is an enormous accumulation of incomes, far beyond their consumption needs, in the hands of a small percentage of Latin Americans.
text_raw:
The
wealth  and  income  of  Latin  America,  in  absolute  quantities,  is  so  great  and  it  is  so
inequitably  controlled  and  distributed  that  there  is  an  enormous  accumulation  of  incomes,
far  beyond  their  consumption  needs,  in  the  hands  of  a  small  percentage  of  Latin
Americans.

text: Much of these excess incomes are wasted, hoarded, or merely used for wasteful competition in ostentatious social display.
text_raw:
Much  of  these  excess  incomes  are  wasted,  hoarded,  or  merely  used  for
wasteful  competition  in  ostentatious  social  display.

text: This, as we shall see, is largely due to the deficiencies of Latin American personalities and character.
text_raw:
This,  as  we  shall  see,  is  largely  due  to
the  deficiencies  of  Latin  American  personalities  and  character.

text: The contrast, from this point of view, between England in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries and Latin America in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries is very instructive.
text_raw:
The  contrast,  from  this
point  of  view,  between  England  in  the  eighteenth  and  nineteenth  centuries  and  Latin
America  in  the  nineteenth  and  twentieth  centuries  is  very  instructive.

text: In both cases there was such a drastic inequity in the distribution of national incomes that the masses of the people were in abject poverty and probably getting poorer.
text_raw:
In  both  cases  there
was  such  a  drastic  inequity  in  the  distribution  of  national  incomes  that  the  masses  of  the
people  were  in  abject  poverty  and  probably  getting  poorer.

text: But in England there were groups benefitting from this inequality who eschewed all self-indulgence, luxury, or ostentatious display of wealth, and systematically invested their growing incomes in creating new and more efficient patterns of utilization of resources.
text_raw:
But  in  England  there  were
groups  benefitting  from  this  inequality  who  eschewed  all  self-indulgence,  luxury,  or
ostentatious  display  of  wealth,  and  systematically  invested  their  growing  incomes  in
creating  new  and  more  efficient  patterns  of  utilization  of  resources.

text: This is in sharp contrast to the situation in Latin America where such excess wealth, in the aggregate, is much greater than that being accumulated, a century or more ago, in England, but is very largely wasted and surely is not being used to create more productive patterns for utilization of resources, except in rare cases..
text_raw:
This  is  in  sharp
contrast  to  the  situation  in  Latin  America  where  such  excess  wealth,  in  the  aggregate,  is
much  greater  than  that  being  accumulated,  a  century  or  more  ago,  in  England,  but  is  very
largely  wasted  and  surely  is  not  being  used  to  create  more  productive  patterns  for
utilization  of  resources,  except  in  rare  cases..

text: The solution to this problem is not, as we have said, to redistribute incomes in Latin America, but to change the patterns of character and of personality formation so that excess incomes will be used constructively and not wasted (nor simply redistributed and consumed).
text_raw:
The  solution  to  this  problem  is  not,  as  we  have  said,  to  redistribute  incomes  in  Latin
America,  but  to  change  the  patterns  of  character  and  of  personality  formation  so  that
excess  incomes  will  be  used  constructively  and  not  wasted  (nor  simply  redistributed  and
consumed).

text: A similar situation exists in regard to foreign exchange.
text_raw: A  similar  situation  exists  in  regard  to  foreign  exchange.

text: Alternately our compassion is stirred and our anger aroused by American reformers and Latin agitators at the iniquities of the colonial character of Latin America's position in the world economy.
text_raw:
Alternately  our  compassion  is
stirred  and  our  anger  aroused  by  American  reformers  and  Latin  agitators  at  the  iniquities
of  the  colonial  character  of  Latin  America's  position  in  the  world  economy.

text: This simply means that Latin America exports raw materials, minerals, and agricultural products (generally unprocessed goods), and imports processed, manufactured goods.
text_raw:
This  simply
means  that  Latin  America  exports  raw  materials,  minerals,  and  agricultural  products
(generally  unprocessed  goods),  and  imports  processed,  manufactured  goods.

text: Since the prices of unprocessed goods are generally more competitive, and therefore more fluctuating, than those of manufactured goods, the so-called "terms of trade" tend to run either favorably for or very unfavorably against Latin America.
text_raw:
Since  the
prices  of  unprocessed  goods  are  generally  more  competitive,  and  therefore  more
fluctuating,  than  those  of  manufactured  goods,  the  so-called  "terms  of  trade"  tend  to  run
either  favorably  for  or  very  unfavorably  against  Latin  America.

text: In the latter case, which has been generally prevalent for the last few years, the prices Latin America has to pay on the world's markets have tended to rise, while the prices that it gets for its own goods have tended to fall.
text_raw:
In  the  latter  case,  which
has  been  generally  prevalent  for  the  last  few  years,  the  prices  Latin  America  has  to  pay
on  the  world's  markets  have  tended  to  rise,  while  the  prices  that  it  gets  for  its  own  goods
have  tended  to  fall.

text: As European economists would say, "The blades of the scissors have
text_raw: As  European  economists  would  say,  "The  blades  of  the  scissors  have

text: opened." American farmers, who speak of the "terms of parity," have been suffering the same way in the American domestic market.

opened."  American  farmers,  who  speak  of  the  "terms  of  parity,"  have  been  suffering  the
same  way  in  the  American  domestic  market.

text: Now, this is perfectly true.
text_raw: Now,  this  is  perfectly  true.

text: The Latin American economy is largely a colonial one (like Australia, New Zealand, West Africa, or Montana).
text_raw:
The  Latin  American  economy  is  largely  a  colonial  one
(like  Australia,  New  Zealand,  West  Africa,  or  Montana).

text: In fact, in Latin America, in recent years, at least half the value of American aid has been wiped away by the worsening of Latin America's terms of trade, which made it necessary for it to pay more and more foreign moneys for its imports at the same time that it got less and less foreign moneys for its exports.
text_raw:
In  fact,  in  Latin  America,  in
recent  years,  at  least  half  the  value  of  American  aid  has  been  wiped  away  by  the
worsening  of  Latin  America's  terms  of  trade,  which  made  it  necessary  for  it  to  pay  more
and  more  foreign  moneys  for  its  imports  at  the  same  time  that  it  got  less  and  less  foreign
moneys  for  its  exports.

text: But the fact remains that this reduction in the supply of foreign exchange available for Latin America's purchases of advanced equipment overseas has been made much worse by the fact that wealthy Latin Americans buy up much of the available supply of such foreign exchange for self-indulgent and nonconstructive spending abroad or simply to hoard their incomes in politically safer areas in New York, London, or Switzerland.
text_raw:
But  the  fact  remains  that  this  reduction  in  the  supply  of  foreign
exchange  available  for  Latin  America's  purchases  of  advanced  equipment  overseas  has
been  made  much  worse  by  the  fact  that  wealthy  Latin  Americans  buy  up  much  of  the
available  supply  of  such  foreign  exchange  for  self-indulgent  and  nonconstructive
spending  abroad  or  simply  to  hoard  their  incomes  in  politically  safer  areas  in  New  York,
London,  or  Switzerland.

text: Estimates of the total of such Latin American hoards abroad range between one billion and two billion dollars.
text_raw:
Estimates  of  the  total  of  such  Latin  American  hoards  abroad
range  between  one  billion  and  two  billion  dollars.

text: The solution to this problem must be found in more responsible, more public-spirited, and more constructive patterns of outlook, of money flows, and of political and social security.
text_raw:
The  solution  to  this  problem  must  be  found  in  more  responsible,  more  public-spirited,
and  more  constructive  patterns  of  outlook,  of  money  flows,  and  of  political  and  social
security.

text: A similar solution must be found for some of the social deficiencies of Latin America, such as inadequate education, housing, and social stability.
text_raw:
A  similar  solution  must  be  found  for  some  of  the  social  deficiencies  of  Latin  America,
such  as  inadequate  education,  housing,  and  social  stability.

text: Widespread tax evasion by the rich; bribery and corruption in public life; and brutality and selfishness in social life can be reduced and largely eliminated in Latin America by changing patterns in Latin American life and utilization of resources without much need for funds, sermons, or demonstrations from foreigners (least of all Americans).
text_raw:
Widespread  tax  evasion  by
the  rich;  bribery  and  corruption  in  public  life;  and  brutality  and  selfishness  in  social  life
can  be  reduced  and  largely  eliminated  in  Latin  America  by  changing  patterns  in  Latin
American  life  and  utilization  of  resources  without  much  need  for  funds,  sermons,  or
demonstrations  from  foreigners  (least  of  all  Americans).

text: This is not an argument for a reduction in American aid or in American concern for Latin America.
text_raw:
This  is  not  an  argument  for  a  reduction  in  American  aid  or  in  American  concern  for
Latin  America.

text: It is a plea for recognition, by all concerned, that the problems of Latin America, and the possible solutions to these problems, rest on questions of structure and sequence and not on questions of resources, wealth, or even know-how.
text_raw:
It  is  a  plea  for  recognition,  by  all  concerned,  that  the  problems  of  Latin
America,  and  the  possible  solutions  to  these  problems,  rest  on  questions  of  structure  and
sequence  and  not  on  questions  of  resources,  wealth,  or  even  know-how.

text: The connection of that last word "know-how" to the whole problem may not be sufficiently clear.
text_raw:
The  connection  of  that  last  word  "know-how"  to  the  whole  problem  may  not  be
sufficiently  clear.

text: We Americans have such pride in our technological achievements that we often seem to feel that we "know how" to do almost everything, but this know-how really exists on two levels.
text_raw:
We  Americans  have  such  pride  in  our  technological  achievements  that
we  often  seem  to  feel  that  we  "know  how"  to  do  almost  everything,  but  this  know-how
really  exists  on  two  levels.

text: One level is concerned with general attitudes such as objectivity, rationality, recognition of the value of social consensus, and such, while the other level is concerned with technological achievement in any specific situation.
text_raw:
One  level  is  concerned  with  general  attitudes  such  as
objectivity,  rationality,  recognition  of  the  value  of  social  consensus,  and  such,  while  the
other  level  is  concerned  with  technological  achievement  in  any  specific  situation.

text: The former level has a great deal to contribute to the Latin American situation, while the latter level (the engineering level, so to speak) has much less to contribute to Latin America than most people believe.
text_raw:
The
former  level  has  a  great  deal  to  contribute  to  the  Latin  American  situation,  while  the  latter
level  (the  engineering  level,  so  to  speak)  has  much  less  to  contribute  to  Latin  America
than  most  people  believe.

text: For example, American agricultural techniques, which are so fantastically successful in the temperate seasonal climate and well-watered and alluvial soils of North America, are frequently quite unadapted to the tropical, less seasonal climate, and semiarid, leached soils of South America.
text_raw:
For  example,  American  agricultural  techniques,  which  are  so
fantastically  successful  in  the  temperate  seasonal  climate  and  well-watered  and  alluvial
soils  of  North  America,  are  frequently  quite  unadapted  to  the  tropical,  less  seasonal
climate,  and  semiarid,  leached  soils  of  South  America.

text: The solution to the Latin American problem of food production is not necessarily to apply North American techniques to the problem, but to discover techniques, different from our own, that will
text_raw:
The  solution  to  the  Latin
American  problem  of  food  production  is  not  necessarily  to  apply  North  American
techniques  to  the  problem,  but  to  discover  techniques,  different  from  our  own,  that  will

text: work under Latin American conditions.
text_raw: work  under  Latin  American  conditions.

text: This situation, applied here to agriculture, is even more true of social and ideological problems.
text_raw:
This  situation,  applied  here  to  agriculture,  is  even
more  true  of  social  and  ideological  problems.

text: The problem of finding constructive patterns for Latin America is much more difficult than the problem of finding constructive priorities.
text_raw:
The  problem  of  finding  constructive  patterns  for  Latin  America  is  much  more  difficult
than  the  problem  of  finding  constructive  priorities.

text: One reason for this is that the unconstructive patterns that now prevail in Latin America are deeply entrenched as a result of centuries and even millennia of persistent background.
text_raw:
One  reason  for  this  is  that  the
unconstructive  patterns  that  now  prevail  in  Latin  America  are  deeply  entrenched  as  a
result  of  centuries  and  even  millennia  of  persistent  background.

text: In fact, the Latin American patterns that must be changed because today they are leading to social and cultural disruption are not really Latin American in origin, or even Iberian for that matter, but are Near Eastern, and go back, for some of their aspects, for two thousand or more years.
text_raw:
In  fact,  the  Latin
American  patterns  that  must  be  changed  because  today  they  are  leading  to  social  and
cultural  disruption  are  not  really  Latin  American  in  origin,  or  even  Iberian  for  that  matter,
but  are  Near  Eastern,  and  go  back,  for  some  of  their  aspects,  for  two  thousand  or  more
years.

text: As a general statement, we might say that the Latin American cultural pattern (including personality patterns and general outlook) is Arabic, while its social pattern is that of Asiatic despotism.
text_raw:
As  a  general  statement,  we  might  say  that  the  Latin  American  cultural  pattern
(including  personality  patterns  and  general  outlook)  is  Arabic,  while  its  social  pattern  is
that  of  Asiatic  despotism.

text: The pattern as a whole is so prevalent today, not only in Latin America, but in Spain, Sicily, southern Italy, the Near East, and in various other areas of the Mediterranean world (such as Egypt), that we might well call it the "Pakistani- Peruvian axis." For convenience of analysis we shall divide it into "Asiatic despotism" and the "Arabic outlook."
text_raw:
The  pattern  as  a  whole  is  so  prevalent  today,  not  only  in  Latin
America,  but  in  Spain,  Sicily,  southern  Italy,  the  Near  East,  and  in  various  other  areas  of
the  Mediterranean  world  (such  as  Egypt),  that  we  might  well  call  it  the  "Pakistani-
Peruvian  axis."  For  convenience  of  analysis  we  shall  divide  it  into  "Asiatic  despotism"
and  the  "Arabic  outlook."

text: We have already indicated the nature of Asiatic despotism in connection with traditional China, the old Ottoman Empire, and czarist Russia.
text_raw:
We  have  already  indicated  the  nature  of  Asiatic  despotism  in  connection  with
traditional  China,  the  old  Ottoman  Empire,  and  czarist  Russia.

text: It goes back to the archaic ... empires, which first appeared in Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus Valley, and northern China before 1000 B.C.
text_raw:
It  goes  back  to  the  archaic
...  empires,  which  first  appeared  in  Mesopotamia,  Egypt,  the  Indus  Valley,  and  northern
China  before  1000  B.C.

text: Basically such an Asiatic despotism is a two-class society in which a lower class, consisting of at least nine-tenths of the population, supports an upper, ruling class consisting of several interlocking groups.
text_raw:
Basically  such  an  Asiatic  despotism  is  a  two-class  society  in
which  a  lower  class,  consisting  of  at  least  nine-tenths  of  the  population,  supports  an
upper,  ruling  class  consisting  of  several  interlocking  groups.

text: These ruling groups are a governing bureaucracy of scribes and priests associated with army leaders, landlords, and moneylenders.
text_raw:
These  ruling  groups  are  a
governing  bureaucracy  of  scribes  and  priests  associated  with  army  leaders,  landlords,  and
moneylenders.

text: Such an upper class accumulated great quantities of wealth as taxes, rents, interest on loans, fees for services, or simply as financial extortions.
text_raw:
Such  an  upper  class  accumulated  great  quantities  of  wealth  as  taxes,  rents,
interest  on  loans,  fees  for  services,  or  simply  as  financial  extortions.

text: The social consequences were either progressive or reactionary, depending on whether this accumulated wealth in the possession of the ruling class was invested in more productive utilization of resources or was simply hoarded and wasted.
text_raw:
The  social
consequences  were  either  progressive  or  reactionary,  depending  on  whether  this
accumulated  wealth  in  the  possession  of  the  ruling  class  was  invested  in  more  productive
utilization  of  resources  or  was  simply  hoarded  and  wasted.

text: The essential character of such an Asiatic despotisnl rests on the fact that the ruling class has legal claims on the working masses, and possesses the power (from its control of arms and the political structure) to enforce these claims.
text_raw:
The  essential  character  of
such  an  Asiatic  despotisnl  rests  on  the  fact  that  the  ruling  class  has  legal  claims  on  the
working  masses,  and  possesses  the  power  (from  its  control  of  arms  and  the  political
structure)  to  enforce  these  claims.

text: A modified Asiatic despotism is one aspect of the social structures all along the Pakistani-Peruvian axis.
text_raw:
A  modified  Asiatic  despotism  is  one  aspect  of  the
social  structures  all  along  the  Pakistani-Peruvian  axis.

text: The other aspect of the Pakistani-Peruvian axis rests on its Arabic outlook.
text_raw: The  other  aspect  of  the  Pakistani-Peruvian  axis  rests  on  its  Arabic  outlook.

text: The Arabs, like other Semites who emerged from the Arabian desert at various times to infiltrate the neighboring Asiatic despotic cultures of urban civilizations, were, originally, nomadic, tribal peoples.
text_raw:
The  Arabs,
like  other  Semites  who  emerged  from  the  Arabian  desert  at  various  times  to  infiltrate  the
neighboring  Asiatic  despotic  cultures  of  urban  civilizations,  were,  originally,  nomadic,
tribal  peoples.

text: Their political structure was practically identical with their social structure and was based on blood relationships and not on territorial jurisdiction.
text_raw:
Their  political  structure  was  practically  identical  with  their  social  structure
and  was  based  on  blood  relationships  and  not  on  territorial  jurisdiction.

text: They were warlike, patriarchal, extremist, violent, intolerant, and xenophobic.
text_raw:
They  were
warlike,  patriarchal,  extremist,  violent,  intolerant,  and  xenophobic.

text: Like most tribal peoples, their political structure was totalitarian in the sense that all values, all needs, and all meaningful human experience was contained within the tribe.
text_raw:
Like  most  tribal
peoples,  their  political  structure  was  totalitarian  in  the  sense  that  all  values,  all  needs,  and
all  meaningful  human  experience  was  contained  within  the  tribe.

text: Persons outside the tribal structure had no value or significance, and there were no obligations or meaning associated in contacts with them.
text_raw:
Persons  outside  the
tribal  structure  had  no  value  or  significance,  and  there  were  no  obligations  or  meaning
associated  in  contacts  with  them.

text: In fact, they were hardly regarded as human beings at all.
text_raw:
In  fact,  they  were  hardly  regarded  as  human  beings  at
all.

text: Moreover, within the tribe, social significance became more intense as blood
text_raw: Moreover,  within  the  tribe,  social  significance  became  more  intense  as  blood

text: relationships became closer, moving inward from the tribes through clans to the patriarchal extended family.
text_raw:
relationships  became  closer,  moving  inward  from  the  tribes  through  clans  to  the
patriarchal  extended  family.

text: The sharp contrast between such a point of view and that associated with Christian society as we know it can be seen in the fact that such Semitic tribalism was endogamous, while the rule of Christian marriage is exogamous.
text_raw:
The  sharp  contrast  between  such  a  point  of  view  and  that
associated  with  Christian  society  as  we  know  it  can  be  seen  in  the  fact  that  such  Semitic
tribalism  was  endogamous,  while  the  rule  of  Christian  marriage  is  exogamous.

text: The rules, in fact, were directly antithetical, since Arabic marriage favors unions of first cousins, while Christian marriage has consistently opposed marriage of first (or even second) cousins.
text_raw:
The  rules,
in  fact,  were  directly  antithetical,  since  Arabic  marriage  favors  unions  of  first  cousins,
while  Christian  marriage  has  consistently  opposed  marriage  of  first  (or  even  second)
cousins.

text: In traditional Arabic society any girl was bound to marry her father's brother's son if he and his father wanted her, and she was usually not free to marry someone else until he had rejected her (sometimes after years of waiting).
text_raw:
In  traditional  Arabic  society  any  girl  was  bound  to  marry  her  father's  brother's
son  if  he  and  his  father  wanted  her,  and  she  was  usually  not  free  to  marry  someone  else

text: It was about a century, say from 1830 to 1930, before the oligarchic alliance of army, landlords, bankers, and upper clergy was seriously challenged in their exploitation of their peasant subjects or the natural resources of their local areas.

text: The same influences, reinforced by other developments, such as growing literacy, population increase, and the introduction of new ideas of European and North American origin, served to weaken the union of the older oligarchic groups so that the solidarity of the military with the other three groups was much reduced.

text: This process of commercialization and incipient industrialization of Latin American society was largely a consequence of foreign investments, which introduced railroads, tram lines, faster communications, large-scale mining, some processing of raw materials, the introduction of electricity, waterworks, telephones, and other public utilities, and the beginnings of efforts to produce supplies for these new activities.

solutions  to  problems  all  the  way  from  Pakistan  to  Peru.

text: The basic reason for this is that our policies in this great area have been based on efforts to find solutions to our own problems rather than theirs: to make profits, to increase supplies of necessary raw materials, to fight Hitler, to keep out Communism, and in recent years to fight the Cold War and prevent the spread of neutralism.

The  basic  reason  for  this  is  that
our  policies  in  this  great  area  have  been  based  on  efforts  to  find  solutions  to  our  own
problems  rather  than  theirs:  to  make  profits,  to  increase  supplies  of  necessary  raw
materials,  to  fight  Hitler,  to  keep  out  Communism,  and  in  recent  years  to  fight  the  Cold
War  and  prevent  the  spread  of  neutralism.

text: On the contrary, the Dulles efforts to bring both areas into the Cold War in a military way by treaties and armaments have succeeded only in bringing Soviet influences and Communism in by methods of subversion, propaganda, and economic penetration that cannot be excluded by military agreements and armaments.

text: And at no time did these military agreements and armaments provide any real strength to keep Russia out as a military threat, for at all times that task rested on the deterrent power of the United States and the Western alliance.

text: Although the Dulles period, because it was a crucial period, shows most clearly the failures of American foreign policy in Latin America, the situation was the same, both before and since Dulles, with a possible brief exception in the first administration of Franklin Roosevelt.

Although  the  Dulles  period,  because  it  was  a  crucial  period,  shows  most  clearly  the
failures  of  American  foreign  policy  in  Latin  America,  the  situation  was  the  same,  both
before  and  since  Dulles,  with  a  possible  brief  exception  in  the  first  administration  of

text: Otherwise, American policy in Latin America has been determined by American needs and desires and not by the problems of Latin Americans.
text_raw:
Otherwise,  American  policy  in  Latin  America  has  been  determined
by  American  needs  and  desires  and  not  by  the  problems  of  Latin  Americans.

text: A brief survey of these policies will show this clearly.
text_raw:
A  brief
survey  of  these  policies  will  show  this  clearly.

text: There are four chief periods in United States policy toward Latin America in the twentietll century.
text_raw:
There  are  four  chief  periods  in  United  States  policy  toward  Latin  America  in  the
twentietll  century.

text: The first, a period of investment and interventionism, lasted until 1933 and was basically a period of commercial imperialism.
text_raw:
The  first,  a  period  of  investment  and  interventionism,  lasted  until
1933  and  was  basically  a  period  of  commercial  imperialism.

text: American money came to Latin America as investments, seeking profits out of the exploitation of the area's most obvious local resources, mineral or agricultural, such as copper, bananas, and petroleum, or as markets for American goods.
text_raw:
American  money  came  to
Latin  America  as  investments,  seeking  profits  out  of  the  exploitation  of  the  area's  most
obvious  local  resources,  mineral  or  agricultural,  such  as  copper,  bananas,  and  petroleum,
or  as  markets  for  American  goods.

text: There was little respect for the people themselves or for their way of life, and intervention by American military and diplomatic forces was always close at hand as a protection for American profits and investments.
text_raw:
There  was  little  respect  for  the  people  themselves  or
for  their  way  of  life,  and  intervention  by  American  military  and  diplomatic  forces  was
always  close  at  hand  as  a  protection  for  American  profits  and  investments.

text: The Good Neighbor Policy, announced by President Roosevelt in 1933, reduced intervention while retaining investment.
text_raw:
The  Good  Neighbor  Policy,  announced  by  President  Roosevelt  in  1933,  reduced
intervention  while  retaining  investment.

text: It was partly a consequence of the idealism and progressive nature of the New Deal itself, but was equally based on the fact that the need of Latin America for American investment funds and for the American market, especially in the depressed conditions of 1933, made it so amenable to our economic and

progressive  nature  of  the  New  Deal  itself,  but  was  equally  based  on  the  fact  that  the  need
of  Latin  America  for  American  investment  funds  and  for  the  American  market,  especially
in  the  depressed  conditions  of  1933,  made  it  so  amenable  to  our  economic  and

text: commercial influence that there was little need for our use of diplomatic intimidation or the Marines.
text_raw:
commercial  influence  that  there  was  little  need  for  our  use  of  diplomatic  intimidation  or
the  Marines.

text: The third and fourth stages in America's Latin American policy, from 1940 to the present, have been concerned with our efforts to involve the area in our foreign policy (not theirs), that is, in the effort to get them as deeply involved as possible in the struggle against Hitler and Japan and, since 1947, in the struggle against the Soviet Union.
text_raw:
The  third  and  fourth  stages  in  America's  Latin  American  policy,  from  1940  to  the
present,  have  been  concerned  with  our  efforts  to  involve  the  area  in  our  foreign  policy
(not  theirs),  that  is,  in  the  effort  to  get  them  as  deeply  involved  as  possible  in  the  struggle
against  Hitler  and  Japan  and,  since  1947,  in  the  struggle  against  the  Soviet  Union.

text: Both of these efforts have been mistakes (with the possible exception of our relations with Brazil and Mexico in the period following 1940) because the states of Latin America, however dutifully they may have lined up in the Hot War against Hitler or the Cold War against Soviet Russia, contributed little more to victory in these struggles than they would have contributed if they had not been pressured by us to line up at all.
text_raw:
Both  of
these  efforts  have  been  mistakes  (with  the  possible  exception  of  our  relations  with  Brazil
and  Mexico  in  the  period  following  1940)  because  the  states  of  Latin  America,  however
dutifully  they  may  have  lined  up  in  the  Hot  War  against  Hitler  or  the  Cold  War  against
Soviet  Russia,  contributed  little  more  to  victory  in  these  struggles  than  they  would  have
contributed  if  they  had  not  been  pressured  by  us  to  line  up  at  all.

text: This four- stage chronology of American policy toward Latin America ignores completely the significant change that has occurred in the history of Latin America itself during the twentieth century, chiefly in the 1950's.
text_raw:
This  four- stage  chronology  of  American  policy  toward  Latin  America  ignores
completely  the  significant  change  that  has  occurred  in  the  history  of  Latin  America  itself
during  the  twentieth  century,  chiefly  in  the  1950's.

text: This is the shift in emphasis in Latin American history, especially in the history of political disturbances and governmental changes from the superficial coups d'etat that were prevalent in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries to the profound economic and social upheavals that first appeared in Mexico in 1910 and were followed in the 1950's by the revolutions in Bolivia, Cuba, and elsewhere.
text_raw:
This  is  the  shift  in  emphasis  in  Latin
American  history,  especially  in  the  history  of  political  disturbances  and  governmental
changes  from  the  superficial  coups  d'etat  that  were  prevalent  in  the  nineteenth  and  early
twentieth  centuries  to  the  profound  economic  and  social  upheavals  that  first  appeared  in
Mexico  in  1910  and  were  followed  in  the  1950's  by  the  revolutions  in  Bolivia,  Cuba,  and
elsewhere.

text: The failure in coincidence between the stages of the history of American policy and the stages of the history of Latin America itself is a fair measure of the irrelevance and futility of our policy.
text_raw:
The  failure  in  coincidence  between  the  stages  of  the  history  of  American
policy  and  the  stages  of  the  history  of  Latin  America  itself  is  a  fair  measure  of  the
irrelevance  and  futility  of  our  policy.

text: That this failure continued into the 1960's was clear in Washington's joy at the military coup that ejected the left-of-center Joao Goulart government from Brazil in April 1964, for that government, however misdirected and incompetent, at least recognized that there were urgent social and economic problems in Brazil demanding treatment.
text_raw:
That  this  failure  continued  into  the  1960's  was  clear
in  Washington's  joy  at  the  military  coup  that  ejected  the  left-of-center  Joao  Goulart
government  from  Brazil  in  April  1964,  for  that  government,  however  misdirected  and
incompetent,  at  least  recognized  that  there  were  urgent  social  and  economic  problems  in
Brazil  demanding  treatment.

text: No real recognition that such problems existed was achieved in Washington until Castro's revolution in Cuba forced the realization.
text_raw:
No  real  recognition  that  such  problems  existed  was  achieved  in  Washington  until
Castro's  revolution  in  Cuba  forced  the  realization.

text: As a consequence the Alliance for Progress should be regarded as the North American reaction to Castro rather than its reaction to Latin America's real problems.
text_raw:
As  a  consequence  the  Alliance  for
Progress  should  be  regarded  as  the  North  American  reaction  to  Castro  rather  than  its
reaction  to  Latin  America's  real  problems.

text: This helps to explain why the achievement of the Alliance for Progress has been so limited.
text_raw:
This  helps  to  explain  why  the  achievement  of
the  Alliance  for  Progress  has  been  so  limited.

text: In its early announcement, by President Kennedy during his second month in office, the projected Alliance for Progress seemed more hopeful than any earlier United States reaction to Latin America's problems had been.
text_raw:
In  its  early  announcement,  by  President  Kennedy  during  his  second  month  in  office,
the  projected  Alliance  for  Progress  seemed  more  hopeful  than  any  earlier  United  States
reaction  to  Latin  America's  problems  had  been.

text: It accepted the idea of central economic planning for the Latin American nations and the role of state intervention in investment and economic life, both of which had been rejected by the Eisenhower Administration.
text_raw:
It  accepted  the  idea  of  central  economic
planning  for  the  Latin  American  nations  and  the  role  of  state  intervention  in  investment
and  economic  life,  both  of  which  had  been  rejected  by  the  Eisenhower  Administration.

text: To these it added two other basic assumptions: that Latin America he required to take steps to help itself and not merely expect grants from the United States and, also, that social improvements, such as better housing, increased literacy, and improved social amenities, be regarded as intrinsic parts of, or even prerequisites to, purely economic expansion, and not he considered, as hitherto, to be incidental consequences of such expansion.
text_raw:
To  these  it  added  two  other  basic  assumptions:  that  Latin  America  he  required  to  take
steps  to  help  itself  and  not  merely  expect  grants  from  the  United  States  and,  also,  that
social  improvements,  such  as  better  housing,  increased  literacy,  and  improved  social
amenities,  be  regarded  as  intrinsic  parts  of,  or  even  prerequisites  to,  purely  economic
expansion,  and  not  he  considered,  as  hitherto,  to  be  incidental  consequences  of  such
expansion.

text: The formal agreement for the Alliance for Progress was signed by all members of the Organization of American States except Cuba, at Punta del Este, Uruguay, on August 17, 1961.
text_raw:
The  formal  agreement  for  the  Alliance  for  Progress  was  signed  by  all  members  of  the
Organization  of  American  States  except  Cuba,  at  Punta  del  Este,  Uruguay,  on  August  17,
1961.

text: Its aims and attitudes were admirable, but required implementation and organizational features that were not covered in the Charter itself and have largely remained deficient since.
text_raw:
Its  aims  and  attitudes  were  admirable,  but  required  implementation  and
organizational  features  that  were  not  covered  in  the  Charter  itself  and  have  largely
remained  deficient  since.

text: Its preamble said, in part, "We, the American Republics, hereby proclaim, our decision to unite in a common effort to bring our people accelerated economic progress and broader social justice within the framework of personal dignity and personal liberty.
text_raw:
Its  preamble  said,  in  part,  "We,  the  American  Republics,  hereby
proclaim,  our  decision  to  unite  in  a  common  effort  to  bring  our  people  accelerated
economic  progress  and  broader  social  justice  within  the  framework  of  personal  dignity
and  personal  liberty.

text: Almost two hundred years ago we began in this Hemisphere the long struggle for freedom which now inspires people in all parts of the world. . . .
text_raw:
Almost  two  hundred  years  ago  we  began  in  this  Hemisphere  the
long  struggle  for  freedom  which  now  inspires  people  in  all  parts  of  the  world.  .  .  .

text: Now we must give a new meaning to that revolutionary heritage.
text_raw:
Now
we  must  give  a  new  meaning  to  that  revolutionary  heritage.

text: For America stands at a turning point in history.
text_raw:
For  America  stands  at  a
turning  point  in  history.

text: The men and women of our Hemisphere are reaching for the better life which today' s skills have placed within their grasp.
text_raw:
The  men  and  women  of  our  Hemisphere  are  reaching  for  the
better  life  which  today' s  skills  have  placed  within  their  grasp.

text: They are determined for themselves and their children to have decent and ever more abundant lives, to gain access to knowledge and equal opportunity for all, to end those conditions which benefit the few at the expense of the needs and dignity of the many."
text_raw:
They  are  determined  for
themselves  and  their  children  to  have  decent  and  ever  more  abundant  lives,  to  gain  access
to  knowledge  and  equal  opportunity  for  all,  to  end  those  conditions  which  benefit  the  few
at  the  expense  of  the  needs  and  dignity  of  the  many."

text: These were fine words, and the specific detail to fulfill them was generally recognized.

These  were  fine  words,  and  the  specific  detail  to  fulfill  them  was  generally
recognized.

text: The latter included "a substantial and sustained growth of per capita incomes at a rate designed to attain, at the earliest possible date, levels of income capable of assuring self-sustaining development, and sufficient to make Latin American income levels constantly larger in relation to the levels of the more industrialized nations....
text_raw:
The  latter  included  "a  substantial  and  sustained  growth  of  per  capita  incomes
at  a  rate  designed  to  attain,  at  the  earliest  possible  date,  levels  of  income  capable  of
assuring  self-sustaining  development,  and  sufficient  to  make  Latin  American  income
levels  constantly  larger  in  relation  to  the  levels  of  the  more  industrialized  nations....

text: In evaluating the degree of relative development, account will be taken not only of average levels of real income and gross product per capita, but also of indices of infant mortality, illiteracy, and per capita daily caloric intake." The minimum desirable rate of economic growth was stated to be 2.5 percent per capita per year.
text_raw:
In
evaluating  the  degree  of  relative  development,  account  will  be  taken  not  only  of  average
levels  of  real  income  and  gross  product  per  capita,  but  also  of  indices  of  infant  mortality,

text: It was, perhaps unrealistically, stated that economic progress should be made "available to all citizens of all economic and social groups through a more equitable distribution of national income, raising more rapidly the income and standard of living of the needier sectors of the population, at the same time that a higher proportion of the national product is devoted to investment." This aim to redistribute income and achieve simultaneously higher consumption and higher investment is, of course, impossible except in the most advanced industrial societies that have already reached such levels of consumption of material goods that further increases in consumption increase problems rather than solve them.

text: To add to this rather confused idea of the process of economic development, the Charter immediately added, "Special attention should be given to the establishment and development of capital-goods industries."

text: The methods of achieving these desirable goals were only incidentally established in the Charter.

The  methods  of  achieving  these  desirable  goals  were  only  incidentally  established  in
