text: The participating Latin American countries were required to formulate, within eighteen months, long-term development programs that would include improved human resources through education and training, a reform of tax structures (including adequate taxation of large incomes and real estate), laws to encourage investment both foreign and domestic, and improved methods of distribution to provide more competitive markets.
text_raw:
The  participating  Latin  American  countries  were  required  to  formulate,
within  eighteen  months,  long-term  development  programs  that  would  include  improved
human  resources  through  education  and  training,  a  reform  of  tax  structures  (including
adequate  taxation  of  large  incomes  and  real  estate),  laws  to  encourage  investment  both
foreign  and  domestic,  and  improved  methods  of  distribution  to  provide  more  competitive
markets.

text: The drawing of such programs in areas that lacked adequate statistical information and had few trained economists was a considerable obstacle to carrying out the Charter, and only a handful of programs were approved in the first three years of the Alliance.
text_raw:
The  drawing  of  such  programs  in  areas  that  lacked  adequate  statistical
information  and  had  few  trained  economists  was  a  considerable  obstacle  to  carrying  out
the  Charter,  and  only  a  handful  of  programs  were  approved  in  the  first  three  years  of  the
Alliance.

text: As part of the Charter the United States offered "to provide assistance under the Alliance" amounting to $20 billion, of which half was to come from the government and half from private sources, over a ten-year period.
text_raw:
As  part  of  the  Charter  the  United  States  offered  "to  provide  assistance  under  the
Alliance"  amounting  to  $20  billion,  of  which  half  was  to  come  from  the  government  and
half  from  private  sources,  over  a  ten-year  period.

text: At that time, the land was extensively exploited in the Asiatic fashion, by applying larger amounts of hand labor to it.
text_raw:
At  that  time,  the  land  was  extensively  exploited  in  the  Asiatic  fashion,  by
applying  larger  amounts  of  hand  labor  to  it.

text: Much of it was terraced; more than half of it was irrigated; there was intensive application of fertilizers, including human waste, and the chief emphasis was on energy- yielding food, mostly rice.
text_raw:
Much  of  it  was  terraced;  more  than  half  of  it
was  irrigated;  there  was  intensive  application  of  fertilizers,  including  human  waste,  and
the  chief  emphasis  was  on  energy- yielding  food,  mostly  rice.

text: The reorganization of Japanese agriculture was largely due to the American Military Occupation (SCAP), and was so successful that the index of agricultural production increased 40 percent in the decade 1951-1961.
text_raw:
The  reorganization  of  Japanese  agriculture  was  largely  due  to  the  American  Military
Occupation  (SCAP),  and  was  so  successful  that  the  index  of  agricultural  production
increased  40  percent  in  the  decade  1951-1961.

text: This revolution rested on two supports: the agrarian reform and technological advances.
text_raw:
This  revolution  rested  on  two  supports:  the
agrarian  reform  and  technological  advances.

text: The agrarian reform redistributed the ownership of land by the government taking all individual land holdings beyond 7.5 acres, all rented land over 2.5 acres, and the land of absentee owners.
text_raw:
The  agrarian  reform  redistributed  the  ownership  of  land  by  the  government  taking  all
individual  land  holdings  beyond  7.5  acres,  all  rented  land  over  2.5  acres,  and  the  land  of
absentee  owners.

text: The former holders were paid for these lands with long-term bonds.
text_raw: The  former  holders  were  paid  for  these  lands  with  long-term  bonds.

text: In turn, peasants without land or with less than the maximum permitted amount of 7.5 acres were allowed to buy land from the state on a long-term, low-interest-rate basis.
text_raw:
In
turn,  peasants  without  land  or  with  less  than  the  maximum  permitted  amount  of  7.5  acres
were  allowed  to  buy  land  from  the  state  on  a  long-term,  low-interest-rate  basis.

text: Cash rents for land were also lowered.
text_raw:
Cash
rents  for  land  were  also  lowered.

text: As a result of this program, Japan became a land of peasant owners with about go percent of the cultivated soil worked by its owners.
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  this  program,  Japan  became  a  land  of  peasant  owners  with  about  go
percent  of  the  cultivated  soil  worked  by  its  owners.

text: The peasants w ere helped in making the transfer because the early period of the Occupation was one of food shortages, inflation, and an active black market with high prices.
text_raw:
The  peasants  w  ere  helped  in  making
the  transfer  because  the  early  period  of  the  Occupation  was  one  of  food  shortages,
inflation,  and  an  active  black  market  with  high  prices.

text: These profits also helped finance the beginnings of the new revolution in agricultural technology.
text_raw:
These  profits  also  helped  finance
the  beginnings  of  the  new  revolution  in  agricultural  technology.

text: This drastic change in farming methods in Japan was toward the American method of farm development, using less and less hand labor and greater amounts of capital, especially in farm machinery and fertilizers.
text_raw:
This  drastic  change  in  farming  methods  in  Japan  was  toward  the  American  method  of
farm  development,  using  less  and  less  hand  labor  and  greater  amounts  of  capital,
especially  in  farm  machinery  and  fertilizers.

text: Today all kinds of power and mechanical equipment, such as threshers, pumps, lifts, sprayers, and such, are common in Japan.
text_raw:
Today  all  kinds  of  power  and  mechanical
equipment,  such  as  threshers,  pumps,  lifts,  sprayers,  and  such,  are  common  in  Japan.

text: Most spectacular has been the spreading of hand tractors or power cultivators of 3 to 7 horsepower, something like American rototillers.
text_raw:
Most  spectacular  has  been  the  spreading  of  hand  tractors  or  power  cultivators  of  3  to  7
horsepower,  something  like  American  rototillers.

text: These have increased from 7,000 in use in 1947 to 85,000 in 1955, and to almost a million by 1962.
text_raw:
These  have  increased  from  7,000  in  use
in  1947  to  85,000  in  1955,  and  to  almost  a  million  by  1962.

text: These can be used with special attachments as plows cultivators, pumps, sprayers, saws, and draft vehicles, and have helped to eliminate draft farm animals and to reduce heavy human labor.
text_raw:
These  can  be  used  with
special  attachments  as  plows  cultivators,  pumps,  sprayers,  saws,  and  draft  vehicles,  and
have  helped  to  eliminate  draft  farm  animals  and  to  reduce  heavy  human  labor.

text: Since a farmer can do as much work, especially plowing, with this piece of equipment, in one day as used to require ten days' work using animal power, he has a longer growing season, can extend the practice of double cropping, and has much more time for other work.
text_raw:
Since  a
farmer  can  do  as  much  work,  especially  plowing,  with  this  piece  of  equipment,  in  one  day
as  used  to  require  ten  days'  work  using  animal  power,  he  has  a  longer  growing  season,
can  extend  the  practice  of  double  cropping,  and  has  much  more  time  for  other  work.

text: Two aspects of this agricultural revolution deserve special mention.
text_raw: Two  aspects  of  this  agricultural  revolution  deserve  special  mention.

text: Japan, like the United States, is now shifting its diet from energy foods, like rice, toward protective foods, like meat, milk, fruit, and green vegetables.
text_raw:
Japan,  like  the
United  States,  is  now  shifting  its  diet  from  energy  foods,  like  rice,  toward  protective
foods,  like  meat,  milk,  fruit,  and  green  vegetables.

text: And Japan, also like the United States, has now broken free from the older alternative of eitl'er high output per acre or high output per unit of labor, and has now reached the stage where both are rising together.
text_raw:
And  Japan,  also  like  the  United  States,
has  now  broken  free  from  the  older  alternative  of  eitl'er  high  output  per  acre  or  high
output  per  unit  of  labor,  and  has  now  reached  the  stage  where  both  are  rising  together.

text: In the ten years of this agricultural revolution (1951-1961) rice production went up 3o percent, but dairy cattle increased ten times, meat products about three times, fruit production almost doubled, and the number of persons engaged in farming has fallen rapidly, by better than 10 percent, or more than 1.5 million persons, in the five years
text_raw:
In
the  ten  years  of  this  agricultural  revolution  (1951-1961)  rice  production  went  up  3o
percent,  but  dairy  cattle  increased  ten  times,  meat  products  about  three  times,  fruit
production  almost  doubled,  and  the  number  of  persons  engaged  in  farming  has  fallen
rapidly,  by  better  than  10  percent,  or  more  than  1.5  million  persons,  in  the  five  years

text: As a result, the percentage of the working population engaged in farming is now about 28 percent, and has a steadily increasing portion of older persons and of females, as the younger males stream steadily to the city, seeking jobs in industry.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  the  percentage  of  the  working  population  engaged  in  farming  is
now  about  28  percent,  and  has  a  steadily  increasing  portion  of  older  persons  and  of
females,  as  the  younger  males  stream  steadily  to  the  city,  seeking  jobs  in  industry.

text: Of course, this transformation in agriculture could never have occurred if there had not been taking place equally drastic changes in industry.
text_raw:
Of  course,  this  transformation  in  agriculture  could  never  have  occurred  if  there  had
not  been  taking  place  equally  drastic  changes  in  industry.

text: These industrial changes, including a high rate of investment, rapid technological change, and excellent demand for industrial products, provided a plentiful supply of jobs and an increased demand for food and other agricultural products by city dwellers.
text_raw:
These  industrial  changes,
including  a  high  rate  of  investment,  rapid  technological  change,  and  excellent  demand  for
industrial  products,  provided  a  plentiful  supply  of  jobs  and  an  increased  demand  for  food
and  other  agricultural  products  by  city  dwellers.

text: These conditions acted like a magnet to attract a growing flood of farm products and energetic young peasants to the cities.
text_raw:
These  conditions  acted  like  a  magnet  to
attract  a  growing  flood  of  farm  products  and  energetic  young  peasants  to  the  cities.

text: The contrast between the structure and distribution of Japan's population and that of other Asiatic nations shows clearly that Japan is no longer a backward, underdeveloped, or colonial area from any point of view.
text_raw:
The  contrast  between  the  structure  and  distribution  of  Japan's  population  and  that  of
other  Asiatic  nations  shows  clearly  that  Japan  is  no  longer  a  backward,  underdeveloped,
or  colonial  area  from  any  point  of  view.

text: The marks of such a backward society are usually a high birthrate and death rate, a largely young, rural population, with the great majority in agriculture, and mostly illiterate.
text_raw:
The  marks  of  such  a  backward  society  are
usually  a  high  birthrate  and  death  rate,  a  largely  young,  rural  population,  with  the  great
majority  in  agriculture,  and  mostly  illiterate.

text: In Japan, all of these characteristics are untrue.
text_raw:
In  Japan,  all  of  these  characteristics  are
untrue.

text: Birth and death rates are very low; the population is aging rapidly, is almost totally literate, has below 29 percent in agriculture, and has over 60 percent resident in areas classified as urban.
text_raw:
Birth  and  death  rates  are  very  low;  the  population  is  aging  rapidly,  is  almost
totally  literate,  has  below  29  percent  in  agriculture,  and  has  over  60  percent  resident  in
areas  classified  as  urban.

text: Moreover, the revolution in Japanese industrial development has shifted the country out of its previous colonial orientation in economic organization and commerce.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  revolution  in  Japanese  industrial  development
has  shifted  the  country  out  of  its  previous  colonial  orientation  in  economic  organization
and  commerce.

text: Before the war, Japan lived by exporting labor, largely unskilled labor.
text_raw: Before  the  war,  Japan  lived  by  exporting  labor,  largely  unskilled  labor.

text: It did this by importing raw materials, working them up by largely unskilled labor into products of light industry, chiefly textiles, and exporting these products for more raw materials and food.
text_raw:
It  did  this  by
importing  raw  materials,  working  them  up  by  largely  unskilled  labor  into  products  of
light  industry,  chiefly  textiles,  and  exporting  these  products  for  more  raw  materials  and
food.

text: Today the Japanese need for imported food is decreasing and is shifting away from its previous food needs, notably rice, to foods of more protective character, such as proteins.
text_raw:
Today  the  Japanese  need  for  imported  food  is  decreasing  and  is  shifting  away  from
its  previous  food  needs,  notably  rice,  to  foods  of  more  protective  character,  such  as
proteins.

text: At the same time, its raw material imports are slowly shifting from those used in light industry, such as raw cotton, to those used in highly skilled industrial lines, such as electronics, where few other nations can compete.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  its  raw  material  imports  are  slowly  shifting  from  those  used  in
light  industry,  such  as  raw  cotton,  to  those  used  in  highly  skilled  industrial  lines,  such  as
electronics,  where  few  other  nations  can  compete.

text: This inevitably means that Japan's trade has been shifting from Asia and other backward areas, where it exchanged cotton textiles for rice, to the United States and Europe where it exchanges cameras, radios, tape recorders, and optical supplies for metals, manufactured goods, or materials for advanced industry.
text_raw:
This  inevitably  means  that  Japan's
trade  has  been  shifting  from  Asia  and  other  backward  areas,  where  it  exchanged  cotton
textiles  for  rice,  to  the  United  States  and  Europe  where  it  exchanges  cameras,  radios,  tape
recorders,  and  optical  supplies  for  metals,  manufactured  goods,  or  materials  for  advanced
industry.

text: Its needs for petroleum, iron ore, and other bulk raw materials are tending to shift to colonial areas, so that its petroleum now comes from the Persian Gulf instead of the United States, and its iron ore comes increasingly from India.
text_raw:
Its  needs  for  petroleum,  iron  ore,  and  other  bulk  raw  materials  are  tending  to
shift  to  colonial  areas,  so  that  its  petroleum  now  comes  from  the  Persian  Gulf  instead  of
the  United  States,  and  its  iron  ore  comes  increasingly  from  India.

text: The social impact of economic changes such as these is far-reaching.
text_raw: The  social  impact  of  economic  changes  such  as  these  is  far-reaching.

text: The cities are growing rapidly, while many rural areas are losing population as their peoples flock to urban areas.
text_raw:
The  cities  are
growing  rapidly,  while  many  rural  areas  are  losing  population  as  their  peoples  flock  to
urban  areas.

text: By 1961, 44 percent of the total population was clustered in 1 percent of the country's total area.
text_raw:
By  1961,  44  percent  of  the  total  population  was  clustered  in  1  percent  of  the
country's  total  area.

text: Tokyo, with 7 million people in 1940, was down to 3 million in 1945, and passed 10 million in 1961.
text_raw:
Tokyo,  with  7  million  people  in  1940,  was  down  to  3  million  in
1945,  and  passed  10  million  in  1961.

text: Other cities grew steadily but at a slower rate, and by the present day are agglomerating into four megalopolitan areas.
text_raw:
Other  cities  grew  steadily  but  at  a  slower  rate,  and
by  the  present  day  are  agglomerating  into  four  megalopolitan  areas.

text: Tens of millions of commuters swarm into these to work each day, and the traffic problem, especially in Tokyo, has become almost insoluble.
text_raw:
Tens  of  millions  of
commuters  swarm  into  these  to  work  each  day,  and  the  traffic  problem,  especially  in
Tokyo,  has  become  almost  insoluble.

text: As might be expected, such rapid material advance and profound social change has given rise to all kinds of social problems.
text_raw:
As  might  be  expected,  such  rapid  material  advance  and  profound  social  change  has
given  rise  to  all  kinds  of  social  problems.

text: Family discipline has weakened, and the older Japanese morality and outlooks are now widely rejected.
text_raw:
Family  discipline  has  weakened,  and  the  older
Japanese  morality  and  outlooks  are  now  widely  rejected.

text: Marxism and existentialism vie for the allegiance of the educated, while the less esoterically informed are satisfied with the pursuit of material success and personal pleasures.
text_raw:
Marxism  and  existentialism  vie
for  the  allegiance  of  the  educated,  while  the  less  esoterically  informed  are  satisfied  with
the  pursuit  of  material  success  and  personal  pleasures.

text: The gap between these two groups is considerable, and much of the stability, both political and social, in Japanese society today seems to rise from the self-satisfaction of the new middle class and the eagerness of many peasants and workers to get into that class and enjoy its benefits.
text_raw:
The  gap  between  these  two  groups
is  considerable,  and  much  of  the  stability,  both  political  and  social,  in  Japanese  society
today  seems  to  rise  from  the  self-satisfaction  of  the  new  middle  class  and  the  eagerness
of  many  peasants  and  workers  to  get  into  that  class  and  enjoy  its  benefits.

text: These benefits increasingly provide a life like that in American suburbia, with television, baseball, bulldozers, picture windows, neon-lighted department stores, mass advertising, instant foods, and weekly slick magazines.
text_raw:
These  benefits
increasingly  provide  a  life  like  that  in  American  suburbia,  with  television,  baseball,
bulldozers,  picture  windows,  neon-lighted  department  stores,  mass  advertising,  instant
foods,  and  weekly  slick  magazines.

text: The speed with which this has come about is almost beyond belief.
text_raw:
The  speed  with  which  this  has  come  about  is  almost
beyond  belief.

text: Commercial television began in Japan in 1953; five years later, 16 percent of urban houses had a set, but by 1961, 72 percent had sets; electric washing machines increased from 29 percent of urban houses in 1958 to 55 percent three years later.
text_raw:
Commercial  television  began  in  Japan  in  1953;  five  years  later,  16  percent
of  urban  houses  had  a  set,  but  by  1961,  72  percent  had  sets;  electric  washing  machines
increased  from  29  percent  of  urban  houses  in  1958  to  55  percent  three  years  later.

text: This salaried middle class is the key to the rapid achievement and political stability of Japan.
text_raw:
This
salaried  middle  class  is  the  key  to  the  rapid  achievement  and  political  stability  of  Japan.

text: Ambitious, hard-working, loyal, reliable, very adaptable to bureaucratic organization, scientific training, and rationalizing processes, they are suspicious of ideologies or extremist doctrines of any kind, and form one of the world's most amazing peoples.
text_raw:
Ambitious,  hard-working,  loyal,  reliable,  very  adaptable  to  bureaucratic  organization,
scientific  training,  and  rationalizing  processes,  they  are  suspicious  of  ideologies  or
extremist  doctrines  of  any  kind,  and  form  one  of  the  world's  most  amazing  peoples.

text: These general attitudes have given Japan the appearance of successful adaptation to democratic political life as determined by the SCAP-imposed constitution of 1947.
text_raw:
These  general  attitudes  have  given  Japan  the  appearance  of  successful  adaptation  to
democratic  political  life  as  determined  by  the  SCAP-imposed  constitution  of  1947.

text: As a matter of fact, the Japanese are basically uneasy about individualism, democracy, mass society, and the speed of their economic change, but few have much of an urge to rock the boat, and those old enough to remember the years of tension and war from 1931 to 1944 have no preference for them.
text_raw:
As  a
matter  of  fact,  the  Japanese  are  basically  uneasy  about  individualism,  democracy,  mass
society,  and  the  speed  of  their  economic  change,  but  few  have  much  of  an  urge  to  rock
the  boat,  and  those  old  enough  to  remember  the  years  of  tension  and  war  from  1931  to
1944  have  no  preference  for  them.

text: There are discontented groups, including the ultra- nationalists on the extreme Right and the various Socialist, Communist, and student groups on the Left.
text_raw:
There  are  discontented  groups,  including  the  ultra-
nationalists  on  the  extreme  Right  and  the  various  Socialist,  Communist,  and  student
groups  on  the  Left.

text: Both of these extremes, especially the former, operate in an atmosphere of considerable unreality.
text_raw:
Both  of  these  extremes,  especially  the  former,  operate  in  an
atmosphere  of  considerable  unreality.

text: The really notable feature of Japanese political ideology is the way in which SCAP's agrarian reform has driven Communism out of the rural areas and restricted it to the cities, chiefly to student groups.
text_raw:
The  really  notable  feature  of  Japanese  political
ideology  is  the  way  in  which  SCAP's  agrarian  reform  has  driven  Communism  out  of  the
rural  areas  and  restricted  it  to  the  cities,  chiefly  to  student  groups.

text: The foundations of the present political system in Japan were established by SCAP in the early years of the Occupation.
text_raw:
The  foundations  of  the  present  political  system  in  Japan  were  established  by  SCAP  in
the  early  years  of  the  Occupation.

text: In the early months of peace, 5,000,000 Japanese military were demobilized and 3,000,000 civilians were repatriated from overseas areas.
text_raw:
In  the  early  months  of  peace,  5,000,000  Japanese
military  were  demobilized  and  3,000,000  civilians  were  repatriated  from  overseas  areas.

text: When Japanese prisoners of war were eventually returned, about 375,000 in the hands of the Russians were never accounted for.
text_raw:
When  Japanese  prisoners  of  war  were  eventually  returned,  about  375,000  in  the  hands  of
the  Russians  were  never  accounted  for.

text: More than 4,200 Japanese were convicted of war crimes, over 700 were executed, and about 2,500 were sentenced to life imprisonment.
text_raw:
More  than  4,200  Japanese  were  convicted  of  war
crimes,  over  700  were  executed,  and  about  2,500  were  sentenced  to  life  imprisonment.

text: An additional 220,000 persons were permanently excluded from public life, and about I,3oo nationalist and extremist organizations were banned.
text_raw:
An  additional  220,000  persons  were  permanently  excluded  from  public  life,  and  about
I,3oo  nationalist  and  extremist  organizations  were  banned.

text: The Shinto religion was separated from the state, forbidden to propagate militaristic or ultra-nationalist doctrines, and Emperor Hirohito was forced to issue a public statement denying that he was divine.
text_raw:
The  Shinto  religion  was
separated  from  the  state,  forbidden  to  propagate  militaristic  or  ultra-nationalist  doctrines,
and  Emperor  Hirohito  was  forced  to  issue  a  public  statement  denying  that  he  was  divine.

text: A Japanese "Bill of Rights" protecting the rights of individuals and political freedoms, on a much more extensive basis than we have in the United States, was issued in 1945.
text_raw:
A  Japanese  "Bill  of  Rights"  protecting  the  rights  of  individuals  and  political  freedoms,
on  a  much  more  extensive  basis  than  we  have  in  the  United  States,  was  issued  in  1945.

text: The centralized police control in the Home Ministry was abolished, and police powers
text_raw: The  centralized  police  control  in  the  Home  Ministry  was  abolished,  and  police  powers

text: were curbed.
text_raw: were  curbed.

text: A new civil code established freedom from family domination for all and equality for females.
text_raw:
A  new  civil  code  established  freedom  from  family  domination  for  all  and
equality  for  females.

text: The Constitution itself, issued by SCAP in 1946, provided that a prime minister be chosen by the 467 members of the House of Representatives, who themselves were chosen by universal adult suffrage.
text_raw:
The  Constitution  itself,  issued  by  SCAP  in  1946,  provided  that  a  prime  minister  be
chosen  by  the  467  members  of  the  House  of  Representatives,  who  themselves  were
chosen  by  universal  adult  suffrage.

text: These were elected from 118 electoral constituencies, each represented by from three to five members, although the voter could cast his ballot for only one candidate.
text_raw:
These  were  elected  from  118  electoral  constituencies,
each  represented  by  from  three  to  five  members,  although  the  voter  could  cast  his  ballot
for  only  one  candidate.

text: This ensured representation for minority views and made it difficult to obtain a majority in the House without coalitions of parties.
text_raw:
This  ensured  representation  for  minority  views  and  made  it
difficult  to  obtain  a  majority  in  the  House  without  coalitions  of  parties.

text: However, the parties have tended to coalesce into two wings around the conservative Liberal Democrats and the Socialist Party.
text_raw:
However,  the
parties  have  tended  to  coalesce  into  two  wings  around  the  conservative  Liberal
Democrats  and  the  Socialist  Party.

text: Except for the period April 1947-October 1948, when the Socialists controlled the government during a period of extreme labor unrest and violence, control has been in the hands of the Liberal Democratic Party and its allied groups.
text_raw:
Except  for  the  period  April  1947-October  1948,  when
the  Socialists  controlled  the  government  during  a  period  of  extreme  labor  unrest  and
violence,  control  has  been  in  the  hands  of  the  Liberal  Democratic  Party  and  its  allied
groups.

text: These have generally won almost two-thirds of the seats in elections over the last ten years (since 1955), while the Socialists have had difficulty in obtaining one-third of the seats.
text_raw:
These  have  generally  won  almost  two-thirds  of  the  seats  in  elections  over  the  last
ten  years  (since  1955),  while  the  Socialists  have  had  difficulty  in  obtaining  one-third  of
the  seats.

text: The chief differences between the two parliamentary groups revolve around foreign affairs, with the Liberal Democrats committed to a pro-Western policy in strong alliance with the United States and rather isolated from Asia.
text_raw:
The  chief  differences  between  the  two  parliamentary  groups  revolve  around  foreign
affairs,  with  the  Liberal  Democrats  committed  to  a  pro-Western  policy  in  strong  alliance
with  the  United  States  and  rather  isolated  from  Asia.

text: The Socialist group wishes to weaken the American connection and resume Japan's traditional position as a leading Asiatic Power.
text_raw:
The  Socialist  group  wishes  to
weaken  the  American  connection  and  resume  Japan's  traditional  position  as  a  leading
Asiatic  Power.

text: The economic orientation of Japan and its booming prosperity have made the task of the Socialists a difficult one.
text_raw:
The  economic  orientation  of  Japan  and  its  booming  prosperity  have  made
the  task  of  the  Socialists  a  difficult  one.

text: The different views of the two parties in domestic politics are reflected in a controversy over the Constitution.
text_raw:

text: He promised immunity to the critics, so long as their criticism contributed to the unity of Red China.
text_raw:
He  promised  immunity  to  the  critics,  so  long  as  their  criticism  contributed  to  the
unity  of  Red  China.

text: These restrictive phrases were widely ignored and, in a few weeks, widespread and often fundamental criticisms of the regime were being voiced in meetings, the press, and especially in educational institutions.
text_raw:
These  restrictive  phrases  were  widely  ignored  and,  in  a  few  weeks,
widespread  and  often  fundamental  criticisms  of  the  regime  were  being  voiced  in
meetings,  the  press,  and  especially  in  educational  institutions.

text: Three evils that Mao had mentioned â€” "bureaucracy, dogmatism, and sectarianism" â€” were being freely denounced, with the Communist Party cadres the chief targets.

Three  evils  that  Mao  had
mentioned â€” "bureaucracy,  dogmatism,  and  sectarianism" â€” were  being  freely  denounced,

Some  critics  suggested  that  the  proper
solution  to  these  problems  was  to  permit  the  establishment  of  a  legal  opposition  party

text: The general consensus of the complaints was aimed at the lack of freedom to speak out, to move about, to disagree, or to publish.

The  general  consensus  of  the  complaints  was

text: On June 8th the government's counterattack began, at first relatively moderately but with increasing insistence.
text_raw:
On  June  8th  the  government's  counterattack  began,  at  first  relatively  moderately  but

text: The principle of free criticism was not revoked, but the publication of Mao's February speech on June 17th set the limits that had presumably always been in effect.

The  principle  of  free  criticism  was  not  revoked,  but  the
publication  of  Mao's  February  speech  on  June  17th  set  the  limits  that  had  presumably

text: Within a year there had been a considerable shake-up of party and state personnel, many discontented persons (revealed by their criticism) had been removed or disciplined in various ways, and "all Rightists had been eliminated." Within  a  year  there  had  been  a  considerable  shake-up  of  party  and

text: One sequel to the "Hundred Flowers" criticism was a reorganization of the upper ranks of the party and government and the provision of a succession to Mao.

One  sequel  to  the  "Hundred  Flowers"  criticism  was  a  reorganization  of  the  upper

text: Mao Tse-tung, son of a peasant who became wealthy on speculation and money- lending, was born in 1893 in Hunan Province.
text_raw:
Mao  Tse-tung,  son  of  a  peasant  who  became  wealthy  on  speculation  and  money-
lending,  was  born  in  1893  in  Hunan  Province.

text: His father, a domestic tyrant and local miser, had less than four acres, but used the labor of his three sons and a hired hand to work them.
text_raw:
His  father,  a  domestic  tyrant  and  local
miser,  had  less  than  four  acres,  but  used  the  labor  of  his  three  sons  and  a  hired  hand  to
work  them.

text: He gave his sons a basic education, but his personal despotism drove his whole family into alliance against him.
text_raw:
He  gave  his  sons  a  basic  education,  but  his  personal  despotism  drove  his
whole  family  into  alliance  against  him.

text: Young Mao's early life thus was one of severe discipline, constant domestic strife, and secret dreams of rebellion.
text_raw:
Young  Mao's  early  life  thus  was  one  of  severe
discipline,  constant  domestic  strife,  and  secret  dreams  of  rebellion.

text: By paying for a substitute worker in his own stead on the family land, he was able to get away to study for five years in Hunan Normal School (finished 1918).

By  paying  for  a
substitute  worker  in  his  own  stead  on  the  family  land,  he  was  able  to  get  away  to  study
for  five  years  in  Hunan  Normal  School  (finished  1918).

text: There he read deeply in Chinese history, especially military history, and formed a discussion group on large social questions.
text_raw:
There  he  read  deeply  in  Chinese
history,  especially  military  history,  and  formed  a  discussion  group  on  large  social

text: Becoming an employee of the library of Peking National University, he continued his reading, discussion, and self-education, and in 1920 was one of the eleven original founders of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).
text_raw:
Becoming  an  employee  of  the  library  of  Peking  National  University,  he
continued  his  reading,  discussion,  and  self-education,  and  in  1920  was  one  of  the  eleven
original  founders  of  the  Chinese  Communist  Party  (CCP).

text: Until 1935, Mao's position in the CCP was that of a dissident, and he was, more than once, reprimanded and demoted, or removed from party positions.
text_raw:
Until  1935,  Mao's  position  in  the  CCP  was  that  of  a  dissident,  and  he  was,  more  than
once,  reprimanded  and  demoted,  or  removed  from  party  positions.

text_raw:

was  that  he  refused  to  accept  the  party's  official  view,  insisted  on  by  Russian-trained

text: Communist leaders, that the revolution must be based on urban industrial workers, the "real proletariat." Instead Mao envisioned the party as a tightly disciplined group that could be raised to power on the revolutionary activities of the great mass of impoverished and discontented peasantry.

Communist  leaders,  that  the  revolution  must  be  based  on  urban  industrial  workers,  the

text: Closely related to this idea were two others that were equally unorthodox:
text_raw:
Closely  related  to  this  idea  were  two  others  that  were  equally
unorthodox:

text: (1) the role of rural guerrilla warfare in wearing down and ultimately defeating a "reactionary government" and (2) a fundamental emphasis on the distinction between "imperialist" and "colonial" nations.
text_raw:
(1)  the  role  of  rural  guerrilla  warfare  in  wearing  down  and  ultimately
defeating  a  "reactionary  government"  and  (2)  a  fundamental  emphasis  on  the  distinction
between  "imperialist"  and  "colonial"  nations.

text: This last point made it possible for Mao to regard the backward and undeveloped colonial areas as possible areas of revolutionary activity, where, as in China, the exploited peasants could provide the revolutionary impetus and could defend their revolutionary achievements by guerrilla warfare.
text_raw:
This  last  point  made  it  possible  for  Mao  to
regard  the  backward  and  undeveloped  colonial  areas  as  possible  areas  of  revolutionary
activity,  where,  as  in  China,  the  exploited  peasants  could  provide  the  revolutionary
impetus  and  could  defend  their  revolutionary  achievements  by  guerrilla  warfare.

text: The more orthodox Communist line was that a revolution could be carried out only by an urban proletariat that could be found only in an advanced industrial area, and that such an industrial base was essential to provide the modern military equipment needed to defend the revolutionary achievement against the counterattacks of aggressive, capitalist countries.
text_raw:
The
more  orthodox  Communist  line  was  that  a  revolution  could  be  carried  out  only  by  an
urban  proletariat  that  could  be  found  only  in  an  advanced  industrial  area,  and  that  such  an
industrial  base  was  essential  to  provide  the  modern  military  equipment  needed  to  defend
the  revolutionary  achievement  against  the  counterattacks  of  aggressive,  capitalist
countries.

text: In a sense Mao was much closer to the realities of modern politics and to the experience of Soviet Russia itself, since it is perfectly clear that no advanced industrial nation will go Communist and that the movement must make its advances in underdeveloped areas if it is to be successful anywhere.
text_raw:
In  a  sense  Mao  was  much  closer  to  the  realities  of  modern  politics  and  to  the
experience  of  Soviet  Russia  itself,  since  it  is  perfectly  clear  that  no  advanced  industrial
nation  will  go  Communist  and  that  the  movement  must  make  its  advances  in
underdeveloped  areas  if  it  is  to  be  successful  anywhere.

text: Since the objections to Mao's position came from the center of world Communist theory in Moscow, Mao distinguished between the Russian and the Chinese experience by calling Russia an "ex-imperialist" country and China an "ex-colonial country." In fact, however, they both became Communist while still backward countries, and did so as a consequence of invasion and defeat of the established government in a foreign war.
text_raw:
Since  the  objections  to  Mao's
position  came  from  the  center  of  world  Communist  theory  in  Moscow,  Mao  distinguished
between  the  Russian  and  the  Chinese  experience  by  calling  Russia  an  "ex-imperialist"
country  and  China  an  "ex-colonial  country."  In  fact,  however,  they  both  became
Communist  while  still  backward  countries,  and  did  so  as  a  consequence  of  invasion  and
defeat  of  the  established  government  in  a  foreign  war.

text: Thus Mao's ...belief that the revolutionary regime comes to power by guerrilla warfare supported by discontented peasantry, may well be correct, based on the Russian precedent, that Communist regimes are more likely to come to power in backward states and will survive there if they are able to use the state's despotic power to direct the utilization of economic resources toward investment to provide a high rate of economic development, as Soviet Russia has done.
text_raw:
Thus  Mao's  ...belief  that  the
revolutionary  regime  comes  to  power  by  guerrilla  warfare  supported  by  discontented
peasantry,  may  well  be  correct,  based  on  the  Russian  precedent,  that  Communist  regimes
are  more  likely  to  come  to  power  in  backward  states  and  will  survive  there  if  they  are
able  to  use  the  state's  despotic  power  to  direct  the  utilization  of  economic  resources
toward  investment  to  provide  a  high  rate  of  economic  development,  as  Soviet  Russia  has
done.

text: Red China, like Soviet Russia, is governed under a parallel structure of the party and the government in which successive layers of assemblies and committees build up from the local level to the central authority.
text_raw:
Red  China,  like  Soviet  Russia,  is  governed  under  a  parallel  structure  of  the  party  and
the  government  in  which  successive  layers  of  assemblies  and  committees  build  up  from
the  local  level  to  the  central  authority.

text: Until 1959, Mao held the chairmanship at the peak of both party and government.
text_raw:
Until  1959,  Mao  held  the  chairmanship  at  the  peak
of  both  party  and  government.

text: As a first step toward establishing a succession that would not repeat the desperate intrigue and violence that had occurred in the Kremlin following Stalin's death, he resigned from the chairmanship ... in favor of Liu Shao-chi, but retained his position as chairman of the Central Committee of the party.
text_raw:
As  a  first  step  toward  establishing  a  succession  that  would
not  repeat  the  desperate  intrigue  and  violence  that  had  occurred  in  the  Kremlin  following
Stalin's  death,  he  resigned  from  the  chairmanship  ...  in  favor  of  Liu  Shao-chi,  but  retained
his  position  as  chairman  of  the  Central  Committee  of  the  party.

text: The third man in the system Chou En-lai, is a member of the seven-man Standing Committee that controls the party, has been premier of the government since 1949, and was also foreign minister in 1949-1958.
text_raw:
The  third  man  in  the
system  Chou  En-lai,  is  a  member  of  the  seven-man  Standing  Committee  that  controls  the
party,  has  been  premier  of  the  government  since  1949,  and  was  also  foreign  minister  in
1949-1958.

text: While the structure of the governmental system of Red China is very similar to that of Soviet Russia, its spirit seems quite different.
text_raw:
While  the  structure  of  the  governmental  system  of  Red  China  is  very  similar  to  that  of
Soviet  Russia,  its  spirit  seems  quite  different.

text: This is reflected in two ways.
text_raw: This  is  reflected  in  two  ways.

text: In Russia the Old Bolsheviks of the early days of the party were all eliminated, mostly by violent death, in the internecine power struggles which went on behind the grim walls of the Kremlin, while the Politburo throughout maintained a monolithic, impassive face to the
text_raw:
In  Russia  the
Old  Bolsheviks  of  the  early  days  of  the  party  were  all  eliminated,  mostly  by  violent
death,  in  the  internecine  power  struggles  which  went  on  behind  the  grim  walls  of  the
Kremlin,  while  the  Politburo  throughout  maintained  a  monolithic,  impassive  face  to  the

text: outside world.
text_raw: outside  world.

text: In Red China most of the party leaders of today are still those who came together to engage in the earliest revolutionary struggles of the party in the 1920'S.
text_raw:
In  Red  China  most  of  the  party  leaders  of  today  are  still  those  who  came
together  to  engage  in  the  earliest  revolutionary  struggles  of  the  party  in  the  1920'S.

text: Moreover, they have, over the past forty years, often differed and even engaged in violent struggles and controversies with each other, but always were able to continue to work together, and to patch up their differences.
text_raw:
Moreover,  they  have,  over  the  past  forty  years,  often  differed  and  even  engaged  in  violent
struggles  and  controversies  with  each  other,  but  always  were  able  to  continue  to  work
together,  and  to  patch  up  their  differences.

text: The real distinction here is that the Kremlin has always insisted on presenting to the outside world a picture of itself as united and infallible.
text_raw:
The  real  distinction  here  is  that  the  Kremlin
has  always  insisted  on  presenting  to  the  outside  world  a  picture  of  itself  as  united  and
infallible.

text: This is why Khrushchev's speech at the Twentieth Party Congress, attacking Stalin, was such a shock to the world....
text_raw:
This  is  why  Khrushchev's  speech  at  the  Twentieth  Party  Congress,  attacking
Stalin,  was  such  a  shock  to  the  world....

text: The key to this rather significant difference in the tone of Communist government in Moscow and Peking may be found in two basic distinctions: a difference of outlook and a difference of procedure.
text_raw:
The  key  to  this  rather  significant  difference  in  the  tone  of  Communist  government  in
Moscow  and  Peking  may  be  found  in  two  basic  distinctions:  a  difference  of  outlook  and  a
difference  of  procedure.

text: In Russia the ancient doctrinaire and rigidly ideologistic tone associated with the traditional Russian outlook and the traditional Russian religious system, both going back to their roots in Greek rationalism and Zoroastrian religion, established patterns of ideology that have continued under materialistic and atheistic Communism.
text_raw:
In  Russia  the  ancient  doctrinaire  and  rigidly  ideologistic  tone
associated  with  the  traditional  Russian  outlook  and  the  traditional  Russian  religious
system,  both  going  back  to  their  roots  in  Greek  rationalism  and  Zoroastrian  religion,
established  patterns  of  ideology  that  have  continued  under  materialistic  and  atheistic
Communism.

text: Such attitudes are foreign to the traditions of Chinese pragmatism.
text_raw: Such  attitudes  are  foreign  to  the  traditions  of  Chinese  pragmatism.

text: Moreover, the origins of Chinese Communist organization in discussion groups in which all those present recognized their own ignorance and the inadequacy of their information on social facts, as well as on Marxist dogma, has continued in the practice of almost endless party meetings on all levels, filled with discussion, debate, and individual examination of one's own position and attitudes.
text_raw:
Moreover,  the  origins  of  Chinese  Communist  organization  in  discussion  groups  in  which
all  those  present  recognized  their  own  ignorance  and  the  inadequacy  of  their  information
on  social  facts,  as  well  as  on  Marxist  dogma,  has  continued  in  the  practice  of  almost
endless  party  meetings  on  all  levels,  filled  with  discussion,  debate,  and  individual
examination  of  one's  own  position  and  attitudes.

text: As one remarkable consequence of these differences between China and the Soviet Union, there are at least half a dozen legal, minor political parties in Red China today.
text_raw:
As  one  remarkable  consequence  of  these
differences  between  China  and  the  Soviet  Union,  there  are  at  least  half  a  dozen  legal,
minor  political  parties  in  Red  China  today.

text: These not only exist and are permitted to participate in the governing process in a very minor way, but they are subject to no real efforts at forcible suppression, although they are subject to persistent, rather gentle, efforts at conversion.
text_raw:
These  not  only  exist  and  are  permitted  to
participate  in  the  governing  process  in  a  very  minor  way,  but  they  are  subject  to  no  real
efforts  at  forcible  suppression,  although  they  are  subject  to  persistent,  rather  gentle,
efforts  at  conversion.

text: Such efforts would, of course, change to ruthless reprisal, if these tamed minor parties made any real effort to change or destroy the position of the Communist Party itself.
text_raw:
Such  efforts  would,  of  course,  change  to  ruthless  reprisal,  if  these
tamed  minor  parties  made  any  real  effort  to  change  or  destroy  the  position  of  the
Communist  Party  itself.

text: These differences between Communism in China and the Soviet Union may be explained most readily in terms of the different traditions of the two countries.
text_raw:
These  differences  between  Communism  in  China  and  the  Soviet  Union  may  be
explained  most  readily  in  terms  of  the  different  traditions  of  the  two  countries.

text: The same applies to their different foreign policies, to which we have already referred.
text_raw:
The  same
applies  to  their  different  foreign  policies,  to  which  we  have  already  referred.

text: The foreign policy of Red China has a number of diverse aims that hold quite distinct status on any list of Chinese priorities.
text_raw:
The  foreign  policy  of  Red  China  has  a  number  of  diverse  aims  that  hold  quite  distinct
status  on  any  list  of  Chinese  priorities.

text: Naturally, in first place is to avoid any foreign- policy action that might jeopardize the Communist regime in China.
text_raw:
Naturally,  in  first  place  is  to  avoid  any  foreign-
policy  action  that  might  jeopardize  the  Communist  regime  in  China.

text: In second place is the desire to restore the traditional international position of old imperial China as a self- sufficient, isolated giant surrounded by subordinate tributary states; in this case the tribute consists of ideological loyalty to the Chinese Communist position.
text_raw:
In  second  place  is
the  desire  to  restore  the  traditional  international  position  of  old  imperial  China  as  a  self-
sufficient,  isolated  giant  surrounded  by  subordinate  tributary  states;  in  this  case  the
tribute  consists  of  ideological  loyalty  to  the  Chinese  Communist  position.

text: In third place is the Chinese desire to restore a unified ideological bloc on a world-wide basis supporting the true (Chinese) version of Marxist-Leninism.
text_raw:
In  third  place  is
the  Chinese  desire  to  restore  a  unified  ideological  bloc  on  a  world-wide  basis  supporting
the  true  (Chinese)  version  of  Marxist-Leninism.

text: This version is not completely orthodox in traditional Marxist-Leninist terms, since it expects Communist regimes to rise in backward and ex-colonial countries rather than in advanced industrial countries, and expects these events to be precipitated and carried through by discontented peasants under intellectual leaders rather than by the industrial proletariat.
text_raw:
This  version  is  not  completely  orthodox
in  traditional  Marxist-Leninist  terms,  since  it  expects  Communist  regimes  to  rise  in
backward  and  ex-colonial  countries  rather  than  in  advanced  industrial  countries,  and
expects  these  events  to  be  precipitated  and  carried  through  by  discontented  peasants
under  intellectual  leaders  rather  than  by  the  industrial  proletariat.

text: On the other hand, this version is certainly closer to the facts of present-day politics, and on many points, such as
text_raw:
On  the  other  hand,  this
version  is  certainly  closer  to  the  facts  of  present-day  politics,  and  on  many  points,  such  as

text: the inevitability of revolution, the necessary imperialist aggression of advanced capitalist states, and the role of war as the midwife of Communism, is closer to Leninism than the ideas actually held in the Kremlin.
text_raw:
the  inevitability  of  revolution,  the  necessary  imperialist  aggression  of  advanced  capitalist
states,  and  the  role  of  war  as  the  midwife  of  Communism,  is  closer  to  Leninism  than  the
ideas  actually  held  in  the  Kremlin.

text: The argument as to which version of Communist ideology, the Chinese or the Russian, is closer to Marxist-Leninist orthodoxy is singularly unrewarding, since both sides claim the advantage here, and the ideology itself, however interpreted, is so remote from the facts of economic-social development in advanced countries that no real virtue can exist in being orthodox.
text_raw:
The  argument  as  to  which  version  of  Communist  ideology,  the  Chinese  or  the  Russian,
is  closer  to  Marxist-Leninist  orthodoxy  is  singularly  unrewarding,  since  both  sides  claim
the  advantage  here,  and  the  ideology  itself,  however  interpreted,  is  so  remote  from  the
facts  of  economic-social  development  in  advanced  countries  that  no  real  virtue  can  exist
in  being  orthodox.

text: The chief fact is that the Chinese version is potentially a much greater source of trouble to the outside world than Khrushchev's ideas of peaceful competition and non-inevitable war.
text_raw:
The  chief  fact  is  that  the  Chinese  version  is  potentially  a  much  greater
source  of  trouble  to  the  outside  world  than  Khrushchev's  ideas  of  peaceful  competition
and  non-inevitable  war.

text: The Chinese version is dangerous simply because it threatens the West in an area where it is particularly vulnerable and where it has shown no great competence, that is, among the underdeveloped nations.
text_raw:
The  Chinese  version  is  dangerous  simply  because  it  threatens  the
West  in  an  area  where  it  is  particularly  vulnerable  and  where  it  has  shown  no  great
competence,  that  is,  among  the  underdeveloped  nations.

text: However, Chinese aggression in the period since 1954 has not been based on this third priority in its foreign-policy schedule but on its second priority, which seeks to create a belt of satellite subordinate states around the Chinese borders.
text_raw:
However,  Chinese  aggression  in  the  period  since  1954  has  not  been  based  on  this  third
priority  in  its  foreign-policy  schedule  but  on  its  second  priority,  which  seeks  to  create  a
belt  of  satellite  subordinate  states  around  the  Chinese  borders.

text: The year 1954 may be taken as the initial date in this effort, because at that time the Peking government published a map of China that showed the Chinese border pushed deeply into Tibet, India, and southeast Asia.
text_raw:
The  year  1954  may  be
taken  as  the  initial  date  in  this  effort,  because  at  that  time  the  Peking  government
published  a  map  of  China  that  showed  the  Chinese  border  pushed  deeply  into  Tibet,
India,  and  southeast  Asia.

text: As early as the end of 1949, the Red Chinese had commenced a moderate intervention in Vietnam, but their most successful effort to restore the traditional Chinese satellite system was in Tibet.
text_raw:
As  early  as  the  end  of  1949,  the  Red  Chinese  had  commenced
a  moderate  intervention  in  Vietnam,  but  their  most  successful  effort  to  restore  the
traditional  Chinese  satellite  system  was  in  Tibet.

text: China's suzerainty in Tibet has been generally recognized by the outside world, even in the years when China was rent by civil wars and banditry.
text_raw:
China's  suzerainty  in  Tibet  has  been  generally  recognized  by  the  outside  world,  even
in  the  years  when  China  was  rent  by  civil  wars  and  banditry.

text: By the treaty of May 23, 1957, Tibet itself accepted this status without recognizing that the status of "suzerainty" could become one of direct subordination, under Chinese pressure.
text_raw:
By  the  treaty  of  May  23,
1957,  Tibet  itself  accepted  this  status  without  recognizing  that  the  status  of  "suzerainty"
could  become  one  of  direct  subordination,  under  Chinese  pressure.

text: This pressure began at once, and reached an acute stage in March 1959, when the Chinese authorities sought to arrest the Dalai Lama, head of the theocratic Tibetan government.
text_raw:
This  pressure  began  at
once,  and  reached  an  acute  stage  in  March  1959,  when  the  Chinese  authorities  sought  to
arrest  the  Dalai  Lama,  head  of  the  theocratic  Tibetan  government.

The  anti-Chinese
revolt  that  resulted  was  crushed  in  two  weeks,  and  the  Dalai  Lama  fled  to  India.

text: During this period Chinese pressure continued into southeastern Asia, in Burma, which desperately tried to maintain a neutralist course, and especially in the successor states of former Indochina.

During  this  period  Chinese  pressure  continued  into  southeastern  Asia,  in  Burma,
which  desperately  tried  to  maintain  a  neutralist  course,  and  especially  in  the  successor
states  of  former  Indochina.

text: The subsequent division of Vietnam, the struggle for Laos, and the valiant efforts of Cambodia to follow Burma's path to neutralism have already been mentioned.
text_raw:
The  subsequent  division  of  Vietnam,  the  struggle  for  Laos,
and  the  valiant  efforts  of  Cambodia  to  follow  Burma's  path  to  neutralism  have  already
been  mentioned.

text: For years, guerrilla operations in South Vietnam and Laos have permitted an increased Chinese intervention in the area and have made increasing demands on American wealth and power to oppose it.

For  years,  guerrilla  operations  in  South  Vietnam  and  Laos  have
permitted  an  increased  Chinese  intervention  in  the  area  and  have  made  increasing
demands  on  American  wealth  and  power  to  oppose  it.

No  solution  to  the  problem  of  southeast  Asia  can  be  based  on  the  belief  that  its
troubles  arise  wholly  ...  from  Communism  or  from  Chinese  aggression.

text: For centuries, the central portion of the Malaysian peninsula, consisting of Laos and Cambodia along the Mekong River, has been under pressure from the Thai peoples to the west and the Vietnamese to the east.

For  centuries,  the
central  portion  of  the  Malaysian  peninsula,  consisting  of  Laos  and  Cambodia  along  the
Mekong  River,  has  been  under  pressure  from  the  Thai  peoples  to  the  west  and  the
Vietnamese  to  the  east.

text: From at least the seventeenth century, the area we regard as Laos was divided into three or more petty kingdoms that were unable to unite in resistance to their more imperialist neighbors.

From  at  least  the  seventeenth  century,  the  area  we  regard  as  Laos
was  divided  into  three  or  more  petty  kingdoms  that  were  unable  to  unite  in  resistance  to
their  more  imperialist  neighbors.

complex  situation.

As  we  have  seen,  French  expenditure  of  $7  billion  and  about  100,000  lives  during  an
eight- year  struggle  ended  at  Geneva  in  1954.

text: The Geneva agreements opened the way to a succession of troubles in Laos by recognizing the Leftist Pathet Lao as the government of two provinces, and recommending that it be admitted to a coalition government after a proved cease-fire and free elections.

The  Geneva  agreements  opened  the  way  to
a  succession  of  troubles  in  Laos  by  recognizing  the  Leftist  Pathet  Lao  as  the  government
of  two  provinces,  and  recommending  that  it  be  admitted  to  a  coalition  government  after  a
proved  cease-fire  and  free  elections.

The  most  vital  clause  provided  that  all  foreign
military  forces,  except  a  French  training  group,  be  withdrawn  from  Laos.

supervise  these  provisions.

text: These agreements settled nothing.
text_raw: These  agreements  settled  nothing.

The  elections  of  December  1955  brought  the
premiership  to  Prince  Souvanna  Phouma;  he  was  a  neutralist  and  brother  of
Souphannouvong,  a  Communist  fellow  traveler  and  founder  of  Pathet  Lao.

The  two
brothers  brought  Pathet  Lao  into  the  government,  but  it  did  not  give  up  its  military  bases
in  the  two  provinces  it  dominated.

The  withdrawal  of  other  military  forces  greatly
increased  the  potential  power  of  Pathet  Lao.

subsequent  elections  in  May  1958,  the  anti-Communist  group  combined  in  August  to  oust

government  in  turn  was  ejected  and  replaced  by  a  Right-wing  military  junta  led  by

Four  months  later,  in  December  1960,  Nosavan  once  again

The  Communist  countries  refused  to  recognize  this
change,  continued  to  recognize  Souvanna  Phouma,  and  increased  their  supplies  to  the

text: At the suggestion of Soviet Russia, the Geneva Conference was reassembled in 1962 and drew up two complicated agreements whose chief consequence was to revive the agreements of 1954 within a more neutralized frame: coalition government, elimination of all foreign military forces, neutrality, and a reactivation of the International Control Commission.
text_raw:
At  the  suggestion  of  Soviet  Russia,  the  Geneva  Conference  was  reassembled  in  1962
and  drew  up  two  complicated  agreements  whose  chief  consequence  was  to  revive  the

Commission.

text: The resulting troika coalition of Leftists, Neutrals, and Rightists served to paralyze the country, while the Pathet Lao guerrillas, using Communist North Vietnam as a base, threatened to secure control of the whole country.

The  resulting  troika  coalition  of  Leftists,  Neutrals,  and  Rightists  served  to
paralyze  the  country,  while  the  Pathet  Lao  guerrillas,  using  Communist  North  Vietnam  as
a  base,  threatened  to  secure  control  of  the  whole  country.

text_raw:
This  effort  broke  out  into  open
warfare  in  the  Plaine  des  Jarres  in  April  1963.

text: The growing success of these attacks over the next few years greatly agitated Washington, where officials generally felt that the fall of Laos, because of its central position, might well lead to a succession of Communist take-overs, in Cambodia, South Vietnam, Thailand, and Burma, leaving India wide open to a Red Chinese intrusion directly across these collaborating areas into the Indian plains.

the  next  few  years  greatly  agitated  Washington,  where  officials  generally  felt  that  the  fall

Some  substance  was  lent  to  this  fear  from  the  fact  that  Red  China  spent  the  years  1955-

offshoots  southward  toward  the  Malay  Peninsula.

text: This fear became intensified in 1962- 1964 as a consequence of the Communist take-over in Burma, the American fiascoes in Vietnam, and the direct Chinese attack on India.

This  fear  became  intensified  in  1962-
1964  as  a  consequence  of  the  Communist  take-over  in  Burma,  the  American  fiascoes  in
Vietnam,  and  the  direct  Chinese  attack  on  India.

The  strange  thing  about  Burma  was  that  the  increase  in  Communist  power  was
brought  about  by  the  army,  which  was  increasingly  dissatisfied  by  the  ineffectual  and
corrupt  government  of  the  democratic  U  Nu.

text: When the ruling Anti- Fascist Party split, U Nu judged it impossible to carry out the approaching elections, and yielded control of the country to a caretaker military government that promised to restore unity, honesty, and adequate administration, and supervise the elections.

By  February  1960,  the  military  leaders  judged  their  task  to  be  achieved,  and  held  the

U  Nu's  section  of  the  Anti-Fascist  Party  won  a  sweeping  victory,  and  he
returned  to  office.

Nu,  suspended  the  constitution,  and  ruled  through  a  junta  of  seventeen  officers.

text: This outlook is reflected in the structure of the Bantu languages, which do not emphasize the tense distinctions of past, present, and future, as we do, but instead emphasize categories of condition, including a basic distinction in the verb between completed and incompleted actions that places the present and the future (both concerned with unfinished actions) in the same category.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: It is perfectly true that the obstacles we have mentioned do not apply to all Africans or to all parts of Africa, but in general it can be said that most Western methods and organizations do not fit the non-Western context of the newly independent countries and that these differ so greatly from one another, or even in some cases (such as India) within a single nation, that the direct application of Western methods to these new areas is inadvisable [until certain principles of government and economics have been adopted].

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: These in turn rest on the most basic features of the Western outlook and traditions, on the way in which our cognitive system categorizes the world, and the value system we apply to this structure of categories.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: In view of the similarity of the problem faced by the newly independent nations, it may seem curious that they have not shown a greater tendency to cooperate with each other or to attempt to form some kind of common front toward the world.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: The chief effort to do this has been in the form of a number of meetings of so-called "uncommitted nations" of which the chief was held at Bandung, Indonesia, in 1955, and a number of efforts to move toward some kind of Pan- African system.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: On the whole, however, this effort toward cooperation has been blocked by three influences:

effort  toward  cooperation  has  been  blocked  by  three  influences:

text: (1) the sensitivity of newly independent nations to preserve this independence intact as long as possible, even to the degree that particularist local interests and rivalries are dominant over common interests;

(2)  the  fact  that  all  these  nations  need  economic  aid  and  technical  assistance

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: In many ways the problems of independence have a distinctly different character in Africa from Asia.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: In Asia, as is traditional along the Pakistani-Peruvian axis, the structure of societies has been one in which a coalition of army, bureaucracy, landlords, and moneylenders have exploited a great mass of peasants by extortion of taxes, rents, low wages, and high interest rates in a system of such persistence that its basic structure goes back to the ... empires before 1000 B.C.
text_raw:
In  Asia,  as  is  traditional  along  the  Pakistani-Peruvian  axis,  the  structure
of  societies  has  been  one  in  which  a  coalition  of  army,  bureaucracy,  landlords,  and
moneylenders  have  exploited  a  great  mass  of  peasants  by  extortion  of  taxes,  rents,  low
wages,  and  high  interest  rates  in  a  system  of  such  persistence  that  its  basic  structure  goes

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: In Africa the situation has been quite different, and has generally been in constant flux.

In  Africa  the  situation  has  been  quite  different,  and  has  generally  been  in  constant
flux.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: This results from a number of influences, of which one is that Africa has been underpopulated and has not developed the kind of land monopolization that supported Asiatic despotism.
text_raw:
This  results  from  a  number  of  influences,  of  which  one  is  that  Africa  has  been
underpopulated  and  has  not  developed  the  kind  of  land  monopolization  that  supported
Asiatic  despotism.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: The dominant social units of African society have been kinship groups: extended families, lineages, clans, and tribes with landownership (generally of little importance) vested in these and often with a fairly wide division between ownership and rights of usufruct.
text_raw:
The  dominant  social  units  of  African  society  have  been  kinship
groups:  extended  families,  lineages,  clans,  and  tribes  with  landownership  (generally  of
little  importance)  vested  in  these  and  often  with  a  fairly  wide  division  between  ownership
and  rights  of  usufruct.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: Moreover, land use in Africa has generally been a fallow system, often of the "slash-and-burn" type, in which land is cropped for a few years and then abandoned for an extended period to recover its fertility.
text_raw:
Moreover,  land  use  in  Africa  has  generally  been  a  fallow  system,
often  of  the  "slash-and-burn"  type,  in  which  land  is  cropped  for  a  few  years  and  then
abandoned  for  an  extended  period  to  recover  its  fertility.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: Thus agriculture has been on a shifting basis, and peasant life in Africa has been almost as mobile as pastoral activities are, without the permanent localism that is associated with rural villages in Eurasia.
text_raw:
Thus  agriculture  has  been  on  a
shifting  basis,  and  peasant  life  in  Africa  has  been  almost  as  mobile  as  pastoral  activities
are,  without  the  permanent  localism  that  is  associated  with  rural  villages  in  Eurasia.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: Moreover, in Africa tillage of the soil, usually by digging stick rather than by plow, has tended to be carried on by women, usually wives, and the relationship of the agricultural worker to any exploiter has been a matrimonial or family relationship rather than a relationship that was basically economic, as in Eurasia's serfdom, hired laborer, or plantation slavery.
text_raw:
Moreover,  in  Africa  tillage  of  the  soil,  usually  by  digging  stick  rather  than  by  plow,  has
tended  to  be  carried  on  by  women,  usually  wives,  and  the  relationship  of  the  agricultural
worker  to  any  exploiter  has  been  a  matrimonial  or  family  relationship  rather  than  a
relationship  that  was  basically  economic,  as  in  Eurasia's  serfdom,  hired  laborer,  or
plantation  slavery.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: All these features of the basic relationships between men and the land in Africa have restricted the growth of the kind of agrarian superstructure associated with Asiatic despotisms, and left instead a very amorphous and fluctuating system in which no complex exploitative system could be screwed down on the masses of the people because these people were too free to move elsewhere.
text_raw:
All  these  features  of  the  basic  relationships  between  men  and  the  land  in  Africa  have
restricted  the  growth  of  the  kind  of  agrarian  superstructure  associated  with  Asiatic
despotisms,  and  left  instead  a  very  amorphous  and  fluctuating  system  in  which  no
complex  exploitative  system  could  be  screwed  down  on  the  masses  of  the  people  because
these  people  were  too  free  to  move  elsewhere.

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: As a result of this, the kinship groups that are the chief feature of rural Africa are constantly mobile, and even today can tell how their common ancestor, a few generations back, arrived in their residence from some other vague place..
text_raw:
As  a  result  of  this,  the  kinship  groups  that
are  the  chief  feature  of  rural  Africa  are  constantly  mobile,  and  even  today  can  tell  how
their  common  ancestor,  a  few  generations  back,  arrived  in  their  residence  from  some

chapter_title: Chapter  73 â€” The  Eclipse  of  Colonialism
text: This mobile and transitory character of native African life has been increased by two other historical features of Africa's past: the pastoral intrusions and slave raiding.

text: From this flowed the Rome Treaty of March 1957, which established the European Economic Community, better known as the Common Market, as well as the European Atomic Community for joint exploitation of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes (Euratom).

text: Both agreements went into effect at the beginning of 1958.
text_raw: Both  agreements  went  into  effect  at  the  beginning  of  1958.

text: The EEC Treaty, with 572 articles over almost 400 pages, like the treaties establishing ECSC and Euratom, looked forward to eventual political union in Europe, and sought economic integration as an essential step on the way.
text_raw:
The  EEC  Treaty,  with  572  articles  over  almost  400  pages,  like  the  treaties  establishing
ECSC  and  Euratom,  looked  forward  to  eventual  political  union  in  Europe,  and  sought
economic  integration  as  an  essential  step  on  the  way.

text: The project originated with the head of the French economic planning commission, Jean Monnet, whose ideas were pushed along by the energy of Foreign Minister Paul-Henri Spank of Belgium.
text_raw:
The  project  originated  with  the  head
of  the  French  economic  planning  commission,  Jean  Monnet,  whose  ideas  were  pushed
along  by  the  energy  of  Foreign  Minister  Paul-Henri  Spank  of  Belgium.

text_raw:
Within  the  three
large  nations,  agreement  was  obtained  by  the  efforts  of  the  leaders  of  the  respective
Christian-Democratic  parties:

text: Adenauer, Schuman, and Alcide de Gasperi.
text_raw: Adenauer,  Schuman,  and  Alcide  de  Gasperi.

text: The Catholic religious background of all three was a significant factor in their willingness to turn from nationalistic to international economic methods, while Spaak's Socialist prestige helped to reconcile the moderate Left to the scheme.

The  Catholic
religious  background  of  all  three  was  a  significant  factor  in  their  willingness  to  turn  from
nationalistic  to  international  economic  methods,  while  Spaak's  Socialist  prestige  helped

text: The slowing up of the process of economic recovery that had begun with the Marshall Plan in 1949 helped to win widespread acceptance of the new effort for joint economic expansion.
text_raw:
The  slowing  up  of  the  process  of  economic
recovery  that  had  begun  with  the  Marshall  Plan  in  1949  helped  to  win  widespread
acceptance  of  the  new  effort  for  joint  economic  expansion.

text: Briefly the Rome Treaty established the methods and time schedule by which the signatory countries, as well as other nations that might wish to join, could integrate their economies into a single, more expansive, system.
text_raw:
Briefly  the  Rome  Treaty  established  the  methods  and  time  schedule  by  which  the
signatory  countries,  as  well  as  other  nations  that  might  wish  to  join,  could  integrate  their
economies  into  a  single,  more  expansive,  system.

text: Tariffs and other restrictions on trade between them were to be abolished by stages and replaced by a common tariff against the outside world.
text_raw:
Tariffs  and  other  restrictions  on  trade
between  them  were  to  be  abolished  by  stages  and  replaced  by  a  common  tariff  against  the
outside  world.

text: At the same time, investment was to be directed so as to integrate their joint economy as a whole, with special attention to the industrialization of backward and underdeveloped regions such as southern Italy.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  investment  was  to  be  directed  so  as  to  integrate  their
joint  economy  as  a  whole,  with  special  attention  to  the  industrialization  of  backward  and
underdeveloped  regions  such  as  southern  Italy.

text: Special consideration was given to agriculture, largely detaching it from the market economy to cushion the integrative process while improving the standards of living and social protection of the farming population.
text_raw:
Special  consideration  was  given  to
agriculture,  largely  detaching  it  from  the  market  economy  to  cushion  the  integrative
process  while  improving  the  standards  of  living  and  social  protection  of  the  farming
population.

text: As part of the integrative process there was to be free movement of persons,
text_raw: As  part  of  the  integrative  process  there  was  to  be  free  movement  of  persons,

text: services, and capital within the Community, witll gradual development of Community citizenship for workers.
text_raw:
services,  and  capital  within  the  Community,  witll  gradual  development  of  Community

text_raw:
This  whole  process  was  to  be  achieved  by  stages  over  many
years.

text: The agricultural agreement, for example, was implemented by an elaborate agreement that was signed after 140 hours of almost continuous negotiation in January 1962.

The  agricultural  agreement,  for  example,  was  implemented  by  an  elaborate
agreement  that  was  signed  after  140  hours  of  almost  continuous  negotiation  in  January
1962.

text: By the middle of that year the internal tariffs among members had been reduced in three stages to half their 1958 levels.
text_raw:
By  the  middle  of  that  year  the  internal  tariffs  among  members  had  been  reduced  in
three  stages  to  half  their  1958  levels.

text: The institutional organization for carrying on this process was similar to that set up for the ECSC and the abortive EDC: a European Parliamentary Assembly of supranational party blocs of Christian-Democrats, Socialists, and liberals sitting and voting together irrespective of national origins; a Council of Ministers representing the member governments directly; an executive High Commission of nine that is enjoined by law to "exercise their functions in complete independence" of their national governments; a Court of Justice witll powers to interpret the treaty and settle disputes; two advisory groups (the Monetary Committee and the Social and Economic Committee); a European Investment Bank to channel funds for integrative and development purposes within the Community; the Overseas Development Fund to do the same for former colonial territories now associated indirectly with the ECC; a European Social Fund for industrial retraining and unemployment compensation; and finally the two associated Communities (ECSC and Euratom).
text_raw:
The  institutional  organization  for  carrying  on  this  process  was  similar  to  that  set  up  for
the  ECSC  and  the  abortive  EDC:  a  European  Parliamentary  Assembly  of  supranational
party  blocs  of  Christian-Democrats,  Socialists,  and  liberals  sitting  and  voting  together
irrespective  of  national  origins;  a  Council  of  Ministers  representing  the  member
governments  directly;  an  executive  High  Commission  of  nine  that  is  enjoined  by  law  to
"exercise  their  functions  in  complete  independence"  of  their  national  governments;  a

groups  (the  Monetary  Committee  and  the  Social  and  Economic  Committee);  a  European
Investment  Bank  to  channel  funds  for  integrative  and  development  purposes  within  the
Community;  the  Overseas  Development  Fund  to  do  the  same  for  former  colonial

retraining  and  unemployment  compensation;  and  finally  the  two  associated  Communities
(ECSC  and  Euratom).

text: These last two were integrated with ECC from the fact that the Parliamentary Assembly, the Court of Justice, and the Council of Ministers are shared by all three communities.
text_raw:
These  last  two  were  integrated  with  ECC  from  the  fact  that  the
Parliamentary  Assembly,  the  Court  of  Justice,  and  the  Council  of  Ministers  are  shared  by
all  three  communities.

text: These organizations have some of the aspects of sovereignty from the fact that their decisions do not have to be unanimous, are binding on states and on citizens who have not agreed to them, and can he financed by funds that may be levied without current consent of the persons being taxed.
text_raw:
These  organizations  have  some  of  the  aspects  of  sovereignty  from  the  fact  that  their

text: On the whole, the supranational aspects of these institutions will be strengthened in the future from provisions in the treaties themselves.

On  the  whole,  the  supranational  aspects  of  these
institutions  will  be  strengthened  in  the  future  from  provisions  in  the  treaties  themselves.

text: All this is very relevant to the remarks in the last chapter on the disintegration of the modern, unified sovereign state and the redistribution of its powers to multilevel hierarchical structures remotely resembling the structure of the Holy Roman Empire in the late medieval period.
text_raw:
All  this  is  very  relevant  to  the  remarks  in  the  last  chapter  on  the  disintegration  of  the
modern,  unified  sovereign  state  and  the  redistribution  of  its  powers  to  multilevel
hierarchical  structures  remotely  resembling  the  structure  of  the  Holy  Roman  Empire  in
