text: The impact of these tentative steps toward an integrative Europe has been spectacular, especially in the economic sphere.
text_raw:
The  impact  of  these  tentative  steps  toward  an  integrative  Europe  has  been  spectacular,
especially  in  the  economic  sphere.

text: In general, the economic expansion of Western Europe, especially its industrial expansion, has been at rates far higher than those of Communist-dominated eastern Europe, with the EEC rates higher than those of non-EEC Western European countries, and considerably higher than those of either Britain or the United States.
text_raw:
In  general,  the  economic  expansion  of  Western
Europe,  especially  its  industrial  expansion,  has  been  at  rates  far  higher  than  those  of
Communist-dominated  eastern  Europe,  with  the  EEC  rates  higher  than  those  of  non-EEC
Western  European  countries,  and  considerably  higher  than  those  of  either  Britain  or  the
United  States.

text: By 1960 the 300 million people of Western Europe had per capita incomes over a third higher than the 260 million persons in the same area had in 1938-1939.
text_raw:
By  1960  the  300  million  people  of  Western  Europe  had  per  capita  incomes
over  a  third  higher  than  the  260  million  persons  in  the  same  area  had  in  1938-1939.

text: Industrial production more than doubled over the same time span, while agricultural production was a third larger with a smaller working force.
text_raw:
Industrial  production  more  than  doubled  over  the  same  time  span,  while  agricultural
production  was  a  third  larger  with  a  smaller  working  force.

text: This optimistic picture was even brighter for the Six of the EEC, whose general economic growth rate was considerably over 6 percent a year during the 1950's.

This  optimistic  picture  was
even  brighter  for  the  Six  of  the  EEC,  whose  general  economic  growth  rate  was
considerably  over  6  percent  a  year  during  the  1950's.

This  was  more  than  double  the  rate
of  growth  in  the  United  States,  which  was  not  much  different  from  that  in  Britain.

increase  from  about  a  third  of  the  income  per  head  in  the  United  States  in  1960  to  more

text: The reasons for this relative boom in the EEC (and in Western Europe generally) in comparison with the slower economic dynamics of the English-speaking countries are of some importance.
text_raw:
The  reasons  for  this  relative  boom  in  the  EEC  (and  in  Western  Europe  generally)  in
comparison  with  the  slower  economic  dynamics  of  the  English-speaking  countries  are  of
some  importance.

text: It does not seem to rest, as might appear at first glance, on a contrast between directed planning and laissez faire, because, within the EEC, the French economy is fairly rigorously planned and the West German economy is surprisingly free, yet both have had high rates of growth.
text_raw:
It  does  not  seem  to  rest,  as  might  appear  at  first  glance,  on  a  contrast
between  directed  planning  and  laissez  faire,  because,  within  the  EEC,  the  French
economy  is  fairly  rigorously  planned  and  the  West  German  economy  is  surprisingly  free,
yet  both  have  had  high  rates  of  growth.

text: The West German conditions, however, have been misleading and have arisen very largely from artificially low wage levels and thus low costs of production, especially on articles for export into the international competitive market, such as Volkswagens.
text_raw:
The  West  German  conditions,  however,  have
been  misleading  and  have  arisen  very  largely  from  artificially  low  wage  levels  and  thus
low  costs  of  production,  especially  on  articles  for  export  into  the  international
competitive  market,  such  as  Volkswagens.

text: These low labor costs arose from the large number of East European refugees seeking work in Germany, a condition that will be of decreasing importance in the future.

These  low  labor  costs  arose  from  the  large
number  of  East  European  refugees  seeking  work  in  Germany,  a  condition  that  will  be  of

text: The conditions of economic growth in the EEC has been based on steady demand, high rates of investment, and liberal fiscal and financial policies.
text_raw:
The  conditions  of  economic  growth  in  the  EEC  has  been  based  on  steady  demand,
high  rates  of  investment,  and  liberal  fiscal  and  financial  policies.

text: In 1961, for example, the rate of net investment in Britain was about 9 percent compared to the West German rate of about 17 percent.
text_raw:
In  1961,  for  example,
the  rate  of  net  investment  in  Britain  was  about  9  percent  compared  to  the  West  German
rate  of  about  17  percent.

text: The high demand that spurred on this process arose from fiscal policies, but also from the large new market of about 100 million persons provided in EEC.

The  high  demand  that  spurred  on  this  process  arose  from  fiscal
policies,  but  also  from  the  large  new  market  of  about  100  million  persons  provided  in
EEC.

text: In Britain and in the United States (with Canada) fiscal policies were much more conservative, with demand somewhat dampened down by efforts to balance budgets, to control inflation, and to influence both adverse balances of international payments and the flows of domestic credit by conservative financial policies (notably, high interest rates).
text_raw:
In  Britain  and  in  the  United  States  (with  Canada)  fiscal  policies  were  much  more
conservative,  with  demand  somewhat  dampened  down  by  efforts  to  balance  budgets,  to

text: Moreover, in both countries, there was a good deal of unproductive expenditure either in misjudged enterprises and inefficient production or in defense and other nonproductive areas.

text: As a consequence, not only have growth rates been low in the English-speaking countries but unemployment rates have been high.

English-speaking  countries  but  unemployment  rates  have  been  high.

text: In 1960, for example, the United States unemployment rate was 5.4 percent and the Canadian 6.9 percent, while that of France was 1.3 percent and of West Germany only 0.9 percent.

In  1960,  for
example,  the  United  States  unemployment  rate  was  5.4  percent  and  the  Canadian  6.9
percent,  while  that  of  France  was  1.3  percent  and  of  West  Germany  only  0.9  percent.

text: This sharp contrast between the prosperity of the EEC and the languishing economy of Britain eventually brought the latter to a recognition of the advantages of membership in the European system.

This  sharp  contrast  between  the  prosperity  of  the  EEC  and  the  languishing  economy  of
Britain  eventually  brought  the  latter  to  a  recognition  of  the  advantages  of  membership  in

text: But the decision was too late, based on wrong motives, and was eventually nullified by the imperious De Gaulle, who. like an elephant, never forgets an injury.

But  the  decision  was  too  late,  based  on  wrong  motives,  and  was
eventually  nullified  by  the  imperious  De  Gaulle,  who.  like  an  elephant,  never  forgets  an

text: Governments in London paid lip service to European unity and to British cooperation with it, but whenever an opportunity offered to take a real step toward European union, Britain balked.

cooperation  with  it,  but  whenever  an  opportunity  offered  to  take  a  real  step  toward

text: Obsessed by the pursuit of the glory of France in the nationalistic era in which his own character had been formed and personally piqued by the rebuffs he had received in his own career, the rejection of his military advice by his superiors in the 1920's and 1930s, the defeats of France in the diplomatic and military arenas in the period 1936-1940, the rebuffs administered by the United States Department of State and the White House to his efforts to make himself the leader of the Free French in 1940-1943, and finally the general belittling, as he saw it, to his ideas and dignity during the liberation â€” all these served to make his outlook more remote, more rigid, and more opinionated until he came to regard himself as the God- given leader for a revived France and came to regard the English-speaking nations as the chief obstacles in his path to this end.

text: The culmination of De Gaulle's irritation with the United States came during the five years 1953-1958, during which he was retired from public life and had to watch, in helpless impotence, John Foster Dulles's studied belittling of France's role in world affairs.

years  1953-1958,  during  which  he  was  retired  from  public  life  and  had  to  watch,  in
helpless  impotence,  John  Foster  Dulles's  studied  belittling  of  France's  role  in  world
affairs.

text: The American Secretary of State's unilateralism and "brinkmanship," his emphasis on the Far East and his ignoring of Europe, his refusal to consult with his NATO allies, and his lack of sympathy for the French position in Indochina, Algeria, and Europe itself â€” all this drove De Gaulle into an icy antipathy for American policy and a conviction that the interests of France could be protected only by France itself and could be furthered as well by collaboration with the Soviet Union as by alliance with the United States.

There  were  sporadic  strikes,  protest  parades,  and
even  riots  of  these  groups  to  call  public  attention  to  their  grievances.

text: Farmers were particularly violent when agricultural prices decreased and industrial prices continued to inch upward.
text_raw:
Farmers  were
particularly  violent  when  agricultural  prices  decreased  and  industrial  prices  continued  to
inch  upward.

text: The Gaullist government hoped to remedy the situation by reducing the costs of distribution through middlemen and thus provide French farmers with an increasing share of the reduced price of produce to the consumer, but on the whole the incredibly inefficient distribution of French farm produce, which forced most produce, regardless of source or destination, to pass through the Parisian markets, was too difficult a problem even for De Gaulle's experts, at least in any time interval that mattered.
text_raw:
The  Gaullist  government  hoped  to  remedy  the  situation  by  reducing  the
costs  of  distribution  through  middlemen  and  thus  provide  French  farmers  with  an
increasing  share  of  the  reduced  price  of  produce  to  the  consumer,  but  on  the  whole  the
incredibly  inefficient  distribution  of  French  farm  produce,  which  forced  most  produce,
regardless  of  source  or  destination,  to  pass  through  the  Parisian  markets,  was  too  difficult
a  problem  even  for  De  Gaulle's  experts,  at  least  in  any  time  interval  that  mattered.

text: To obtain concessions, the farmers rioted, often on a large scale, such as an outburst of 35,000 of them at Amiens in February 1960.
text_raw:
To
obtain  concessions,  the  farmers  rioted,  often  on  a  large  scale,  such  as  an  outburst  of
35,000  of  them  at  Amiens  in  February  1960.

text: They blocked national automobile routes with their tractors, spread unsold or unremuneratively priced farm produce over the roads or city streets, and responded with violence when efforts were made to disperse them.
text_raw:
They  blocked  national  automobile  routes
with  their  tractors,  spread  unsold  or  unremuneratively  priced  farm  produce  over  the  roads
or  city  streets,  and  responded  with  violence  when  efforts  were  made  to  disperse  them.

text: Through this whole period, De Gaulle's conduct of the government, through his handpicked prime ministers, made a shambles of the Fifth Republic constitution, which had been tailored to his specifications.
text_raw:
Through  this  whole  period,  De  Gaulle's  conduct  of  the  government,  through  his
handpicked  prime  ministers,  made  a  shambles  of  the  Fifth  Republic  constitution,  which
had  been  tailored  to  his  specifications.

text: Since a government could not be overthrown by defeat of a bill but only by a specific vote of censure, and this latter would lead to a general election in which all of De Gaulle's prestige could be used against those who had voted for the censure, the ordinary deputy's love of office and reluctance to wage an expensive and risky electoral campaign made it possible for De Gaulle's premiers to obtain almost any law he desired.
text_raw:
Since  a  government  could  not  be  overthrown  by
defeat  of  a  bill  but  only  by  a  specific  vote  of  censure,  and  this  latter  would  lead  to  a
general  election  in  which  all  of  De  Gaulle's  prestige  could  be  used  against  those  who  had
voted  for  the  censure,  the  ordinary  deputy's  love  of  office  and  reluctance  to  wage  an
expensive  and  risky  electoral  campaign  made  it  possible  for  De  Gaulle's  premiers  to
obtain  almost  any  law  he  desired.

text: The older political leaders were very restive under this system but could mobilize no organized opposition to it, because no one could see any real alternative to De Gaulle.
text_raw:
The  older  political  leaders  were  very  restive  under  this
system  but  could  mobilize  no  organized  opposition  to  it,  because  no  one  could  see  any
real  alternative  to  De  Gaulle.

text: A significant example of De Gaulle's high-handed operations may be seen in the way he forced through the bill to create an independent French nuclear force without allowing the Assembly to debate the issue or to vote on the bill itself (November-December 1960).
text_raw:
A  significant  example  of  De  Gaulle's  high-handed  operations  may  be  seen  in  the  way
he  forced  through  the  bill  to  create  an  independent  French  nuclear  force  without  allowing
the  Assembly  to  debate  the  issue  or  to  vote  on  the  bill  itself  (November-December  1960).

text: This was done under Article 49 of the constitution, which allows the government to pass a bill on its own responsibility without consideration by the Assembly unless a vote of censure is passed by a majority (277) of all the deputies.
text_raw:
This  was  done  under  Article  49  of  the  constitution,  which  allows  the  government  to  pass
a  bill  on  its  own  responsibility  without  consideration  by  the  Assembly  unless  a  vote  of
censure  is  passed  by  a  majority  (277)  of  all  the  deputies.

text: By use of this article, the three readings of the Nuclear Arms bill were replaced by three motions of censure that obtained no more than 215 votes.
text_raw:
By  use  of  this  article,  the  three
readings  of  the  Nuclear  Arms  bill  were  replaced  by  three  motions  of  censure  that
obtained  no  more  than  215  votes.

text: There seems to have been a clear majority, both in the Assembly and in the country as a whole, against the nuclear force, but few were willing to risk the fall of the government with no acceptable alternative in sight, and even fewer were willing to precipitate a general election.
text_raw:
There  seems  to  have  been  a  clear  majority,  both  in  the
Assembly  and  in  the  country  as  a  whole,  against  the  nuclear  force,  but  few  were  willing
to  risk  the  fall  of  the  government  with  no  acceptable  alternative  in  sight,  and  even  fewer
were  willing  to  precipitate  a  general  election.

text: As might be expected in such a system, the danger of assassination as a method for changing a government increased greatly, but De Gaulle continued on his imperturbable course in spite of a number of attempts on his life.
text_raw:
As  might  be  expected  in  such  a  system,  the  danger  of  assassination  as  a  method  for
changing  a  government  increased  greatly,  but  De  Gaulle  continued  on  his  imperturbable
course  in  spite  of  a  number  of  attempts  on  his  life.

text: One of the chief dangers to the Gaullist regime came from the discontent of the highest officers in the armed forces, but the mutiny and revolt of several army contingents in Algeria in April 1961 showed fairly clearly that this opposition movement was largely restricted to the highest officers, and De Gaulle was able to eliminate them and thus to reduce them, like the rest of his opponents, to angry impotence or to assassination efforts.
text_raw:
One  of  the  chief  dangers  to  the
Gaullist  regime  came  from  the  discontent  of  the  highest  officers  in  the  armed  forces,  but
the  mutiny  and  revolt  of  several  army  contingents  in  Algeria  in  April  1961  showed  fairly
clearly  that  this  opposition  movement  was  largely  restricted  to  the  highest  officers,  and
De  Gaulle  was  able  to  eliminate  them  and  thus  to  reduce  them,  like  the  rest  of  his
opponents,  to  angry  impotence  or  to  assassination  efforts.

text: De Gaulle's success in retiring from public life the only surviving Marshal of France, Alphonse Juin, clinched his superiority over the army.
text_raw:
De  Gaulle's  success  in  retiring
from  public  life  the  only  surviving  Marshal  of  France,  Alphonse  Juin,  clinched  his
superiority  over  the  army.

text: Equally successful, and typical of De Gaulle's actions, were his constant appeals to public opinion, by television or on personal regional tours, or by local elections or plebiscites, against the disunited opposition, especially against the traditional political party leaders.
text_raw:
Equally  successful,  and  typical  of  De  Gaulle's  actions,  were  his  constant  appeals  to
public  opinion,  by  television  or  on  personal  regional  tours,  or  by  local  elections  or
plebiscites,  against  the  disunited  opposition,  especially  against  the  traditional  political
party  leaders.

text: A successful example of these techniques occurred in 1962 when De Gaulle decided to change the method of electing the president (or reelecting himself) from the constitutional method of choice by an electoral college of 80,000 "notables" to election by popular vote.
text_raw:
A  successful  example  of  these  techniques  occurred  in  1962  when  De
Gaulle  decided  to  change  the  method  of  electing  the  president  (or  reelecting  himself)
from  the  constitutional  method  of  choice  by  an  electoral  college  of  80,000  "notables"  to
election  by  popular  vote.

text: To bypass the Senate, which was constitutionally entitled to vote on such matters and would unquestionably reject the change, De Gaulle announced that the amendment would be submitted to a popular referendum of the whole electorate.
text_raw:
To  bypass  the  Senate,  which  was  constitutionally  entitled  to
vote  on  such  matters  and  would  unquestionably  reject  the  change,  De  Gaulle  announced
that  the  amendment  would  be  submitted  to  a  popular  referendum  of  the  whole  electorate.

text: This method of changing the constitution by referendum was denounced as unconstitutional by all the political parties except his own, and was declared illegal by the Council of State.
text_raw:
This  method  of  changing  the  constitution  by  referendum  was  denounced  as
unconstitutional  by  all  the  political  parties  except  his  own,  and  was  declared  illegal  by  the
Council  of  State.

text: Gaston Monnerville, president of the senate, who would become president of France if De Gaulle died, denounced the referendum as illegal, and accused De Gaulle of "malfeasance." When De Gaulle's rage at Monnerville became evident, the Senate reelected Monnerville as its presiding officer with only three dissenting votes.
text_raw:
Gaston  Monnerville,  president  of  the  senate,  who  would  become  president  of  France  if
De  Gaulle  died,  denounced  the  referendum  as  illegal,  and  accused  De  Gaulle  of
"malfeasance."  When  De  Gaulle's  rage  at  Monnerville  became  evident,  the  Senate
reelected  Monnerville  as  its  presiding  officer  with  only  three  dissenting  votes.

text: The Assembly, in an overnight session, October 4-5, 1962, passed a vote of censure with 280 votes.
text_raw:
The
Assembly,  in  an  overnight  session,  October  4-5,  1962,  passed  a  vote  of  censure  with  280
votes.

text: By the referendum on the constitutional change, on October 28, 1962, De Gaulle achieved his purpose with almost 62 percent of the votes registering "ayes" (this was only 46 percent of the registered votes because of the 23 percent non- voting) in spite of the fact that his proposal was opposed by all political parties except his own.
text_raw:
By  the  referendum  on  the  constitutional  change,  on  October  28,  1962,  De  Gaulle
achieved  his  purpose  with  almost  62  percent  of  the  votes  registering  "ayes"  (this  was  only
46  percent  of  the  registered  votes  because  of  the  23  percent  non- voting)  in  spite  of  the
fact  that  his  proposal  was  opposed  by  all  political  parties  except  his  own.

text: The following month, November 1962, in the general election made necessary by the vote of censure, De Gaulle's bloc won 234 seats out of 480, with an additional 41 seats committed to his support.
text_raw:
The  following
month,  November  1962,  in  the  general  election  made  necessary  by  the  vote  of  censure,
De  Gaulle's  bloc  won  234  seats  out  of  480,  with  an  additional  41  seats  committed  to  his
support.

text: The Right was practically wiped out in the election, although the Communists increased slightly to 41 seats.
text_raw:
The  Right  was  practically  wiped  out  in  the  election,  although  the  Communists
increased  slightly  to  41  seats.

text: This pattern of personal and rather arbitrary rule, opposed by the older ruling groups but sustained by the ordinary Frenchman whenever De Gaulle asked for such support, has continued to be the pattern of De Gaulle's political system, and will undoubtedly continue unless he meets some unforeseen sharp diplomatic defeat or a domestic economic collapse.
text_raw:
This  pattern  of  personal  and  rather  arbitrary  rule,  opposed  by  the  older  ruling  groups
but  sustained  by  the  ordinary  Frenchman  whenever  De  Gaulle  asked  for  such  support,  has
continued  to  be  the  pattern  of  De  Gaulle's  political  system,  and  will  undoubtedly  continue
unless  he  meets  some  unforeseen  sharp  diplomatic  defeat  or  a  domestic  economic
collapse.

text: Both of these are unlikely at the present time.
text_raw: Both  of  these  are  unlikely  at  the  present  time.

text: While French political life passed through these stages of superficial drama and fundamental boredom, British political life wallowed in a malaise of mediocrity.
text_raw:
While  French  political  life  passed  through  these  stages  of  superficial  drama  and
fundamental  boredom,  British  political  life  wallowed  in  a  malaise  of  mediocrity.

groups  were  actually  discontented,  and  certainly  none  was  enthusiastic  about  the  situation

text: The Conservative Government came to office in 1951, was returned in the elections of 1955, and returned again in the elections of October 1959.
text_raw:
The  Conservative  Government  came  to  office  in  1951,  was  returned  in  the  elections  of

text: Anthony Eden served a brief and rather unsuccessful prime ministership from the retirement of Winston Churchill in April 1955 until his own retirement in favor of Harold Macmillan in January 1957.
text_raw:
Anthony  Eden  served  a  brief
and  rather  unsuccessful  prime  ministership  from  the  retirement  of  Winston  Churchill  in
April  1955  until  his  own  retirement  in  favor  of  Harold  Macmillan  in  January  1957.

text: The latter's term of office had no spectacular failures such as Eden had experienced in the Suez Crisis of October 1956, but on the whole there were also no great successes.
text_raw:
The
latter's  term  of  office  had  no  spectacular  failures  such  as  Eden  had  experienced  in  the
Suez  Crisis  of  October  1956,  but  on  the  whole  there  were  also  no  great  successes.

text: Macmillan sought to avoid issues if possible, to strengthen contacts with the United States and the Commonwealth by personal diplomacy, to follow Washington's policy as closely as possible without appearing openly obsequious, and to hold a fairly tight rein over the Conservative Party and the House of Commons.
text_raw:
Macmillan  sought  to  avoid  issues  if  possible,  to  strengthen  contacts  with  the  United
States  and  the  Commonwealth  by  personal  diplomacy,  to  follow  Washington's  policy  as
closely  as  possible  without  appearing  openly  obsequious,  and  to  hold  a  fairly  tight  rein
over  the  Conservative  Party  and  the  House  of  Commons.

text: An endless series of nasty little problems were met and somehow disposed of, to be followed by the rise of similar problems without any significant changes of course or speed.
text_raw:
An  endless  series  of  nasty  little
problems  were  met  and  somehow  disposed  of,  to  be  followed  by  the  rise  of  similar
problems  without  any  significant  changes  of  course  or  speed.

text: Abroad, the chief problems arose from the demands of various areas within the Commonwealth for self-government and the intrusion of the racial issue into these disputes, especially in Central Africa, East Africa, British Guiana, and Malaya.
text_raw:
Abroad,  the  chief  problems
arose  from  the  demands  of  various  areas  within  the  Commonwealth  for  self-government
and  the  intrusion  of  the  racial  issue  into  these  disputes,  especially  in  Central  Africa,  East
Africa,  British  Guiana,  and  Malaya.

text: The chief problems at home were equally endless and were concerned with the continual weakness of the pound sterling on the foreign exchange market and the social problems associated with the British economic expansion, such as increased vehicular traffic, spreading juvenile and adolescent delinquency, an apparent decline in the level of adult moral behavior, and the growing attacks, especially in industry and finance, on the economic bases of the older Establishment.
text_raw:
The  chief  problems  at  home  were  equally  endless
and  were  concerned  with  the  continual  weakness  of  the  pound  sterling  on  the  foreign
exchange  market  and  the  social  problems  associated  with  the  British  economic
expansion,  such  as  increased  vehicular  traffic,  spreading  juvenile  and  adolescent
delinquency,  an  apparent  decline  in  the  level  of  adult  moral  behavior,  and  the  growing
attacks,  especially  in  industry  and  finance,  on  the  economic  bases  of  the  older
Establishment.

text: In general, there was a slow spreading disillusionment with the structure of English society, especially with the continued dominance hy the old established families of political and economic life.
text_raw:
In  general,  there  was  a  slow  spreading  disillusionment  with  the  structure  of  English
society,  especially  with  the  continued  dominance  hy  the  old  established  families  of
political  and  economic  life.

text: This was especially notable among the middle and lower middle classes, while the lower class was, apparently, less antagonistic because of the continued relative prosperity and, above all, from the weakening of what might be called the Labour Party ideology of class conflict.
text_raw:
This  was  especially  notable  among  the  middle  and  lower
middle  classes,  while  the  lower  class  was,  apparently,  less  antagonistic  because  of  the
continued  relative  prosperity  and,  above  all,  from  the  weakening  of  what  might  be  called
the  Labour  Party  ideology  of  class  conflict.

text: In spite of a weakening of class antagonisms, there was a spreading rejection of the established class structure of England as it had existed for about a century.
text_raw:
In  spite  of  a  weakening  of  class  antagonisms,  there  was  a  spreading  rejection  of  the
established  class  structure  of  England  as  it  had  existed  for  about  a  century.

text: The good manners of the lower and middle classes, which had made visits to England such a pleasure, have slowly worsened, since they have come to be regarded as a mark of acceptance of the rigid class structure of the country, something that is decreasing in all classes.
text_raw:
The  good
manners  of  the  lower  and  middle  classes,  which  had  made  visits  to  England  such  a
pleasure,  have  slowly  worsened,  since  they  have  come  to  be  regarded  as  a  mark  of
acceptance  of  the  rigid  class  structure  of  the  country,  something  that  is  decreasing  in  all
classes.

text: This shift is evident even in legislation, such as an Act of 1963, permitting peers to give up their titles in order to run for office in the House of Commons.
text_raw:
This  shift  is  evident  even  in  legislation,  such  as  an  Act  of  1963,  permitting  peers
to  give  up  their  titles  in  order  to  run  for  office  in  the  House  of  Commons.

text: It is, perhaps, most threatening in the animosity expressed by some of the new class of very rich who reject the established social prestige of the older aristocratic families.
text_raw:
It  is,  perhaps,
most  threatening  in  the  animosity  expressed  by  some  of  the  new  class  of  very  rich  who
reject  the  established  social  prestige  of  the  older  aristocratic  families.

text: This last point is of some importance, for it may mark the end of a very significant period of English history.
text_raw:
This  last  point  is  of  some  importance,  for  it  may  mark  the  end  of  a  very  significant
period  of  English  history.

text: In this history the English social structure was retained because of its flexibility rather than its rigidity.
text_raw:
In  this  history  the  English  social  structure  was  retained  because
of  its  flexibility  rather  than  its  rigidity.

text: Access to higher social levels had never been closed to those with the energy and luck to work upward.
text_raw:
Access  to  higher  social  levels  had  never  been
closed  to  those  with  the  energy  and  luck  to  work  upward.

text: These climbers invariably
text_raw: These  climbers  invariably

text: became strong defenders of the class structure, buying country houses, sending their children to boarding schools, and adopting the accent and other distinctive idiosyncrasies of the English upper classes.
text_raw:
became  strong  defenders  of  the  class  structure,  buying  country  houses,  sending  their
children  to  boarding  schools,  and  adopting  the  accent  and  other  distinctive  idiosyncrasies
of  the  English  upper  classes.

text: This "aping of their betters" on all levels preserved the English class structure and provided the relatively frictionless character of English social life.
text_raw:
This  "aping  of  their  betters"  on  all  levels  preserved  the
English  class  structure  and  provided  the  relatively  frictionless  character  of  English  social
life.

text: Frictions have now appeared at the very time that class antagonisms have been weakened.
text_raw:
Frictions  have  now  appeared  at  the  very  time  that  class  antagonisms  have  been
weakened.

text: The reason for this has been the slow spreading in Britain of a kind of individualistic and nominalistic outlook that had been prevalent in much of the Western world for several generations but had been played down in Britain, until the last decade or so, by the pressures to conform on those who wished to rise socially and even on those who wished to remain in their same social level.
text_raw:
The  reason  for  this  has  been  the  slow  spreading  in  Britain  of  a  kind  of
individualistic  and  nominalistic  outlook  that  had  been  prevalent  in  much  of  the  Western
world  for  several  generations  but  had  been  played  down  in  Britain,  until  the  last  decade
or  so,  by  the  pressures  to  conform  on  those  who  wished  to  rise  socially  and  even  on  those
who  wished  to  remain  in  their  same  social  level.

text: As a result, traditionally in England, individualists have been eccentrics, that is, persons so well established that their social positions could not be changed notably by their personal behavior.
text_raw:
As  a  result,  traditionally  in  England,
individualists  have  been  eccentrics,  that  is,  persons  so  well  established  that  their  social
positions  could  not  be  changed  notably  by  their  personal  behavior.

text: This is now changing.
text_raw: This  is  now  changing.

text: Increasingly, those who wish to remain in their social status and, most significantly, a surprising number of those who are rising in the economic, academic, and political hierarchies feel called upon to reject in an explicit fashion the established class structure.
text_raw:
Increasingly,  those  who  wish  to  remain  in  their  social  status  and,  most  significantly,  a
surprising  number  of  those  who  are  rising  in  the  economic,  academic,  and  political
hierarchies  feel  called  upon  to  reject  in  an  explicit  fashion  the  established  class  structure.

text: This began with the writings of Labour Party intellectuals early in the century; but it has now become so widespread that rising young men today still continue to rise without conforming to the established behavioral patterns of their aspirant levels.
text_raw:
This  began  with  the  writings  of  Labour  Party  intellectuals  early  in  the  century;  but  it  has
now  become  so  widespread  that  rising  young  men  today  still  continue  to  rise  without
conforming  to  the  established  behavioral  patterns  of  their  aspirant  levels.

text: One reason for this, of course, is that control of the ladders to success are no longer so closely held.
text_raw:
One  reason  for
this,  of  course,  is  that  control  of  the  ladders  to  success  are  no  longer  so  closely  held.

text: In the old days, the merchant bankers of London, EC2, controlled fairly well the funds that were needed for almost any enterprise to become a substantial success.
text_raw:
In
the  old  days,  the  merchant  bankers  of  London,  EC2,  controlled  fairly  well  the  funds  that
were  needed  for  almost  any  enterprise  to  become  a  substantial  success.

text: Today much larger funds are available from many diverse sources, from abroad, from government sources, from insurance and pension funds, from profits of other enterprises, and from other sources.
text_raw:
Today  much
larger  funds  are  available  from  many  diverse  sources,  from  abroad,  from  government
sources,  from  insurance  and  pension  funds,  from  profits  of  other  enterprises,  and  from
other  sources.

text: These are no longer held under closely associated controls and are much more impersonal and professionalized in their disposal, so that, on the whole, an energetic man (or a group with a good idea) can get access to larger funds today and can do so without anyone much caring if he accepts the established social precedents.
text_raw:
These  are  no  longer  held  under  closely  associated  controls  and  are  much
more  impersonal  and  professionalized  in  their  disposal,  so  that,  on  the  whole,  an
energetic  man  (or  a  group  with  a  good  idea)  can  get  access  to  larger  funds  today  and  can
do  so  without  anyone  much  caring  if  he  accepts  the  established  social  precedents.

text: At the same time, on lower levels, young men working their way upward, although not, perhaps, to "the top," no longer conform in dress and behavior to the expected patterns of respectability of their social aspirations, but often show a more or less open defiance of these.
text_raw:
At  the  same  time,  on  lower  levels,  young  men  working  their  way  upward,  although
not,  perhaps,  to  "the  top,"  no  longer  conform  in  dress  and  behavior  to  the  expected
patterns  of  respectability  of  their  social  aspirations,  but  often  show  a  more  or  less  open
defiance  of  these.

text: The most obvious, and in a way most frightening, examples of this are to be found in the open defiance of all respectability by adolescents and post-adolescents of various social levels, but chiefly low ones, who have rioted by the thousands at various seaside resorts on long weekends in recent years.
text_raw:

text: The former Socialist Utopia, the Soviet Union, became the archenemy, and the United States, previously regarded as the epitome of capitalist corruption, became a combination of St. George and Santa Claus; the postwar experience with nationalization disillusioned all but the most doctrinaire of Socialists, and the majority of voters, once they had obtained the basic elements of social welfare, medical care, and social insurance in the immediate post-war period, showed a strange preference for moderate or even Conservative leaders rather than for the advocates of Left-wing policies..

1964,  and  the  death  that  year  of  Jawaharlal  Nehru,  who  had  been  prime  minister  of  India
from  the  achievement  of  independence  in  1947,  the  governments  of  all  major  countries
except  France  and  Red  China  underwent  significant  shifts  of  personnel  in  a  period  of
about  fifteen  months.

text: This gave rise to a "pause" in world history for almost all of 1963- 1964, during which each country placed increased emphasis on its domestic problems, especially on the demands of its citizens for increased prosperity, civil rights, and social security.
text_raw:
This  gave  rise  to  a  "pause"  in  world  history  for  almost  all  of  1963-
1964,  during  which  each  country  placed  increased  emphasis  on  its  domestic  problems,
especially  on  the  demands  of  its  citizens  for  increased  prosperity,  civil  rights,  and  social
security.

text: Since the same tendency became evident also in France and Red China where the previous leaders continued in power, the last two years covered by this book were years of hesitation, decreased world tension, and confused plans for future courses.
text_raw:
Since  the  same  tendency  became  evident  also  in  France  and  Red  China  where
the  previous  leaders  continued  in  power,  the  last  two  years  covered  by  this  book  were
years  of  hesitation,  decreased  world  tension,  and  confused  plans  for  future  courses.

text: Tragedy and Hope?
text_raw: Tragedy  and  Hope?

text: The tragedy of the period covered by this book is obvious, but the hope may seem dubious to many.
text_raw:
The  tragedy  of  the  period  covered  by  this  book  is  obvious,  but  the
hope  may  seem  dubious  to  many.

text: Only the passage of time will show if the hope I seem to see in the future is actually there or is the result of mis-observation and self-deception.
text_raw:
Only  the  passage  of  time  will  show  if  the  hope  I  seem
to  see  in  the  future  is  actually  there  or  is  the  result  of  mis-observation  and  self-deception.

text: The historian has difficulty distinguishing the features of the present, and generally prefers to restrict his studies to the past, w here the evidence is more freely available and where perspective helps him to interpret the evidence.
text_raw:
The  historian  has  difficulty  distinguishing  the  features  of  the  present,  and  generally
prefers  to  restrict  his  studies  to  the  past,  w  here  the  evidence  is  more  freely  available  and
where  perspective  helps  him  to  interpret  the  evidence.

text: Thus the historian speaks with decreasing assurance about the nature and significance of events as they approach his own day.
text_raw:
Thus  the  historian  speaks  with
decreasing  assurance  about  the  nature  and  significance  of  events  as  they  approach  his
own  day.

text: The time covered by this book seems to this historian to fall into three periods: the nineteenth century from about 1814 to about 1895; the twentieth century, which did not begin until after World War n, perhaps as late as 1950; and a long period of transition from 1895 to 1950.
text_raw:
The  time  covered  by  this  book  seems  to  this  historian  to  fall  into  three  periods:
the  nineteenth  century  from  about  1814  to  about  1895;  the  twentieth  century,  which  did
not  begin  until  after  World  War  n,  perhaps  as  late  as  1950;  and  a  long  period  of  transition
from  1895  to  1950.

text: The nature of our experiences in the first two of these periods is clear enough, while the character of the third, in which we have been for only half a generation, is much less clear.
text_raw:
The  nature  of  our  experiences  in  the  first  two  of  these  periods  is  clear
enough,  while  the  character  of  the  third,  in  which  we  have  been  for  only  half  a
generation,  is  much  less  clear.

text: A few things do seem evident, notably that the twentieth century now forming is utterly different from the nineteenth century and that the age of transition between the two was one of the most awful periods in all human history.
text_raw:
A  few  things  do  seem  evident,  notably  that  the  twentieth  century  now  forming  is
utterly  different  from  the  nineteenth  century  and  that  the  age  of  transition  between  the
two  was  one  of  the  most  awful  periods  in  all  human  history.

text: Some, looking back on the nineteenth century across the horrors of the age of transition, may regard it with nostalgia or even envy.
text_raw:
Some,  looking  back  on  the
nineteenth  century  across  the  horrors  of  the  age  of  transition,  may  regard  it  with  nostalgia
or  even  envy.

text: But the nineteenth century was, however hopeful in its general processes, a period of materialism, selfishness, false values, hypocrisy, and secret vices.
text_raw:
But  the  nineteenth  century  was,  however  hopeful  in  its  general  processes,  a
period  of  materialism,  selfishness,  false  values,  hypocrisy,  and  secret  vices.

text: It was the working of these underlying evils that eventually destroyed the century's hopeful qualities and emerged in all their nakedness to become dominant in 1914.
text_raw:
It  was  the
working  of  these  underlying  evils  that  eventually  destroyed  the  century's  hopeful  qualities
and  emerged  in  all  their  nakedness  to  become  dominant  in  1914.

text: Nothing is more revealing of the nature of the nineteenth century than the misguided complacency and optimism of 1913 and early 1914 and the misconceptions with which the world's leaders went to war in August of 1914.
text_raw:
Nothing  is  more
revealing  of  the  nature  of  the  nineteenth  century  than  the  misguided  complacency  and
optimism  of  1913  and  early  1914  and  the  misconceptions  with  which  the  world's  leaders
went  to  war  in  August  of  1914.

text: The events of the following thirty years, from 1914 to 194;, showed the real nature of the preceding generation, its ignorance, complacency, and false values.
text_raw:
The  events  of  the  following  thirty  years,  from  1914  to  194;,  showed  the  real  nature  of
the  preceding  generation,  its  ignorance,  complacency,  and  false  values.

text: Two terrible wars sandwiching a world economic depression revealed man's real inability to control his life by the nineteenth century's techniques of laissez faire, materialism, competition, selfishness, nationalism, violence, and imperialism.
text_raw:
Two  terrible  wars
sandwiching  a  world  economic  depression  revealed  man's  real  inability  to  control  his  life
by  the  nineteenth  century's  techniques  of  laissez  faire,  materialism,  competition,
selfishness,  nationalism,  violence,  and  imperialism.

text: These characteristics of late nineteenth-century life culminated in World War II in which more than 50 million persons, 23 million of them in uniform, the rest civilians, were killed, most of them by horrible deaths.
text_raw:
These  characteristics  of  late
nineteenth-century  life  culminated  in  World  War  II  in  which  more  than  50  million
persons,  23  million  of  them  in  uniform,  the  rest  civilians,  were  killed,  most  of  them  by
horrible  deaths.

text: The hope of the twentieth century rests on its recognition that war and depression are man-made, and needless.
text_raw:
The  hope  of  the  twentieth  century  rests  on  its  recognition  that  war  and  depression  are
man-made,  and  needless.

text: They can be avoided in the future by turning from the nineteenth-century characteristics just mentioned and going back to other characteristics that our Western society has always regarded as virtues: generosity, compassion, cooperation, rationality, and foresight, and finding an increased role in human life for love, spirituality, charity, and self-discipline.
text_raw:
They  can  be  avoided  in  the  future  by  turning  from  the
nineteenth-century  characteristics  just  mentioned  and  going  back  to  other  characteristics
that  our  Western  society  has  always  regarded  as  virtues:  generosity,  compassion,
cooperation,  rationality,  and  foresight,  and  finding  an  increased  role  in  human  life  for
love,  spirituality,  charity,  and  self-discipline.

text: Some things we clearly do not yet know, including the most important of all, which is how to bring up children to form them into mature, responsible adults, but on the whole we do know now, as we have already shown, that we can avoid continuing the horrors of 1914-1915, and on that basis alone we may be optimistic over our ability to go back to the tradition of our Western society and to resume its development along its old patterns of Inclusive Diversity.

Some  things  we  clearly  do  not  yet  know,  including  the
most  important  of  all,  which  is  how  to  bring  up  children  to  form  them  into  mature,
